name: libSceAgc.L45
text: [sceAgcDcbSetWorkloadsActive and sceAgcDcbSetWorkloadComplete](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgc/DcbState/src/Workload.cpp) (libSceAgc) and [sceAgcDriverRegisterWorkloadStream](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Resource/src/Registration.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the driver call records only the stream id (1 to 31; it returns 0 for any argument and keeps no stream record), and the DCB calls write the packets [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/main/src/libs/agc.cpp) writes: an 18-dword (active) or 12-dword (complete) `IT_NOP` packet with the stream id, and for active the 64-bit mask of the workload ids, for complete the workload id and the 64-bit clear mask of that id. Both return null for a null command buffer, an unregistered or out-of-range stream, a workload id above 63, and for active a duplicate id or a count of 0 or above 63. The layouts and checks come from KytyPS5 alone; the console oracle in [prosper](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper/blob/main/prosper/tests/data/console_oracle/agcbuild.golden.tsv) measures the null return only for unregistered streams, not the packet contents of a registered one. The error codes the console driver returns for an invalid or repeated registration are unknown, so registration never fails here. PPSA29866 calls sceAgcDcbSetWorkloadsActive while building its command buffers (sceAgcDcbSetWorkloadComplete was not observed); nothing else was observed.

Not measured on the console; PPSA02801 imports both (OpenAGC's import analysis), no title is shown calling them.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L115
text: A [COND_INDIRECT_BUFFER](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp) (`sceAgcCbBranch`) runs only with the always-pass compare function; a comparison or a predicated packet throws. Modes 1 and 2 run the first buffer, assumed to be the if-then and if-then-else modes of AMD's PM4 packet. [sceAgcCbBranch](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgc/Cb/src/Branch.cpp) does not check the compare address of an always-pass branch or the address of an empty buffer, as PPSA14632 passes an uninitialised compare address and a null else buffer of 0 dwords.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L167
text: [EVENT_WRITE stream-out statistics events](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, opcode 0x46) - `SAMPLE_STREAMOUTSTATS1`-`3` and `SAMPLE_STREAMOUTSTATS` (event types 0x01-0x03 and 0x20 in [navi10_enum.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/0fcb05b72344f40806cbe810de8872f1698bf053/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/navi10_enum.h#L14155-L14188)) are accepted on the graphics queue as a 2-dword packet with event index 0 and do nothing. [nvd.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/0fcb05b72344f40806cbe810de8872f1698bf053/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/nvd.h#L326-L347) documents these events only with the sampling index (3, or `EVENT_INDEX__SAMPLE_STREAMOUTSTATS*` 8-11 on gfx10); the index-0 packet has no destination dwords, and what the CP does with it is neither documented nor measured on hardware. AnyPS5 does not emulate the VGT stream-out counters, so there is nothing to sample. The sampling indices throw that sampling to memory is not implemented, and other indices, other sizes and the compute queue throw. [sceAgcDcbEventWrite](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgc/DcbFlow/src/Sync.cpp) ignores the address for every event type except 0x38 and 0x39, so a call with one of these event types and an address builds the index-0 packet: nothing is written and nothing throws. Whether the console's builder emits a sampling packet for an address is not known.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L32
text: [SET_PREDICATION](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (AGC driver) - boolean predication follows the AMD PM4 encoding [Mesa](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/amd/common/sid.h) uses: operation 3 reads 64 bits and 4 reads 32 bits, and bit 8 runs predicated packets when the value is non-zero (clear: when it is zero); the bit 12 hint is ignored. The address must have its low 4 bits clear, as `sceAgcDcbSetPredication` writes it. Query predication (Z-pass, primitive count), a predicated COND_EXEC, predicated command buffer chains and flips in predicated command buffers throw

name: libSceAgcDriver.L199
text: [Flip packets raise the graphics end-of-pipe event](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Packets/PacketExecution.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a flip delivers the queue's end-of-pipe event (`sceAgcDriverAddEqEvent`) once the work recorded before it completes, as a `RELEASE_MEM` with `INT_SEL` does, but only on a queue that has never delivered an interrupt from such a release: the queue is latched the first time a release interrupt reaches the event queue, and flips on that queue deliver nothing while its own release interrupts keep arriving. The latch is cleared when the queue has flipped five times without another interrupt from its own releases: the fifth flip delivers the event and unlatched the queue, so a title that waits on the flip event after latching recovers only if it submits further flips. The bound cannot be by time: the next release interrupt can arrive seconds later than a suppressed flip across loading stalls, and delivering an unexpected flip event on a queue that pairs flips with releases can crash; no fixed window short enough to unblock a waiting title keeps such a title alive. Whether the console raises the event from the flip itself or from an interrupt its flip sequence contains is not measured; nor is how the console behaves for a title that waits on the flip event and also raises release interrupts on the same queue.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L41

text: [Tessellation factor ring](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/State/src/Configuration.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `sceAgcDriverSetTFRing` records the ring and `sceAgcDriverGetTFRing` reports it. Nothing is written to the recorded ring: tessellated draws run as Vulkan tessellation stages, which keep their factors on the host, so a title that reads tessellation factors from the ring finds none. A null base or a zero size throws; [ps5-opengl's AGC runtime](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl/blob/67c873f985eaefe0a72f713529e5632eaa01139c/src/platform/ps5_agc_native_runtime.c) calls `sceAgcDriverSetTFRing(0, 0)` in its cleanup, and what that does on the console is unknown.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L98
text: [Pending storage-image results](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) are stored when something reads their memory, not when the GPU work that wrote them completes. A title that waits for that work, frees the image and reuses its memory can have the new data overwritten by the late store (#1970). A title's own CPU reads are not seen either, so a title that reads the results after waiting for a label reads stale memory. Explicit-size file writes (`write`, `pwrite`, `writev`, `pwritev`, AIO and `fwrite`) synchronize their source ranges through the [host-read hook](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/GuestArena.cpp); other host readers are not covered. `APS5_STORE_AT_FLIP=1` stores every pending result at each flip and `APS5_STORE_AT_LABEL=1` before each label the GPU writes; both store every pending image, not only the ones the waited-for work wrote, and neither is on by default.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L63
text: [Initial stencil state](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/include/QueueState.hpp) uses zero for `DB_STENCIL_CONTROL`, `DB_STENCILREFMASK` and `DB_STENCILREFMASK_BF` (context `0x10b`-`0x10d`), including after `CLEAR_STATE`. The public V0, V4, V5 and V7-V11 [register-default tables](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgc/Command/include/RegisterDefaultsData.hpp) supply these values. Linux's [GFX10 clear-state table](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/clearstate_gfx10.h) agrees on the control register but uses `0x01000000` for the reference masks; the console reset values have not been measured. Planet Coaster (PPSA01736 v01.017) enables stencil tests without writing the control register.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L108
text: [PM4 submission rings](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/SubmissionRing.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) keep only the first 512 dwords of each submission, so the packets past them are not printed. The [failure report](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/FailureReport.cpp) dump does not allocate from the C runtime heap: packet names come from static strings, each line is formatted with integer and string conversions into a 512-byte stack buffer and written with one `WriteFile`. It still runs on whatever state the crash left. It waits about 100 yields for each ring's lock and otherwise prints that queue as busy, so a crash while recording a submission loses that queue's ring. It reads the rings without checking them, so a crash that corrupted them can fault inside the dump; such a fault during the report of an unhandled exception stops in that report's `Sleep(INFINITE)` and the process hangs instead of ending. The reports run at most once per process. Linux has no crash report: there the rings are printed only by `APS5_STALL_WATCHDOG_SECS`.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L100
text: Windows host-pointer imports of the guest mapping itself are compared instead of write-watched, except writable imports of private `MEM_WRITE_WATCH` memory when the import probe keeps the write watch and a settle queue exists: those of 1 MiB or more stay watched, and smaller ones return to the watch once their settle has completed, unless a storage image overlaps them (see Pages under an import window): a driver can mark imported pages dirty after the synchronous import window. Shared memory imported through a separate writable alias retains protection-based tracking on the guest views; driver access to the import alias does not disarm those views. [GuestMemory](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/GuestMemory.cpp) excludes every overlapping 64 KiB tracker block while its backing is retained. A full block replaced by fresh private backing regains tracking and gets a new generation; protection changes, partial replacements and shared remappings do not restore it. Excluded blocks keep their write-watch marks as a hint only (`UntrackedHint`): a storage image or a sampled texture snapshot over them compares its bytes again after a mark in its range, a driver store, a mapping change or a recorded GPU write instead of at every collect epoch or lookup, and a mark the driver makes without a CPU store costs one comparison. This preserves CPU edits through byte comparisons but limits snapshot reuse on excluded blocks to draws of one collect epoch and disables unit shadows for them; restoring tracking on import retirement without replacing the backing remains unimplemented.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L101
text: [Pages under an import window](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/GuestMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) whose write protection was resolved while a host import that leaves its range watched was made are compared with the bytes they held before the import and count as stored over only when those differ. A CPU store of the bytes already there within the window cannot be told apart from an import that resolves the write protection without storing, as the NVIDIA driver (610.57.04) does for every imported page, so such a store does not win over pending results. Where host-pointer and dma-buf imports differ in whether they stay watched, a failed host-pointer import and the dma-buf import after it are two windows, and the pages the failed one resolved count as stored over. On Windows, the NVIDIA driver (617.42) marks every page of a host import of private `MEM_WRITE_WATCH` memory written, asynchronously, until a GPU use of the import completes; a 4-byte read of it on the settle queue ends that even while main-queue work that used the import first is still running, and an earlier import of the same pages whose first use runs after that read marks none of them (`agc_import_settle_first_use`, `agc_import_settle_earlier_import`). Such an import stays watched only after a 4-byte read of it on the settle queue has completed inside the window. Each one waits for that read, which keeps its window open for one round trip on the settle queue, so a same-value CPU store from another thread in that time counts as unchanged too. An import made where no settle queue exists is compared instead. An import of under 1 MiB is not settled inside its window, because the settle blocks the importing thread and a title that imports a 64 KiB buffer around every submission lost about 19 % of its frame rate to that wait (Dripl1x, #6060). It is compared until its read, submitted in a batch by a later import lookup under `GpuMutex` while the imports match the registry, has completed; a later lookup then returns its whole blocks to the write watch, each stamped as a CPU store, so whatever was derived from them while they were compared reads as changed once. Its blocks stay compared while storage results are pending over them, and those of an import retired before that stay compared.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L102
text: [Settled dma-buf imports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestBufferMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): on Linux a dma-buf import of 1 MiB or more is read by a 4-byte copy on the settle queue right after it is made (`settleImport`), so the kernel maps its pages for the GPU there and not in the first submission that uses it (about 2 s for a 3 GiB import on RADV). The import's buffer is shared with the settle queue's family. An import made at map time settles on the guest thread that maps the range, inside its map call, so that thread waits while the kernel maps the pages: 0.47 to 2.2 s for the 3 GiB range of Hades (PPSA03355) and 0.49 to 4.3 s for the 4.5 GiB range of ASTRO BOT (PPSA21567) on RADV. Both titles map these ranges at start-up; a title that maps large ranges during gameplay stalls its mapping thread for as long. An import made from a submission settles under the GPU mutex, so its frame still pays for it; a smaller import, and every import on a device with no settle queue (one without a copy-capable queue besides the main one), pays in its first submission. A range imported through a host pointer, as lavapipe imports shared memory, is not settled

name: libSceAgcDriver.L103
text: [Sparse dma-buf imports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestBufferMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): on Linux a shared-backed range larger than one 64 MiB udmabuf buffer is imported as one sparse buffer bound to the 64 MiB buffers, on a queue of its own when the device has a second family that binds sparse memory. The path is decided before anything is imported, and a failure after that throws. A range whose offset in the backing file is not a multiple of 64 KiB starts its sparse buffer at the 64 KiB block below it (`HostImport::lead`). A range takes the single udmabuf import instead, which udmabuf's `size_limit_mb` refuses above 64 MiB by default so the range is copied, when the buffer's sparse block size is larger than 64 KiB (it is 64 KiB on RADV), when the sparse buffer does not accept every memory type a chunk import can have, when the backing file ends inside its last chunk, or when it is imported at map time on a device with no second family (the bind then needs the GPU mutex); the NVIDIA proprietary driver imports no dma-buf memory

name: libSceAgcDriver.L104
text: [Unnormalized S# coordinates](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestSamplerResource.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `FORCE_UNNORMALIZED` uses a Vulkan `unnormalizedCoordinates` sampler, so the S# LOD range, LOD bias and mip filter are not applied, which is exact only on a one-level view.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L105
text: An [unnormalized S#](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestSamplerResource.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) maps clamp mode 0 (repeat) on X and Y to clamp-to-edge as required by Vulkan unnormalized coordinates, and assigns the magnification filter when minification and magnification filters differ (since unnormalized coordinates sample at LOD 0). Anisotropy, TRUNC_COORD, MC_COORD_TRUNC and other clamp modes still throw. Secondary LOD bias (LOD_BIAS_SEC, bits [19:14]) is accepted and ignored, matching RDNA2 hardware measurements across explicit and implicit samples. High on Life (PPSA15388, #4736) uses secondary LOD bias and unnormalized coordinates with clamp mode 0 and differing min/mag filters during home base and city rendering.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L106
text: [Background link-time-optimized relink of library pipelines](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/include/PipelineLinkOptimization.hpp) (libSceAgcDriver) is skipped on every GPU under NVIDIA's proprietary Vulkan driver (`VK_DRIVER_ID_NVIDIA_PROPRIETARY`), so those pipelines keep their fast-linked form. The optimized link loses the device when bound on an RTX 3080 (Ampere, #2866) and an RTX 4060 (Ada, #3434); an RTX 5060 and an RTX 5080 (Blackwell) on the same driver do not, so the scope is wider than the evidence. No standard Vulkan query tells the architecture apart, and the driver version that fixes it is unknown. `APS5_NO_PIPELINE_LTO` disables the relink on every driver.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L107
text: [8_SRGB and 8_8_SRGB textures](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/TextureFormat.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) that the device samples as R8_SRGB or R8G8_SRGB use its own decode, which need not match gfx1035: NVIDIA's R8_SRGB is one bf16 step off in 29 of 256 codes. A device that cannot sample them gets an RGBA8 sRGB copy instead (a blit of the R8 or RG8 texels, refreshed with the storage image's version), whose decode is likewise the device's; 3D textures and storage images that are not single-depth and format-matched are copied from their snapshot instead.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L109
text: [WAIT_REG_MEM](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Synchronization/WaitMemory.cpp) reports a diagnostic after `APS5_GPU_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` without treating the timeout as completion. An unsatisfied wait keeps polling and checking driver failures; a missing producer can therefore leave its queue waiting indefinitely. Existing recorded-label shortcuts remain in use.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L11
text: [Initial point context](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/include/QueueState.hpp) - new queues and CLEAR_STATE seed PA_SU_POINT_SIZE 0x00080008 and PA_SU_POINT_MINMAX 0xffff0000, matching every public context table in libSceAgc/Command/include/RegisterDefaultsData.hpp. Cocoon (PPSA08766) reaches geometry point output without writing these registers in the observed startup. Applying the SDK context defaults to initial/CLEAR_STATE driver context is inferred; GPU power-on reset state is not measured and is not the source of these values. Explicit writes and pushed/restored contexts retain their own values.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L110
text: A [WAIT_REG_MEM](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Synchronization/WaitMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) on a queue 0x20 label can time out while the awaited word holds the address of another slot of the same label area instead of 0 or 1, with no store to that label in the PM4 ring window (`APS5_PM4_RING`). What writes the address (guest CPU or the emulator) and whether the console would have satisfied the wait before the slot was reused are unverified; the wait keeps polling and its queue stays blocked. Seen in several titles on a Windows NVIDIA GPU; not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L111
text: [PM4 type-0 packets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Packets/CommandValidation.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a dword whose packet type is 0, a zero header word included, is rejected with `unsupported PM4 packet type`, so the submission throws. Whether the console's command processor skips or executes such dwords, and what a run of them in front of a REWIND packet means, is unverified; shadPS4 (`liverpool.cpp`) and KytyPS5 (`pm4.cpp`) also treat type 0 as unsupported. One such submission begins with a seven-dword NOP and an eight-dword ACQUIRE_MEM, then 169 dwords of zero headers (dwords 15 to 183, zero in one run and stale words in another), and its packets start at dword 184, as sections of NUM_INSTANCES, SET_BASE, REWIND, NOP and ACQUIRE_MEM separated by zero gaps of 26 to 455 dwords (odd lengths included); letting a zero header through only moved the stop to a stale word.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L112
text: [COND_EXEC](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Packets/PacketExecution.cpp) reads its condition after the earlier packets of its queue complete. Without PFP_SYNC_ME the console's graphics PFP reads it ahead of the ME, so a title that races the read sees a later value here.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L113
text: A [flip inside a COND_EXEC range](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Packets/CommandValidation.cpp) throws: the flip is reserved with the video output when the buffer is submitted, and how the console withdraws a skipped one is unknown.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L114
text: A [COND_EXEC range](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp) must hold whole packets and end inside its command buffer. A chained INDIRECT_BUFFER or a REWIND inside a range throws, as what the CP does with the skipped dwords then is unknown.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L116
text: A [label or store](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) (`RELEASE_MEM`, `WRITE_DATA`, `DMA_DATA`) into guest memory the device has no host import of waits for all recorded work and is then written by the CPU, so the queue worker stalls once per such label. The console's CP stores it in stream order without that stall.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L117
text: [WRITE_DATA to thread-trace user-data registers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) updates the queue's UCONFIG values for register destinations `0xc340..0xc347`, including repeated writes to one address; these are not guest-memory labels. The range follows AMD's GFX10 `SQ_THREAD_TRACE_USERDATA_0..7` definitions in [the Linux register header](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/asic_reg/gc/gc_10_1_0_offset.h) and the packets emitted by PPSA21564's bundled AGC driver before its EOP flip. Other register destinations throw. GPU thread-trace capture and its user-data stream are not emitted; only the final register state is retained. Console trace behavior is unverified.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L118
text: [WRITE_DATA with DST_SEL 3](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) writes guest memory like DST_SEL 5. AMD's GFX10 header names 3 the GDS, but Killzone: Liberation (PPSA11142) writes its frame fence with `sceAgcDcbWriteData(dst 6, cache policy 3, write confirm)`, which the SPRX-confirmed encoding ([OpenAGC](https://github.com/OpenAGC/OpenAGC/blob/main/src/cb_builders.c)) turns into DST_SEL 3 with a 40-bit label address in the title's own memory that `RELEASE_MEM` and `WAIT_REG_MEM` then use; the console must write that label or the title would wait on it forever. Whether the console routes it through the GDS or a cache is unknown

name: libSceAgcDriver.L119
text: [SET_*_REG_INDIRECT](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) reads its register list when the command buffer is submitted, with the packets. The console's graphics PFP reads it when it reaches the packet, so a list written after the submission (by the CPU, or by GPU work ahead of the packet behind PFP_SYNC_ME) is read here before that write. When the list read at submission holds an offset dword that is not a register offset (bits 16-27 set, or the 0xffffffff sentinel), the worker reads the list again where the packet executes and writes that copy. PPSA23566 (UFC 6) intermittently submits a SET_CONTEXT_REG_INDIRECT whose first entry is 0x038f038f or 0x03900390 in both copies; what the PFP does with such an entry is unknown, so a copy that still holds one throws unless `APS5_SKIP_INVALID_INDIRECT_REGISTERS=1`, which skips its invalid entries and writes its valid ones.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L120
text: The [shader float mode](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (`FLOAT_MODE`, `DX10_CLAMP`, `IEEE_MODE` and `FP16_OVFL` of `COMPUTE_PGM_RSRC1` and `SPI_SHADER_PGM_RSRC1_PS/GS/HS`, bit positions from Mesa's `gfx10.json` and `gfx103.json`) is decoded into `GuestContext::floatMode` and is part of the shader cache keys and the serialized request (#981). `IEEE_MODE` is read by `v_min_f32`, `v_max_f32`, `v_min3_f32`, `v_max3_f32` and `v_med3_f32`, their f16 forms, `v_min_f64` and `v_max_f64`, `IEEE_MODE` and the `FLOAT_MODE` output denormal bits by the output modifier, `DX10_CLAMP` by the clamp modifier, `FP16_OVFL` by every instruction with an f16 result (see its entry), and the whole mode by the 16-bit interpolation instructions (see their entries). With IEEE=1 a signaling NaN operand returns that NaN quieted (the first operand checked first, min3/max3 as two nested pairs, med3 as min3 when any operand is NaN), measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) over every combination of ±0, ±1, ±inf, denormals, quiet and signaling NaNs with f32 denormals kept and flushed. IEEE=0 and unknown modes keep the previous f32 lowering, which matches IEEE=0. The f16 forms choose their NaN results on the bits: a NaN operand returns the other operand unchanged (src0 when both are NaN), and with IEEE=1 a signaling NaN operand returns that NaN quieted, in the same order as f32. `v_min_f64` and `v_max_f64` quiet a signaling NaN operand the same way with IEEE=1; with IEEE=0 they return src0 unchanged when src1 is NaN, otherwise src1 when src0 is NaN. Both were measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f32 denormals kept and flushed and f16/f64 denormals kept; RDNA2 has no f64 min3, max3 or med3. Unknown modes follow IEEE=0. `v_min_f16` and `v_max_f16` flush each denormal input to its signed zero when bit 0 of the f16/f64 denormal field is clear (0 and 2); fields 1 and 3 preserve inputs, even when output flushing is enabled. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, including signed zeros, NaNs and neg/abs modifiers. Unknown modes keep f16 denormals. `v_min_f64` and `v_max_f64` flush subnormal inputs to signed zero when bit 0 of the f16/f64 denormal field is clear (0 and 2); fields 1 and 3, and an unknown mode, preserve inputs. The fully flushed and preserved f64 behavior was [measured on gfx1036](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/2036); split-mode selection follows [LLVM's denormal-mode enumeration](https://llvm.org/docs/AMDGPUUsage.html#floating-point-denorm-mode-enumeration-values). Other f64 arithmetic does not model these denormal controls. NaN quieting in f16 arithmetic (the unary instructions and the f32 arithmetic follow it, see below) and `FLOAT_MODE` (f32 denormals flushed before the min/max compare in Astro's Playroom's 0xc0) still follow a single mode, as the entries below record. The mode comes from the registered shader header's `sh_registers`, the same source at registration and at draw/dispatch so the prepared artifact keys match. A title that rewrites RSRC1 at run time, or a raw compute program with no header, compiles with that mode or none.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L121
text: A [WAIT_REG_MEM](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Synchronization/WaitMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) that a compute queue passes on another queue's recorded label store, before the GPU has executed it, is landed before the queue's next dispatch, draw, COND_EXEC or predicated packet reads guest memory: the worker polls until memory satisfies the wait or no unfinished batch writes the label. The graphics queue (queue 0) is exempt, as landing its waits costs PPSA01341 about a quarter of its frame rate; a title that fills memory a graphics command buffer reads after it submits the buffer behind such a wait reads it early there. `APS5_LAND_WAITS_ALL_QUEUES=1` lands the graphics queue's waits too.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L122
text: [CPU reads behind an address-based build](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Draw/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - an address-based store (FLAT/GLOBAL, or through a descriptor the recompiler cannot resolve to a static buffer) is not recorded as a pending write: its batch holds a lease on the registered allocations instead, and the flush hook does not wait for it. A DISPATCH_INDIRECT whose arguments are read on the CPU first finishes the batches recorded with a lease (`Graphics::FinishLeaseWork`). These reads do not, so they can see guest memory from before such a build ran: the indirect draw arguments and draw count of a draw resolved on the CPU (`Pm4::ReadDrawArguments`, `Pm4::ReadDrawCount`), the count record of the [copy kernel](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Memory/BufferCopy.cpp) HLE (guarded only by its shape check), and the checks in [Submission.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp) that decide whether a queue awaits a label only the title writes (`awaitsTitle`, `orderReleased`). No test covers them and no title has been seen to read such memory there.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L123
text: The [dispatches that follow a compute queue's wait](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Dispatch/DispatchAhead.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver), up to the next wait that memory does not satisfy, a packet that writes guest memory other than a label, or a conditional packet, are resolved (memory captured, shader recompiled) when the wait passes, as the CP reads them right after it; the graphics queue is exempt (`APS5_GROUP_CAPTURE_ALL_QUEUES=1` includes it). The device still reads guest memory when the dispatch is issued; when that memory no longer matches the capture, the dispatch is resolved again from current memory.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L124
text: [PA_CL_CLIP_CNTL](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `CLIP_DISABLE` (bit 16) and `DX_LINEAR_ATTR_CLIP_ENA` (bit 24) are accepted without changing pipeline state: Vulkan clips primitives against viewport guard bands and clips `NoPerspective` outputs linearly; what clearing bit 24 or setting bit 16 changes on the console beyond standard clipping is undocumented.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L125
text: [10_11_11 unorm color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) render into R32_UINT attachments: the pixel shader packs each export, rounded to nearest even like format-30 image stores, which is assumed to match the CB's conversion.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L126
text: [11_11_10 float color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) render into R32_UINT attachments: the pixel shader packs each export toward zero like format-43 image stores (overflow to the largest finite value, negatives to zero, NaN kept), which is assumed to match the CB's conversion; only the reversed component order (COMP_SWAP 2) is accepted.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L127
text: [PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL.PROVOKING_VTX_LAST](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Pipeline.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) uses Vulkan's last-vertex mode for native primitives. Bit 19 follows [opengnm's `flatshade_first` mapping](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl/blob/db752da4c89380af228497b5b6852163a4e61069/src/gallium/ps5/ps5_screen.c#L2244); vertex selection follows [Vulkan](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/drawing.html#drawing-primitive-topologies), without console measurements. A [rect-list](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/RectListShaders.cpp) draw in last mode gives all four corners of each rectangle the flat inputs of its third vertex through the generated control stage, as first mode gives them those of its first, so Vulkan's choice of provoking vertex for the tessellated triangles does not matter; which vertex the console takes for a rectangle is not measured either. A geometry program's primitives keep the vertex indices of its own primitive export on the [mesh path](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp), so last mode takes their flat inputs (from [Vulkan](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/vertexpostproc.html#vertexpostproc-flatshading)) and their [layer](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) from the last index of each primitive, while their per-vertex inputs keep the order of first mode ([Vulkan](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/primsrast.html#primsrast-barycentric)); that the console does the same for an exported primitive is not measured. Last mode throws without `VK_EXT_provoking_vertex`, for tessellation primitives, for triangle strips or fans assembled for a geometry program (whose odd-triangle order on the console is not measured), explicit per-vertex flat inputs, and triangle strips whose pixel shader reads a vertex slot itself (`v_interp_mov_f32`, or 16-bit interpolation, which is not checked yet), since the vertex order of odd strip triangles [depends on the device](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDeviceFragmentShaderBarycentricPropertiesKHR.html). `v_interp_p1_f32` and `v_interp_p2_f32` read P10 and P20 against the guest's I and J, which come from `gl_BaryCoordKHR` in the same vertex order as the per-vertex values, so the order cancels out and strips with only those reads draw. A FLAT_SHADE input without pass-through that is read through `v_interp_mov_f32` P10 and not P20 [returns the provoking vertex's value](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ShaderInfoCollector.cpp), like P0. ps5-opengl reads every flat input that way, and its driver passes the GL 4.6 CTS on a PS5 (#1413). The lane itself was not measured on the console, so with the first provoking vertex such a shader throws.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L128
text: [Dual-source blending](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) takes the MRT1 export as the second source of the MRT0 blend, as RADV and radeonsi program it; what the CB does with other export or target layouts is unknown, so they throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L129
text: [Blending into reversed-order color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - 8_8_8_8 and 16_16_16_16 targets with `COMP_SWAP` 2 or 3 keep the exported alpha in their first channel and red or blue in their fourth, which Vulkan would blend with the color and the alpha equation respectively. The color block is taken to blend in shader export order and apply `COMP_SWAP` afterwards: the alpha equation and every source-alpha factor use the exported alpha, and the destination alpha is the first channel. This follows the `CB_TARGET_MASK` text of the AMD [SI](https://xorg.freedesktop.org/docs/AMD/old/SI_3D_registers.pdf) (p. 229) and [CIK](https://xorg.freedesktop.org/docs/AMD/old/CIK_3D_registers_v2.pdf) (p. 238) register references ("the order of components after blending and before COMP_SWAP is applied"). RADV builds `CB_BLENDn_CONTROL` without regard to the swap ([radv_pipeline_graphics.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/amd/vulkan/radv_pipeline_graphics.c#L650-L709)) and renders R4G4B4A4, B4G4R4A4, R5G5B5A1 and B5G5R5A1 with `SWAP_STD_REV` and `SWAP_ALT_REV` ([vk_format.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/vulkan/util/vk_format.c#L43-L48), [ac_formats.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/amd/common/ac_formats.c#L609-L624)). Mesa CI's Navi10 (gfx1010) CTS run ([job 112381553](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/jobs/112381553), [112381554](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/jobs/112381554)) passes all 400 `blend.format.<format>.states` cases of each of those formats, including separate alpha and destination-alpha factors. It is not measured on gfx1013 or on 8_8_8_8 and 16_16_16_16 targets. Factor pairs Vulkan applies per channel are used directly. Otherwise the pixel shader only copies values: it writes the exported alpha, each channel's own export or the constants 0 and 1 into a second color at location 0 index 1 (and 1 into a channel of the first color whose source factor is ONE, moving its export into the factor), and the blend forms every factor, `1 -` and product from those copies through `SRC1_COLOR`/`SRC1_ALPHA` factors. The blend unit therefore rounds them as it rounds a plain Vulkan blend of the same export; Vulkan does not require a second-source color to be converted like the first, but on an RTX 5080 and lavapipe every reversed-order case of the execution test is bit-identical to the same draw into a `SWAP_STD` target, which the test checks. Factor combinations that copies cannot express (for example `ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` in the alpha equation with `SRC_COLOR` in the color equation), sRGB, SNORM and integer targets, constant and second-source factors, destination-alpha and `SRC_ALPHA_SATURATE` factors in the color equation, different color and alpha operations, MIN or MAX with factors other than ONE, other color exports when the blend needs the second color, and devices without `dualSrcBlend` throw. Gran Turismo 7 (PPSA01317) blends `CB_BLEND0_CONTROL` 0x65010504 into such a target (#4782).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L130
text: [DB_SHADER_CONTROL.CONSERVATIVE_Z_EXPORT](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderInputState.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) becomes `DepthLess`/`DepthGreater`. For a pixel shader that breaks the promise, the host driver decides whether its interpolated Z is depth-tested before shading; what the console does then was not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L131
text: [DB_SHADER_CONTROL.STENCIL_TEST_VAL_EXPORT_ENABLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) becomes `FragStencilRefEXT` when available, taken from the second MRTZ channel of the 32_GR and 32_ABGR formats as Mesa's AMD drivers write it ([`emit_ps_mrtz_export`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/3e32b0e1f132231b7a972c1b0b5b06c7e16cf8b9/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_ps_late.c#L194)); the console was not measured. The host value is the test value of both faces and what `REPLACE_TEST` writes, so a stencil operation that writes all ones or the operation value throws with it, as do a stencil clear draw and the UINT16_ABGR layout. A device without the extension uses the bounded replay described above. On such a device a draw first drops the export when the reference cannot change its result (`StencilReferenceUnused`: no stencil test or attachment, or on both faces a compare that ignores it and no reachable `REPLACE` through a non-zero write mask), and its pixel shader is then compiled at its first draw, not when its ABI is resolved. A device with the extension keeps the export, so each such shader keeps one pixel variant.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L132
text: [DB_SHADER_CONTROL.STENCIL_OP_VAL_EXPORT_ENABLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the pixel shader supplies the stencil operation source value per pixel, in place of `DB_STENCILREFMASK.STENCILOPVAL`. Only the operations that take that value read it: `REPLACE_OP` and the clamped and wrapping add and subtract (codes 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9), and the logic operations, which throw already ([AMD_stencil_operation_extended](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/AMD/AMD_stencil_operation_extended.txt), [AMD_shader_stencil_value_export](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/AMD/AMD_shader_stencil_value_export.txt)). Vulkan has no per-pixel operation value. Without `STENCIL_TEST_VAL_EXPORT_ENABLE`, a `REPLACE_OP` reachable through a non-zero write mask (`StencilOperationValueReplaces`) becomes `REPLACE` with the exported value as `FragStencilRefEXT`, or the bounded replay without the extension; this requires a compare that ignores the test value and no `ONES` or `REPLACE_TEST` on either face, and early tests throw. The value is taken from bits 8-15 of the second MRTZ channel: the PPSA27836 pixel shader that uses it shifts it left by 8 before `exp mrtz` (`v_lshlrev_b32 v0, 8, v0`), which is the only evidence for the layout. The add and subtract operations, and `REPLACE_OP` with a test value export, throw. With the 32_GR or 32_ABGR Z format and no such operation, or without a stencil test, the export cannot change the result and is ignored. Other Z formats throw. The console was not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L133
text: [DB_SHADER_CONTROL.DEPTH_BEFORE_SHADER](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderInputState.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) becomes `EarlyFragmentTests`, and so does `Z_ORDER` `EARLY_Z_THEN_LATE_Z` or `EARLY_Z_THEN_RE_Z` without kill, Z export, mask export or stencil export; with alpha-to-coverage the tests stay late. The meaning of the bit and of `Z_ORDER` 3 follows Mesa (`src/amd/registers/gfx10.json`; RADV sets the bit for `early_fragment_tests` in `src/amd/vulkan/radv_shader.c`). What the console does with `DEPTH_BEFORE_SHADER` and a Z export, a mask export, a stencil export or alpha-to-coverage together was not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L134
text: [PA_SC_CONSERVATIVE_RASTERIZATION_CNTL](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - 0x6001 uses Vulkan overestimation on devices that add at most 1/256 pixel and keep degenerate triangles; the console's uncertainty region and degenerate handling are unmeasured. A value with `OVER_RAST_ENABLE` and `UNDER_RAST_ENABLE` clear is decoded as disabled even when `UNCERTAINTY_REGION_MODE` or the `OUTER_`/`INNER_UNCERTAINTY_EDGERULE_OVERRIDE` bits (19:16) are set, as PPSA01474 writes 0xe6000; that these fields have no effect without over- or underestimation is assumed from their names, not measured. With `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` = 0 the `PERSP_CENTROID` and `LINEAR_CENTROID` inputs get the pixel-centre barycentrics, as without conservative rasterization ([shader debt](shader.md)): the one rasterized sample sits at the pixel centre, so every centroid the rasterizer could pick for an overestimated pixel is that point; that it does not move the centroid towards the primitive when the sample is uncovered is inferred, not measured. With more rasterized samples, and when a single-sample draw is raised to a multisampled color target, centroid inputs throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L135
text: [Descriptor pool chain](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - each pool holds two storage buffer descriptors more than a set can take, as a workaround: RADV (Mesa 26.0 and later) lets a `FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET` pool place a set up to 32 bytes past the pool's buffer ([`util_vma_heap_init`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/amd/vulkan/radv_descriptor_pool.c) is given `bo_size + RADV_POOL_HEAP_OFFSET` as a size), and with a page-multiple pool size those bytes are an unmapped page

name: libSceAgcDriver.L136
text: [CMASK fast clears](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - each fast-cleared CMASK tile (code 0) is stored as `CB_COLOR_CLEAR_WORD` into its 8x8 texels at the first draw into the target or at its fast-clear eliminate or DCC decompress pass, not as the color block writes the tile, and the CMASK is then stored as expanded (0xF): a texture or copy read of the target after that draw and before the title's eliminate sees the clear value in tiles no draw wrote, where the console keeps their previous bytes. Tile addresses follow the pipe-aligned SW_64KB_Z_X CMASK equation for 16 pipes; other CMASK swizzle modes, a cleared tile of a DCC target and a fast clear of a 3D or array color target throw; base mip 0 of a 2D mipmapped color target is supported (offset follows AMD Addrlib `Gfx10Lib::HwlComputeCmaskInfo` reverse mip-chain ordering preceding base mip 0, unverified on PS5 hardware; mipmapped targets with 8 or 16 bpp throw until `dsMipmapHtileFix` mip-tail shrinkage is modelled). A tile with a code other than 0 and 0xF keeps its texels like an expanded tile: PPSA18391 (engine: Clickteam Fusion) fast clears a target whose CMASK it never initialized, so some of its nibbles hold leftover values such as 1 and 10; what the console does with such codes on a single-sample target is unverified on hardware. Single-sample views with `viewMip > 0` skip CMASK fast-clear decoding since CMASK metadata only covers base mip 0 on AMD hardware (Mesa `si_state.c` similarly clears `FAST_CLEAR` for level > 0).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L138
text: [HTILE depth fast clears](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - HTILE is not modeled. Only RADV's `clear_htile_mask` compute kernel (17 GFX10 words, 64x1x1 groups) is recognized, and only when it leaves ZMASK at 0 (`user[4]` and `user[5]` low nibbles both 0); the dispatch still runs, and the host depth image is cleared to `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` the next time the surface with that `DB_HTILE_DATA_BASE` address is bound. The address match is exact, so a clear of a different HTILE range does not hit. HTILE initialization, the stencil-only update, and fast clears made by the SDK's own paths, CP DMA fills or other kernels are not covered and leave the depth image as it was. The kernel words are the ones the PR author saw RADV submit; they are not compared with Mesa's source. A second kernel, the 9-word dword fill PPSA01802 (Kena: Bridge of Spirits) clears its depth HTILE with (64x1x1 groups, one `buffer_store_format_x` per thread through the stride-4 V# in `user[0..3]`, the value read by `s_buffer_load_dword` through the V# in `user[4..7]`), is taken as a fill of that range when the store format is 32_UINT, 32_SINT or 32_FLOAT and the value V# covers the dword (NUM_RECORDS times its stride, or NUM_RECORDS bytes when the stride is 0) ([`MatchMemoryValueFill`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp), then the whole-HTILE and ZMask rules of `NoteDepthMetadataFill`). The value is read from guest memory when the dispatch is decoded, so a value that earlier GPU work in the same submission has not written back yet is not seen. When the [fill HLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Memory/BufferFill.cpp) takes the dispatch instead (an output descriptor of one 32-bit value per element, a value descriptor that covers the loaded dword, a 16-byte aligned range), the value is read again when the fill is recorded, after the labels queued before it, and the HTILE fill is noted with that value.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L139
text: [HTILE written by other kernels](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - when a depth target is bound and its HTILE was written since it was last read, the words over its whole pipe-aligned metadata (`HtileMetadataBytes`, the extent `HtileFillCovers` takes) are read, outside the surfaces mutex since the read waits for recorded work: when every one marks the depth (ZMask 0) or the stencil (SMem 0) cleared, the surface takes that fast clear and the words are stored back as expanded (depth only: ZMask 15 over the full Z range; with stencil: ZMask 15, Z range and SMem, SR1 and SR0 3), so only the title's next clear clears it again. PPSA29141 clears its depth every frame with a compute kernel the fill hooks do not recognize (`InvokeHTileClearComputeShader` in its `ClearMRT` pass); without this its depth kept every earlier frame and moving objects left black trails. PPSA25344 (Unreal Engine 5) reads its HTILE after the depth prepass in its Nanite depth export, which takes a tile with ZMask 0 as holding the clear value; without the expanded words the export put Nanite depth over the prepass and the Nanite material pass painted over the meshes in front. The word layouts are Mesa radv's for GFX10. Metadata with some tiles cleared is not modelled, and the compression state draws leave in HTILE is not tracked, so a title reading its HTILE after a draw sees the stored expanded words. A recognized HTILE fill or clear makes the next bind read the words again. A slice other than 0 of a depth array is read at its own HTILE (`DB_HTILE_DATA_BASE` plus the slice times `HtileMetadataBytes`) but the HTILE word layout of slices 1 and up is not modelled (PPSA05684's tile masks need X8 and Y8 to take Z0 and Z1 as well, slices 4 and up unmeasured), which neither the check that every word is cleared nor the store-back of each word in place needs, so such a slice takes the clear like slice 0. A depth-only HTILE whose tiles all have ZMask 0 but different Min/Max Z (per-tile clear values, PPSA05684's cascades) is taken as a whole-surface clear to `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR`, the value the DB's depth test reads for a cleared tile (`HTILE_Z_CLEAR_REG` in Mesa's `src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.h`: the clear word "only clears HiZ", "the DB register contain[s] the full clear values"); the HiZ test before it, which rejects against each tile's own Min/Max Z range (the HTILE definitions in the same file), is not modelled, so a draw that HiZ would reject over a tile cleared with Min/Max Z 0 is tested against `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` instead. A multisampled depth target, and any target whose HTILE overlaps a resident native depth guard, skips this read and store-back and goes to the native multisample depth owner, which keeps its own refusal for a fast-clear transition.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L14
text: [Optional BMP frame dumps](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) use checked host stdio. An open, header, pixel or close failure prints one diagnostic and disables subsequent BMP dumps for the process; queued frames drain without more file I/O. Pixel validation and allocation failures retain the existing fatal path. The CPU fixture checks identical BMP bytes and real pipe failures. VideoOut flips on an RTX 3060 continue after a first dump that cannot be opened; header, pixel and close failures during presentation are unmeasured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L140
text: [RADV fill-memory kernel](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Memory/BufferFill.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the [fill HLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Memory/BufferFill.cpp) takes RADV's 16-byte `fill_memory` compute kernel (`MatchClampedGlobalFill`: 11 GFX10.3 words, 64x1x1 groups, six user SGPRs with the address in `user[2..3]`, the largest store offset in `user[4]` and the value in `user[5]`; each thread stores 16 bytes at `min(thread * 16, user[4])`) as a fill of `min(threads * 16, user[4] + 16)` bytes. RADV initializes and fast-clears DCC keys and other metadata with it, so the key and metadata tracking sees such a fill where it is in the command stream; run as a dispatch, its global stores name no range, and a key fill was only seen once it had landed, after later writes to the surface. Only a 16-byte aligned address and largest offset are taken. RADV's 4-byte variant (fills below 16 bytes), other Mesa versions' encodings and other compilers still run as dispatches. The kernel words are the ones vkQuake's PS5 RADV build (Mesa 25.2) submitted; they are not compared with the NIR builder's output for other targets.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L141
text: [Host imports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestBufferMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) on Linux skip ranges that are not mapped read-write, which are copied instead. The NVIDIA driver (595.91.07) refuses `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` imports of read-only or executable mappings (and shared mappings of regular files) with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`, after which every `vkAllocateMemory` on the device fails the same way. Read-only ranges are never imported, even on drivers that accept them. Shared mappings of regular files are not checked for. On Windows, an alias of adjacent registered ranges is refused if any page is not a shared view; a range made entirely of shared views is aliased run by run, including across sections or nonconsecutive section offsets. Adjacent registered ranges are joined into one import: the largest aligned power-of-two block, from twice the import alignment up to the 8 MiB window, that holds the requested address and that they fill exactly, so a block only grows by doubling as its window fills. A block that would exceed the budget, would replace an import a build holds, or fails (a refused Windows alias, `vkAllocateMemory`) steps down to the next smaller block; a failed block is not tried again until one of its ranges changes. Ranges larger than the window are imported one at a time. A buffer bound across adjacent ranges that are each larger than the window, or bound exactly over adjacent ranges of any size (from the first one's start to the last one's end), joins them into one import when it is bound, and their own imports are retired; a buffer that crosses any other two imports is copied. A heap grown in pieces re-imports its joined run only when a buffer is bound exactly over all of its pieces, or when a sparse descriptor heap over it is bound: a heap a shader binds whole while only the pieces from its base are mapped is bound in place from the import of that run, its views ending at the import's end as the copy's do, once the previous bind of that address saw the same last mapped byte (a heap that grows between every two of its binds stays copied; one bound more often than it grows is joined again after each growth) and at most 64 times per joined run base; past that, with a message, it is not joined again: it is bound in place while an existing import covers its run and copied otherwise, until no registered range starts at that base or the device changes. Ranges larger than the window are taken to be registered whole and never grown in pieces: a title that grows a heap in pieces larger than 8 MiB re-imports the joined run each time a bound buffer crosses into a new piece. The 8 MiB window is a choice: unbounded runs were re-imported whole on every growth of a heap mapped in small pieces, and the NVIDIA driver (610.57.04, 615.78.08) then refused imports or lost the device. Not measured on RADV.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L142
text: [Cube texture descriptors](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestTextureResource.cpp) with equal `BASE_ARRAY` and `DEPTH` expose six faces starting at `BASE_ARRAY`. Measured with `image_load`, `image_sample` and `image_get_resinfo` on RX 6600 (gfx1032), using 64x64 R32_UINT faces and base slices 0, 5 and 6. Other ranges containing fewer than six faces still throw: hardware load bounds and filtered-sample addressing differ. A range of six faces or more that does not end on a whole cube keeps every slice up to `DEPTH`, the bound loads use on hardware; sampling the cube it cuts short is out-of-range cube-array sampling. Out-of-range cube-array sampling remains unimplemented. Samplers with `DISABLE_CUBE_WRAP` are created with `VK_SAMPLER_CREATE_NON_SEAMLESS_CUBE_MAP_BIT_EXT`, the flag RADV maps to that bit (Mesa `src/amd/vulkan/radv_sampler.c`, `src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.c`); without `VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map` a cube texture sampled through such a sampler throws. PS5 equivalence has not been measured on console hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L143
text: [Array layer views](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestTextureResource.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `ArrayLayersServeView` lets a 2D texture at a 2D array image's base address, or a 2D array texture over its first layers, view that image (`Texture::CanCopyFrom`). Mesa-built homebrew (ps5-opengl) writes the view's last slice plus one to `CB_COLOR_ATTRIB3.MIP0_DEPTH`, so a slice-0 render target is a two-layer array image, and the title samples it as a plain 2D texture (SuperTuxKart PPSA69421 drew a black 3D scene and minimap without this). The per-layer layout of a mipmapped array is assumed equal to a standalone surface's; it is not measured on the console. A 2D texture at a later slice's address still gets an image of its own.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L144
text: [Multisampled CMASK](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a multisampled color target's CMASK is decoded under CB_COLOR_INFO FAST_CLEAR (bit 13, as for a single-sample target) or COMPRESSION (bit 14). Which bit a multisampled target sets is inferred: its fast clears were seen on GTA V's multisampled targets through their CMASK fills, not in a register dump. A COMPRESSION-only target's zero CMASK is not read as cleared (inferred: zero means cleared only under FAST_CLEAR), so only a fill after its first use clears it. A slice of a multisampled array is its own image at its own address with its own CB_COLOR0_CMASK (inferred from the register layout). Its CMASK is main's whole-metablock size.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L145
text: [Multisampled CMASK state](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a multisampled target has no guest texels, so its CMASK state comes from fills rather than from a read at each draw as a single-sample target's does. A fill of the whole CMASK with 0 clears the host image at the target's next use, one with 0xffffffff marks it expanded, and any other pattern, or a fill that covers only part of the CMASK, throws at the next use (inferred: main's rule that a mixed CMASK is unmodeled, applied to the one host image). A FAST_CLEAR target starts from its CMASK keys at its first use, and a COMPRESSION-only target starts expanded. Copies by DMA into the CMASK are not seen, and a later use with another CMASK address throws. The clear does not rewrite the CMASK bytes as expanded, so a new target over the same CMASK (a different extent, so a different image) seeds from them again and clears once more.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L146
text: [Multisampled color fills](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a multisampled target's samples are on the host, so a fill of its color memory is applied at its next use: a uniform fill over the whole of it clears the host image to that value, and a pending CMASK fast clear takes precedence over the fill and over a fill that would throw. Its color memory is a single mip and slice of addrlib's block dimensions for its sample count (ComputeThinBlockDimension). A fill over part of it, a fill reaching the start of a target whose footprint is not computed (linear), and a fill value with no exact clear value in the format (sRGB channels other than 0 and 1) throw at the next use. A fill before the target's first use is not seen (the host image starts at 0), nor are copies or shader writes into its color memory. A uniform compute fill over exactly the whole color memory with an exact clear value is not stored into guest memory, since only the host image holds the samples. A target is retired only when its whole guarded range is unmapped or its allocation removed, so if a title reuses that memory for other data while it stays mapped, a read the guard does not check (a buffer read through a V# or a pointer) sees the bytes from before the fill.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L147
text: [Multisampled texture no draw rendered to](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - sampling a multisampled texture whose surface no draw rendered to creates the host target from the T# and clears it to the color a single 32-bit value repeated over the whole footprint encodes, padding up to whole tile blocks included. Inferred, not measured on the console: that the samples of such a surface are the guest color memory, as a title that clears its canvas on the CPU (ps5-opengl `ps5_clear_msaa4_color`) relies on. Memory that is not one repeated value, tile modes other than Standard4KB, Standard64KB and RenderTarget, unmapped memory and values with no exact clear color throw. CPU writes to the surface after its host target exists are not seen by the host.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L148
text: [Multisampled targets in CB passes](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a CB eliminate or DCC pass over a multisampled target throws, since its texels are on the host and only a CB resolve and an FMASK decompress (`CB_COLOR_CONTROL` mode 5) are modeled. The FMASK decompress only applies the pending CMASK fast clear to the host image; it requires a CMASK address, and the target's DCC and FMASK contents are not interpreted. DCC over a multisampled target is accepted only in that pass and throws everywhere else. A CB resolve into a fast-clear destination throws: the resolve writes the destination's texels but not its CMASK, which would still read as cleared.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L149
text: [Multisampled target guest access](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the memory a multisampled color target throws on (CPU read, index buffer read, fixed-function vertex buffer read, DMA copy, texture or storage image read) uses fragment-aware 64 KiB render-target blocks. [AMD Addrlib's GFX10 thin-block rule](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/core/addrlib2.cpp#L1680-L1712) gives the block width and height from element bytes and fragment count; its [surface-size calculation](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp#L4000-L4005) rounds both extents to those blocks and multiplies by element bytes and fragments. Thus a 1920x1080 4x RGBA8 surface occupies 0x1fe0000 bytes, leaving the next allocation at +0x2000000 outside the guard. The 2x and 8x block orientations differ from treating the fragments as a larger element. Console address-layout equivalence has not been measured. Other tile modes retain the conservative `max(CB bytes * samples, width * height * element bytes * samples)` bound, which may still reject a distinct allocation. Live targets remain cached per device, surface address, format, extent and sample count. Retired cache owners are removed on the next target, sampled or storage lookup; outstanding recorded work and sampled views retain their images. Ordinary sampled and storage bindings check the color-target guard before resource reuse, including precollected sampled lookups. Reused image tables do not invalidate on multisample color-target registration yet; their per-element fault handling and native multisample sampling require a separate reuse proof.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L150
text: [CB resolve sample count](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a draw with CB_COLOR_CONTROL in resolve mode is a CB resolve when either PA_SC_AA_CONFIG or CB_COLOR0_ATTRIB.NUM_SAMPLES is multisampled, and takes its sample count from CB0. Inferred, not from documentation: PPSA36082 resolves its 4x targets with no sample count in PA_SC_AA_CONFIG, and radeonsi sets PA_SC_AA_CONFIG to 0 for a multisampled framebuffer when rasterizer multisampling and line smoothing are off. PA_SC_AA_CONFIG is only compared with CB0 while PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_0.MSAA_ENABLE is set: PPSA08270 resolves a 4x 512x512 target with MSAA_ENABLE off and PA_SC_AA_CONFIG still at 2x (0x00108001) from earlier draws.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L151
text: [Custom MSAA sample locations](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) support a uniform 1x1 pattern for 2, 4 or 8 samples through VK_EXT_sample_locations. Patterns varying across the guest's 2x2 pixel grid use a 2x2 sample location grid, anchored at the framebuffer origin like the guest's while the window offset is zero, on devices whose `maxSampleLocationGridSize` for the sample count is a multiple of 2x2. On other devices every pixel takes the pattern's pixel (0,0) locations (`PA_SC_AA_SAMPLE_LOCS_PIXEL_X0Y0_*`, its first registers and the corner the grid is anchored at), and the first such pipeline of each sample count logs `[gpu] no 2x2 sample location grid`. The RTX 5070 reports 2x4 for 2 samples, 2x2 for 4 and 1x2 for 8; an AMD Radeon integrated GPU reports 2x2 for each; an RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (driver 617.42) reports 1x1 for every count. With that stand-in the top-left pixel of every 2x2 quad matches the console and the other three use its positions. A pattern that only reorders one set of positions between pixels, as a 2x checkerboard pattern puts its samples at x = +4/16 and -4/16 and swaps them on odd rows, keeps every position and the number of samples a primitive covers in each pixel, so a resolve that averages a pixel's samples, or takes their minimum or maximum, sees the console's values. Sample i of an odd row then holds what the console stores in sample 1 - i: a pass that reads the samples by index, as checkerboard reconstruction does, exchanges the two half-pixels of odd rows, which can show as combing along vertical edges, and per-sample shading, sample-mask exports and coverage inputs see the swapped indices too. A pattern whose pixels hold different positions draws pixel (0,0)'s positions in each pixel whose own differ. A device's pipelines and render pass begins take the same stand-in for a given pattern, so a sample-location-compatible depth image is not drawn with one set of locations and transitioned or tested with another. A multisampled rasterizer drawing into one-sample color targets, and a one-sample depth target if any, with MSAA_ENABLE set, no alpha-to-coverage and no coverage pixel input is drawn with one sample at sample 0's location in each pixel of the grid, as the targets keep only sample 0's coverage. Without PS_ITER_SAMPLE such a draw also refuses centroid inputs, and keeps PERSP_SAMPLE, LINEAR_SAMPLE and ANCILLARY: a pixel shaded once is taken to get sample 0's barycentrics and sample index 0. With PS_ITER_SAMPLE only sample 0's invocation reaches the targets, so its sample and centroid barycentrics are taken to be sample 0's and the draw is shaded once. Both are inferred, not measured. The pixel shader runs once per pixel with sample number 0, so ANCILLARY reads sample 0 and POS_X_FLOAT and POS_Y_FLOAT keep the position `SPI_BARYC_CNTL` names. PERSP_CENTER and LINEAR_CENTER inputs on this path are interpolated at sample 0's location on the host, where the console uses the pixel center; one-sample depth images are created with `SAMPLE_LOCATIONS_COMPATIBLE_DEPTH` when the device supports it, as multisampled ones already were; this is how VK_AMD_mixed_attachment_samples defines the case, and it is not measured on PS5 hardware. Other mixed sample counts throw. Devices without the required sample count, four subpixel bits or the full guest coordinate range refuse custom patterns. Depth images remain in GENERAL between draws, and render passes cannot continue across pattern changes. Guest offsets retain the existing decoder's signed four-bit, sixteenth-pixel interpretation; PS5 coverage and interpolation equivalence have not been measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L152
text: [Single-sample scan into a multisampled depth target](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a draw with `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` = 0 and `PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_0.MSAA_ENABLE` clear into a multisampled depth target rasterizes the depth target's sample count with every sample at the pixel center, as a single-sample scan into a multisampled color target already does. radeonsi programs this `MSAA_ENABLE` and `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG` with the depth buffer's own sample count when GL multisampling is disabled on a multisampled framebuffer ([L1066-L1068](https://github.com/openbsd/xenocara/blob/1b39033df8d928ec247ca64448c4a63c72302db7/lib/mesa/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state.c#L1066-L1068), [L3485-L3512](https://github.com/openbsd/xenocara/blob/1b39033df8d928ec247ca64448c4a63c72302db7/lib/mesa/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state.c#L3485-L3512)), although its comment lists Z samples as at most the coverage samples ([L3439](https://github.com/openbsd/xenocara/blob/1b39033df8d928ec247ca64448c4a63c72302db7/lib/mesa/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state.c#L3439)) and it sets `DB_EQAA.MAX_ANCHOR_SAMPLES` to the Z sample count, where PPSA18216 sets `DB_EQAA` to 0. GL then lets every sample take the single-sample depth ([L185-L190](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L185-L190)) and the fragment be treated as in multisampling with full coverage ([L422-L425](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L422-L425)), which is what this draws: each depth and stencil sample is tested and written with the depth at the pixel center. GL also lets an implementation test only a centermost sample and set every sample from it ([L425-L434](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L425-L434)), which differs when a pixel's stored samples differ; which one the console does, whether it instead evaluates the depth plane at each sample position, and how its occlusion queries count such a draw, is not measured on hardware. Points, lines, alpha-to-coverage, `DB_EQAA` Z interpolation or overrasterization, a pixel program reading the sample index, a sample-mask export and a single-sample color target next to the multisampled depth target throw

name: libSceAgcDriver.L153
text: [DCC display buffers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) are presented only when all keys of the console's DCC extent agree on uncompressed or a fast-clear code, padding keys included; other keys, and register-clear keys over a pending image, throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L154
text: [Storage image write-back](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) stores the GPU results over a CPU-stamped range whose guest bytes equal the copy taken when the image's layers got their generation (images up to 1 MiB whose guest bytes were settled at that point, with no unit shadow, pending image results or recorded GPU store over them; other images keep the previous rule: the CPU's bytes win). A CPU store that rewrites the baseline value after the GPU changed it is not told apart from no store, and the GPU result wins there. The 1 MiB limit is a choice, not a console value. A range a queued draw commit still has to read is left pending whatever the stamps say ([`DrawPipeline::HeldReads`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Draw/DrawPipeline.hpp)), so a title that recycles one allocation between an index buffer and a storage image sees the draw's own indices; the trade is a title that reads a surface as index data and means the image gets the pre-image bytes instead, since the reservation does not compare the command-stream positions of the draw and of the image's write. `APS5_NO_QUEUED_DRAW_READ_ORDER=1` restores the old behaviour, and the `[storage]` line counts the listings the hold turned away (`held for a queued draw read`) and the `[draw] pipelined` line the stores it held. The hold covers what the commit reads of guest memory: the index range, the vertex input ranges as their descriptor extents ([`QueuedDrawReadRanges`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Memory/WrittenBuffers.cpp), since the bytes a draw fetches depend on the highest index, which only the commit knows) and the source of a queued DMA copy. Every other commit-time read goes through the flush hook, so it sees the bytes the hold protects. Two commit-time reads are outside the hold: the texels a register or cmask clear materialization reads from the draw's own colour target (through the hook, so ordered, but the hold does not cover a render target), and a CPU read whose store the hold turned away, which sees the pre-image bytes. Nothing retries a refused store: the image reaches guest memory with the next flush of that range (the queue worker's idle store, a `WAIT_REG_MEM` poll over it, a later read or write of it).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L155
text: [16-bit float display buffers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/DisplayBuffer.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, libSceVideoOut) - pixel formats `0xC001000622000000` and `0xC001000600000000` are taken as R16G16B16A16 and B16G16R16A16 float, eight bytes per texel, as [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/59183dbfa81ed7efdff6069177fed50de0552725/src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/image/imageInfo.h) maps them and [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/VideoOut/VideoOutTypes.cs) names them (`Rgba16Float`, `Bgra16Float`); PPSA11386 registers 3840x2160 tiled buffers of the first. The tiled layout is assumed to be the 8-byte SW_64KB_R_X equation of `TextureSwizzleEquations.hpp` applied to full coordinates, as addrlib applies it, by analogy with the 32-bit scanout; `ColorTargetLayout` applies the equations to in-block coordinates, which for 8-byte texels differs in every odd 64-row block row (address bit 11 takes y bit 6) and for 16-byte texels also differs, so a float display buffer written through `WriteColorTarget` and presented from guest memory would show those rows misplaced. The values are assumed to be linear light and are encoded with the sRGB curve for the 8-bit output. Bits 32-39 of these formats are `0x06`, as in the 10-bit formats SharpProspero lists without sRGB transfer, while its sRGB formats have `0x00`, its 10-bit PQ formats `0x04` (with `0x07` in bits 40-47) and its float BT.2100 PQ formats `0x07`: they show only that these formats are not the sRGB ones. NaN and negative values give 0, values of 1 and above give 255, alpha is linear. Neither the layout nor the transfer is verified against console or title frames, and HDR output is not modelled. DCC metadata on a float buffer throws.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L156
text: [BT.2100 PQ display buffers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/include/PqToSdr.hpp) (libSceAgcDriver, libSceVideoOut) - pixel formats `0x8100070422000000` and `0x8100070400000000` are taken as 10:10:10:2 texels with BT.2020 primaries and the SMPTE ST 2084 transfer, red or blue in the low bits, as [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/VideoOut/VideoOutTypes.cs) names them (`Rgb10A2Bt2100Pq`, `Bgr10A2Bt2100Pq`) and [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/59183dbfa81ed7efdff6069177fed50de0552725/src/graphics/host_gpu/renderer/image/imageInfo.h) maps the first; PPSA01317 registers display buffers of the first when its output reports HDR. With HDR output they are presented unchanged through an HDR10 swapchain (`VK_COLOR_SPACE_HDR10_ST2084_EXT`, 10-bit, with `VK_EXT_hdr_metadata`); otherwise they are converted to 8-bit sRGB: ST 2084 EOTF, BT.2020 to BT.709 primaries with negative components clipped, a luminance tone map and the sRGB encoding. The tone map is ours: min(203 nits, white level) is SDR white (the BT.2408 HDR reference white), luminance passes unchanged up to 0.75 of it and an extended Reinhard shoulder above reaches 1.0 at the white level, the peak sceSystemServiceGetHdrToneMapLuminance last reported to the title (or the current one when it never asked), since titles read it once. How a console shows such a buffer on an SDR display is unknown. Alpha is opaque.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L157
text: [HDR output override](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/HostHdr.cpp) - setting `APS5_FORCE_SDR` suppresses HDR availability reported to titles while retaining the detected display and surface capabilities. It selects the existing SDR presentation path; it does not add support for floating-point BT.2100 PQ buffers (`0xC001070722000000` and `0xC001070700000000`), whose presentation remains refused. The override does not change the host display settings.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L158
text: [DCC key stores](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DccMetadata.cpp) cover the console's DCC extent only for pipe-aligned DCC of single-level, single-layer 4-byte SW_64KB_R_X surfaces; other surfaces, and every texture and color target key read, cover one byte per 256 bytes.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L159
text: [DCC key fills over other images](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a uniform fill at a live image's `dccAddress`, at least one key per 256 bytes long, is a key fill of that image even when other live images overlap it, but only while it is no longer than the image's key extent (`DccKeyCount`, the pipe-aligned count); a longer one is classified by its overlaps as before. The bound is inferred, not measured on a title: a longer fill also writes the bytes past the keys, which the overlapping image may own. Whether the title's bloom-target key fills stay within the extent was not checked (`APS5_TRACE_DCC_KEYS` prints the length of the fills classified as keys, not of the refused ones).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L16
text: [Inactive vertex point size](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) - `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL.USE_VTX_POINT_SIZE` is accepted for lines, triangles and rectangles with `GS_EN` and `HS_EN` clear, when polygon mode is disabled or both faces are filled. Points, patches and absent routing or rasterization registers still throw. Bit 16 selects the misc export's X component as PointSize ([AMD CIK register reference](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/programmer-references/CIK_3D_registers_v2.pdf), PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL); ignoring it for non-point rasterization follows [Vulkan PointSize](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/PointSize.html). This is inferred, not measured on console hardware. XashPS5 (PPSA19111 v1.3) sets `0x01210000` on a filled triangle draw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L160
text: [Comp-to-single DCC keys](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DccMetadata.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - key 0x10 (`GFX9_DCC_CLEAR_SINGLE` in Mesa `ac_descriptors.h`) uniform over a surface makes every texel the element at the start of its 256-byte block, the top-left texel of the block where radv's `build_clear_dcc_comp_to_single_shader` stores the clear color. Sampled textures and storage images read that expansion (a storage image's first write stores the keys uncompressed, as under a clear code), and a CB DCC decompress pass stores it over the texels. A fast-clear eliminate over such keys throws, as a metadata pass over mixed keys does; color targets that render over such keys use their stored texels, and textures read mixed keys, and comp-to-single keys of a format whose element does not divide 256 bytes, as stored. "Uniform" is judged over the key bytes the driver reads, one per 256 surface bytes (see DCC key stores above), so a pipe-aligned surface whose keys differ past that range is expanded as if all were comp-to-single, as for the other clear codes. Not verified on hardware

name: libSceAgcDriver.L161
