text: [8_SRGB color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) on a device that cannot attach and blend R8_SRGB render into an RGBA8_SRGB copy of the target, so the sRGB encode, decode and blend rounding are the device's; the console's are not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L162
text: [8_SRGB color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) on such a device throw unless they are single-mip 2D surfaces with a resident image; linear targets have none.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L163
text: [5_6_5 color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) render into R5G6B5. The field holding X is in bits 0-4, Y in 5-10 and Z in 11-15, as for the other AMD formats; the component swap picks which export fills them, following `ac_translate_colorswap` in [Mesa 26.2.2 ac_formats.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/amd/common/ac_formats.c), which programs `SWAP_STD_REV` (2) for a surface with red in bits 11-15. With `SWAP_STD_REV` red goes to bits 11-15, R5G6B5's red, so the exports are written as they are; with `SWAP_STD` (0) red goes to bits 0-4 and the exports are written with X and Z exchanged, as for 1_5_5_5. The decoded format, component mapping and write mask are tested, and an execution test draws 32_ABGR exports into tiled and linear targets in both orders and compares every stored texel with that layout on the host device; the export direction is not measured on a PS5. Only UNORM with those two component orders is accepted; `SWAP_ALT` and `SWAP_ALT_REV` keep throwing. Destination alpha reads as 1, as Vulkan defines it for a format without alpha, which is not measured on the console. Constant blend colors with `SWAP_STD` go through the `0xc6` component-swap handling, which is not tested for this format. R5G6B5 has no entry in the DCC and multisample clear-encoding tables, so a CB DCC decompress or eliminate of DCC clear codes other than 0000 and a fast clear of a multisampled 5_6_5 target throw, as for 1_5_5_5. PPSA27305 renders into this format with `SWAP_STD_REV` (discussion #6434).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L164
text: [1_5_5_5 color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) render into A1R5G5B5. AMD formats keep the first component in the least significant bits (X in bits 0-4, Y in 5-9, Z in 10-14, W in bit 15, as in the [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4) `kSurfaceFormat1_5_5_5` doc comment and as measured for textures in the packed 16-bit textures entry), while A1R5G5B5 keeps R in bits 10-14 and B in bits 0-4, so the pixel exports are written with X and Z exchanged, which makes the stored bits follow the guest layout. The decoded format, component mapping and write mask are tested, and an execution test draws 32_ABGR exports into tiled and linear targets and compares every stored texel with the guest layout on the host device; the export direction is not measured on a PS5. Only UNORM with the standard component swap is accepted. Constant blend colors go through the same component-swap handling as other targets with that export mapping (`0xc6`), which is not tested for this format. PPSA06699 renders into this format.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L165
text: [COPY_DATA from the GPU clock](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, `SRC_SEL` 9) writes the host steady clock in 10 ns ticks when the packet runs, the same counter as the `RELEASE_MEM` timestamp, not the console's GPU clock. The `COPY_DATA` cache policy fields are accepted and have no effect.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L166
text: [COPY_DATA from a register](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, `SRC_SEL` 0) copies the value the queue holds for a shader, context or user config register (`COUNT_SEL` two consecutive ones) and throws for a register with no value. A dispatch records `COMPUTE_DISPATCH_INITIATOR` and, for `DISPATCH_DIRECT`, `COMPUTE_DIM_X/Y/Z` in the shader registers; `DISPATCH_INDIRECT` clears the three counts. Neither the register values the CP writes nor the copy's ordering against in-flight dispatches have been measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L168
text: [INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_INDIRECT](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Pm4.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, opcode 0x91) loads INDEX_BASE, INDEX_BUFFER_SIZE (in indices) and INDEX_TYPE from the 16-byte record at `attribute_base + attribute_index * 16`, read when the packet runs. The record layout (address low, address high, size, type) is PAL's [`IndexAttribIndirect`](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/hw/gfxip/gfx9/gfx9Chip.h#L60-L67) and the packet is the one [`BuildIndexAttributesIndirect`](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/hw/gfxip/gfx9/gfx9CmdUtil.cpp#L2586-L2613) writes; neither is measured on a PS5 or seen in a title. `indirect_mode` 1 (`addr_offset`, which only PAL's ExecuteIndirect path emits) throws, and so does a record whose index type is above 3, as INDEX_TYPE does.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L169
text: [16-bit RGBA color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) support the standard and the alternate (`COMP_SWAP` 1) component order. Alternate swaps red and blue in shader exports, write masks and constant-color blend factors, following `ac_translate_colorswap` in [Mesa 26.2.2 ac_formats.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/amd/common/ac_formats.c). Blending into the reverse orders (`COMP_SWAP` 2 and 3) is covered by the reversed-order blending entry, and simultaneous targets requiring conflicting blend constants throw. Console equivalence has not been measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L17
text: [Native multisampled depth clears](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) accept the recognized HTILE mask kernel's direct full-range dispatch after its GPU writes complete. Every metadata byte needs tracked driver-store coverage since notification, no intervening CPU or depth write, and HTILE words proving the current clear value of zero or one. Partial, overlapping, indirect and unproven producers remain unsupported. Existing sampled views retain the native image; guest depth publication and metadata-fill transitions remain unimplemented. Windows shared imports retain write tracking through separate aliases; private host imports that lose tracking and copied or mirrored HTILE uploads remain unsupported. Clear-word encoding and console equivalence remain unmeasured on PS5 hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L170
text: [UINT16_ABGR color exports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - export format 7 is accepted only into an unsigned integer target, and each 16-bit value reaches the target unchanged; a value beyond a narrower target's range (`R8_UINT`) is undefined in Vulkan, and whether the console clamps or truncates it is not confirmed. SINT16_ABGR (8) throws

name: libSceAgcDriver.L171
text: [Layered color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - 3D color targets with 64 KiB render-target or 4 KiB standard tiling render several slices, and so does a `CB_COLOR_VIEW` slice range on a 2D array target through the array's resident image, or on a surface of one slice as an array of the view's last slice + 1 slices, one slice pitch apart: a layered draw into an array without its resident image, a layered draw with a depth target, and color targets of different slice counts throw. The vertex layer export (`PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` USE_VTX_RENDER_TARGET_INDX) reaches the shader only for a layered draw and is otherwise ignored, as before; a layer beyond the view's last slice is undefined in Vulkan, while the console's handling (clamping to `SLICE_MAX`) is not modeled, and a view whose last slice lies past the surface is clamped to its last slice. DCC keys of a 3D color target are taken as one key per 256 bytes over the whole surface, every slice included, and only uniform keys (all uncompressed, or one fast-clear code) are interpreted, as for 2D targets; mixed keys leave the stored texels as they are. The console's DCC key layout for 3D surfaces is not checked (LEGO Horizon Adventures' (PPSA14632) lighting volumes are DCC)

name: libSceAgcDriver.L172
text: [VGT_TF_PARAM](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - DISTRIBUTION_MODE is taken as scheduling only; the host tessellator decides the order of a patch's triangles.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L173
text: [Local programs](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) that the hull header leaves at address 0 are prepared at their first draw, one artifact per tessellation configuration, instead of at registration.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L174
text: [Packed 16-bit textures](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/TextureFormat.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `5_6_5`, `1_5_5_5` and `4_4_4_4` are viewed as R5G6B5, A1R5G5B5 and B4G4R4A4 (the 4-bit format every Vulkan device can sample; R4G4B4A4 is optional and lavapipe lacks it) with a swizzle that reads X from the low bits, and a DST_SEL of the missing W of `5_6_5` reads X. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035), not on the console: through `image_load` and `image_sample_lz`, X, Y, Z (and W of `1_5_5_5` and `4_4_4_4`) come from the low, middle and high fields, and W of `5_6_5` returns X (the low 5 bits), not 1.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L175
text: [Min/max S# reduction](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestSamplerResource.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `FILTER_MODE` 1 and 2 use Vulkan's min and max reduction (the same `SQ_IMG_FILTER_MODE` values RADV programs). Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035), not on the console: only texels of non-zero weight are reduced, and the weight is taken after rounding to the 8-bit subtexel grid (a sample within 1/512 texel of a centre reduces that texel alone); a driver with other `subTexelPrecisionBits` reduces a different set there. Gathers ignore the mode.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L176
text: [Min/max S#](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestSamplerResource.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver, shader recompiler) - throws with a linear mip filter, depth or color-texture compare, or bilinear or anisotropic filtering of an image the recompiler point-samples (sint, converted, depth-bits). With anisotropy the host sampler reduces over its own footprint; [RADV](https://github.com/openbsd/xenocara/blob/1b39033df8d928ec247ca64448c4a63c72302db7/lib/mesa/src/amd/vulkan/radv_sampler.c#L185-L232) programs the same S# for such a Vulkan sampler. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1030 in [#5156](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/5156#issuecomment-6155265616), gfx1035 in #5821), not on the console: without derivatives (`image_sample_lz`), min or max with anisotropic bilinear returns the bilinear minimum or maximum and with anisotropic point the point result, at every ratio field 0 to 4; with derivatives (`image_sample_d`, a 4:1 footprint), anisotropic bilinear at ratio field 2 or 4 reduces over the texels of all its anisotropic taps (the minimum or maximum along the major axis), not one bilinear footprint. A host that is not AMD reduces over its own anisotropic footprint, and Vulkan leaves nearest filtering with anisotropy to the host driver.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L177
text: [FORCE_DEGAMMA](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Sampler.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - an S# that forces sRGB decoding adds nothing to an sRGB texture, as in shadPS4 (PS4). Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035), not on the console: `8`, `8_8` and `8_8_8_8` sRGB textures sample bit for bit the same with and without the bit (point and bilinear; BC formats not measured). Other textures throw; on the same hardware their UNORM `8`, `8_8` and `8_8_8_8` forms sample bit for bit as the sRGB format (decoded before filtering).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L179
text: [VertexBufferReadSize](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/include/VertexInput.hpp) and the [vertex staging copy](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a vertex fetch whose index is at or past the descriptor's `num_records` no longer throws for `OOB_SELECT` 0 and 1. The copy still spans the whole fetch, but the bytes from `num_records * stride` onward read as zeros, so the out-of-range vertex is `(0, 0, 0, 0)`. Measured with `buffer_load_format_xyzw` (`idxen`) through the [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) on RDNA2 gfx1036 for PPSA01325's word 3 `0x0004dfac` (`OOB_SELECT` 0) in #2241: indices 3, 4 and 5 over 3 records each return `00000000 00000000 00000000 00000000`, W included, unlike Vulkan `robustBufferAccess`, which returns `(0, 0, 0, 1)`. The zeros come from the record check, not from memory: stored values placed past the records are ignored, and a `num_records` 6 control returns them. `RESOURCE_LEVEL` 1, `OOB_SELECT` 1 and FORMAT 74 `32_32_32_FLOAT` give the same zeros, in wave32 and wave64; gfx1013 (the console) is not measured. `OOB_SELECT` 2 returns the stored values past the records and `OOB_SELECT` 3 compares `num_records` against the byte offset, both measured on the same setup in #2241; the two keep throwing past `num_records` here, since each needs its own rule. Zero-stride descriptors (`stride` 0) keep their separate byte-count check and are not covered here. Each out-of-range fetch is copied alone and outside the draw-snapshot cache, which is neither read nor written for it: a reused snapshot would carry another draw's bytes into the zero region, and a stored zero-padded copy would hand zeros to a later in-range draw at the same address. The valid prefix is still flushed for GPU writes before it is read.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L18
text: [Native depth allocation retirement](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) covers sampling-eligible multisampled owners only. Successful release notifications must cumulatively cover both complete depth and HTILE ranges; protection changes, failed releases and partial coverage keep the original guards. Retired owners leave lookup and metadata routing, while held views and recorded work retain their images. Retirement of single-sample or sampling-ineligible depth attachments and console equivalence remain unimplemented or unmeasured. The regression uses real allocation-registry operations with a no-op host-release callback, so it does not validate the host unmap backend.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L180
text: [Draw snapshot buffer descriptors](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) rewrite each affected array from element zero, preserving unchanged descriptors. MoltenVK 1.4.2 writes auxiliary buffer lengths at index `i` instead of `start + i` for partial array updates ([MVKDescriptorSet.mm, BufferAuxSize](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/blob/v1.4.2/MoltenVK/MoltenVK/GPUObjects/MVKDescriptorSet.mm#L1051)). Per-element writes therefore let one buffer length replace another even when Vulkan buffer handles and ranges are correct.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L181
text: The [driver](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) binds at most 262144 table images per pipeline, fewer under lower sampled-image limits; the rest fault when selected. A device without runtime descriptor arrays or variable-count bindings throws.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L182
text: [Image storage tables](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - every bound element of a storage table is marked written and stored back after each dispatch, whether or not a lane wrote it. Two elements over the same bytes are therefore both stored back, and the order of their write-backs decides the result: PPSA26344's compute 0x80001e5f00 binds the stencil plane at 0x505f350000 twice, as R8_UINT in its own tile mode and as R8_UNORM in another. Rejecting the second writer of the same bytes per element, and per-element written bits from the GPU, are not implemented. The storage table binding is declared with its full capacity, so a set that holds one does not fit a chain descriptor pool and gets a dedicated pool. That capacity is a choice, not a device limit: the smallest of the sampled table capacity, 4096 and a quarter of `maxPerStageDescriptorStorageImages`. The sampled table capacity is not reduced by it, so a device with tight storage-image limits can fail layout validation. A storage element is rejected when its absolute index in the set reaches that capacity, even when few of the set's table elements are storage: the index counts every table element before it in the set, sampled ones included, and the element faults when a lane selects it. Atomic, packed, BY2/BY4 and dynamic-mip stores through a table still fault on use. `PresyncSurfaces` walks only the sampled table, so a store-only table's images are not presynced. Tables that mix sampled and storage elements, a T# that is both read and written through a table, non-uniform storage indexing and non-2D storage modes are not covered by tests.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L183
text: [Image-table S#s](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) reading opaque black borders fault on selection: no runtime BC-swizzle pair check, even for valid swizzles 0/4 with direct or table T#s. Unselected entries do not fault. Table T#/direct S# keeps the direct check: only opaque-black swizzles moving alpha fault.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L184
text: An [image-table T#/S# pair](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) with anisotropic `ANISO_OVERRIDE` faults on selection: dynamic mip-level pairing is unimplemented, including otherwise-valid single-level and mipmapped tables. Direct pairs keep their override behavior. Unselected entries, anisotropy without the override and the override without anisotropy stay supported.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L185
text: [Table S#s](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) that clamp to border fault only when selected: four variants cannot encode dynamic integer/float pairing. This also rejects otherwise-valid float pairs.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L186
text: [Table T#s](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) paired with direct S#s fault when a paired border class differs from the decoded image class. Depth-bit views use float borders. Matching float pairs and inactive mismatches do not fault.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L187
text: [Table S#](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) DISABLE_CUBE_WRAP faults on selection without `VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map`: no runtime dimension check, including valid non-cube direct/table T#s. Unselected entries do not fault; with the feature this bit alone is accepted. Table T#/direct S# faults only for cubes needing the missing feature.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L188
text: An [image table](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) whose record range overlaps a buffer or storage image written by its own dispatch faults (`table written by its dispatch`) when any entry is selected, even if the write misses the selected record. A selected column's range is its record and the bytes of the record before the descriptor.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L189
text: An [image table](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) T# whose surface has no mapped byte faults when selected instead of becoming a zero texture as a direct T# does; what the console returns for it is not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L19
text: [Native MSAA depth attachment feedback](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) is not implemented. A draw sampling a native multisampled depth view while attaching its source image throws before pipeline creation or render-pass recording, including read-only attachment feedback. Sampling that image in a separate draw or dispatch remains supported. The refusal compares the held native image views and their device and attachment identity; single-sample depth behavior is retained.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L190
text: [User-data callees](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a compute shader's `s_swappc_b64` whose source pair is a user-data pair, or a copy of one made with `s_mov_b32` or `s_mov_b64` in the same block, calls the code at the address that user data holds. At dispatch the callee is read from guest memory up to its `s_setpc_b64` on the link pair, one copy of it is appended per call after the caller's last instruction, and the call is rewritten to `s_call_b64` to that copy. The words after the caller's last instruction are dropped from the recompiled code; in the shaders seen they are metadata or constants the caller reads relative to its program counter, and those reads go to the captured guest code, which linking does not change. A caller that jumps through a table among those words, which the control flow analysis reads from the recompiled code, throws. A copy runs at another program counter than the callee, so a callee that reads its program counter, makes a call, ends the program, jumps through another pair, returns before code it branches to, spans more than 64 KiB or is not readable throws. Callees are read again whenever a dispatch misses the dispatch cache; a dispatch that hits it reuses the linked program, so a title that rewrote a callee in place at the same address would keep running the old code.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L191
text: [Table callees](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a compute shader's `s_swappc_b64` whose source pair is two consecutive dwords of an `s_buffer_load_dword*`, or a copy of them made with `s_mov_b32` or `s_mov_b64` in the same block (a conditional branch forward past the call between them is crossed), calls one of the targets that buffer holds when the load's buffer descriptor comes from an `s_load_dwordx4` without SOFFSET from a user-data pointer, or from a pointer pair that two `s_mov_b32` of a literal or inline constant set, and the load's SOFFSET from an `s_lshl_b32` by 2 to 24 bits. The descriptor load may be in an earlier block, such as before a per-lane loop around the call, when it is the only write of the descriptor registers that reaches the buffer load on every path back from it, and no `s_call_b64` or statically resolved call lies on those paths; the paths may run through any `s_swappc_b64` that is not resolved statically, the table call itself included, whose callee is assumed to keep the descriptor registers. The chain compares the target each iteration actually loads, so a callee that changes them can only make a later target miss the chain and fault as an unlinked call. Paths follow fall-through, direct branches and the `s_setpc_b64` jumps whose target the control flow analysis resolves. A path that reaches, before a write of the descriptor registers, the program's first instruction, the entry of an in-program function (an `s_call_b64` target, whose callers are not followed), or an instruction that nothing modelled jumps or falls into fails the search. At dispatch the descriptor and the buffer are read from guest memory, and every non-zero 64-bit value at the loaded offset plus a multiple of the shift's stride, below the descriptor's size (stride times num_records, or num_records bytes with stride 0), is read as a user-data callee and appended once per call. The call becomes a branch to a chain that compares the source pair with each target (`s_cmp_lg_u32` with a literal and `s_cbranch_scc1` per dword) and `s_call_b64`s the copy that matches; no match runs the original `s_swappc_b64` as an unlinked call. There is one chain for each value SCC has at the call, and the chain sets SCC back to that value (`s_cmp_eq_u32 0, 0` or `s_cmp_lg_u32 0, 0`) before the callee or the unlinked call runs. The searched range is the descriptor's whole size, which covers the range the load can reach whether it is checked in bytes or in strides; which one the PS5 uses for `s_buffer_load` was not measured. More than 64 distinct targets, a buffer above 64 MiB or a copy out of `s_call_b64` range throws. As with user-data callees, the buffer is read again only when a dispatch misses the dispatch cache, so a target a title adds to the buffer later is an unlinked call when a cached program runs.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L192
text: [AGC FS table](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Lifecycle.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the driver maps 2 MiB at 0xF_E0000000 when it is created and fills the table that libSceAgc keeps at 0xF_E0040000 (six 16-byte V# slots, slot 0 describing eight 16-byte records) the way PS5 12.00 libSceAgcDriver and libSceAgc do, but every record points at one AnyPS5 routine that only returns (`s_setpc_b64` on the link pair). Sony's routines, which order work before a title's `ds_ordered_count`, are not modeled, and the other five slots stay zero.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L193
text: [DB_RENDER_CONTROL resummarize draws](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - HTILE is not modeled, so a RESUMMARIZE_ENABLE draw without depth or stencil tests and without color writes changes no modeled state and draws nothing. A pure resummarize with pass-through D16/D32 depth, no depth writes or bounds test, no stencil plane, no color writes and no running pixel stage also draws nothing; other resummarize, copy or decompress draws throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L194
text: [Comparison-sampled R32 float and R16 unorm textures](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) whose surface a storage image holds are sampled from a D32_SFLOAT or D16_UNORM image that the GPU refills from the storage image whenever its version moves, because Vulkan compares only depth formats. Only surfaces of at least 1 MiB (`APS5_DEPTH_COPY_MIN_KIB`) that are not 3D take the copy; smaller ones stay CPU snapshots compared against guest memory. With copies of small surfaces, one title hit an intermittent boot-time crash that was not explained.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L195
text: [Null vertex buffer V#](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/include/VertexInput.hpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a V# whose four dwords are all zero is bound to a zeroed vertex buffer of the attribute's size with stride 0, so every component of its attribute reads 0. This follows the V# fields in the [AMD RDNA2 ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) (`NUM_RECORDS` 0, `DST_SEL` 0 selects 0), not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L196
text: [Descriptor pool recycling](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) avoids individually freed sets: [RADV 26.2.2](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-26.2.2/src/amd/vulkan/radv_descriptor_pool.c) initializes its free-set heap with 32 bytes beyond the backing allocation. An allocation-only RX 6600 test reproduces acceptance of a 4,128-byte set in a 4,096-byte pool; the path without individual frees rejects it. Pools reset after their last set is released. A cached set can retain unused slots in an exhausted pool until eviction; peak gameplay pool memory remains unmeasured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L197
text: [16-bit depth with stencil](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) is stored as `D24_UNORM_S8_UINT`, or `D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT`, on a device without `D16_UNORM_S8_UINT` as an attachment. Depth comparisons, clears and the depth image see the wider format's precision, so results at the 16-bit quantization boundary can differ from the console; the constant depth bias is scaled by 256 for D24, and a non-zero constant on the D32 float fallback throws. Not measured on console hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L198
text: [Depth surfaces created over storage writes](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a depth surface created without HTILE copies its depth plane from the storage image at the plane's address, a pending one first, when that image has the plane's extent, one level, a 2D view or a 2D array view (its layer 0 is copied) and a 16-bit format for a 16-bit plane or a 32-bit format for a 32-bit plane. A multisampled surface, a surface the device stores in another format, a surface with HTILE and a surface without such an image start from `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR`, and the stencil plane from `DB_STENCIL_CLEAR`; CPU writes to the plane's memory are not read. Not measured on the console, where the plane is that memory.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L20
text: [Native multisampled depth sampling](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) accepts numeric D16 or D32, two/four/eight samples, one Z_X slice and mip, and pipe-aligned HTILE without stencil or VRS, with ITERATE_256 on or off: the initial import reads no compressed Z planes, and Mesa's HTILE clear words (`radv_get_htile_fast_clear_value`) and Addrlib's HTILE footprint do not depend on ITERATE_256, which `ac_descriptors.c` ties to TC reads of compressed MSAA HTILE. Sampling eligibility is recorded before the attachment's first host clear: every HTILE word must prove the same initial clear of zero or one, and the complete sample-aware depth and HTILE ranges must be accessible and write-watched. Unsupported initial state or device sampling support retains attachment rendering but sampling throws; eligibility is never retried. Sampling rejects later guest writes, queued external GPU writes, and unproven HTILE clear/fill transitions. Guest publication, arbitrary guest depth import, stencil/raw-bit sampling, arrays and storage access remain unimplemented. The block footprint follows main's AMD Addrlib thin-block rule; the accepted HTILE clear words and PS5 equivalence are not measured on console hardware. PPSA99902's historical resident eight-sample D32 reader is documented in [#419](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/419#issuecomment-6105597729).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L200
text: [Host import windows and budget](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestBufferMemory.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a registered range larger than 64 MiB is imported one 64 MiB window at a time for buffer and fill accesses; an access across window edges imports the cells it touches, grown to the union of the range's imports it overlaps. An address-based build (`AcquireRegistered`) imports the range whole and replaces its windows. Live imports stay under a budget: `APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB`, else the larger of 6 GiB and half the physical memory, at most the largest host heap less the larger of 2 GiB and half that heap (imports, type-3 mirrors and buffers and textures placed in host memory share it; on a 16 GiB machine whose host heap is half the memory, a 2 GiB reserve left too little for the rest). Where the device enables `VK_EXT_memory_budget`, that host heap's reported budget less its other usage and an eighth, in 64 MiB steps, read at most once a second, also bounds the default budget once an import's `vkAllocateMemory` has failed; a set `APS5_HOST_IMPORT_MIB` is never lowered by the report. The report's other usage includes the host-visible copies and heap mirrors that stand in for refused imports, so it grows with the refusals; the first time the report would lower the budget, `[gpu] host import budget: host heap ...` prints the heap's reported budget and usage and the live imports. An import's `vkAllocateMemory` failure within an eighth of the budget, or the third in a row, lowers the budget to the live imports until the device or the configured budget changes; an isolated failure further below only marks its range failed. Live imports are not capped by `maxMemoryAllocationCount`: NVIDIA's Windows driver reports 4096, while Village held 27,167 live imports without a failure. A new import beyond it retires the least recently used imports not used in the last 256 lookups; one that would not fit even then is refused before anything is retired, and imports made when a range is mapped never evict. A heap mirror, sparse or not, whose range has left the write watch is refreshed in full at each use, every block counted as written; a build plans its range again only once the import path takes the range. A request that may not evict (an address-based build, an import when a range is mapped) remembers a refused range or block, with the live bytes and the budget at the refusal, and is answered from that memory, still counted as refused, until live imports drop below those bytes, the budget changes or one of its ranges changes. A request that may evict remembers its refusal too, answering later requests for the same run from memory with the room the refusal left (a request whose range fits in that room steps down to a smaller block without scanning the imports again, and a refusal that stepped down is remembered for each block it tried), while no import was made or retired, the budget has not grown, the import window and the run are unchanged, and no import can have become evictable since: the use count stays below the first use at which an import that was neither evictable nor held could leave the 256-lookup protection, and either the build floor has not risen or no held import could leave it yet. A join remembers its refusal the same way, apart from other requests for the same run, so a buffer bound across refused ranges does not try the join again at every upload. The shutdown line `[gpu] host imports at shutdown` gives the live, made, refused (and remembered) and failed counts per requester. The 64 MiB window, the 256-lookup protection, the 2 GiB reserve, the eighth, the 64 MiB steps and the three failures are choices, not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L201
text: [Periodic pipeline cache saves skip busy intervals](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/PipelineCache.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the saver thread snapshots the Vulkan pipeline cache only when no pipeline creation holds it (`TryLockForSnapshot`); otherwise it skips that 10 s interval. A blocking snapshot queued behind a long creation (an NVIDIA compile of a 1.5M-word compute pipeline runs for minutes) makes the writer-preferring `shared_mutex` hold every later pipeline creation on every queue until that compile ends, which froze Yōtei's (PPSA26344) loading at frame 797-799 for the whole compile. While creations overlap without a gap, no periodic save happens, so a crash in that stretch loses the pipelines built since the last save; `SaveNow` and the teardown save still wait for the lock. How often busy stretches skip saves in practice is not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L202
text: [Registration preparation at submit](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `Driver::Submit` waits for every registration-time shader preparation queued before the call, not only those of the shaders the commands use, so a submission behind a long queue of unrelated preparations waits for all of them on the submitting thread. Waiting there instead of in the queue worker keeps the GPU side of a submission short: a title that sees a submission take seconds treats the GPU as hung (Goat Simulator 3, PPSA04159, then stops submitting and its garbage collector fails a 10 s timeout). On the console shaders are compiled ahead of time, so neither wait exists; how long a title tolerates a slow submit call is not known.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L203
text: [Resource cache entries holding released textures](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a sampled texture the texture cache drops while something else holds it, or makes without caching (`admitTexture` refusing a first use), is marked released, and `ResourceCache::Insert` refuses descriptor sets that hold one and removes the entries that do. The removal waits for the next insert: until then `Find` still returns those entries and their textures stay alive. One process-wide flag starts the sweep, so while the sampled cache is over its budget every insert scans all entries (1,024 at start, up to 16,384 after growth, or `APS5_RESOURCE_CACHE_ENTRIES`, each with its textures); that cost is not measured. When `ReleaseTextureCaches` runs on device memory exhaustion, the sampled textures these entries hold are only marked released and are freed at the next insert, so the immediate allocation retry gets no memory back from them. A draw or dispatch whose textures the cache refused builds its descriptor sets again on each use for as long as the cache stays full; the count bounds (`APS5_RESOURCE_CACHE_ENTRIES`, `APS5_RESOURCE_CACHE_TABLE_ELEMENTS`) still bound nothing by bytes, and sampled textures made outside the texture cache (the disabled cache, depth-surface copies) are never marked. Measured on one title on one RTX 4090: with the default bounds, sampled textures held outside the cache peaked at 2,836 MiB (7,830 MiB before) and device-local heap 0 stayed under its 22.9 GB budget for the whole run (26,357 MiB before, which aborted with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` at the wolf scene). Whether the extra descriptor-set builds cost frame time elsewhere is not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L205
text: [Sampled MSAA surface geometry](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/TextureTiling.cpp) supplies the fragment-aware linear size and one mip for a tiled 2D surface at two, four or eight fragments. Unsupported arrays, mip chains, extents and block sizes throw. Linear descriptors retain the existing geometry path, including its use when sampling an existing native target; a linear MSAA guest layout is not modeled. The range calculation follows AMD Addrlib's thin-block dimensions. Console layout equivalence and title effects of the additional mip metadata remain unmeasured. This does not add sample upload or readback.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L206
text: [Unclamped normalized color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - CB_COLOR_INFO targets with BLEND_CLAMP clear (bit 15) on UNORM and SNORM formats are accepted when blending is disabled (ENABLE clear or BLEND_BYPASS set). Vulkan converts unblended shader values and clamps to the normalized range automatically; blending into an unclamped normalized target remains unmodeled because Vulkan always clamps inputs prior to blending.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L208
text: [Multisample image readback](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleReadback.cpp) fetches unsigned R8/R16/R32/R32G32/R32G32B32A32 or D32 depth samples through a 2D array view in GENERAL, in layer/y/x/fragment order. The caller owns producer completion, image transitions and resource lifetimes. It implements Vulkan per-sample fetches, not guest-memory publication, metadata expansion or PS5 layout equivalence; D32 exceptional-value preservation has not been measured. Other formats, sample counts and invalid ranges throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L210
text: [Thick SW_4KB_S_X volumes](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/TextureTiling.cpp) use AMD addrlib's GFX10 non-RB+ 16-pipe `GFX10_SW_4K_S3_X_PATINFO` equations for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16-byte elements, including packed mip tails. The layout follows [AMD PAL c5e80007](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp); it has not been measured on console hardware. Other thick swizzle modes outside the supported families still throw. Mipmapped 3D color targets remain refused by the color-register decoder.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L211
text: [Viewport depth range remap](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - on a device without `VK_EXT_depth_range_unrestricted` a viewport depth range outside [0, 1] (Minecraft PPSA17221 draws its world with `PA_CL_VPORT_ZSCALE` 1, `ZOFFSET` 0 in negative-one-to-one clip space) is folded into the vertex shader: `RemapPositionDepth` scales clip z so z/w is the console's depth, the pipeline's depth clamp applies the console's `PA_SC_VPORT_ZMIN/ZMAX` clipped to [0, 1] (exact for a normalized depth target or none; Minecraft clamps its float depth target to [-1, 1], so a depth below 0 is stored as 0 there, which only a later test or read at exactly 0 can tell, and the first such draw is reported once), and two extra `gl_ClipDistance` elements restore the near and far planes depth clamping removes. The mode is a pipeline specialization constant (`PipelineSpecialization::DepthRemapBase`); scale and offset are read from the draw's push block (two words at byte 104, `DepthRemapPushOffsetBytes`, so a remapped draw's stage push data ends before it), so draws that differ only in them share one vertex module and one pipeline. The remap serves the vertex path only; mesh and tessellation draws with such a range still throw. Whether the console clamps before or after its depth bias and how it treats a clamp range narrower than the transform's are not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L212
text: [Benchmark rewrite failure test off Windows](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/PerformanceTrace.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `ReplaceGzipFile` checks that a write failing at `<name>.tmp` keeps the previous `aps5-bench.json.gz` only on non-Windows builds: the `std::ios_base::failure` thrown inside the MinGW ofstream did not unwind to the test's catch, so Windows CI covers only the failed move.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L214
text: [Sampled array windows](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/TextureTiling.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a sampled 2D array, 1D array or cube view whose base array slice is past 0 is built from its viewed slices only (`ViewedArrayWindow`), at the guest address of its base slice. The window is taken only when the surface is thin, has no DCC metadata, and, for a 64 KiB XOR swizzle, when the base slice keeps every slice bit of the swizzle equation at zero (R_X 1-byte elements: a base slice that is a multiple of 16). Any other view still builds slices 0 to its last slice. A window and a whole-array view of the same surface are separate images over overlapping memory, kept coherent by the existing overlap rules, at the cost of the memory and uploads of both. Ghost of Yotei (PPSA26344) samples a 256x256 cube array at slices 4299..7232, built at 1467 MiB instead of about 3.8 GB.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L215
text: [2D reads of 2D arrays](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a sampled image whose shader shape is 2D and whose T# is a 2D array is built from its base slice alone: the T# is narrowed to that slice (`FirstLayerDescriptor`) before its decode, cache key and image, in stage A records, stage B bindings, revalidation and image tables. A whole-array read of the same T# keeps its own cache entry, so both images exist when a title uses both. Storage images read or written through a 2D shape are not narrowed and still build every slice the T# names. Ghost of Yotei (PPSA26344) reads a 3328x1872 R_X T# of 1537 slices this way: the whole array was a 12.4 GiB image that did not fit the device-local budget of an RTX 4090.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L216
text: [Sampled and storage views of 1 GiB or more](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) that stay whole are only logged (sampled views by `cachedTexture`, storage views by `cachedStorageTexture`), with the registered guest range holding their base and how many of their slices fit in it; nothing is capped to that range. Ghost of Yotei (PPSA26344) samples a 1467 MiB cube array window of which only 838 of 2934 slices lie inside its 3380 MiB range: the rest is read from whatever follows the range. Whether such slices are ever sampled is not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L217
text: [Color export type against the target format](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the export-format check refuses a `UINT16_ABGR` export (`SPI_SHADER_COL_FORMAT` 7) into a target whose color-buffer number format is not unsigned integer, but not the reverse. A 32-bit export (`32_R`, `32_GR`, `32_AR` or `32_ABGR`) into an unsigned-integer target leaves `uintExport` clear, so the recompiler declares the fragment output `float4`; `DecodeColorBuffer` maps a number format of 4 to `R32_UINT` from the color buffer alone, independent of the export format, so the float output reaches an integer attachment. Desktop drivers keep the raw bits, but the Khronos validation layer reports `Undefined-Value-ShaderFragmentOutputMismatch` and MoltenVK's Metal compiler refuses the pipeline. Which export format a title pairs with a 32-bit integer target is not measured, so the output type is left following the export format rather than the attachment.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L219
text: [Long Windows pipeline-cache paths](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/PipelineCache.cpp): `readHeader` and the failed-read existence check still use ordinary paths. A filename beyond MAX_PATH can prevent header reuse or be reported missing; the shared content reader and journal normalization do not cover these calls.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L22
text: [Indices far past every vertex fetch](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - when a draw's highest index is at least 64Ki vertices past the largest per-vertex record count, every index past that count is moved to it in a copy of the indices, so the zero-padded vertex copies are not sized to the original index (PPSA04159 draws a list of `0xffffffff` with primitive restart off, which asked for 160 GiB). Each attribute fetched by vertex index reads zeros there as at the original index (out-of-bounds select 0 or 1); a draw with another out-of-bounds select keeps its indices. The vertex index the shader sees changes for the moved indices, which a shader that reads it directly would notice

name: libSceAgcDriver.L23
text: [Depth clear draws](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - a draw with `DB_RENDER_CONTROL.DEPTH_CLEAR_ENABLE` is taken to write `DB_DEPTH_CLEAR` to every pixel it covers whatever the depth test, depth bounds and depth bias say: it is drawn with an always-passing depth write and the viewport depth range pinned to the clear value. The draw is rasterized as submitted, so its coverage is the draw's own. Whether the DB still applies the depth test or HiZ to such a draw is not measured

name: libSceAgcDriver.L24
text: [GS_FAST_LAUNCH geometry](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - `VGT_SHADER_STAGES_EN.GS_FAST_LAUNCH = 1` with a point list and `GE_CNTL` groups of one vertex and one primitive decodes as one point per subgroup, with the primitive limit taken from `GE_NGG_SUBGRP_CNTL.PRIM_AMP_FACTOR` and the GS/ES VGPR counts not required. Follows how RADV drives mesh shaders on gfx10.3 (`ac_nir_lower_ngg.c`, the workgroup index comes from the vertex id of the first thread), not measured on the console. Fast launch 2, other group sizes or input primitives and indexed fast-launch draws still throw. PPSA03671's fast-launch draws decode, but the title stops earlier in a wave64 vertex program, so they have not reached the GPU yet.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L25
text: [Line-strip geometry output](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - a geometry program with `VGT_GS_OUT_PRIM_TYPE = 1` (line strip) runs as a mesh shader with `OutputLinesEXT`: each primitive export is one line whose two vertex indices are packed like the three of a triangle, as Mesa's NGG lowering exports line strips (`ac_nir_lower_ngg_gs.c`), and each input primitive gets `VGT_GS_MAX_VERT_OUT - 1` lines where a triangle strip gets `- 2` triangles. A subgroup gets at least `GE_MAX_OUTPUT_PER_SUBGROUP` line slots, because Mesa's lowering exports one primitive, possibly null, per emitted vertex; whether the console's compiler does the same is not known, and triangle strips keep `- 2` per input. A fast-launch subgroup takes its line count from `GE_NGG_SUBGRP_CNTL.PRIM_AMP_FACTOR` as for triangles. Line output counts as lines for the polygon offset decode, as on the vertex path. The lines are drawn 1 pixel wide with Vulkan's default line rasterization, like lines on the vertex path: `PA_SU_LINE_CNTL` is not read, and neither its width nor the console's line rules were measured. Points, rectangle lists, per-stream types and line strips from a vertex program on the mesh path still throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L26
text: [Alpha-to-coverage](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - only `DB_ALPHA_TO_MASK = 0xaa01` is accepted: the enable bit with the four quad offsets at 2 and no `OFFSET_ROUND`, the undithered setting [radeonsi](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/bffd91947efc1932da99aca69fc540d6d4201b0c/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state.c#L371-L381) programs. Draws are single-sampled, so the pixel shader [writes](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) `SampleMask` 0 when its MRT0 alpha is below one half or NaN and all ones otherwise, and runs with late fragment tests. That rule was measured on a Radeon 660M (gfx1035, RADV with `RADV_DEBUG=noatocdithering`, which programs the same register) for 0, -0, 0.25, the two floats below one half, one half, the two above, 0.75, 1, 2, -1, both infinities and both NaNs, and is pinned in [AlphaToCoverage.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/AlphaToCoverage.cpp); it is not measured on gfx1013. Vulkan's `alphaToCoverageEnable` is not used: the NVIDIA driver 615.78.08 dithers single-sample coverage (an alpha of 0.25 writes half the pixels of an RTX 3050 Laptop target). Other offsets, `OFFSET_ROUND`, a sample-mask export, and an MRT0 that is missing, swizzled, packed or exported without a floating-point alpha throw. A draw without a color target on MRT0 keeps alpha-to-coverage from its MRT0 export, as [radeonsi exports MRT0 as `32_AR` for alpha-to-coverage without a color buffer](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-24.0.0/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state_shaders.cpp#L2425-L2431). A draw that enables alpha-to-coverage with no MRT0 export still throws: what the console covers then is not measured. Default dithered `DB_ALPHA_TO_MASK = 0x18701` additionally uses a per-quad sample-mask table [measured on gfx1036](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/4451#issuecomment-6124848921) for eight standard samples with FP16_ABGR or 32_ABGR exports; other sample counts, custom locations, EQAA combinations and dithered UNORM16/SNORM16 exports throw. The dithered rule is not measured on gfx1013.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L27
text: [A one-sample target under a multisampled rasterizer without MSAA_ENABLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` > 0 with `PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_0.MSAA_ENABLE` clear, one-sample color targets and no depth target, or a one-sample depth target with no color target or one-sample color targets, is drawn as a one-sample draw at the pixel center. Without the bit every sample is taken to be at the pixel center (see the entry for a multisampled target rasterized without MSAA_ENABLE below), and a one-sample target is taken to keep the coverage of sample 0, so a one-sample depth target is tested and written once per pixel with the depth at the pixel center. That is the rule [`VK_AMD_mixed_attachment_samples`](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/blob/193ebe195f47ffc5004683d1659e71c725658c4d/chapters/fragops.adoc#L2510-L2516) gives a color target with fewer samples than the rasterizer, but Vulkan reaches it only beside a depth or stencil target with the rasterizer's sample count ([VUID-VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo-subpass-01505](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs/blob/193ebe195f47ffc5004683d1659e71c725658c4d/chapters/pipelines.adoc#L3033-L3041)), so here it is an analogy, and for a one-sample depth target an extension of it. [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp#L127-L128) also rasterizes with the largest sample count of the bound depth and color targets ([L416-L417](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp#L416-L417), [L477-L480](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp#L477-L480)), and reads `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG` only for a `SAMPLE_COVERAGE` input ([L174-L177](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp#L174-L177)). This is not measured on hardware. `PS_ITER_SAMPLE`, an `ANCILLARY` or `SAMPLE_COVERAGE` pixel input and a sample-mask export throw in a pixel program that runs, because what the console gives them under a multisampled configuration is not known; a depth-only draw that skips its pixel program is drawn with the null program, and its `PS_ITER_SAMPLE` and pixel input bits are ignored. Points, lines and alpha-to-coverage throw as for a multisampled target. With a one-sample depth target, `DB_EQAA` Z interpolation (`INTERPOLATE_COMP_Z`, `INTERPOLATE_SRC_Z`) or overrasterization (`OVERRASTERIZATION_AMOUNT`, `ENABLE_POSTZ_OVERRASTERIZATION`) also throws. METAL GEAR SOLID: Peace Walker (PPSA18216) draws a one-sample color target under a 4x configuration this way; the first draw of its opening movie binds a one-sample depth target and no color target under the same configuration.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L28
text: [MSAA_ENABLE on a single-sample target](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - `PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_0.MSAA_ENABLE` with `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES = 0` is drawn like the same state without the bit when sample 0 of the four `PA_SC_AA_SAMPLE_LOCS_PIXEL_*_0` registers is at the pixel center and the draw rasterizes filled triangles or rectangles (`VGT_PRIMITIVE_TYPE` 7 or 17 as well as the triangle types) with alpha-to-coverage and conservative rasterization off. [RADV](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/745709a000482a4a24c91faef5c5a40bd653a863/src/amd/vulkan/radv_cmd_buffer.c#L13606-13609) programs this state for one-sample custom sample locations on GFX10 and later, where the bit makes the rasterizer use the programmed location of sample 0 ([061bc615](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/commit/061bc6151a11597f720535f00e79a5752e24aff6)); that the bit changes nothing else for such a draw is inferred from that and is not measured on hardware. EA Sports UFC 5 (PPSA03541) reaches a rect-list draw in this state. Other locations of sample 0, absent location registers, points, lines, alpha-to-coverage and conservative rasterization throw

name: libSceAgcDriver.L29
text: [A multisampled target rasterized without MSAA_ENABLE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - `PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` > 0 with `PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_0.MSAA_ENABLE` clear is drawn with the target's sample count and every sample at the pixel center, as a single-sample scan into a multisampled target already is. On GFX10 and later the bit is what makes the rasterizer use the programmed sample locations ([RADV 061bc615](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/commit/061bc6151a11597f720535f00e79a5752e24aff6)), and with multisampling disabled GL rasterizes at the pixel center and gives the fragment full coverage, which radeonsi programs by clearing the bit; that the hardware does the same with `MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` > 0 is inferred from these and is not measured on hardware. A depth target with the same sample count also has every sample at the pixel center, so each depth and stencil sample is tested and written with the depth at the pixel center, as GL allows when multisampling is disabled ([L185-L190](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L185-L190), [L422-L425](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L422-L425)). GL also lets an implementation test only a centermost sample and set every sample from it ([L425-L434](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Registry/blob/6af574a14089ccfee87efe230ebcdd8742859813/extensions/ARB/ARB_multisample.txt#L425-L434)), which differs when a pixel's stored samples differ; which one the console does, and how its occlusion queries count such a draw, is not measured on hardware. `DB_EQAA` Z interpolation or overrasterization and a sample-mask export with a depth target throw. Points, lines and alpha-to-coverage throw. SONIC SUPERSTARS (PPSA06888) draws such a 2x target, and METAL GEAR SOLID: Peace Walker (PPSA18216) a 4x depth and color pair.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L31
text: [User data registers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Diagnostics.cpp) (AGC driver) - a `SPI_SHADER_USER_DATA_*` or `COMPUTE_USER_DATA_*` register the title never wrote reads as 0 when a stage's RSRC2 count covers it, as Kyty (zeroed `UserSgprInfo`) and SharpEmu (missing registers read 0) do, and as AMD PAL and Mesa initialize them; the console's value is not confirmed

name: libSceAgcDriver.L33
text: [Barycentrics without mesh shaders](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Draw/Draw.cpp) (AGC driver) - a pixel shader that reads barycentrics on the mesh path is emulated only on a device with `VK_EXT_mesh_shader`; a device with neither it nor `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric` (reported on Linux RADV with a GCN 5 GPU) throws that the device has neither the barycentric extension nor mesh shaders, because a geometry stage cannot follow a mesh stage and no other route is implemented. `VK_AMD_shader_explicit_vertex_parameter`, which a GCN 5 device on RADV exposes, is an unexplored option.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L34
text: [NGG vertex programs on the mesh path](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - an unregistered vertex program with `PRIMGEN_EN` that uses LDS or `s_barrier` runs on the geometry (mesh) path. Each input primitive is assumed to yield at most one output primitive, the subgroup is bounded by `GE_MAX_OUTPUT_PER_SUBGROUP` as a vertex budget, and the GS/ES VGPR count checks are skipped, because the merged inputs keep their positions. Taken from the code Mesa's ACO emits for NGG culling and from PPSA59322 and PPSA99010 draws, not measured on hardware. Registered programs keep the vertex path

name: libSceAgcDriver.L35
text: [VGT_SHADER_STAGES_EN 0x02002008](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - this one value, `ES_EN` = 1 without `HS_EN` on a non-patch draw, is drawn as the vertex path. AMD's CIK register reference calls `ES_EN` = 1 `ES_STAGE_DS` (the ES stage runs the tessellation evaluation shader), which does not explain it on a non-patch draw. Seen only on PPSA29413 and not verified on the console; other vertex-path values with `ES_EN` set still throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L36
text: [Strided buffer overhang](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a strided buffer descriptor that ends less than one stride past the end of the readable registered allocation holding its base is bound only up to that allocation's end, even when another readable allocation starts right there. This assumes the bytes past the end are the rounded-up `num_records` of the last record (RADV rounds it up), which no fetch inside the buffer reads; a guest that really keeps a vertex split across two adjacent allocations would read zeros for the cut tail. Taken from the RetroArch Dolphin core case in #2912, not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L37
text: [Buffer descriptor CACHE_SWIZZLE hint](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - bit 30 of word 1 in a buffer resource descriptor (`words[1] & 0x40000000u`) is normalized to zero when binding guest buffers in `ShaderResources::addGuestBuffer`. On GFX10 (gfx1013), bit 30 of V# word 1 is `CACHE_SWIZZLE` (Mesa's `gfx10-rsrc.json`: STRIDE [29:16], CACHE_SWIZZLE [30], SWIZZLE_ENABLE [31]), a cache-bank hint with no effect on the address or data, which is dropped here.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L38
text: [Buffer descriptors past the range limit](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a buffer V# whose size is over `maxStorageBufferRange` is bound only up to the end of the readable registered allocation holding its base when that allocation ends before the limit, and as the empty placeholder buffer, like a null V#, when no registered allocation holds its base; a V# over an allocation that reaches the limit still throws. Titles leave such words in descriptor slots their shaders do not reach on the path taken (PPSA10528 binds `c8010002 2c6bec20 c0053c00 04000013`, about 33 TB from an address above the user address space). What the console returns for an access past the bound range is not known; here the device's robust buffer access decides. Follows the review of #3202, not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L39
text: [Vertex fetch overhang](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a zero-padded vertex fetch whose valid range (`num_records * stride`) ends less than one stride past the end of the readable memory at its base copies only the readable bytes and reads the rest as zeros, instead of failing the draw; a longer overhang still fails. This extends the strided buffer overhang rule above (the last record is the rounded-up `num_records`) to the staging copy and is not measured on hardware. The observed case is a fetch of 14858 records of 44 bytes that ends 8 bytes past the end of the 0xa0000-byte mapping holding it.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L40
text: [Zero-stride vertex fetch range](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/include/VertexInput.hpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - for a stride-0 V# with OOB_SELECT 2 the whole fetch reads memory unless NUM_RECORDS is 0; with OOB_SELECT 3 it reads zero when NUM_RECORDS is 0 and throws when the fetch only partly fits. Rules taken from the GFX10 OOB_SELECT table in Mesa [ac_descriptors.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.c), not measured on hardware. Whether OOB_SELECT 3 checks each dword of a multi-dword fetch separately is unknown. OOB_SELECT 0 and 1 keep the structured record checks.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L43
text: [Shader headers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - registration and ABI resolution read fixed header fields through aligned copies, so the header pointer itself may have any alignment. PPSA26344 passes headers 4 and 1 bytes past an 8-byte boundary, and PPSA01317 passes 4-byte-aligned headers to ABI resolution; console alignment requirements are unknown

name: libSceAgcDriver.L44
text: [Registered shader types](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - types 0, 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 are prepared and type 5 is skipped. Any other type, such as type 8, is logged (`unsupported registered shader type 8; it is not prepared at registration`) and left unprepared at registration, and throws when it is used later. Hello Neighbor 2 (PPSA07426), Ad Infinitum (PPSA10600) and Ghostrunner (PPSA03685) register type 8 headers and run on past them; what a type 8 header describes is unknown, #1892 found no context registers in it.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L45
text: [NGG vertex workgroups](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - type-2 PRIMGEN programs using DS instructions or `s_barrier` are prepared with the draw's routing and primitive registers on the existing mesh path. The workgroup requirement follows [Mesa's NGG lowering](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/b3588f78dd7fd46fbadc7ecd487e5f14d4213e4b/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_ngg.c#L1135); the mesh path supplies LDS and two guest lanes per host invocation for wave64 on a 32-lane host subgroup. Console routing has not been measured. Passthrough and tessellation keep their existing paths; unsupported mesh assembly and subgroup budgets throw.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L46
text: [Shader header copies](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Shaders/ShaderRegistry.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a header bound for a draw or dispatch at another address than the registered one is accepted when its fixed fields match the registered header, and every array it points at still holds the registered bytes; the registered header's metadata is used. `user_data` is not compared (PPSA21567 binds such a copy of a vertex shader header with `user_data` set to null; whether the console reads the copy's `user_data` is unknown). A copy whose registers, context registers, specials or semantics differ, or whose arrays are unreadable, throws `... refers to a replaced shader header`; what the console does with a header a title patches while relocating it is not measured. PPSA01325 (#2914) resolves the ABI with such a copy

name: libSceAgcDriver.L47
text: [HtileFillCovers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a fill is taken to cover a depth surface's whole HTILE when it spans 32 KiB per 1024x512 pixel block from DB_HTILE_DATA_BASE, the pipe-aligned SW_64KB_Z_X metadata extent AMD PAL's gfx10 addrlib gives for GB_ADDR_CONFIG 0x00100044 (1-8 samples, D16/D32); other metadata layouts are not decoded. A partial fill is ignored (the surface keeps its contents); not measured on the console.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L48
text: [Depth fast clear through HTILE](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a surface cleared by an HTILE fill is cleared to DB_DEPTH_CLEAR, also when it is next sampled. For a depth-only HTILE the clear word also carries a value (radv writes `minz = maxz = round(depth * 0x3fff)`, `HTILE_Z_CLEAR_REG` in Mesa's `src/amd/common/ac_descriptors.h`, and allows TC-compatible fast clears only to 0.0 or 1.0); which of the two the texture unit returns for a cleared tile was not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L49
text: [Depth-only and stencil HTILE fill](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - in a whole-HTILE fill, ZMask (bits 0-3) 0 clears the depth and SMem (bits 8-9) 0 clears the stencil, while SMem 3 leaves the stencil alone (`HtileFillClears`); other SMem values are taken to leave it alone too. The bit meanings follow the gfx10 HTILE layout as the code reads it, not a measurement; `agc_driver_depth_fast_clear_submit` pins them for the paths the Driver takes.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L50
text: [Depth and stencil plane fills](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a fill that covers a known depth surface's whole stencil plane (`DepthSliceBytes` of its extent at one byte per texel) with four equal bytes clears the host stencil to that byte the next time the surface is bound, sampled or stored to, and a fill that covers the whole depth plane (two or four bytes per texel) clears the depth when the dword is a float in 0.0-1.0, or two equal 16-bit halves read as UNORM for D16 (`NoteDepthMetadataFill`). A partial fill, a dword whose bytes differ, a depth value outside 0.0-1.0 (0xff000000 is seen), a multisampled surface, or a fill made before the surface exists leave the host image as it was. An HTILE fill or a recognized HTILE clear kernel noted after a plane fill replaces its value with DB_DEPTH_CLEAR/DB_STENCIL_CLEAR. On the console the fill writes the plane the depth block reads; the surfaces this was seen on keep the stencil out of HTILE (PPSA26525 Heretic + Hexen and PPSA21444 DOOM + DOOM II reset the Cohtml UI stencil plane to 1 with a 0x01010101 fill every frame, then draw with stencil Equal 1 and 2), and what the console returns for a plane fill under a compressed HTILE was not measured. `agc_driver_depth_plane_fill` pins the rules.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L51
text: [HTILE address of a depth array slice](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `decodeDepth` adds the `DB_DEPTH_VIEW` slice offset to the Z and stencil addresses but not to `htileAddress`, so every slice of a layered depth target shares slice 0's HTILE address and a fill of slice 0's HTILE marks all slices cleared. Astro's Playroom fills the HTILE of each of its three shadow cascades 0x40000 apart (0x24000 bytes of tiles each) back to back before drawing, so the result is still right there; a title that clears one slice between draws to another would lose depth. The per-slice HTILE stride is not derived yet.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L53
text: [Vertex input and color target overlap](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (AGC driver) - direct draws exclude the descriptor prefix skipped by `firstVertex` or `firstInstance` from the alias check; indexed draws conservatively use index zero as the lower bound before adding `firstVertex`. Indirect draws still check the full descriptor extent. Reads of the active target's bytes remain unsupported; same-draw console ordering is not established.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L57
text: [Workgroup count split](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - a direct dispatch over `maxComputeWorkGroupCount` runs as `vkCmdDispatch` chunks, each bound to a pipeline variant whose workgroup offset specialization constants add the chunk's base to `WorkgroupId` and `GlobalInvocationId`. A variant is built when its chunk base is first recorded, not when the dispatch is prepared. A split of a shader with device-memory LDS throws: its slot base reads the chunk's `NumWorkgroups`, not the dispatch's. Chunks are ordered by a compute barrier, which the console does not have between workgroups of one dispatch.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L58
text: [Scan-resistant sampled texture admission](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - while the sampled texture cache is over its budget but within a quarter over it, the first use of a texture it does not hold in a present is refused (used for its draw, then released, never cached) when its least recently used entry was used in the current or previous present, and a later use in the same present is refused when that entry was used in the current present. So a working set larger than the budget keeps a stable subset: a texture used more than once in a present still evicts an entry not yet used in that present, so a working set with interleaved multi-use textures rotates as on main, and the textures that arrive after the cache fills are created again at each use for as long as the least recently used entry is from the current present, including in the transition present after a scene change. Past a quarter over the budget the entries are evicted as before, so after the budget falls the cache can sit at up to 125% of the reduced budget until entries stop being used. Entries unused for two presents are evicted as before. A later use can evict an entry from the previous present and then be refused when the next least recently used entry is from the current present, so that entry is created again in the next present. The "current or previous present" window is an unmeasured threshold: it was chosen, not derived. Measured once, as one A-B-A series on one title (loading phase about 33000 textures per frame against a 5.4 GiB budget) on one RTX 4090, 3600 s each: 932 / 968 / 941 frames, evictions after frame 620 2.72M -> 1.17M, texture creations unchanged (about 5.8M). Nothing is measured on other titles or GPUs, and a title whose per-present working set only slightly exceeds the budget now re-creates the excess textures at every use.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L59
text: [Texture cache budgets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - the storage image cache's budget is what the reported heap budget leaves after the heap's use other than the cached storage images (at least the sampled textures alive) and an eighth of the budget, capped at a quarter of the budget and at `TextureCacheBudget` (a quarter of the heap's size, at least 2 GiB), never below 512 MiB; the sampled cache's budget reserves `TextureCacheBudget` for the storage cache and never falls below 2 GiB. The storage budget keeps no room for the part of that 2 GiB floor the sampled textures alive do not use: it gives room back as they grow, at its next read. As the heap's other use grows the sampled budget reaches its floor first, then the storage budget falls. Each cache trims only at its next insert, a storage image is allocated before its insert reads the budget, and both budgets read the heap at most once a second, so a burst between two reads, sampled textures included, can still exceed the reported budget. The eighth is the sampled formula's value reused and the 512 MiB floor and the caps the earlier ones; none was measured beyond PPSA11386 on one 10 GB GPU and PPSA16064 on one 8 GB GPU, and a title whose storage working set exceeds the shrunk budget re-creates storage images at each use.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L60
text: [Polygon primitive type](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (AGC driver) - `VGT_PRIMITIVE_TYPE` 21 (`PrimitiveType::Polygon`) decodes to `VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_FAN` and is treated as inactive for vertex point size, like triangle fans and strips. PPSA01317 (Gran Turismo 7) submits polygon draws; whether the console performs polygon-mode decomposition or custom vertex routing is unverified.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L61
text: [Native multisampled DCC fast clears](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) import uniform 0000/0001/1110/1111 keys into a single-layer, level-zero SW_64KB_R_X color image with 2, 4 or 8 fragments. Color and DCC/CMASK ranges must stay write-watched and unchanged; expanded or mixed initial DCC, register CMASK clears, compressed payloads, color transforms, lossy modes, other metadata changes, guest publication and writes over a live owner throw. A whole-range DCC fill with one of those keys, landed or still recorded, is taken as its fast clear; a partial fill, or a CMASK changed without a whole fill, throws. Driver-mediated reads of the color and metadata stay guarded. The metadata extent follows [AMD Addrlib](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp#L347-L454) with the [PS5 Mesa model](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/0b2d6d1a61d9bbf89cf8beb88a696144f67c61f8/src/amd/vulkan/winsys/ps5/radv_ps5_winsys.c): GFX10.1, 16 pipes, 256-byte interleave, two maximum compressed fragments. Console geometry, concurrent guest mutation and transitions outside this subset are unverified.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L64
text: [Type-0 and type-1 texture descriptors](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestTextureResource.cpp) (`TYPE` = 0 or 1 in dword 3) with a nonzero base are bound as null images, like a zero base. TYPE 0 comes from a gfx1036 (RDNA2) measurement in issue #4139 (image sample, load and resinfo return zero, no fault). TYPE 1 comes from a gfx1010 (RDNA1) measurement in #4139 and #5828 (`image_sample_lz`, `image_sample_b`, `image_load` and `image_get_resinfo` return zero, no fault) with format 22 only; TYPE 1 is not measured on RDNA2, with other formats or with depth-compare reads (`image_sample_c*`). Neither type was measured on the console's gfx1013.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L65
text: [Multisampled color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/MultisampleTarget.cpp) lose their guest-read guards and cannot be reused after a successful allocation removal or unmap covers their full guarded range. The next target, sampled or storage lookup removes retired cache owners; recorded work and sampled views keep their images alive until their last reference is released. Partial unmaps keep the guard; partial allocation reuse and guest access to live multisampled data remain unsupported.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L66
text: [Stencil reference export replay](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) on devices without `VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export` replays the low eight bits of the values proved from constant, select and phi exports, with an export proved on every kept path. An export the prover cannot bound replays all 256 eight-bit values, one pass per value per triangle (logged once per process). It records instances, then their triangles, then the reference classes of each triangle. One pipeline filters fragments at shader termination against a dynamic push value before late stencil and depth tests. The [Vulkan stencil-reference replacement rule](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/FragStencilRefEXT.html) discards bits above the attachment's stencil width; supported stencil attachments have eight bits. Numeric subgroup observations throw except bounded own-lane mask plumbing and group control with kept-lane and derivative-helper coverage proved. WQM inputs must exclude helper contributions, since [non-quad subgroup operations may treat helpers as inactive](https://docs.vulkan.org/glslext/latest/glslext/khr/GL_KHR_shader_subgroup.html). Readonly guarded SRT reads may report internal host faults; these draws wait and check faults before publishing results, and loops throw. Indirect draws, restart, strips, fans, tessellation, mesh, multisampling, early tests, ordered pixel execution, guest shader memory writes, other fault-producing memory access, clocks, primitive ID inputs, attachment feedback and pipeline face/channel splits throw. An exhausted stage push range throws. Equivalence to console ordering has not been measured on console hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L68
text: [32-bit depth-bits reads of guest memory](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a sampled 32_UINT or 32_SINT T# with a depth swizzle mode that no live depth surface matches reads the guest bytes through an R32_SFLOAT image, as the recompiler's depth-bits read expects, and the shader casts the fetched value back to the stored dword. On RX 6700 XT (gfx1031, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002) the read keeps float denormals, the sign bit alone and quiet and signaling NaN payloads bit for bit. A host that canonicalizes NaNs or flushes denormals on a 32-bit float fetch would change those dwords, and other drivers are not measured.
