A live depth surface whose extent or base level differs from the T# is not used; the read takes the guest bytes, as the 32-bit float and 16-bit views already do.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L69
text: [Reused depth storage](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp): a storage view with another extent or a format that cannot hold the cached depth plane uses guest memory. Depth rendering is not written back to those guest bytes; this admission rule does not prove allocation reuse or preserve a depth writer through an incompatible view. A 2D storage view, or a one-layer 2D array view of layer 0, of level 0 with the plane's extent and format (32-bit float or the 32-bit depth-bits layout for the depth plane, 16-bit unorm for D16, 8-bit uint for the stencil plane) is a storage image that is [filled](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) from the depth image before every use and, when the shader writes it, copied back after the work: a whole-plane copy through a staging buffer each way. A dispatch of the 15-word 8x8x1 image clear kernel ([`MatchStorageImageClear`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp): one colour read from the V# in `user[8..11]` stored to every texel of the T# in `user[0..7]`) that covers the whole plane and stores 0 or 1 through a 16-bit unorm view, 0 or 0xffff through a 16-bit uint view, or 0 or a normal float in (0, 1] through a 32-bit float or integer view leaves out the copy-in and replaces the copy-out by a clear of the depth image to that value; the dispatch still writes the storage image. The colour is read again when the copy-out is replaced, and a changed value keeps the copy-out. Indirect dispatches, partial last groups, dispatches that queue on the draw pipeline, other values and formats, a plane the kernel covers only partly and stencil planes keep both copies. A written view is also left pending like any other storage image, so the plane's content, drawn depth included, reaches guest memory on the next flush of that range. A 2D array view of more than one slice of the depth plane, or of a later slice, is a storage image over the slices from 0 to its last (`LayeredDepthStorage`); only the slices from its base slice to its last are copied: a slice that has a depth surface at the plane's address plus a whole depth slice per layer (`DepthSliceBytes`, as for the depth plane copies below) is copied from that surface before every use and back to it after the work, every bound slice each time, through a staging buffer; the other slices hold guest memory like any storage image. These images are kept per address, extent, slice count, base slice, format and tile mode until the device goes away, outside the storage cache's budget. Such a view needs a layer pitch equal to that slice size, and another view of the same memory (the 2D view of its first slice, a view from another base slice, or a sampled copy) is a separate image, copied in before and out after each use, so views that are written before a flush and share a slice do not merge: the later copy-out wins, so their results are not merged. A matching view still throws when it is a cube, a 2D array of more than one layer of the stencil plane or from a later slice, or another level, when the surface is multisampled, when it names the depth plane of a 16-bit depth with stencil surface the device stores in a wider format, and when it was written after another view of the same plane (another format, tile mode, address or dimension) replaced it, as two such views bound in one dispatch are. Stored depth values outside 0..1 are not clamped, and Vulkan leaves that copy undefined without `VK_EXT_depth_range_unrestricted`. `agc_driver_depth_storage_dispatch` pins these paths; none is measured on the console.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L70
text: [Collapsed color array views](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) preserve the selected slice in the XOR address equation when the view is represented as a shifted 2D surface. Native Vulkan coverage checks R_X draws, array reads, publication and re-upload for slices 1-3; Lost Soul Aside PPSA26358 validates the RGBA16F cube mip chain on Windows/NVIDIA. Other devices and console comparisons remain unverified. Full-array views retain their layer addressing.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L71
text: A [depth surface](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) is retired when a color target or a written storage image it does not serve overlaps it, or when it is sampled through a view it cannot serve and guest memory over it was written since it was last bound; lookups then skip it, so sampling reads the memory like any texture. Bound again, it keeps its own depth instead of the bytes written over it, except for the depth planes the next entry keeps in guest memory. Without write watching, a view it cannot serve still throws. A retired surface also gives up its depth and stencil planes, so another surface sharing them no longer copies from it.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L72
text: [Depth planes in guest memory](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): only single-sample `D32_SFLOAT` and `D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT` planes with the 64 KiB Z swizzle (`SW_MODE` 24) reach guest memory; D16, other swizzles, stencil and multisampled planes keep depth in the host image only. A plane drawn since its last store is stored, uncompressed, when a buffer upload, a `GuestBuffers` V#, an image lookup or a pending-store flush overlaps it; CPU reads and reads through address-based heaps are not caught. Guest writes are ordered when collected (bind, flush, collect epoch), not when made, at 64 KiB granularity: a collected write reloads the whole plane unless an HTILE clear is pending. A store outside a recorder waits for the GPU. The console keeps HTILE-compressed tiles compressed in memory until a decompress (Mesa `ac_descriptors.h`).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L73
text: [Depth plane copies](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/DepthSurface.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a depth plane sampled as a 2D array or a cube, or a D16 plane read as `R16_UINT`, is copied into an image of its own (`DepthPlaneCopy`), kept per base address, extent, format and slice count; a slice comes from the live depth surface when one is bound at the slice's address and from guest memory (detiled) otherwise. A draw or dispatch that binds the plane copies again only the slices that changed and records nothing when none did: a surface slice when its image or write serial differs from the one copied (the serial is bumped when the surface is created, when a draw binds it as its depth target, when a pending fast clear is applied and when a written storage view of the plane is copied back), a guest-memory slice when its bytes were written since they were last read (`GuestMemory::UnchangedSince`), a snapshot write overlaps them, or its address, size or tile mode changed. The surface of the latest depth draw is copied at every use until another depth target is bound, since that draw may still be recorded after the copy. A slice's address is the base plus a whole 64 KiB-block depth slice per layer (`DepthSliceBytes`), and the cube face order is the array order; both are inferred from the titles' use, not measured on hardware. A 2D-array T# whose `BASE_ARRAY` is past slice 0 reads slices `BASE_ARRAY` to `LAST_ARRAY` of the copy, which holds slices 0 to `LAST_ARRAY`, and a 2D binding of it reads slice `BASE_ARRAY`; that follows the colour 2D-array semantics and the titles that hit it (PPSA01556, PPSA03912), and was not measured on hardware for depth surfaces. Planes with mips, a cube or a 2D T# with a base slice other than 0, a `BASE_ARRAY` past `LAST_ARRAY`, a cube with other than 1 or 6 slices, and other views of the planes still throw, and so do these copies of a 16-bit plane with stencil that the device stores as D24 or D32 (16-bit depth with stencil, below).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L74
text: [Repacked format-43 copies](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a sampled texture of format 43 (10-bit R, 11-bit G and B unsigned floats from bit 0) is uploaded into a `B10G11R11_UFLOAT` image with its R and B fields swapped (`RepackTextureWord`) and viewed with R and B swapped back. A texture whose results a storage image still holds is copied from it again, whole, whenever the image changed (`RefreshDepthCopy`); a 3D one is flushed to guest memory and uploaded instead. Storage reads and writes of format 43 keep the packed `R32_UINT` path.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L75
text: [SW_64KB_Z_X color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ColorTargetLayout.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) use the texture equations and 64 KiB block geometry of `SW_64KB_Z_X`, whose addresses are checked against [AMD addrlib GFX10](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp) in the texture tiling tests. Any 256-byte pipe/bank XOR below the block size is accepted, as for `SW_64KB_R_X` targets and Z_X textures; which of those bits the console honours, and the render results, are not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L76
text: [SW_64KB_D_X color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ColorTargetLayout.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) use the existing texture block/mip geometry and equations from [AMD addrlib GFX10 non-RB+](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/imported/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp) for 16 pipes and 256-byte interleave. The address-reference tests use legal pipe/bank XOR bits for that configuration. Raw column bits outside the source configuration's pipe/bank mask 0xcf00 throw; their console meaning is unresolved. Console address equations and render results have not been measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L77
text: [Per-face depth bias](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): Vulkan has one depth bias per draw, so a draw that rasterizes both faces with different front and back bias (PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL, PA_SU_POLY_OFFSET_FRONT/BACK_*) is recorded twice, front faces with the back faces culled and then back faces with the front faces culled. The vertex stages run twice, so a vertex shader that writes memory writes twice, and all front faces land before all back faces instead of in primitive order, which differs only for blending or stencil updates that depend on the order.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L78
text: [Draw recipes with depth targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): direct draw recipes record and replay with active depth targets, matching the bound depth surface view by its target view identity; altered depth surface addresses or incompatible view handles trigger a recipe miss and pipeline rebuild.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L79
text: [Partial rect-list primitives](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a rect-list draw whose vertex or index count is not a multiple of 3 draws its complete rectangles and leaves out the 1 or 2 vertices after them, because rect lists are drawn as Vulkan patch lists of 3 control points, which generate [⌊vertexCount/3⌋ patches](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#drawing-patch-lists). What the console draws for the incomplete rectangle is not measured; Palworld (PPSA23126) draws 4 vertices × 9 instances as a rect list when its character creation opens.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L80
text: [8_8 UINT color targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) decode as `R8G8_UINT` with the same component-swap mapping as 8_8 UNORM/SNORM (`0xe4` / `0xec`). Follows the existing 8 and 8_8_8_8 UINT paths; not measured on the console. RetroArch (PPSA99169) uses it during menu startup.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L81
text: [Quad-list primitives](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Draw.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): primitive type 19 (DI_PT_QUADLIST, 0x13) translates to Vulkan triangle lists by generating 6 indices per 4-vertex quad in a synthetic 32-bit index buffer during draw input preparation (triangles (0, 1, 2) and (0, 2, 3) for first provoking vertex; (0, 1, 3) and (1, 2, 3) for last provoking vertex). Incomplete trailing vertices (< 4) are discarded. Indirect draws, primitive restart and draw recipes are unsupported for quad-list primitives. Console behavior for incomplete quads has not been measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L82
text: [Separate alpha blend into 8_8 SWAP_ALT targets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Pipeline.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): the second channel of a two-channel target with `COMP_SWAP` 1 holds the alpha export, but Vulkan blends it with the color equation of the R8G8 attachment, so a draw whose alpha equation differs from its color equation is recorded twice, the first channel with the color equation and the second with the alpha factors and operation moved into the color equation. The vertex stages run twice, so a vertex shader that writes memory writes twice, and occlusion counts include both passes. Draws that write depth or stencil, pixel shaders that write memory and factors of the destination alpha throw. That the hardware blends the second channel with the alpha equation is taken from Mesa's `si_translate_colorswap` and radeonsi's use of it for luminance-alpha formats, not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L83
text: [Unexported pixel inputs](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderInputState.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a pixel input whose `SPI_PS_INPUT_CNTL` parameter the previous stage does not export is programmed as a default-value input (`OFFSET` bit 5, `DEFAULT_VAL` 0, FP16 high half too) and reads (0, 0, 0, 0), as radeonsi's `SI_PS_INPUT_CNTL_UNUSED` does and as rect-list draws already do. The console's value for an unwritten parameter cache entry is not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L84
text: [Per-sample pixel shading](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): `PA_SC_MODE_CNTL_1.PS_ITER_SAMPLE` (bit 16, [PS5_Mesa GFX10.3 registers](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/0b2d6d1a61d9bbf89cf8beb88a696144f67c61f8/src/amd/registers/gfx103.json)) on a multisampled draw enables Vulkan sample shading with a minimum rate of 1.0, so the pixel program runs once per sample. The draw throws when the device lacks `sampleRateShading`. On a single-sample draw the bit has no effect and is dropped. That the console runs the pixel program once per covered sample, and what it does with the other multisample registers in that mode, is taken from the register name and Vulkan's definition, not measured on hardware. Without the bit the pixel program runs once per pixel: the recompile request carries the mode (`iteratesSamples`), the ancillary's sample number reads 0 instead of `SampleId`, whose use would make Vulkan shade per sample, and the sample barycentrics and positions are evaluated at sample 0, whose locations the request carries (`sampleLocations`, every sample's in an iterated draw). `DB_EQAA.PS_ITER_SAMPLES`, the number of samples an iterated shader covers, is not read: an iterated draw runs once per sample.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L85
text: [Unused pixel programs](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a bound pixel program is skipped when color masks have no intersection and DB export and execution enables are clear, regardless of retained SPI_SHADER_Z_FORMAT. This follows [AMD PAL DbShaderControl](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/hw/gfxip/gfx9/gfx9AbiToPipelineRegisters.h) and its [GFX10 register definitions](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/pal/blob/c5e800072a32f68b6ccc4422936d96167c6e0728/src/core/hw/gfxip/gfx9/chip/gfx9_plus_merged_registers.h), not a hardware measurement. Enabled DB_ALPHA_TO_MASK conservatively retains the program even with ALPHA_TO_MASK_DISABLE, because DecodeState currently enables Vulkan alpha-to-coverage without applying that override. Console behavior for these combinations has not been measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L86
text: [Sample masks](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) - `PA_SC_AA_MASK_X0Y0_X1Y0` and `PA_SC_AA_MASK_X0Y1_X1Y1` hold one 16-bit sample mask for each pixel of the aligned 2x2 quad ([Mesa gfx10.json](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/7b87f8ad226e/src/amd/registers/gfx10.json#L13512)); only the bits of the `MSAA_NUM_SAMPLES` rasterized samples count, and at one sample bit 0 of a pixel's field covers every sample of the target the draw is raised to. A mask equal for the four pixels is the Vulkan `pSampleMask`, the case [radv](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/7b87f8ad226e/src/amd/vulkan/radv_cmd_buffer.c#L13633) and [radeonsi](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/7b87f8ad226e/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state.c#L4218) program; with early fragment tests it needs `earlyFragmentSampleMaskTestBeforeSampleCounting` ([radv](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/7b87f8ad226e/src/amd/vulkan/radv_physical_device.c#L2079) reports it). A mask that differs between the pixels is applied in the pixel shader without early fragment tests: a pixel whose mask covers all or none of its samples is demoted to a helper invocation by `gl_FragCoord` parity and killed when the program returns (the Radeon 860M's Windows driver 32.0.13058.8001 writes undefined colour for a demoted pixel whose export leaves its output unwritten), and otherwise the pixel's mask is ANDed into `gl_SampleMask` (with alpha-to-coverage and the mask export) after demoting invocations whose `SampleMask` input it leaves empty. A pixel program with early Z that writes memory under depth, stencil or depth-bounds tests is therefore refused. That XnYm is the pixel at (x mod 2, y mod 2) = (n, m) is read from the field names; that the mask removes samples before the depth and stencil tests and occlusion counting is inferred from radv implementing the Vulkan sample mask test with it; and that it takes no part in the centroid (`AA_MASK_CENTROID_DTMN` 0) is inferred from radv setting that bit only for conservative rasterization. None of it is measured on gfx1013. A mask equal for the four pixels that removes some but not all samples of a pixel is refused with active centroid inputs, since where Vulkan puts the centroid relative to `pSampleMask` is implementation-defined, and any partial mask is refused with conservative rasterization (radv sets `PREZ_AA_MASK_ENABLE` and `POSTZ_AA_MASK_ENABLE` [there](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/7b87f8ad226e/src/amd/vulkan/radv_cmd_buffer.c#L13653), which 0x6001 leaves clear).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L87
text: [Covered-centroid raster state](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) accepts PA_SC_AA_CONFIG.COVERED_CENTROID_IS_CENTER only when the pixel program is skipped or SPI_PS_INPUT_ENA and SPI_PS_INPUT_ADDR have no active perspective or linear centroid input. Bit 29 follows [PS5_Mesa GFX10.3 registers](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/0b2d6d1a61d9bbf89cf8beb88a696144f67c61f8/src/amd/registers/gfx103.json); [RADV](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/0b2d6d1a61d9bbf89cf8beb88a696144f67c61f8/src/amd/vulkan/radv_cmd_buffer.c) sets it on GFX10.3 and later. Active centroid interpolation and unspecified input registers still throw. Console covered-pixel centroid results were not measured.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L88
text: [Compute LDS beyond the device's shared-memory limit](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) lives in a coherent storage buffer with one slice of `LDS bytes / 4 + 1` dwords, rounded up to an even count so that 64-bit atomics stay 8-byte aligned, per workgroup (the dword after the LDS is the atomic lock on a device without `shaderBufferInt64Atomics`), shared by all such dispatches and grown in 1 MiB steps up to `maxStorageBufferRange`; a dispatch whose slices do not fit throws. It is slower than shared memory and its cost was not measured. An indirect dispatch of such a program always reads its group counts on the CPU. Its results are pinned against the in-limit semantics in `agc_driver_lds_beyond_device_limit`, not measured on hardware.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L89
text: [AGC buffer allocations](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/BufferPool.cpp) retry host/device out-of-memory once after reclaiming idle pool buffers and fully unused slab blocks. Live buffers and blocks with live slots are retained. Live images and other retained resources have no global memory bound; allocation failure still throws when reclaim cannot satisfy the request.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L90
text: [Host placement after a device-memory refusal](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/BufferPool.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): when the driver refuses a device-local allocation with `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY` after the pool's trim and the texture-cache release, device buffers and images (textures, storage textures, block, repacked, depth, depth plane and stencil copies, render, depth and multisampled targets and attachment proxies) are allocated in a host memory type their requirements allow. A host-placed device buffer leaves the pool on release. A host-placed image keeps that placement until it is destroyed and is never moved back to device memory, so every access to it crosses PCIe for its lifetime. The placements are counted in a rate-limited `[bufferpool]` line with the cumulative MiB, not the resident bytes. The 1x1 denormal clear probe still allocates device memory directly and throws on a refusal.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L91
text: [Pipeline journal](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/PipelineJournal.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): the journal is append-only and never compacted, so a module a later run no longer builds pipelines from stays in the file until it is deleted, and the whole file is read into memory while the replay runs (its modules reference that buffer until the last replayed pipeline was built). Only the first `APS5_PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENTRIES` pipelines recorded are replayed (a record is never rewritten, so a pipeline past the bound stays past it), and the pipeline store evicts the least recently used entry past `APS5_PIPELINE_STORE_ENTRIES` (1024 each): a title with more configurations rebuilds the rest at the draw as before. A compute pipeline is replayed over the set layout `DescribeSetLayouts` derives from the result's bindings, which a dispatch that finds it resident checks against its `ShaderResources` layout only under `APS5_VERIFY_SET_LAYOUTS=1`. Recording and replay are best effort: a record whose write fails is lost, an entry whose build fails is skipped, and both are counted in the `[pipeline-journal]` line rather than stopping the run. A replayed pipeline that the title never asks for again costs its build time and its driver memory (its optimized relink is deferred to its first draw, so a run whose first frames bind many replayed pipelines queues their relinks then); nothing ages recipes out of the file. Two runs sharing the file take turns under its lock file, but each only knows the modules it loaded or wrote itself, so a module the other run appended meanwhile may be appended again (the loader keeps the first copy). Records a run appends after another run's load are replayed by that run only after its next start. The file header's format number is the only guard against a change of the recipe codec, `CanonicalPipelineState` or the store key that keeps the structures' sizes (the recompiler's source version does not cover the driver's sources).

name: libSceAgcDriver.L92
text: [Graphics pipeline libraries](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/PipelineLibrary.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): a pipeline is fast-linked at the draw and relinked with `VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_LINK_TIME_OPTIMIZATION_BIT_EXT` on a background thread, and binds the optimized one from the next draw on. Draws recorded before that use the fast link, whose vertex stage keeps the outputs the fragment stage does not read: on RADV (Radeon 660M, Mesa 26.2.4) 346 of 483 Astro's Playroom vertex shaders paired with a fragment stage that reads none of them used more VGPRs (median 8 more, up to 2.5 times), and on an RTX 4090 13 of 15 PPSA36082 vertex shaders up to 68 instead of 38 (#2242). The optimized link compiles to the same code as a whole pipeline

text: [`APS5_THREAD_PRIORITY=rt`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/ThreadPriority.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) lowers the process's hard `RLIMIT_RTTIME` when it is above `APS5_THREAD_RTTIME_US` or rtkit's `RTTimeUSecMax`, because [rtkit](https://github.com/heftig/rtkit/blob/c295fa849f52b487be6433e69e08b46251950399/rtkit-daemon.c#L592-L637) (`verify_process_rttime`) reads the hard limit from `/proc/<pid>/limits` and refuses real-time scheduling when it is higher. An unprivileged process cannot raise the hard limit again, so it stays lowered for the process and its threads even when rtkit then refuses the request (burst limit, user or start-time checks) and the thread throws. rtkit's `MaxRealtimePriority` and `RTTimeUSecMax` are read first, so an unreachable rtkit or a priority above its maximum leaves the limit untouched. The lowered limit only matters for threads that later run under a real-time policy

name: libSceAgcDriver.L95
text: AMD image descriptors with `TYPE=0` are treated as null for read-only image slots even when the base and other words are nonzero: `image_load` on a gfx1035 with such a T# returns 0,0,0,0, and the same descriptors were seen in direct reads in PPSA01341 on an RTX 4070. Writable and atomic image slots and entries of an image table keep faulting because there is no hardware measurement for them, and the reserved types 2-7 also fault. `TYPE=1` is treated as null in the same read-only slots: gfx1035 reads it as zeros too, and gfx1010 returns zeros for `image_sample_lz`, `image_sample_b`, `image_load` and `image_get_resinfo` with format 22 (#5828); it is not measured on RDNA2, with other formats or with depth-compare reads (`image_sample_c*`). gfx1013 behavior is unverified

name: libSceAgcDriver.L96
text: On a device without VK_EXT_robustness2's `nullDescriptor`, such as MoltenVK, a null image descriptor in a typed heap is a [placeholder image](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/PlaceholderImages.cpp) of that heap's type, 1×1 and cleared to zero, which every null descriptor of the heap shares. Reads give zeros, as `nullDescriptor` allows, but stores and atomics to it are kept, so a later read of a null storage image can return them, and a depth comparison compares against depth 0. A heap whose placeholder the device cannot create, for example 1D or 3D depth, 64-bit atomics without 64-bit image atomics, or multisampled storage without `shaderStorageImageMultisample`, throws when a null descriptor reaches it.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L97
text: [Draw input snapshots](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/ShaderResources.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver): `PrepareDrawBindings` caps read-only input buffer snapshots at 64 MiB (overridable via `APS5_DRAW_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MIB`). Larger inputs (streaming heaps, bindless pools) or draws exceeding the cumulative budget skip the per-draw snapshot and bind in place, avoiding multi-gigabyte CPU copy stalls (such as Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart PPSA01474 stalling at frame ~380 copying 36 GB every 5 s). If the title rewrites those large ranges on the CPU before GPU completion, the in-place binding observes the modification, as verified by `drawSnapshotCapTests`.

name: libSceAgcDriver.L99
text: [Pending storage-image results over memory outside the write watch](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/Texture.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) leave to the CPU the 64 KiB blocks whose bytes differ from the ones saved at the upload, the fill, the image copy, the previous store or the moment their range left the watch (`Unwatch`, or a host import that does not stay watched), and the blocks the watch saw the CPU write before that moment. A store made on the GPU saves its bytes through a host-visible copy that becomes the saved bytes when its batch completes; a store or a refresh that needs them earlier waits for that batch. A unit without a write generation saves the guest bytes when results land in it outside the watch. One whose range leaves the watch while its results are pending saves its bytes through the unwatch hook, which also runs when a failed collect takes a range out of the watch. A range that leaves the watch without the hook running over it (an import fallback that unwatched without saving) leaves its pending results without saved bytes; storing such results throws. A unit whose results were stored while its blocks were watched keeps only a generation; when its blocks leave the watch while nothing is pending, the hook saves nothing, and results that land in it afterwards have neither saved bytes nor a watch, so storing them throws too.

FFmpeg returns PCM in its native speaker order. The implicit stream layout, PCM channel order and invalid family-0 channel count result are not verified on a console. Family 255 with one channel is decoded as one mono stream, the same as family 0; this is assumed, since the stream count, coupled stream count and channel mapping that a family-255 Opus header carries ([RFC 7845 section 5.1.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7845#section-5.1.1)) are not passed. FMOD in PPSA29141 sets a total shorter than a sound's frames and reads the frames after it on later runs; with the output held at the total its stream reader waited for them forever and the last buffer repeated. The console's handling of the frames after the total is not documented; a reset (`SetGaplessDecode` with the reset flag, `ClearContext`, initialization) starts a new segment. An ATRAC9 run job without `RUN_MULTIPLE_FRAMES` decodes its whole input as one with it: FMOD in PPSA29141 puts two run jobs in one batch with the second's input right after the whole of the first's. No `std::set_unexpected` is exported and the exception header's unexpected handler is never set, so the handler is always the default one, which calls `std::terminate` ([cxa_default_handlers.cpp](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/3b5b5c1ec4a3095ab096dd780e84d7ab81f3d7ff/libcxxabi/src/cxa_default_handlers.cpp#L88-L99)); it therefore forwards to libc's `__cxa_call_terminate`, which begins the catch and runs the current terminate handler. That matches libcxxabi except for which terminate handler runs: there `std::terminate` after `__cxa_begin_catch` ([cxa_exception.cpp L470-L477](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/3b5b5c1ec4a3095ab096dd780e84d7ab81f3d7ff/libcxxabi/src/cxa_exception.cpp#L470-L477)) runs the handler saved in the caught exception's header ([cxa_handlers.cpp L72-L93](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/3b5b5c1ec4a3095ab096dd780e84d7ab81f3d7ff/libcxxabi/src/cxa_handlers.cpp#L72-L93)), which `__cxa_throw` and `__cxa_init_primary_exception` set to `std::get_terminate()` when the exception is thrown ([cxa_exception.cpp L209-L214](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/3b5b5c1ec4a3095ab096dd780e84d7ab81f3d7ff/libcxxabi/src/cxa_exception.cpp#L209-L214), [L279](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/3b5b5c1ec4a3095ab096dd780e84d7ab81f3d7ff/libcxxabi/src/cxa_exception.cpp#L279)), while here the current global handler runs, as AnyPS5's own `std::terminate` does. The two differ only if `std::set_terminate` was called between the throw and this call. A null header terminates because this emulator's libc `__cxa_begin_catch` terminates on null (libcxxabi does not define that case). Dynamic exception specifications that would let a replaced unexpected handler throw a permitted type are not modelled

name: libSceAmpr.L6
text: [AMPR WriteAddressFromCounterPairOnCompletion](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAmpr/Export.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - the pair of an even counter n is assumed to give counter n in the low 32 bits and n + 1 in the high 32 bits. Wait compare values, wait flush and counter index ranges follow the [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) reimplementation; the flush is accepted and has no effect, as commands run in order

name: libSceAmpr.L7
text: [AMPR command buffer offsets](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAmpr/Export.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - recording with a current offset greater than the bound memory size throws before calculating remaining capacity or writing a command. This validates the emulator's own command-buffer encoding; the console's response to a corrupted opaque buffer object is unknown.

name: libSceAmpr.L8
text: [AMPR command sizes](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAmpr/Export.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - commands use the emulator's own encoding with an 8-byte header, so `Nop(n)` takes 8 + 4n bytes where the console record is n dwords including its header (`NopWithData(n)`: (n + 1) dwords). The measure functions agree with the appended sizes, but a title that pads to an exact offset or the end of the buffer with `Nop(remaining / 4)` gets `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EBUSY` or a shifted offset. The at-start flag of the `_04_00` writes is ignored; commands run in order, each after the previous one completes

name: libSceAmpr.L9
text: [APR map begin and end](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAmpr/Export.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - as in ampr_emu, `MapBegin`/`MapDirectBegin` map when they run and `MapEnd` only closes the region; while a region is open a second begin and every completion write return `EPERM`, the at-start `_04_00` writes are accepted

name: libSceAppChecker.L5
text: [sceAppCheckerAbort, sceAppCheckerExecute and sceAppCheckerExecuteEx](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAppChecker/Export.cpp) (libSceAppChecker) - names and NIDs are present in the [aerolib symbol database](https://github.com/zecoxao/sce_symbols/blob/master/aerolib.csv) and are attributed to this module by `sceAppChecker` symbol prefix; the library is absent from the PS5 3.20 export inventory, so the pairing is not firmware-verified and no credible prototypes were found. The declarations have no parameters solely to resolve imports; this is not an ABI claim and callers must not call them until signatures are verified

name: libSceAppContent.L10
text: [Additional content](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAppContent/Export.cpp) (libSceAppContent) is not installed or mounted: `sceAppContentAddcontMount` answers `NOT_FOUND` for every entitlement label and `sceAppContentAddcontUnmount` for every mount point, as no add-content mount is ever handed out; `sceAppContentGetAddcontInfo` answers `DRM_NO_ENTITLEMENT` for every label and `sceAppContentGetAddcontInfoList` reports 0 entries; `sceAppContentAddcontEnqueueDownload` answers `PARAMETER` for a null label and `NOT_FOUND` otherwise, since no download is ever queued; `sceAppContentAddcontDelete` answers `PARAMETER` for a null label and `NOT_FOUND` otherwise, since no additional content is ever installed. `sceAppContentGetAddcontDownloadProgress` answers `PARAMETER` for a null label or progress and `NOT_FOUND` otherwise, as [dlc_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/dlc_emu/blob/fcf69b16d46a9850578bce19dc2c1b4dc867cbb5/src/dlc_modules/dlc_content.cpp#L2328-L2341) does for a label that is not installed additional content, and never writes the progress. Its 16-byte layout (`DataSize`, then `DownloadedSize`, both 64-bit) follows [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/AppContent/AppContent.cs#L45-L54) and is unused here. The signatures of `sceAppContentAddcontEnqueueDownload` and `sceAppContentGetAddcontDownloadProgress` follow [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/AppContent/AppContent.cs#L140-L148), and the signature of `sceAppContentAddcontDelete` follows [dlc_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/dlc_emu/blob/fcf69b16d46a9850578bce19dc2c1b4dc867cbb5/src/dlc_modules/dlc_content.h#L91-L92); dlc_emu is not a console measurement and no console source gives the error codes, so the signatures and the error codes are unverified

A null mount point returns `PARAMETER` and another mount point returns `NOT_MOUNTED` as in `sceAppContentTemporaryDataFormat` and `sceAppContentDownloadDataGetAvailableSpaceKb`; the console's error codes for both and its behaviour with files still open are unverified

name: libSceAppContent.L11
text: [Temporary app-content storage](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAppContent/Export.cpp) tracks one `/temp0` mount, preserves its files on unmount, and rejects new path resolutions until remount. Mount, format, space-query and unmount errors follow [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/sys/sys_path.pas); the pointer ABI is also declared by [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/main/src/SharpProspero/Interop/AppContent/AppContent.cs). Existing open host descriptors remain usable after unmount; console behaviour with open files is unverified. Host filesystem failures still throw.

name: libSceAudio3d.L9
text: [libSceAudio3d bed path](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Export.cpp) (libSceAudio3d) - bed PCM is mixed and played: `sceAudio3dBedWrite` and `sceAudio3dBedWrite2` queue a bed, bounded by `queue_depth` and `NOT_READY` when full, `sceAudio3dPortAdvance` consumes one and mixes it into a stereo frame with a linear-balance pan and a 5.1/7.1 downmix, and an advance with no bed queued mixes silence ([Mixer.hpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Mixer.hpp)) and queues the frame, and `sceAudio3dPortPush` opens a type-126 AudioOut port on first use and submits the queued frames to it. The explicit `sceAudio3dAudioOutOpen`, `sceAudio3dAudioOutOutput` and `sceAudio3dAudioOutOutputs` exports queue their blocks and the port drains them. The attribute enum values and the panning model are unverified

name: libSceAudio3d.L30

[shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4) returns the total samples instead (`len * channels`) and fpPS4 returns 0; no console measurement settles it

text: [libSceAudio3d](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Export.cpp) (libSceAudio3d) - `sceAudio3dObjectSetAttributes` validates the port, the reserved object and the attribute array (an object id that was never reserved returns the invalid-object error, while shadPS4 returns success for it; neither is measured on a console), treating the reset-state attribute as valid with a null value and requiring a value for the others, but the identifiers and the value of each are not interpreted, so an object has no samples, no gain and no position: the ids of the `PCM`, `GAIN` and `POSITION` attributes and the `POSITION` layout are unknown (the aerolib NID list gives the names only, the Orbital IDA type database the signatures only and shadPS4's values are PS4). `sceAudio3dPortSetAttribute` accepts the late reverb level and the downmix spread attributes and ignores them, and `sceAudio3dPortFlush` drops the frames queued by `sceAudio3dPortAdvance` instead of mixing and submitting them to an output

text: [sceAudio3dPortAdvance buffer mode](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Export.cpp) (libSceAudio3d) - a mode other than 2 returns `NOT_SUPPORTED` (0x80EA0008), the value [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4) uses for it and the one [prosper](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper) reads from the PS5 module's own error table, where 0x80EA0008 is what the per-port calls return for a buffer mode they do not support. shadPS4 and prosper refuse only mode 0 in `sceAudio3dPortAdvance` and modes 0 and 1 in `sceAudio3dPortPush`, while [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5) requires mode 2 at `sceAudio3dPortOpen` and halts otherwise, so this library refuses every other mode at the open and the check here is unreachable. 0x80EA0005 is `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, not `NOT_SUPPORTED`

name: libSceAudio3d.L28
text: [Audio3d bed downmix coefficients](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Mixer.hpp) (libSceAudio3d) - the centre and the surrounds fold into stereo with a 0.7071 gain and the LFE channel is dropped, which follows [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4) (PS4): its `DOWNMIX_CENTER` and `DOWNMIX_SURROUND` are 0.7071 and its `DOWNMIX_LFE` is 0, so the `if constexpr` that adds the LFE is compiled out. [prosper](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper) disagrees on the LFE only: it folds it into both sides with a 0.5 gain, in its AudioOut2 main bed path, which is not an Audio3d path. KytyPS5 has no Audio3d mixing at all. The absolute level is unmeasured: fpPS4 scales the front by 1 + 3/sqrt(2) instead of 1

name: libSceAudio3d.L29
text: [Audio3d bed channel order](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Mixer.hpp) (libSceAudio3d) - the buffer is read as L, R, C, LFE, Ls, Rs, Lrs, Rrs, the standard order, which three references agree on: [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4) reads the front, centre, LFE and surround samples at those indices, [prosper](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper) documents FL, FR, FC, LFE and then surround pairs, and fpPS4 names them `_FL=0 _FR=1 _FC=2 _LF=3 _SL=4 _SR=5 _BL=6 _BR=7`. fpPS4's `STD` layout swaps the side and back pairs, which this library does not model

name: libSceAudio3d.L32
text: [sceAudio3dPortAdvance on a full queue](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudio3d/Export.cpp) (libSceAudio3d) - a full queue returns `NOT_READY` (0x80EA0007) instead of throwing, which follows [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4), the only reference with a body: it returns `ORBIS_AUDIO3D_ERROR_NOT_READY` when the mixed queue is at the port's depth. [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5) halts instead and prosper has no queue at all

name: libSceAudioIn.L45
text: [sceAudioInHqOpen, sceAudioInAsyncOpen](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioIn/Export.cpp) (libSceAudioIn) open the same port as `sceAudioInOpen`, so `sceAudioInInput`, `sceAudioInGetSilentState` and `sceAudioInClose` accept their handles. The signatures agree across [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/fc5d2cc219c43c8c8f354153e7b3d0c04a5d506e/src/core/libraries/audio/audioin.cpp), [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/60977b29103452b9681ae10c7a9011d44965bf16/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioIn.cs) and [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/c86c8b4d9333a766cc8c4495f89f893bf35e6199/src/libs/audio.cpp). HqOpen is limited to 128 samples at 48 kHz, as [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/c86c8b4d9333a766cc8c4495f89f893bf35e6199/src/libs/audio.cpp) and [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/60977b29103452b9681ae10c7a9011d44965bf16/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioIn.cs) describe the higher-quality path: a longer grain returns the invalid-size error and a lower rate the invalid-frequency error. AsyncOpen also accepts the 384-sample grain, the largest [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/60977b29103452b9681ae10c7a9011d44965bf16/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioIn.cs) documents for the low-latency path, and returns the invalid-size error for every other size; the console's shorter average return interval of an async port's blocks is not modelled, so like a synchronous port `sceAudioInInput` paces one grain at a time. Param 0x10 opens a float mono port like 0x11, as [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/c86c8b4d9333a766cc8c4495f89f893bf35e6199/src/libs/audio.cpp) accepts both, while SharpProspero documents only 0x11. Host capture pacing and console behavior remain unverified.

text: [sceAudioOut2ContextGetQueueLevel](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut2Context.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) with an SDL device counts the grains that `sceAudioOut2ContextAdvance` completed and no push has consumed as queued, together with the pushed grains beyond the 40 ms cushion, up to `queue_depth`. Whether the console counts them is unknown. Pushes that fill the cushion leave the level at 0, so a title that renders as many grains as the level leaves room for and pushes them on another thread rendered a full queue again after each of those pushes: PPSA23226's Wwise sink passes the available count to the sound engine as the number of frames to render, advances once per frame and pushes on a separate thread, and exceeded 16 completed grains. Counted, the completed grains keep such a title at most `queue_depth` grains ahead of its pushes.

name: libSceAudioOut.L5
text: [sceAudioOut2ContextAdvance and sceAudioOut2ContextPush](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut2Context.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) - with an SDL device, Advance snapshots each port's PCM and gain; Push consumes completed grains in order and a blocking Push waits for Advance when none is ready. Inferred from PPSA26358, which rewrites the same 512-frame, 12-channel float buffer on a producer thread and pushes on another thread. Console buffer ownership, snapshot timing and empty-queue errors are unverified. Completed grains remain queued until Push consumes them, so memory use grows with an unconsumed PCM backlog. The console backlog limit is unverified. A nonblocking Push without a completed grain throws; this is a runtime restriction, not a console measurement. Context destruction concurrent with active calls remains unsupported. Without an SDL device the existing wall-clock path remains.

name: libSceAudioOut.L128
text: [AudioOut2 contexts](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut2Context.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) with an SDL device and no `sceAudioOut2ContextAdvance` calls read a grain's port buffers at the next push, at least 100 us after the grain was pushed, and play the mix behind a 40 ms cushion that the queue level leaves out. When the hardware reads the buffers is not known. The timing follows a title whose mixer fills a buffer after pushing it, reuses it two pushes later, and may still be writing it when the next push follows within microseconds. The last grain pushed before a title stops pushing is never read or played.

name: libSceAudioOut.L26
text: [sceAudioOut2PortGetState](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut2Port.cpp) and [sceAudioOut2GetSpeakerInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut2SpeakerArray.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) - the port state reports the channel count of the port's data format, output main, volume 127 and a zero reroute counter and flags. Taking the channel count from the data format follows [SharpEmu](https://github.com/sharpemu/sharpemu/blob/main/src/SharpEmu.Libs/Audio/AudioOut2Exports.cs), another emulator. A payload process on a PS5 (firmware 13.60), which is not the foreground application, read output 0, volume -1 and reroute counter 5 for its main ports, and 6 channels for an 8-channel port on a 5.1 system, so a title's values are unverified, including the output of a pad port, the volume after `sceAudioOut2PortSetAttributes` and the reroute counter on a device change. The speaker info reports type 0 with available bits `0x3`, the front left speaker at +30 degrees and the front right one at -30, and -360 for the azimuth and elevation of every other slot. On that console the type followed the HDMI device type and the available bits its channels: type 0 with the device set to TV, 1 to AV amplifier and 2 to sound bar, which [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioOut2.cs) names television, AV receiver and sound bar (3 is headphones there), and available bits `0x3` for 2 channels and `0x3F` for 5.1 (centre at 0, surround pair at +110 and -110, -360 for the LFE). The front pair and the empty slots read the same in every setting; 7.1 on the AV amplifier reported 2 channels on that console's HDMI chain. The host output is always reported as a stereo television here. The console also returns `0x80268006` before `sceAudioOut2Initialize`, `0x80268001` for flags above 1 and `0x8026800C` for a null pointer, which are not modelled. ASTRO BOT and ASTRO's PLAYROOM reportedly stop on an assertion that depends on these values (#4317), but which field matters has not been isolated

text: [sceAudioOutExOpen, sceAudioOutExConfigureOutput, sceAudioOutExClose](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) - the HDMI bitstream calls follow [PS5-Audio-Passthrough-Research](https://github.com/sainsaji/PS5-Audio-Passthrough-Research/blob/cf3c921d79bf00db4847f31b68a7bd95a8037cd7/docs/FINDINGS.md#L31-L80), which disassembles firmware 12.70's libSceAudioOut and logs the calls on a console. `sceAudioOutExOpen(user, mode)` returns `0x80260015` for a mode above 10 or outside mask `0x61F`; otherwise it opens a port of internal type 6 in S16 stereo, 256 frames at 48000 Hz for modes 0, 1, 2 and 9 and 1024 frames at 192000 Hz for modes 3, 4 and 10. `sceAudioOutExConfigureOutput(control, flags, mode, target, option)` returns `0x80268009` when `control` is not 0, takes modes 0 to 10 and 0xFF and targets 1 to 3 and 0xFF, and returned 0 on the console; `sceAudioOutExClose` returned 0. The argument registers match [Jelly5](https://github.com/02dnot/Jelly5/blob/552b866d89b2a58b27f7f7b0484dc743ce235526/app/src/jelly5_bitstream.cpp#L26-L28) and PPSA99051's [bitstream_out.cpp](https://github.com/sainsaji/PS5-Audio-Passthrough-Research/blob/cf3c921d79bf00db4847f31b68a7bd95a8037cd7/sample-app/src/platform/ps5/bitstream_out.cpp#L29-L32). Audio reaches the host through SDL as PCM and the host has no HDMI bitstream output, so an Ex port has no host device: `sceAudioOutOutput` paces it at its own rate and drops its IEC 61937 bursts, and `sceAudioOutExConfigureOutput` changes nothing. Nonzero `flags` or `option`, other modes or targets, `sceAudioOutExClose` of a handle that is not an Ex port, and `sceAudioOutGetPortState` on an Ex port throw, since the console's answers are unknown

text: [sceAudioOutSysOpen, sceAudioOutSysConfigureOutput, sceAudioOutSysClose](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) - imported by PPSA99051 and PPSA99997, which fail to load without them; the signatures follow [EVO-PLAYER-PS5](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5/blob/da0c0451333bab82e79fffd2de4718e917f9dcb0/projects/evoplayer/core/src/audio/evo_pt.cpp#L24-L29), whose audio code both titles share, and are not confirmed on a console. `sceAudioOutSysOpen(user, mode)` opens a port only for mode 5, the TrueHD MAT route: [the same project's carrier table](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5/blob/da0c0451333bab82e79fffd2de4718e917f9dcb0/projects/evoplayer/core/src/audio/iec61937.cpp#L125-L140), read from sceAudioOutExOpen's own tables in firmware 12.70, describes it as a 768 kHz port of 1024 S16 8-channel frames whose 16-byte frames are consumed at 192 kHz; every other mode throws. Audio reaches the host through SDL as PCM and the host has no HDMI bitstream output, so like an Ex port a Sys port has no host device: `sceAudioOutOutput` paces it at its own rate and drops the MAT bursts. `sceAudioOutSysConfigureOutput(type, flags, mode, target, option)` accepts only the observed `(1, 0, 5, 1, 0)` HDMI MAT switch and changes nothing; other arguments throw. `sceAudioOutSysClose` closes a Sys port and throws for any other handle. The restore path EVO-PLAYER-PS5 takes after a Sys port calls `sceAudioOutExConfigureOutput(0, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0)`, so no Sys reset combination is known

name: libSceAudioOut.L130
text: [sceAudioOutSysGetHdmiMonitorInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut.cpp) (libSceAudioOut) reports an HDMI sink without a monitor name or audio descriptors: it zeroes the 0x180 bytes and returns 0, since audio reaches the host through SDL as PCM and there is no EDID to describe. The arguments `(type, info, size)`, the required size 0x180 and the fields titles read (monitor name at +0x0B, 13 bytes; descriptor count as a 32-bit value at +0x94; 8-byte descriptors `[coding type, channels, rate mask, 0, extra, 0, 0, 0]` from +0x98) come from [PS5-Audio-Passthrough-Research](https://github.com/sainsaji/PS5-Audio-Passthrough-Research/blob/c3be9c2afcb8f7838784ead0fe1c12a2ceea965a/docs/FINDINGS.md) (firmware 12.70, one monitor). What a console without an HDMI audio sink returns, an error or no descriptors, is unknown. The other bytes, among them the header at +0x90 (`01 09 4f 00` on that monitor), have no known meaning and are written as 0. No LPCM descriptor is reported for the host device, as the rate mask and extra byte of one are not known. A null buffer returns `0x80260004` like the other AudioOut calls; the console's code is not measured. Monitor type 0x10, which the console also accepts, other types and sizes other than 0x180 throw: their results and error codes are unknown.

text: [Legacy vibration ports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioOut/src/AudioOut.cpp): PPSA99902's [public input wrapper](https://github.com/Nazky/UnleashedRecomp-Prospero/blob/2ce067a1d51bb58670c7ee4a3aed893c504da805/UnleashedRecomp/hid/driver/sdl_hid.cpp#L316) opens type 10 with 256 stereo S16 or F32 frames at 48000 Hz. Mono duplicates its channel as AudioOut2 does; wider vibration layouts throw. Native controller output uses AudioOut2's four-channel layout, or its six-channel PulseAudio mapping. Without a controller sound card the existing RMS motor transform is applied to segments of at most 256 frames, scheduled by the legacy queue's frame count and rate; drain and close remove only that port's segments. Concurrent sources combine by the maximum per motor, and the pad consumer uses this approximation only for controllers other than DualSense. This host timing and motor model is not a console measurement or waveform reproduction; legacy native output is unmeasured on hardware, and user routing retains the single-controller limitation. AudioOut2 retains its separate 80 ms peak hold.

The system options layout is unknown (only checked for non-null); the fourth argument of `sceAudioPropagationSourceCalculateAudioPaths` is unknown; `sceAudioPropagationSourceGetAudioPath` is assumed to output an 8-byte path handle. The meaning of the `RenderInfo` word at +0x28 is unknown (PPSA21567 and PPSA21564 pass 2); only 2 is accepted. Both titles pass one `RenderInfo` per call: a count of 0 throws, and larger counts are handled element by element without proof. name: libSceAudioPropagation.L9
text: [sceAudioPropagationSourceSetAudioPath](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioPropagation/Export.cpp) (libSceAudioPropagation, NID `tKSmk2JsMAA`) - `(uint64_t path, const void* data, float gain)` follows [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioPropagation.cs) and SAROS's call, which passes a handle from `sceAudioPropagationSourceGetAudioPath`, path data and gain 1.0. Path updates are unsupported and every call throws without reading or writing caller memory. The no-propagation model yields no path handles; path allocation, ownership, rendering and console error codes remain unknown.

name: libSceAudioPropagation.L5
text: [libSceAudioPropagation](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAudioPropagation/Export.cpp) implements only the no-acoustic-propagation path: the system keeps a 16-byte header in the title's CPU memory (no GPU memory), rooms, portals, sources and materials are tracked handles, attributes are validated and have no effect, no rays are requested and sources report no audio paths. Ray results, path calculation and audio paths are accepted only when empty and throw otherwise; `sceAudioPropagationSourceRender` preserves each destination mix because there are no path contributions, following the additive-output contract in [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Audio/AudioPropagation.cs); console behaviour has not been measured. It adds no dry signal. Objects still alive when their system is destroyed become unusable, and their later destroy or unregister is a no-op: PPSA21567 releases its reference-counted room, portal and source owners just before `sceAudioPropagationSystemDestroy`, so the order for every object is not proven. Occlusion, reflections and reverb from level geometry are absent; in-game behaviour remains unverified.

name: libSceCesCs.L6
text: [EUC-JP (CP51932) conversions](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/Export.cpp) (libSceCesCs): `sceCesUcsProfileInitEucJpCp51932` marks the caller's sheet with an 8-byte tag and returns it as the profile. `sceCesUtf8StrToMbcsStr`, `sceCesUcs2StrToMbcsStr`, `sceCesMbcsStrToUtf8Str`, `sceCesMbcsStrToUcs2Str`, their `Get*Len` forms and `sceCesEucJpToUcs2` convert ASCII, the JIS X 0201 half-width katakana (`0x8E` + `0xA1`-`0xDF`, U+FF61-U+FF9F) and the two-byte rows `0xA1`-`0xFE` for that profile, and every character for the CP1252 and CP1251 profiles. The two-byte table ([JisX0208.hpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/JisX0208.hpp), 7336 of 8836 cells) is Microsoft code page 932 read through the standard JIS row/cell to Shift-JIS arithmetic, so it includes NEC row 13 and the NEC-selected IBM rows 89-92 and maps the Microsoft variants (U+FF5E at `0xA1C1`, U+2225, U+FF0D, U+FFE0-U+FFE2) instead of JIS X 0208's; that the console's CP51932 table equals it is assumed from the Microsoft code page, not measured. A character with several cells encodes to the lowest cell. A well-formed but unassigned cell answers `UNASSIGNED_CODE`, a trail byte outside `0xA1`-`0xFE` `INVALID_ENCODE`, a cut pair `SRC_BUFFER_END`; the console's errors for these are not known. Three-byte JIS X 0212 (`0x8F`) characters convert through a second table ([JisX0212.hpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/JisX0212.hpp), 6067 of 8836 cells) read from the Unicode consortium's [JIS0212.TXT](https://unicode.org/Public/MAPPINGS/OBSOLETE/EASTASIA/JIS/JIS0212.TXT); that the console's CP51932 table equals it is assumed from that mapping, not measured. A well-formed but unassigned three-byte cell answers `UNASSIGNED_CODE` and a cut triple `SRC_BUFFER_END`. A character with cells in both JIS X 0208 and JIS X 0212 encodes to the two-byte form, and one only in JIS X 0212 to the three-byte form. Signatures follow [orbital](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/master/tools/ida/db_types.json). The string forms stop at the source limit or at a zero code unit, which is neither converted nor counted, and write no terminator; `*Len` outputs count code units consumed and produced. A code point outside the BMP answers `UNASSIGNED_CODE`. Unverified on hardware.

Its signature follows the Orbital type database linked above; it uses the existing CP51932 profile and JIS tables, with their mapping and profile-layout assumptions listed above, converts one character (including zero), and writes no terminator. name: libSceCesCs.L7
text: [Shift-JIS (CP932) conversions](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/Export.cpp) (libSceCesCs): `sceCesUcsProfileInitSJis1997Cp932` marks the caller's sheet with an 8-byte tag and returns it as the profile. `sceCesUtf8StrToMbcsStr`, `sceCesUcs2StrToMbcsStr`, `sceCesMbcsStrToUtf8Str`, `sceCesMbcsStrToUcs2Str`, and their `Get*Len` forms convert ASCII, JIS X 0201 half-width katakana (`0xA1`-`0xDF`, U+FF61-U+FF9F), two-byte Shift-JIS sequences (`0x81`-`0x9F` and `0xE0`-`0xFC` lead, `0x40`-`0x7E` and `0x80`-`0xFC` trail) mapped to JIS X 0208 row/cell indices against the CP932 table ([JisX0208.hpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/JisX0208.hpp)), and the IBM extensions (`0xFA40`-`0xFC4B`, 388 characters) decoded to their corresponding JIS X 0208 code points. The user-defined area (`0xF040`-`0xF9FC`, which CP932 maps to Private Use Area U+E000-U+E757) and unassigned lead/trail combinations answer `UNASSIGNED_CODE`, an invalid lead or trail byte `INVALID_ENCODE`, a cut sequence `SRC_BUFFER_END`. Characters with multiple cells encode to the lowest cell. Signatures follow [orbital](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/master/tools/ida/db_types.json). Unverified on hardware.

name: libSceCesCs.L11
text: [Unicode scalar conversions](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceCesCs/Unicode.cpp) (libSceCesCs) - console error precedence, optional length pointers and length units are unverified. text: [sceFiberGetInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFiber/Export.cpp) reports the requested-size window at the top of the host stack used for execution, rather than the original caller buffer, which is retained and pinned. The additional 1 MiB host-call margin below that window is not included in `size_context`. Planet Coaster (PPSA01736 v01.017) uses this range for ChakraCore garbage-collector stack scans; reporting the unused caller buffer makes the scan cross unmapped memory. The range is covered by a regression test while running, switching and migrating a fiber between threads. Console behavior for substituted host stacks has no direct equivalent and is not measured.

name: libSceFiber.L12
text: [Fiber stacks](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFiber/Export.cpp) (libSceFiber) - a fiber whose context is smaller than 64 KiB runs on an mmap'd host stack of its context size plus 1 MiB, so host calls made from it (21 KiB deep when PPSA01341 reaches SPIRV-Tools from a 16 KiB context) do not overwrite the contexts packed next to it; a larger context is the stack, as on the console. PPSA05684 needs the second: its job fibers have 64 KiB and 512 KiB contexts, the 512 KiB ones at 1 MiB-aligned addresses, and find their job record by masking the stack pointer (`~0xfffff` for the 512 KiB ones), which a host stack breaks (the game waits forever in GameInit, or faults later in a 64 KiB fiber). The 64 KiB limit is chosen between these two titles, not measured: a title with small contexts that also derives state from the stack pointer, or one whose host calls exceed what is left of a large context, is not covered

text: [Font writing lines](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFont/src/WritingLine.cpp) (libSceFont) - `sceFontWritingLineWritesOrder`, `sceFontWritingLineRefersRenderStep`, `sceFontWritingLineGetRenderMetrics`, `sceFontWritingLineGetOrderingSpace` and `sceFontWritingLineClear` follow the PS4 11.00 `libSceFont.sprx` (firmware module, read from its disassembly and compared call for call on random sequences): runs are linked in visual order by embedding level, the space at each spaced join is summed for the line, steps walk the visual order from the left (form `0x12`) or from the right (form `0x11`) and the render metrics grow as steps are consumed. The PS5 library was not measured. Not from that module: form `0x10` is accepted and treated as left to right and a detail with id `0x0FD5` is accepted (the PS4 library rejects both); the memory argument of `sceFontCreateWritingLine` and the rest of the detail are not read (the PS4 library validates its library object there); an unknown writing form, another detail id, a null line pointer on creation, unknown and null handles (except in `sceFontWritingLineRefersRenderStep`, which returns null for a null line) and a null output of `sceFontWritingLineGetRenderMetrics` throw instead of returning the PS4 error codes, which are not confirmed for the PS5; `sceFontDestroyWritingLine` was not compared. Lines are allocated on the host, not in the font memory the title passes to the library: FreeType needs about 1 MiB per CJK face, which the title's font memory is not sized for.

The 64-bit writing attribute is read as the PS4 11.00 `libSceFont.sprx` reads it: low byte `0xFA`, embedding level in bits 8-15 (0 to 126), bit 30 and bit 31 marking space before and after the run; the PS5 library was not measured, and the names of the two bits are ours. PPSA01325 builds its attribute the same way (`0xFA | level << 8`, bits 30 and 31) and passes a null metrics pointer when its run has no metrics object. Attribute 0 is accepted and treated as `0xFA` with level 0 and no spacing bits, as before this reading; the PS4 library rejects it and what the PS5 library does with it is unknown. Any other attribute, a level above 126 and a null orderer throw: the PS4 library returns `0x80460002` for them, not confirmed for the PS5

text: [sceFontDefineAttribute, sceFontGetAttribute](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFont/src/Style.cpp), [sceFontGlyphDefineAttribute, sceFontGlyphGetAttribute](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFont/src/Render.cpp) (libSceFont) - the signatures `(handle, int attribute, int* oldAttribute)` and `(handle, int attribute, int* nowAttribute)`, and the same shape for a glyph, follow the [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/main/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Font/SceFont.Engine.cs) bindings, matching the IDA type database of [Orbital](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/master/tools/ida/db_types.json) and [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/d2413fc2ebd91d1b7234197c2dd5bd48e1cb6a51/src/libs/libFont.cpp#L1249-L1264), not confirmed on a title. Every handle and every glyph keeps one attribute, an opaque int whose meaning and valid values are unknown: define stores the new value and returns the previous one, and get returns the stored value with its `attribute` argument unused, as in KytyPS5. An attribute never set is 0. The null checks and the invalid-object errors follow the other libSceFont functions and diverge from [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/d2413fc2ebd91d1b7234197c2dd5bd48e1cb6a51/src/libs/libFont.cpp#L1251-L1265), which returns `OK` for a null handle or glyph after writing 0 to the old-attribute pointer: every other handle and glyph entry point in this library reports the invalid object instead, and a title that passes one is already failing. shadPS4 leaves both exports unimplemented, so there is no second implementation to compare. PPSA01325 calls the glyph define with 0x11 on a glyph from `sceFontGenerateCharGlyph` that it deletes unused and draws with `sceFontRenderCharGlyphImageHorizontal`; the three bindings all read the third argument as an out pointer, not a value, so this call sets the glyph's attribute to 0x11. text: [libSceFreeType](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceFreeType/src/GuestObjects.cpp) (libSceFreeType) - the guest reads copies of the bundled FreeType's face, size and glyph slot, updated after each call that changes them. Their private fields (`driver`, `memory`, `stream`, `sizes_list`, `extensions`) are null, and `subglyphs` is null whatever `num_subglyphs` reports. The outline points are copied as 64-bit coordinates; changes the guest makes to them and to the outline flags are written back before `FT_Render_Glyph`, while replacing the outline arrays, or a coordinate the host `FT_Pos` cannot hold, throws. `FT_New_Face` resolves the guest path and reads the whole file into memory; on Windows, where FreeType's `long` is 32 bits, a font of 2 GiB or more throws. Libraries and faces are never freed, since `FT_Done_Face` and `FT_Done_FreeType` are not exported. The bundled FreeType's own functions are kept out of the exports with `--exclude-libs` on Windows and Linux only; on macOS they stay exported, so a guest import of another FreeType function could resolve to them instead of failing at start-up

A wait woken by `sceHttpDestroyEpoll`, or by the `sceHttpTerm` that ends the last context, returns 0 events. The epoll calls return `BEFORE_INIT` (0x80431001) while no `sceHttpInit` context is alive and `INVALID_ID` (0x80431100) for an unknown context or handle, and `sceHttpTerm` returns the same errors instead of succeeding for any id. The completion's `event_type` value is unknown and left 0. PPSA17221 completes its request object only after `sceHttp2SendRequestAsync` returns, and its handler for a synchronous failure calls `shared_from_this` before that, so a send must not fail synchronously. PPSA15508 passes null kqueue and extra options at original VA 0xb63931, then calls `sceHttp2WaitAsync` with a 24-byte result and a 2,000,000 timeout, and checks the result at offset 8. A null kqueue option therefore retains the same offline completion for direct waiting without an event notification. The timeout is not used because the offline result is already complete. This path follows the original title call and caller control flow, not a console measurement. A supplied kqueue with a missing user event, an extra option, and a wait with no completed operation still throw

text: [sceImeOpen, sceImeUpdate, sceImeSetText, sceImeSetCaret, sceImeClose](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceIme/Export.cpp) (libSceIme) - the event ids (Open 0, UpdateText 1, UpdateCaret 2, PressClose 4, PressEnter 5), the caret directions (left 1, right 2), the error codes and the text event payload follow the PS4 reimplementation in [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/b72489d8c24e63fc56a29fe2c90120ab768a210d/src/core/libraries/ime/ime.cpp); none is measured on a PS5. Events are queued and delivered by `sceImeUpdate` only when it is passed the handler given to `sceImeOpen`, with that call's `arg`. A text event points `str` at a copy of the text kept in `work`, and `inputTextBuffer` holds the same text; both are terminated, `caret_index` is the caret after the edit and the one edit area has the edit position and the change in UTF-16 units (0 for Enter and Close). An edit sends one UpdateText; a caret move sends one UpdateCaret per UTF-16 unit, as shadPS4 does. Enter inserts a line break with the multiline option and sends PressEnter otherwise; Escape sends PressClose. Typed text is cut to `maxTextLength` without splitting a surrogate pair, line breaks are dropped without the multiline option, and the BasicLatin, URL, mail and number types do not filter characters. `sceImeOpen` checks, in shadPS4's order, the user, type, enter label, input method, option bits (the `sceImeGetPanelSize` mask), `maxTextLength` (1 to 2048), the text buffer, the position (below 1920x1080, or 3840x2160 with the over-2K option), the alignments, the extended priority and reserved bytes, `work` (non-null, 4-byte aligned), the handler, the reserved bytes and the initial text (no unpaired surrogate, no line break without the multiline option); shadPS4's SDK-dependent option, language and extended-option masks and its work-overlap check are not applied, and only the text copy is written to `work`. `sceImeSetText` keeps the caret unless the text became shorter, `sceImeSetCaret` rejects an index past the text with `0x80bc0030`, and neither sends an event. `sceImeSetTextGeometry` accepts any geometry while a panel is open, since no panel is drawn

name: libSceIme.L62
text: [sceImeOpen text filter](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceIme/Export.cpp) (libSceIme) runs on the text edits of host input - typing, backspace, forward delete and a multiline Enter - following [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/1211958b4eb38256cc0c5c7ba92d668820c05389/src/libs/ime.cpp), not confirmed on a PS5. The host input thread only queues the edit under the IME mutex; `sceImeUpdate` applies it on the title's thread, where the filter also runs with the mutex released - like the event handler, so a filter that calls back into `sceIme*` cannot deadlock - and the structural edit and the filtered commit are serialized under the mutex, with a commit after the session closed or reopened dropped by a session id. The filter is guest code and `ImeTextFilter` and `ImeExtKeyboardFilter` are declared `APS5_VABI` like `EventHandler`. The filter is called with the edited text, a buffer of `maxTextLength` UTF-16 units and its length; a nonzero return, an output longer than the capacity, an unpaired surrogate or, without the multiline option, a line break keeps the edit unfiltered. An accepted output replaces the text, the caret stays where the edit put it and is clamped to the text and normalized past a surrogate pair, and one UpdateText is sent with the minimal edit delta of the whole old and new text, as KytyPS5 computes it; an output equal to the previous text sends no event. Caret moves, PressEnter without multiline, PressClose, `sceImeSetText` and `sceImeSetCaret` do not run the filter, as in KytyPS5; a `sceImeSetText` or `sceImeSetCaret` that lands while the filter runs bumps a revision beside the session id, and the filtered commit is dropped when either changed, as KytyPS5 drops the commit when its revision changed, so the title's own text or caret setting wins, the edit is discarded and sends no event. An external keyboard filter is accepted and stored on the session: it is called only for keyboard events that carry key data, which the host input path does not produce - it delivers text and actions, as KytyPS5's host API queues external inputs with a zeroed key and skips the filter for them - so it is never called

name: libSceJobManager.L5
text: [sce::Job::JobManager](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceJobManager/Export.cpp) (libSceJobManager) is written from the disassembly of the copies PPSA01474 and PPSA36082 ship in `sce_module`, and `guest_job_manager_tests` passes against both of those modules as well: the memory size formula, the error codes, sync point ordering, the per-sequence limits and the priority order are the original's. Compute sequences submit through `sceAgcDriverSubmitAcb` on the queue their mask bit selects and are checked the same way by `agc_driver_job_manager_compute_tests`: results, ordering against CPU dispatches and sync points, limits and sizes match the two modules. The command stream is simpler than the original's: every compute dispatch is submitted with its own label write and interrupt, where the original batches the label write and rewinds commands it encoded ahead, and the command buffers and labels live on the host heap. The per-queue command size in `calculateRequiredMemorySize` is a constant (104, 148 and 32 bytes per dispatch, sync point and wait), which is what the original measures by running the builders of this project's libSceAgc. A compute dispatch on a CPU sequence throws (the original does not check), and a failing `sceAgcDriverAddEqEvent` throws. `shutdown` throws while a compute sequence has work in flight, a sequence's label total is written as 32 bits, and since the label is host memory no GPU import covers, the driver drains recorded work before each label write. The manager's state lives on the host heap, with only the block header written to the title's memory; the original keeps everything in that block, and a block smaller than 0x2d8 bytes throws here. The worker sleep policy, the spin count and the persistent thread count are validated and stored but change nothing, a factory priority above 1 throws, `shutdown` throws while a thread is blocked in a sequence wait, and using a sequence after its `destroy` throws. `initialize` returns 0 where the original returns the result of its last import (`BG26hBGiNlw`, not resolved to a name), the `sceRazorCpuJobManager*` profiler calls are not made, and a worker thread that cannot be created or configured throws where the original does not check. The order of the sequence and factory virtual functions is read from the modules' vtables only, since no title that calls them has been run

The handler signatures follow the mangled names. A handler applies to the `Value` it is set on and to the values that `Value` holds then, and `Parser::parse` gives the values it creates the handlers of the `Value` it parses into, since the title reads the errors its handlers record after accessing parsed members; copies, `push_back` and `Object::operator[]` do not carry them, and how the console finds the handler of an accessed value is unknown. A typed getter on a non-null value of another type calls the type mismatch handler with the requested type, the value, null and the context, and returns the value the handler returns if it has the requested type, else the getter's default; passing null as the third handler argument (the second `Value` pointer), and the order of the two `Value` pointers, remain unverified against the console. The element access failure handler is not called: a failed `operator[]` or `getValue` on a value carrying it throws, as the error code the console passes, which the title records as its error, is unknown; without one the access still reaches the null-access callback. The special float handler is not called: serializing a non-finite real throws with or without it, as the `FunctionType` values and the `bool*` output are unknown, and the title's handler returns a different replacement for each of its two types

name: libSceLibcInternal.L13
text: [fdopendir](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceLibcInternal/Directory.cpp) (libSceLibcInternal) follows FreeBSD 11's [`fdopendir`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/lib/libc/gen/opendir.c#L67-L74): it sets `FD_CLOEXEC` on the descriptor first, and the stream starts at the descriptor's current position instead of the first entry. On Windows the stream skips the entries the descriptor's cursor (`lseek` or `getdirentries`) has passed, which assumes that the descriptor and the stream list a directory in the same host order; on Linux the stream is opened on a duplicate of the descriptor, which shares its position. The Linux path is not run by the tests here. As in FreeBSD, a descriptor that is not open fails with `EBADF`, one that is not a directory with `ENOTDIR` (both leave it open, and `FD_CLOEXEC` stays set on the latter), and `closedir` closes it

name: libSceLibcInternal.L14
text: [fstatvfs](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceLibcInternal/FilesystemStatistics.cpp) (libSceLibcInternal) converts `_fstatfs` to the 88-byte `struct statvfs` as FreeBSD 9.2's `sfs2svfs` does (`f_bsize` from the transfer size, `f_frsize` from the block size, `f_favail` equal to `f_ffree`, `f_fsid` 0, `ST_RDONLY` and `ST_NOSUID` only). Differences: `f_namemax` is the `statfs` value, not `fpathconf(_PC_NAME_MAX)`; negative `f_bavail` and `f_ffree` wrap to unsigned without `EOVERFLOW`, as the same-width copy in FreeBSD does; inode counts are 0 on Windows, inherited from `_fstatfs`; a null output returns `EFAULT` after the descriptor is validated, where FreeBSD would fault. Layout and conversion are unverified against the PS5 library (PS5MC imports `fstatvfs` but was not run)

Warnings go to the guest's current `stderr` prefixed with `__progname`, where FreeBSD's `warnx` keeps the `stderr` of its first call. A null `getopt` option string, a null argument vector or argument, a negative `optind` and an `optind` moved inside a pending permutation throw where FreeBSD faults. `getopt_long_only` is not exported. That the console's `libSceLibcInternal` uses this FreeBSD code is unverified
