name: libSceLibcInternal.L15
text: [posix_spawn and posix_spawnp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceLibcInternal/Spawn.cpp) (libSceLibcInternal) create no process. FreeBSD 11.4 returns the error the child's exec leaves ([`_posix_spawn_thr`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/posix_spawn.c#L227-L231), [`do_posix_spawn`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/posix_spawn.c#L295-L303)), and `posix_spawnp` searches `PATH`, or `_PATH_DEFPATH` when it is unset, ending with `ENOENT` when no directory holds the program ([`_execvpe`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/exec.c#L272-L281), [`execvPe`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/exec.c#L257-L260)). So when the program is not in the guest file system both return `ENOENT` and leave the process ID unwritten; when it is there they throw. PPSA99305 (Dusklight) reaches this when SDL looks for `zenity` to show a file dialog. The attributes and file actions are not applied, so one that would fail in the child is not reported, and whether the console's application sandbox lets the child be created at all (FreeBSD returns that error first) is unverified. The attribute and file action calls keep FreeBSD 11.4's objects. Null or uninitialized objects, which FreeBSD dereferences, throw.

text: [sceNetSetsockopt, sceNetGetsockopt](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) (libSceNet) take `SO_SNDTIMEO` and `SO_RCVTIMEO` (0x1005, 0x1006) as a 16-byte `struct timeval`, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`sosetopt` and `sogetopt`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/sys/kern/uipc_socket.c#L2657-L2690) do, and Sony's 0x1105 and 0x1106 as an `int` of microseconds. A [console log of ProsperoLight](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoLight/issues/49) (firmware 12.20) shows receives timing out every 100 ms after it gave 0x1006 a `{0, 100000}` timeval. The errors for a value shorter than a timeval (`EINVAL`) or out of range (`EDOM`), and `sceNetGetsockopt` cutting the timeval to the caller's length, follow FreeBSD's `sooptcopyin` and `sooptcopyout` and are not measured on a console

name: libSceNet.L189
text: [sceNetSetsockopt](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) (libSceNet) stores `SO_ONESBCAST` (`0x10000`, [shadPS4's `ORBIS_NET_SO_ONESBCAST`](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/libraries/net/net_types.h)) per socket and `sceNetGetsockopt` reads back the value that was set, as shadPS4 does; PPSA34501 sets it and crashes later when it fails with `EOPNOTSUPP`. Sends ignore it. FreeBSD 11.4's [ip(4)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?manpath=FreeBSD+11.4-RELEASE&query=ip&sektion=4) documents the like-named `IPPROTO_IP` option `IP_ONESBCAST`: a datagram sent to an interface's directed broadcast address, such as 192.168.2.255, leaves through that interface with its destination rewritten to 255.255.255.255, and only on a socket allowed to set `SO_BROADCAST`. Here host routing selects the outgoing interface and the destination is not rewritten. shadPS4 also leaves sends unchanged, and its [TODO](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/libraries/net/net.cpp#L2467-L2470) reads the option the other way round: a send to 255.255.255.255 would be converted to the interface's broadcast address. Whether the console's `SOL_SOCKET` option behaves like `IP_ONESBCAST`, and what it reads back, is not verified on hardware. FreeBSD 11.4's `sogetopt()` reads several boolean socket options back as their flag bit (`so_options & optname`, `sys/kern/uipc_socket.c`), not as the value set; whether the console does so for `0x10000` is unknown

name: libSceNet.L191
text: [sceNetSetsockopt, sceNetGetsockopt](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) (libSceNet) set `TCP_NODELAY` (`IPPROTO_TCP`, 1) on the host socket of a stream socket and read it back as `TF_NODELAY` (4) or 0, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`tcp_default_ctloutput`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/sys/netinet/tcp_usrreq.c#L1626-L1650) does. Every other `IPPROTO_TCP` option (`TCP_MAXSEG`, `TCP_NOPUSH` and `TCP_KEEPIDLE` among them, which FreeBSD implements) fails with `ENOPROTOOPT`, and the `IPPROTO_TCP` level on a socket that is not a stream socket fails with `EINVAL`, as [`ip_ctloutput`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/sys/netinet/ip_output.c#L943-L944) answers it. A set on a connection that FreeBSD's [`tcp_ctloutput`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.4/sys/netinet/tcp_usrreq.c#L1498-L1502) refuses with `ECONNRESET` (refused, reset or in `TIME_WAIT`) succeeds here because the host accepts it. A null value with a nonzero length fails with `EINVAL`, where FreeBSD's `kern_setsockopt` returns `EFAULT`, and a get into less than an `int` fails with `EINVAL`, where `sooptcopyout` truncates. text: [sceNetRecv, sceNetRecvfrom and sceNetRecvmsg](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) (libSceNet) on a datagram socket with no local address wait on Windows until a bind, connect or send gives it one, checking the host socket every 10 ms. Winsock fails such a receive with `WSAEINVAL`, where FreeBSD 11.4's `soreceive_dgram` waits for a datagram (`sys/kern/uipc_socket.c`). A non-blocking socket fails with `EAGAIN` at once, and the receive timeout ends the wait with `EAGAIN`; when the address comes first, the call waits for a datagram only for what is left of the timeout. A `sceNetShutdown` of the receive side ends the wait and the receive returns 0, and a zero-length receive returns 0 without waiting, as `soreceive_dgram` does when the socket can't receive more or nothing was asked for. An abort or close ends the wait, and the host receive then fails as it did before

Unverified on hardware. Lookups run synchronously over the host resolver, which cannot be interrupted: an abort while a lookup runs on another thread returns at once, and that lookup fails with `EINTR` without writing its output only when the host call returns; the abort flags are then ignored, as shadPS4 does for a running lookup. Unlike shadPS4, which ignores them, other abort flag bits throw, and `sceNetResolverStartNtoaMultipleRecords` throws for any flag, including async (1) and 0x10000 (IP address literals disabled), as `sceNetResolverStartNtoaMultipleRecordsEx` does

text: [MSG_DONTWAIT](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) (libSceNet) - console ordering between competing readers and writers is unmeasured. The per-call behavior follows FreeBSD 11.4's `soreceive_generic` and `sosend_generic` (`sys/kern/uipc_socket.c`); `0x80` is FreeBSD's flag value (`sys/sys/socket.h`). name: libSceNgs2.native.L34
text: [sceNgs2GeomCalcListener](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Geom.cpp) builds an orthonormal world-to-listener transform. The row-major matrix, front-axis priority and flag 1 for right-handed input follow [PS5PCEM](https://github.com/iStark/PS5PCEM/blob/d2534bac6325a2c61c0fa88977e5321074304484/src/hle/ngs2_geom.zig); they have not been measured on PS5 hardware. Velocity stays in world coordinates and positive finite sound speed is preserved. Orientation vectors are normalised and up is made perpendicular to front, so non-unit and slightly tilted vectors are accepted. When front and up are parallel, up is replaced by `(0,1,0)` or `(1,0,0)` so the basis stays defined: PPSA15552 (Dead Cells) passes `orient_front={0,0,1}` with `orient_up={0,0,1}` after moving the listener, which PS5PCEM rejects; the console error code is unknown. Unknown flags, zero orientation vectors, nonfinite input and an unrepresentable translation still throw without changing the output; console error codes are unknown, and a nonpositive sound speed throws where PS5PCEM and [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/df5b9b92be7dfd463b47756b707d6d356a9f0550/src/libs/ngs2.cpp) default it to 343. KytyPS5 always writes the identity matrix, so the transform rests on PS5PCEM plus that Dead Cells case. Dead Cells (PPSA15552) reaches this call after the custom sampler rack in #4334. This does not implement source attenuation, panning or Doppler in `sceNgs2GeomApply`.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L33
text: [sceNgs2GeomResetListenerParam, sceNgs2GeomResetSourceParam](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Geom.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - the structures (12, 16, 16, 60, 96, 108, 32 and 308 bytes) come from [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5)'s `ngs2.cpp` and match [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)'s `ngs2_geom.h` field for field, but only KytyPS5 gives the behaviour - shadPS4 logs and returns success without writing the output. The defaults (orient front +Z, orient up +Y, sound speed 343, cone 1/360/1/360, rolloff 0/1000000/1/1, doppler factor, full-band, LFE and maximum level 1, two speakers and matrix format 2) are unverified on a PS5 title; KytyPS5 and iStark/PS5PCEM agree on them. PPSA15552 (Dead Cells) calls `sceNgs2GeomResetSourceParam` after creating its racks. A null output address returns `INVALID_OUT_ADDRESS` as elsewhere in the library rather than throwing as KytyPS5 does. `sceNgs2GeomApply` is now a minimal pass-through that follows [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5)'s `Ngs2GeomApply` (shadPS4 only stubs it): pitch 1, source position, volume the larger of the source minimum and maximum level, and a diagonal of the source maximum level (1 when it is not positive) over `matrix_format` channels (0 is two, at most 8). The listener and `flags` are ignored, so source attenuation, distance rolloff, panning and Doppler stay unimplemented; neither KytyPS5 nor this has been measured on a PS5, and a null output address returns `INVALID_OUT_ADDRESS` where KytyPS5 exits

name: libSceNgs2.native.L26
text: [sceNgs2SystemSetSampleRate, sceNgs2SystemSetUserData, sceNgs2SystemGetUserData, sceNgs2SystemLock, sceNgs2SystemUnlock](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/System.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - shadPS4 only checks the system handle (`INVALID_SYSTEM_HANDLE`) and SharpProspero names what each call does; neither gives the other limits. A sample rate of 0 and a null user data pointer throw, any other rate is accepted, and changing the rate while a sampler filter is enabled throws because the filter coefficients were computed for the old rate. `sceNgs2SystemLock` and `sceNgs2SystemUnlock` follow [prosper's notes](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper/blob/d61eb2c0ad2de879ef74df9c4aa050c512804a18/prosper/src/hle/audio/hle_audio.cpp#L4367-L4384) on the PS5 module: Lock takes a per-system lock and counts nested holds, Unlock releases one hold from any thread and returns 0 without a hold, and `sceNgs2SystemRender` only tries the lock: while another thread holds it, Render clears one grain of each output, leaves the render count and voices unchanged and returns 0. The other calls do not wait for the system lock. Peace Walker (PPSA18216) holds it while it spins on a flag that its audio thread clears only after `sceNgs2SystemRender` and eight `sceNgs2VoiceGetStateFlags` calls, so on the console neither can wait for it. Whether the console's voice and rack calls take the lock at all is not known. `sceNgs2RackLock` still holds the library's lock until `sceNgs2RackUnlock`, as before

name: libSceNgs2.native.L40
text: [NGS2 rack lock and voice callbacks](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Rack.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - `sceNgs2RackLock` gives the calling thread the rack, nested. Rack locks, renders and rack or system destroys exclude each other across threads and systems, including during a render's voice callbacks; a thread nests them, also from its own callbacks, and a callback that waits for another thread's rack lock or render never returns. Other NGS2 calls from other threads go ahead, and a block-end or repeat callback runs with the internal lock released. The console's behaviour for other threads' calls during a rack lock is not measured. PPSA36591 holds a rack lock on its main thread while it waits for one of its own locks, held by a thread in `sceNgs2VoiceGetStateFlags`; it froze while the rack lock held the internal lock. `sceNgs2RackUnlock` of a rack this thread has not locked returns `0x804A8202`; the console code is unknown. UserFx process handlers keep the internal lock.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L18
text: [NGS2 streaming PCM waveforms](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - PPSA21402 streams its music by adding one block whose `num_samples` is the whole track and whose `data_size` is a 16 KiB first piece, with `CONTINUE`, and then adds each following piece with flag `0x2` (called `APPEND` here) and the same `num_samples`. No reference describes flag `0x2`. A 16-bit PCM block without skipped samples or repeats whose `num_samples` exceed its data is assumed to start such a stream; flag `0x2` is assumed to append the block's data to the last streaming block, ignoring its `num_samples`; the voice is assumed to output silence without advancing while it has played all appended data and `CONTINUE` is set; and the waveform is assumed to end at `num_samples` or, once `CONTINUE` is cleared, at the end of the appended data. `sceNgs2VoiceGetState` reports the bytes played as `decoded_data_size`, which the title uses to release its queued data, and the read position as `waveform_data`. Appending to a block that is not a stream, or other formats, skipped samples, repeats and partial frames, throw

name: libSceNgs2.native.L10
text: [NGS2 ATRAC9 waveform loops](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Atrac9.cpp) accepts one integer forward `smpl` loop. Inclusive RIFF endpoints and encoder-delay adjustment follow [vgmstream riff.c](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream/blob/7dc938fa2f210943b37c7b6511852b516ef432ab/src/meta/riff.c). PPSA03747 supplies a 60-byte sampler chunk with one loop, `samplerData` 24, start 256, inclusive end 299224 and delay 256 for 298969 audible samples. The chunk size and loop count bound the records; `samplerData` is not interpreted. Output positions are assumed to use audible samples and an exclusive end. Blocks split into an optional intro, a repeated range and an optional tail; zero play count means infinite repeats, positive play count includes the first pass. ATRAC9 ranges include a preceding codec frame for decoder history. The output block layout, repeat-count mapping and error codes are unverified on hardware. Multiple, reverse, alternating and fractional loops throw.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L11
text: [NGS2 submixer UserFx](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Custom.cpp) (control `0x20000004`) invokes the title's callback after input mixing on every playing grain, including silence. The 40-byte control and 48-byte process context follow [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/945dbc3cc3eee80ac3e053b438502ed936fa6bb2/src/core/libraries/ngs2/ngs2_submixer.h). PPSA03747 installs a peak-meter callback; its code confirms the channel pointers, user data 0, channel count, grain size and sample-rate offsets and returns 0. Other user data words are preserved. Flags are assumed to be 1 after registration/restart and 0 thereafter, following UserFx2's first-process convention; this callback does not inspect them. Null handlers disable the effect, setup clears it, and nonzero callback results throw. These lifecycle and error semantics are unverified on console hardware.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L12
text: [NGS2 voice callback after setup](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - a sampler or mixer setup clears the voice callback with the rest of the voice state. PPSA18216 registers a block-end callback for a streamed music voice, later sets the same voice up again for one-shot ATRAC9 blocks with user data 0, and registers the callback again before it streams again; its callback dereferences the block's user data, so it must not run for the one-shot blocks. A setup made from inside the voice's own callback clears that callback as well, so a callback that sets its voice up again and queues the next block runs once instead of for every block; PPSA18216 never sets a voice up from inside its callback, so that ordering is unverified. Unverified on console hardware.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L13
text: [NGS2 ATRAC9 streaming](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Atrac9.cpp) keeps waveform duration and skip counts across compressed input blocks. The shared `APPEND` flag (2), called `ONLY_DATA` in the compressed-data reference, ignores an ATRAC9 continuation block's sample, skip and repeat counts, following [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/bb98f26433fa9e711c219aac1711fe8ecba5bf3a/src/libs/ngs2.cpp); PPSA03747 confirms a 262044-byte initial buffer declaring 11310532 samples, followed by 16384-byte buffers with flags 3. Incomplete superframes are retained until more input arrives. Input-block completion callbacks allow refills; the final callback of a logical waveform waits for its buffered PCM to drain, preserving the existing complete-block repeat behaviour. This buffering, callback timing, decoded-byte accounting and starvation silence are unverified on hardware. A closed ATRAC9 stream ending before its declared samples throws; fragmented ATRAC9 waveforms with repeats are unsupported. PCM streaming retains its existing append validation and early-close behaviour.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L14
text: [NGS2 mastering voice gain](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - the param id 0x30000004 is taken from PPSA22520 and the layout from [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)'s `OrbisNgs2MasteringVoiceGainParam`; no reference gives the units or range. The levels are assumed to be linear factors applied when the mastering voice is mixed into the render buffer, so the voice's own samples stay unscaled; the LFE level applies to channel 3 of 6- and 8-channel voices, assuming the L R C LFE order of the AudioOut2 entries above, and the full-band level to the rest. Negative levels are accepted, and a new setup resets both levels to 1

name: libSceNgs2.native.L15
text: [NGS2 stereo mastering voice into a surround buffer](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Render.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - PPSA21402 renders a 2-channel mastering voice into a 6- or 8-channel render buffer, which the mixing stage rejected. The console's conversion is unknown: the left and right channels are assumed to go to the first two buffer channels (front left and right) and the remaining channels stay silent, with no centre, LFE or surround content. Any other channel count mismatch still throws

name: libSceNgs2.native.L16
text: [NGS2 voices without a format](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - a sampler voice whose setup has no format (all zero) accepts an add of no waveform blocks without `APPEND`, which only applies `RESET` and the `CONTINUE` state, and matrix levels with no levels, which clear that matrix. PPSA36591 sets such a voice up, adds no blocks and sets no levels when a button is pressed at its title screen. Whether the console returns success or an error there is not measured; blocks with data, `APPEND` and an empty matrix on a voice with a format are still refused

name: libSceNgs2.native.L17
text: [NGS2 silent waveform blocks](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native): flag `0x10` (named `SILENCE` here; no public reference names it) lets a waveform block declare samples without data. PPSA04867 adds one block with flags `0x11`, `data_size` 0 and `num_samples` 16385, then another with flags `0x11` and a fully specified 0x800-byte, 1024-sample mono block, which takes the ordinary path. A dataless block under the flag outputs `num_samples` frames of silence, reports them through `decoded_data_size`, and finishes like a complete block; a dataless block without the flag still throws as not fitting its data. The flag's real name, its interaction with ATRAC9 and repeats, and the console's `waveform_data` for silent blocks are unverified on hardware

name: libSceNgs2.native.L21
text: [NGS2 port matrix](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Render.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - a port without a matrix, or with a selected matrix whose levels were never set, mixes through a default channel map: mono reaches both stereo channels at -3 dB and the 5.1 and 7.1 centre, stereo folds to mono at -3 dB per side, and wider sources fold down with 0.5 and -3 dB gains. The map and the equivalence of an unset matrix with no matrix were measured from the PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`, not yet from the PS5 library. That library only accepts submixer and mastering voices with 1, 2, 6 or 8 channels, so the map into 3, 4, 5 or 7 channels throws. A matrix set with fewer levels than the destination needs still mixes only the rows it has

name: libSceNgs2.native.L23
text: [NGS2 custom module ids](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Custom.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - a custom rack with a module id other than 0x13 (sampler rack), 0x1d and 0x1f (submixer rack) throws. Trails in the Sky 2nd Chapter (PPSA35169) creates a rack with module id 0x20 (`NGS2: custom module id 0x20 is not implemented`, #4246); which module it is, and its structure, are unknown.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L24
text: [NGS2 reverb rack](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Reverb.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native, rack 0x2001) - follows the PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`, read and checked against its output at 11.025 to 48 kHz, including parameter changes during playback (differences at float rounding level); not yet compared with the PS5 library. Structure layouts come from [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)'s `ngs2_reverb.h` and the param ids 0x20010000 (setup) and 0x20010001 (I3DL2) from PPSA22520. Only the default `reverb_size` of 1 is handled, with its 14400-sample reflection buffer; other sizes and the library's half-rate mode throw. System sample rates below about 7.5 kHz, where an allpass delay would have no samples, throw. Setup only accepts equal input and output channel counts

name: libSceNgs2.native.L31
text: [sceNgs2VoiceControl sampler filter](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - param `0x1000000a`, its layout and meaning follow KytyPS5 only: location 1 type 1 is an RBJ low-pass biquad at the system sample rate after resampling, scaled by `level`, a set `channel_mask` bit bypasses that channel, type 0 turns the filter off. Other locations and types throw. The voice keeps playing a filter tail after its last block until the history is zero, with outputs below 1e-20 flushed to zero (a KytyPS5 choice); the console's tail length is unknown

name: libSceNgs2.native.L32
text: [sceNgs2PanInit / sceNgs2PanGetVolumeMatrix](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Pan.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - follow the PS4 firmware 11.00 `libSceNgs2.sprx`, read and checked against its output for 2, 4, 5 and 7 speakers into 1, 2, 6 and 8 channels; not yet confirmed on the PS5 library. Speakers are taken in the order L R, L R Ls Rs, L R C Ls Rs or L R C Ls Rs Lb Rb and kept in a fixed circular order, not sorted; without angles the defaults are 90/270, 40/110/250/320, 0/40/110/250/320 and 0/40/110/150/210/250/320 degrees. As in that library, defaults converted to radians keep the wrap-around entry in degrees, so angles past the last speaker pan almost fully to it. Error codes are not known for the PS5, so invalid arguments throw, including a speaker angle equal to the unit angle, on which that library loops forever. Angles so large that adding or subtracting a turn leaves them unchanged throw for the same reason

name: libSceNgs2.native.L35
text: [NGS2 custom sampler rack](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Custom.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native, rack 0x4001) - implements bounded support for the custom sampler rack and its built-in module 0x13 (Custom Voice Filter), unblocking PPSA15552 (Dead Cells) startup. Structure layouts come from [shadPS4's ngs2_custom.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/main/src/core/libraries/ngs2/ngs2_custom.h) (OrbisNgs2CustomVoiceFilterParam, 40 bytes) and live trace correlation from [prosper's hle_audio.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mattias800/prosper/main/prosper/src/hle/audio/hle_audio.cpp) (0x40001300 command and parameters like 10000.0f and 0.707f). Routes parameter updates via the 0x40001300 command family into the Biquad filter engine. Filter type 0 clears the destination filter; type 1 configures the RBJ low-pass biquad frequency, Q and level. Other filter types and unmodeled configurations throw.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L36
text: [sceNgs2VoiceGetState custom sampler](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native, rack 0x4001) - only the size and one field come from a title. PPSA15552 (Dead Cells) calls it on custom sampler voices with a 48-byte buffer at two sites (eboot `0x1740f90`, `0x1741009`) and reads only the 64-bit value at offset 16: the first site keeps it and the second subtracts the kept value, so it is filled with the voice's decoded sample count. Other sizes return `INVALID_OUT_SIZE` as for the other racks. The state flags fill the common voice state; the remaining fields stay zero. shadPS4's `OrbisNgs2CustomSamplerVoiceState` is about 80 bytes and does not match the size this title passes, so the field names and the console's value are unverified

name: libSceNgs2.native.L41
text: [sceNgs2RackGetVoiceHandle voice index](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Rack.cpp) (libSceNgs2.native) - an index at or beyond the rack's voice count returns `0x804A8305` and leaves the output handle untouched, after the null-output and rack-handle checks that keep their order and codes. The value is read from the PS5 `libSceNgs2.native.sprx` export `MwmHz8pAdAo` (firmware 10.01 at `0x11f10`, 12.70 at `0x12130`, and every module from 1.00 to 12.70 checked in [#5916](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/5916#issuecomment-6172832590)): an index at or past the rack's voice count returns it through the same error helper that answers `0x804A8010` for a null output, and the output handle is written only on success. The rack is checked before the output pointer, and an invalid rack returns `0x804A8202`. Heretic + Hexen (PPSA26525), DOOM + DOOM II (PPSA21444) and STAR WARS: Dark Forces Remaster (PPSA19728) create a one-voice reverb rack, take voice 0 and ask for voices 1 to 3 at start-up, log the failures and go on

name: libSceNgs2.native.L5
text: [NGS2 voice validation](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Voice.cpp) returns `0x804A8203` for an invalid voice in Control, RunCommands, GetState, GetStateFlags, GetPortInfo and QueryInfo, following the type-4 handle error in [prosper's PS5 module analysis](https://github.com/mattias800/prosper/blob/d61eb2c0ad2de879ef74df9c4aa050c512804a18/prosper/src/hle/audio/hle_audio.cpp#L4478). Control checks a null parameter list first (`0x804A8360`); GetState resolves the voice before output validation, and GetState rejects sizes below 8 before a null output. Existing rack-specific exact state sizes, other argument precedence and command layouts are retained; arbitrary-sized state copies and full console behavior remain unverified. These values follow module analysis, not new console execution.

name: libSceNgs2.native.L9
text: [NGS2 render buffer capacity](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNgs2.native/src/Render.cpp) is treated as available storage for one configured grain. PPSA01880 passes 303104 bytes for 256 stereo float frames (2048 bytes); rendering writes or clears only those frames and preserves the remaining capacity. Non-null silent outputs now undergo the same supported-format and minimum-size checks as audible outputs, with channel counts limited to 1 through 8. Unused null outputs remain ignored. The console's handling of surplus capacity and invalid silent output descriptors has not been measured; invalid descriptors throw rather than return guessed SDK errors.

text: [NP state callbacks](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpManager/Export.cpp) (libSceNpManager) - the registration rules are [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L857-L901)'s: `sceNpRegisterStateCallbackA` keeps up to 8 callbacks and returns the slot plus 1, a null callback returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a callback already registered `CALLBACK_ALREADY_REGISTERED` and a ninth one `CALLBACK_MAX` (0x8055001D, [np_error.h](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_error.h#L38)); `sceNpUnregisterStateCallbackA` returns `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an id outside 1..8 and `CALLBACK_NOT_REGISTERED` for an empty slot; the legacy [sceNpRegisterStateCallback](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L981-L1005) keeps one callback with the same errors. Each registration gets `SIGNED_OUT` for the initial user (0x10000000) once, from the next `sceNpCheckCallback` on the calling thread. For the A form this follows [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/9e41d8320a2774b303fbad344c2347e8d0292e83/src/libs/network.cpp#L3959-L3974), whose [sceNpRegisterStateCallbackA](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/9e41d8320a2774b303fbad344c2347e8d0292e83/src/libs/network.cpp#L4021-L4034) marks the registration pending. KytyPS5 never calls the legacy callback ([sceNpRegisterStateCallback](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/9e41d8320a2774b303fbad344c2347e8d0292e83/src/libs/network.cpp#L4009-L4019) stores nothing); it is called as `(user, SIGNED_OUT, nullptr, userdata)`, as in shadPS4, which passes an NpId only for `SIGNED_IN` ([L823](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L823), [L938-L940](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L938-L940)). shadPS4 instead queues `SIGNED_OUT` from the user service login event and delivers it from `sceNpCheckCallback` ([DispatchPendingNpStateCallbacks](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L903-L962)); the reachability callback is not given an initial `UNAVAILABLE`, unlike that function ([L922-L961](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/15abf68c9b52c4b04d094f2837719fdb871021f3/src/core/libraries/np/np_manager.cpp#L922-L961)). A callback being delivered when another thread unregisters it is still called once. When and how often the console calls the state callbacks, and the errors, are not measured

name: libSceNpTrophy2.L19
text: [Damaged records](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TrophyStore.cpp): a line in `_trophy/<user id>_<service label>.txt` or `.stats.txt` that is not a new `<id> <value>` pair (a blank line, a carriage return, a repeated or negative id, a value that is not a number) makes `readRecord` throw a `std::runtime_error` that names the file and the line. Every call that reads that record then throws it instead of returning, which stops the title as any throwing export does, so the title gets no return value; main returned 0 from these calls. The failed read is not kept, so each later call reads the file again and throws again until the file is fixed or deleted. The unlock record is read by `sceNpTrophy2GetTrophyInfo`, `sceNpTrophy2GetTrophyInfoArray` and `sceNpTrophy2GetGameInfo` for a created context, by `sceNpTrophy2GetGroupInfo` and `sceNpTrophy2GetGroupInfoArray` when the title's trophy data is loaded, by a `sceNpUniversalDataSystemPostEvent` of an `_UnlockTrophy` that the trophy data does not refuse, and by a statistic change when the trophy data is loaded; the stat record by a `sceNpUniversalDataSystemPostEvent` of an event that a statistics rule copies and by the trophy queries of a progressive trophy with a statistic. What the console does with a damaged record is not known.

name: libSceNpTrophy2.L15
text: [Trophy queries](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TrophyInfo.cpp) report the title's [trophy data](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TrophyPackage.cpp) (`sce_sys/trophy2/trophyNN.ucp`) and the unlocks in the [trophy store](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TrophyStore.cpp). Without the file, or when it is malformed, they report the old placeholders and `sceNpTrophy2GetTrophyInfoArray` lists only trophy 0. Icons are not read. Hidden trophies report their names and descriptions; whether the console blanks them before the unlock is not known. `progress_percentage` weighs gold 6, silver 2 and bronze 1 and leaves the platinum out, as KytyPS5 does (the ratio of the published PSN trophy points); the console's formula is not known. A trophy or group that is not in the file throws. A context that was not created or was destroyed reports placeholders and no unlocks and returns success; the console's errors for it are unknown.

name: libSceNpTrophy2.L18
text: [Platinum](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TitleTrophies.cpp): an unlock through any path unlocks the platinum that the trophy names in `platinumTrophyId` once every trophy naming that platinum is unlocked, as KytyPS5 does; trophies without `platinumTrophyId` are not required. With the title's trophy data loaded, a posted `_UnlockTrophy` of a trophy that is not in the data, of a platinum or of a progressive trophy is not stored and prints a `[trophy] ignored` line, as KytyPS5 refuses them, so a progressive trophy unlocks only through its statistic; without trophy data any id of 0 or more is stored, including ids the data would make the platinum, a progressive trophy or no trophy, and the platinum is not unlocked when the trophies it needs are. The console's behaviour is not known.

text: [Events](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpUniversalDataSystem/src/Event.cpp): `sceNpUniversalDataSystemCreateEvent` copies `prop` and returns the event's own property object through `prop_ptr`, as [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/9e41d8320a2774b303fbad344c2347e8d0292e83/src/libs/libTrophy.cpp) does; `sceNpUniversalDataSystemEventPropertyObjectSetObject`, `SetArray` and the array setters for objects and arrays store a copy of `value` and return the stored copy through `value_ptr`. Destroying a property object or array that its Create function did not return (an event's property object or a stored copy) does nothing, as its owner frees it. These ownership rules are not verified on a console, nor are the output of `sceNpUniversalDataSystemEventToString` (still `{}`) and `sceNpUniversalDataSystemEventEstimateSize` (still 3).

name: libSceNpUniversalDataSystem.L9
text: [Trophy events](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpUniversalDataSystem/src/Event.cpp): `sceNpUniversalDataSystemPostEvent` stores an `_UnlockTrophy` event with an int32 `_trophy_id` of 0 or more as an unlock for the user and service label of its context, as KytyPS5 does, except an id that [libSceNpTrophy2](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TrophyStore.cpp) refuses when the title's trophy data is loaded (one not in the data, a platinum or a progressive trophy). `_UpdateTrophyProgress`, named only by a third-party unlocker, is logged once per trophy and not interpreted. A context need not be registered, and every post of an event that `sceNpUniversalDataSystemCreateEvent` returned and that is not yet destroyed returns success (a null or any other event pointer stops the game): KytyPS5's errors for an unknown or unregistered context and for a malformed unlock are not verified. The storage statistics stay zero.

name: libSceNpUniversalDataSystem.L10
text: [Statistics](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpUniversalDataSystem/src/Event.cpp): every other event goes through the title's rules in `sce_sys/uds/udsNN.ucp`, which [libSceNpTrophy2](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNpTrophy2/src/TitleTrophies.cpp) reads. Only statistics with `"aggregation":"latest"` and `dataType` `uint32` or `uint64` are kept, as in KytyPS5; no public source documents the other aggregations or types, so their definitions and rules are skipped. Only rules whose condition is an `eventName` alone and whose input is a `$.name` path (dotted for nested objects) are applied. A value is used when it is an integer of any width that is not negative and fits the statistic's type and `minValue`/`maxValue`; KytyPS5 requires the statistic's exact width, and whether the console converts, clamps or rejects other values is not known. Statistics are stored per user and service label, and every trophy's `unlockCondition` is compared after each event that sets one.

name: libSceOpusDec.L10
text: [sceOpusDecDecode](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceOpusDec/Export.cpp) (libSceOpusDec) returns exactly the packet's duration, as libopus does. FFmpeg resamples narrowband SILK from 8 kHz and holds back 24 samples of the first narrowband packet after the decoder starts or after a packet of another bandwidth, releasing them with the next packet that is not narrowband. The decoder keeps FFmpeg's output in order and pads the start with silence, so such a packet begins with 24 samples (0.5 ms) of silence and the output after it is 24 samples late; libopus has no such gap

name: libSceOpusDec.L11
text: [sceOpusDecDecode](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceOpusDec/include/OpusDecoder.hpp) (libSceOpusDec, libSceOpusCeltDec) decodes at 48000 Hz and converts to a lower creation rate with FFmpeg's resampler, where libopus decodes at that rate directly. The resampler's filter delay is padded with silence at the start of the stream like the narrowband delay above, so the output is late by that delay and is not sample-identical to libopus; which of the two the console matches is not measured

name: libSceOpusDec.L9
text: [libSceOpusDec](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceOpusDec/Export.cpp) uses FFmpeg for mono/stereo signed-16 decoding at the creation rates the research lists: 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000 and 48000 Hz. The six signatures, 640-byte opaque state allocation and byte-count return follow [public PS5 decoder research](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-hardware-audio-decoding/blob/26be5a12f92b2cdc67f8a9e082fd69ae0e9a35a2/docs/DECODING.md#direct-opus-abi) and [ProsperoRadio](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoRadio/blob/2c4029c3a8f43e9e1dfef98374d94d99b14d745d/src/opus_decoder.cpp). Console PCM equivalence and error codes are unverified. Other sample rates, packet loss concealment, invalid inputs and termination with live decoders throw. Context identifiers and host decoder state are private registries; the firmware's opaque state layout and error recovery are unknown.

text: [libScePlayGo](../../../core/libs/prx/libScePlayGo/Export.cpp) - the chunk set comes from `playgo-chunkdefs.xml` (every listed chunk plus chunks 0 through the default chunk), otherwise from `sce_sys/playgo-chunk.dat`, whose `plgx` header is read as holding the chunk count as a 16-bit value at offset 0x0A and ids 0 to count - 1 are taken as valid. The field was identified on four dumps, where exactly that many 0x20-byte entries follow from offset 0x100 (RIDE 4 PPSA01599: 35, Persona 5 Royal PPSA05110: 25, LEGO Horizon Adventures PPSA14632 and Kena PPSA01802: 1); the rest of the format is not decoded and ids are assumed to be contiguous. Every listed chunk is reported as installed (`LOCAL_FAST`). Without either file, a package with `sce_sys/playgo-scenario.json` (PPSA01748, whose dump lists no chunks) accepts every chunk id as installed, and `scePlayGoGetChunkId` lists ids 0 to 999. A title that builds its set of installed chunks from that list skips any chunk it does not see. The console's chunk limit is not known here, and a package with more chunks would see ids from 1000 up as not listed. A package with no `playgo-*` file in `sce_sys` (PPSA03001, PPSA03490 and PPSA01285 here) accepts chunk 0; querying any other id throws with a message naming the missing `playgo-chunk.dat` and `playgo-scenario.json`, since the incomplete dump cannot establish whether that id exists; `APS5_PLAYGO_UNLISTED_CHUNKS=installed` answers every such id as installed (`LOCAL_FAST`, which PPSA15388 needs to load its saves) and `=absent` answers `SCE_PLAYGO_ERROR_BAD_CHUNK_ID` (which ends PPSA03001's id walk), as the user's choice for that dump. A `sce_sys` that holds other `playgo-*` files (`playgo-ficm.dat`, `playgo-hash-table.dat`) without `playgo-chunk.dat` or `playgo-scenario.json`, or a `playgo-chunk.dat` without a `plgx` header and a nonzero count, throws naming the file, because no such dump is known. These answers are unverified on a console, as is the console's answer for an id outside a package's chunk table.

The console also writes `currentContexts` and the allocator counters when the byte count is smaller than their offset; only the requested bytes are written here.

Signatures follow [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/60977b29103452b9681ae10c7a9011d44965bf16/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Net/Http.cs#L195-L252), which also says the socket stays open after `sceSslDeleteConnection`. The behaviour below was measured on a PS5 on system software 13.40 with a ps5-payload-dev payload (every call printed with its return, a TLS 1.2 test server on the LAN presenting leaves issued by the test fixture root loaded with `sceSslLoadCert`, from an elfldr process rather than a title); what differs for a title process is unknown. An unknown context returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID` (0x8095F006) from `sceSslCreateConnection`, and every connection call on an unknown or deleted connection id or on a connection whose context was terminated returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID`. `sceSslCreateConnection` returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` (0x8095F007) for a null host and does not check the socket: `sceSslConnect` on a descriptor that is not a socket returns `SCE_NET_ERROR_EBADF` (0x80410109). `sceSslConnect` runs a TLS 1.2 client handshake with Mbed TLS 3.6.7 over the host socket that the guest number maps to in the libkernel or libSceNet socket table, and `sceSslRead` and `sceSslWrite` carry application data over it. TLS 1.3 is compiled out: the console offers TLS 1.2 only (its ClientHello carries 12 suites and no supported_versions extension) and a TLS 1.3-only server gets `SSL_ERROR_FATAL_ALERT` (0x8095F010) from it, as from this build. Connection state is allocated from the context's pool and returned to it by `sceSslDeleteConnection`; a connection keeps the pool alive after `sceSslTerm`, whose connections return `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID` from then on. The console's pool use for one connection with a two-certificate chain peaked at 80,544 bytes in a 256 KiB pool (5,568 after `sceSslInit`, 12,000 after loading one CA); a 16 KiB pool fails the connect with `SSL_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` (0x809517D5) there and here. The server's chain is checked against the CAs loaded with `sceSslLoadCert`, the host name the connection was created with (case-insensitively; an IP literal sends no SNI and matches an IP subject alternative name; an empty host sends an empty SNI and fails `CN_CHECK`) and, when enabled, its validity dates, and `sceSslConnect` returns the first failure the connection's verify options select (the verify option entry below lists the bits, codes and initial options); no root bundle is shipped and the console's built-in roots are unknown, so with no CA loaded a connection with the initial options returns `SSL_ERROR_UNKNOWN_CA` (0x8095F00C), as on the console. A client certificate loaded with `sceSslLoadCert` is sent when the server asks for one. A failed verification is final: close_notify is sent, later `sceSslConnect` calls return the same code (also after the `WANT_POLLIN` rounds of a non-blocking socket), and `sceSslRead` and `sceSslWrite` throw, as the console's codes for them were not measured. With a verify callback set it is called once after the handshake, outside the connection's lock, with the context id, the bits of the enabled checks that failed (`KNOWN_CA_CHECK` 0x20, `CN_CHECK` 0x4, the date checks when enabled, 0 when the chain passed), handles to a copy of the peer chain as received (the leaf first, the root last when the server sent it) that the certificate readers of the connection's context accept until the connection is deleted (the handles stay registered in the context until it is terminated; the console frees them at the delete), the chain length and the user argument. A chain fault that no option names (`SSL_ERROR_INVALID_CERT` without a callback) throws when a callback is set, as the bits the console passes for it were not measured. A non-negative return accepts the connection whatever the bits were; a negative return fails the connect with `SSL_ERROR_APPLICATION_VERIFICATION_CALLBACK_CHECK` (0x8095F0FD) and the callback runs again, with the same chain, from every later `sceSslConnect`, `sceSslRead` and `sceSslWrite` of the connection, which return 0x8095F0FD while it keeps refusing and proceed once it accepts. A `sceSslConnect` from inside the callback, or from another thread while it runs, throws. `sceSslRead` and `sceSslWrite` before `sceSslConnect` run the handshake and verification themselves and return its code when it fails. A non-blocking socket that would block returns `SSL_ERROR_WANT_POLLIN` (0x8095F013) or `SSL_ERROR_WANT_POLLOUT` (0x8095F014) from `sceSslConnect`, `sceSslRead` and `sceSslWrite`; the next `sceSslConnect` resumes the handshake, and `sceSslWrite` returns the part it sent before blocking (the console returned 32 KiB of a 64 KiB write). A blocking libSceNet socket whose `SO_RCVTIMEO` expires returns `SSL_ERROR_WANT_POLLIN` as well, and the call can be repeated; `SSL_ERROR_READ_TIMEOUT` (0x80951710) is never returned. libkernel keeps its timeouts above the host socket, so they do not bound SSL reads and writes on a libkernel socket. `sceSslRead` with flags 0 reads until `len` bytes arrived or the stream ended and with any other flags (`MsgFlagPartialRead` 1 measured, 2 behaved the same) returns what the first record delivers; a non-blocking read that got some bytes returns them. It returns 0 after the server's close_notify and after a transport that ends without one, every later read 0 again, and `SSL_ERROR_EOF` (0x8095177C) and `SSL_ERROR_SOCKET_CLOSED` (0x8095170D) never from a read. A reset (`ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, `WSAECONNRESET`, `WSAECONNABORTED`, `WSAENETRESET`) returns `SCE_NET_ERROR_ECONNRESET` (0x80410136) from `sceSslRead` and `SCE_NET_ERROR_EPIPE` (0x80410120) from `sceSslWrite`, on every later call too; a record that fails its MAC returns 0x80951D55 from `sceSslRead` after the fatal alert goes out. `sceSslWrite` accepts flags 0 only, `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` otherwise, sends all of `len`, capped at `INT_MAX`, and returns the count; it keeps writing after the peer's close_notify or a stream that ended without one, as the console does. A fatal alert during the handshake returns `SSL_ERROR_FATAL_ALERT` and ends the transport: later `sceSslConnect` calls return 0, `sceSslRead` 0 and `sceSslWrite` `SSL_ERROR_SOCKET_CLOSED`, as measured. A transport that ends without close_notify or a reset during the handshake returns `SSL_ERROR_SOCKET_CLOSED`, the session is dropped and the next `sceSslConnect` starts over; those two handshake cases and `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_CERT` (0x8095F00A) for a verification failure no option names were not measured. Other handshake and socket failures, a read or write after a failed verification, a write after `sceSslClose`, a null buffer and a read or write from inside the callback throw, as their console codes are unknown. A connection serializes its reads and writes, so a read blocked in one thread holds back a write on the same connection from another. `sceSslDeleteConnection` sends no close_notify and returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID` when repeated. `sceSslTerm` leaves the context's connections to `sceSslDeleteConnection`, which then returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID`; a second `sceSslTerm` returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID` and `sceSslInit` with a pool size of 0 returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EINVAL` (0x80020016). `sceSslSetVerifyCallback` accepts any callback, null included, and returns 0. The console's first `sceSslConnect` in a process took 23.8 s before its ClientHello left, a one-time initialisation not emulated. `SSL_ERROR_BEFORE_INIT` (0x8095F001) is never returned, as the library keeps no state apart from its contexts

The verify options select which verification failures `sceSslConnect` reports (see the connection entry above), with the bit values SharpProspero's `SceSslVerifyOption` gives: `SERVER_VERIFY` 0x1, `CN_CHECK` 0x4, `NOT_AFTER_CHECK` 0x8, `NOT_BEFORE_CHECK` 0x10, `KNOWN_CA_CHECK` 0x20. The initial options are `SERVER_VERIFY`, `CN_CHECK` and `KNOWN_CA_CHECK` (0x25): the console accepted an expired and a not-yet-valid server certificate until 0x8 or 0x10 was enabled, which then returned `SSL_ERROR_NOT_AFTER_CHECK` (0x8095F00D) and `SSL_ERROR_NOT_BEFORE_CHECK` (0x8095F00E); whether 0x2 (`CLIENT_VERIFY`) starts enabled was not determined and it is kept off. A check that is disabled is not reported, whatever the chain. Bits outside 0x3F return `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` (0x8095F007) from both calls. Disabling 0x1, 0x4 or 0x20 from the payload stopped its process through the kernel's debug exception path (`mDBG: Sending signal ... signo: 0xa0020101`, 6 of 6 attempts; disabling 0x2, 0x8 and 0x10 returned 0), so whether a title may clear them is unknown; this build clears them, as titles import the call. `sceSslSetMinSslVersion` accepts the `SceSslVersion` values 2 (SSL 3.0) to 5 (TLS 1.2) and returns `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` for 0, 1 and anything above 5; the console has no TLS 1.3 value. Every accepted value gives the same handshake, as Mbed TLS 3 speaks TLS 1.2 and nothing older and TLS 1.3 is compiled out, which matches the console offering TLS 1.2 only. `sceSslSetAlpn` stores the string up to its terminator, split on commas into the protocols offered in the handshake (the console sent `h2,http/1.1` as the two names and a wire-format string as one name), a second call replaces the list, an empty string returns `SSL_ERROR_BAD_LENGTH` (0x80951773), and a null list throws (not measured). `sceSslGetAlpnSelected` returns the protocol the server selected, still after `sceSslClose`, or null before the handshake and when none was selected; the pointer is owned by the connection. An unknown connection and a connection whose context was terminated return `SSL_ERROR_INVALID_ID` (0x8095F006) from the four setters and throw from `sceSslGetAlpnSelected`, whose console return was not measured

CA queries return independently owned snapshots; unload clears active credentials while outstanding snapshots remain valid. text: [sceSystemServiceLoadExec](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceSystemService/Export.cpp) (libSceSystemService) - besides `"exit"`, it starts the title's own `/app0/eboot.bin` or another executable under `/app0` that the relinker converted with `--executable`, which is looked up beside the running one (`/app0/picker/picker.bin` as `picker.picker.bin` with the running executable's extension). The main executable is the one `APS5_EBOOT` names, which the first call sets to its own path. After the guest shutdown the old process ends without running guest exit handlers or host destructors; as during `exit`, a guest thread that calls a library the shutdown has stopped waits for the end instead of unwinding. `"exit"` ends the process after the host shutdown without running the title's `atexit` and `__cxa_atexit` handlers, since the console's shell closes the title instead; a line the title writes just before through its own thread, such as a forwarded standard error line, may not be printed. [VLC for PS5](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC/blob/86bb7d474a303f62bb3c2fc12f728db4846085b8/src/platform_ps5.c#L565-L571) (PPSA85300) relaunches itself with no arguments; RetroArch (PPSA99169) starts its frontend picker with `{"", NULL}`, and the picker starts `eboot.bin` with `{"--ps5-mode=retroarch", NULL}` or `/app0/es-de/es-de.bin` ([picker.cpp](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/blob/bead80725cc11e3c5c65bd9424b0a4494ae36d45/frontends/picker/picker.cpp#L444-L446)), so the list holds only arguments. A list with a first entry becomes the whole guest `argv`, with no program name in front ([LoadExec.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceSystemService/LoadExec.cpp)): a [PS5 RetroArch console transcript](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/blob/bead80725cc11e3c5c65bd9424b0a4494ae36d45/evidence/loadexec-second-image/relaunch-test.jsonl) records a restart with one argument entering with `argc=1`, `argv[0]="--ps5-relaunch=1"`, and a launch from the home screen with `argc=1`, `argv[0]=""` ([relaunch_ps5.cpp](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_RetroArch/blob/bead80725cc11e3c5c65bd9424b0a4494ae36d45/src/relaunch_ps5.cpp#L161-L164)). For such a list Linux replaces the process with `fexecve`, and macOS with `posix_spawn` and `POSIX_SPAWN_SETEXEC`: the PID and the standard streams stay, the other descriptors are closed and the working directory becomes the executable's. Windows starts a suspended process that inherits only the standard streams and a handle of the old process, and its entry stub waits for the old process to end before it loads the title's libraries, so a shell or script that started the title sees it end. A null list or one without a first entry keeps the earlier launch: the new executable gets only its own path as its command line (`CreateProcessW` on Windows, `execv` on Linux and macOS), so its `argv[0]` is the host path, and the old process ends without waiting for it. What the console passes for such a list is not known, nor are its argument limits and error codes. Paths outside `/app0` and unconverted executables throw

name: libSceUsbd.L5
text: [libSceUsbd](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceUsbd/Export.cpp) passes the calls through to the host with [libusb](https://github.com/libusb/libusb) built from the `3rdparty/libusb-cmake` submodule. Devices, handles and descriptors are libusb's own objects: the device, config, interface and endpoint descriptor layouts of [FreeBSD 11.4 libusb](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/lib/libusb/libusb.h) match libusb's field for field, which `static_assert` pins. Each one handed to the title is tracked, and a pointer this library did not return throws. Errors are libusb's codes mapped to `0x80240000 - code`, with `LIBUSB_ERROR_OTHER` at `0x802400FF`, following [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/libraries/usbd/usbd.cpp); the null arguments FreeBSD libusb rejects ([libusb10.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/lib/libusb/libusb10.c), [libusb10_desc.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/lib/libusb/libusb10_desc.c), [libusb10_io.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/lib/libusb/libusb10_io.c)) return `0x80240002`, and `sceUsbdOpen` and `sceUsbdGetActiveConfigDescriptor` throw on a null device, which it dereferences. A submitted transfer is copied into a host transfer whose completion copies the status, actual length and iso packet results back and then calls the title's callback from `sceUsbdHandleEventsTimeout`; transfer flags other than short-not-ok and add-zero-packet throw. `sceUsbdAttachKernelDriver` returns 0 as FreeBSD's stub does, `sceUsbdCheckConnected` reports a device gone when reading its configuration fails with `LIBUSB_ERROR_NO_DEVICE` (FreeBSD asks the kernel directly), and `sceUsbdEventHandlingOk` returns 1. When the host has no USB access, initialization keeps the empty device list and event handling waits for its timeout. Opening, descriptors, string and control requests, interface claims and an asynchronous control transfer were checked against an Xbox 360 controller on Windows; the transfer layout, the argument lists, the error codes and isochronous transfers are unverified on PS5

The compute, decoder memory and decode input structures and the first 0x28 bytes of the 0x50-byte decoder config are those of libSceVideodec2, and decoding goes through it. The 0x78-byte AVC picture info is filled with Videodec2's leading fields and the cropping fields only. OUTPUT_PENDING (0x81510115), INPUT_QUEUE_EMPTY (0x81510116) and DECODE_PENDING (0x81510117) follow from the codes each call's assert accepts. At most four decoded pictures are queued and the last one is held until `sceVdecswFinalizeDecodeSequence`; the console's queue depth is unknown. `sceVdecswSyncDecodeInput` / `sceVdecswSyncDecodeOutput` retry the TrySync variants until they stop returning DECODE_PENDING / OUTPUT_PENDING; they do not sleep beyond a yield, so another thread must drain outputs when the picture queue is full. `sceVdecswGetHevcPictureInfo` still throws: the 0xb8-byte HEVC picture layout is in shadPS4's `vdecsw.h`, but this wrapper only keeps AVC picture info from Videodec2

text: [sceVideoOutOpen, bus 0x20](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/Output.cpp) (libSceVideoOut) - PPSA05666 opens the PS VR2 output as `sceVideoOutOpen(255, 0x20, 0, NULL)` after `sceHmd2ReprojectionEnableVrMode(0x2000F)`, and its own log calls the bus `SCE_VIDEO_OUT_BUS_TYPE_HMD2_MAIN`. The console answers `0x80290001` from a process that is not a game, with the headset connected and worn or not, for users 255 and 0 and for a null or zeroed open parameter, so that is returned here before the other argument checks; what a game gets with a headset attached is not measured. On the handle the title then calls `sceVideoOutRegisterBuffers2` with set 0, two buffers, a 4000x2040 attribute (tiling 0, pitch 0, pixel format `0x8100000022000000`), category 16 and a null option, where each `VideoOutBuffers.data` points at a 16-byte `{pointer, 2}` whose pointer is the structure it passed to `sceHmd2ReprojectionEnableMirroring`, holding per-eye 2000x2040 texture descriptors rather than frame memory; then `sceVideoOutConfigureOutput` and `sceVideoOutIsOutputSupported` with mode `0x2000F`, and the GPU waits on buffer 0 of that handle. None of that is modelled: the HMD output needs a VR backend. With the error code as its handle the title's next call, `sceVideoOutRegisterBuffers2`, throws here for the unknown handle; the console's answer to it is not measured. The TV bus answers `0x8029001E` to the HMD modes `0x20001` and `0x2000C` to `0x20010` on the console, as here

text: [HDR output](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/HostHdrProbe.cpp) (libSceVideoOut, libSceSystemService) - `sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus` reports dynamic range 2 and flag bit 0 (named HDR in [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/VideoOut/VideoOutTypes.cs)) only on Windows, while the window's Vulkan surface offers a 10-bit HDR10 swapchain with `VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace` and `VK_EXT_hdr_metadata` and DXGI (`IDXGIOutput6::GetDesc1`) reports the window's monitor in `DXGI_COLOR_SPACE_RGB_FULL_G2084_NONE_P2020`; `sceSystemServiceGetHdrToneMapLuminance` then reports the monitor's peak, full-frame peak and black level. A monitor that reports no usable peak gets a default of 1000 nits peak and full frame, 0 nits black. On Linux and other hosts the output stays SDR: a surface can offer HDR10 formats while the display is not in HDR (KDE Wayland with RADV lists them with the output's HDR disabled), and SDL2 and Vulkan expose no output HDR state; a compositor or output-state signal is needed first. The surface formats are read again when DXGI's monitor report changes and when the swapchain is recreated; a compositor that changes them without making the swapchain out of date is not seen until then. Every open port's output mode event fires when HDR output becomes available or unavailable and when its luminance changes; the console's events for an HDR change are unknown. Detection starts when VideoOut is first used: `sceSystemServiceGetHdrToneMapLuminance` called before that reports SDR, and no event fires for the availability found at start-up beyond the one every output-mode subscription gets when it is made. Console HDR settings (calibrated peak, the SDR-in-HDR conversion block) are not modelled

text: [sceVideoOutIsOutputSupported](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/Output.cpp) (libSceVideoOut) - mode 1 is supported; mode 15 is supported when the current host display runs at 120 Hz or above. Configuring mode 15 requires attribute3 bit 0x40; this single-bit mask is inferred from the measured full value 0x80040, not isolated by a console measurement. Vblanks run at 119.88 Hz until mode 1 restores 59.94 Hz. Display modes are read through SDL; a move to a slower display falls back the configured output mode to mode 1, fires the output-mode event and continues at 59.94 Hz. The console's exact fallback behaviour when a 120 Hz display is lost has not been measured; this fallback avoids the abort in #7877 and matches the HDMI output mode renegotiation that a display change requires. Selecting another host display mode and VRR are not implemented. The console answers per display and per title: with a 120 Hz TV it also answers 1 for mode 15 (119.88 Hz), and [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan/blob/5b5e4fc2d80fdb67a4f61ba9e6a8a424026bb8a5/docs/HARDWARE_FINDINGS.md) measured that `sceVideoOutConfigureOutput` accepts 15 only from a title whose param.json declares high-frame-rate output (attribute3 0x80040). Modes 4, 7, 8, 12-14, 16-17 and 19 return `VIDEO_OUT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_OUTPUT_MODE` here, as they did on the measured display. Mode 18 throws, because one console answered 0x80290016 and another 0x8029001E. The name `VIDEO_OUT_ERROR_UNKNOWN_OUTPUT_MODE` for 0x8029001E is ours. Word 3 of the output options is accepted with any value, as on the console, and its meaning is unknown. PPSA12544 probes `0xd000000a`, which the console answers with 0x8029001E, so the title selects 3840 pixels; PPSA26344 at `0xCD0946` passes `(handle, 0xf, nullptr, nullptr, 0)` and branches on the result equalling 1

text: [sceVideoOutGetBufferLabelAddress](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/Buffer.cpp) exposes a port-owned contiguous array of 16 aligned 64-bit labels and returns its count. Astro Bot PPSA21564's bundled AGC driver passes a pointer output and addresses each label at `base + index * 8`. The count, zero initialization on registration, and release of the previous displayed buffer when its replacement completes follow [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/23c41333822fe8eca4c609b43119180af63ae4ac/src/core/libraries/videoout/video_out.cpp) and its driver; PS5 console equivalence has not been measured. Labels live until the port closes, and reopening creates a new array. Error precedence follows the reference for null output and the existing open-port policy for handles. Exact scanout release timing, repeated same-buffer flips and concurrent guest label stores remain unverified. EOP-flip registration and interrupt tokens remain unimplemented; exposing these labels does not implement that separate API.

name: libSceVideoOut.L27
text: [sceVideoOutRegisterBuffers, sceVideoOutGetFlipStatus, sceVideoOutGetVblankStatus](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/Buffer.cpp) (libSceVideoOut) - PS4 callers. A handle is treated as PS4 once buffers are registered through the PS4 `sceVideoOutRegisterBuffers`; from then on its flip and vblank status are written in the PS4 64- and 32-byte layouts, with `tsc` and `submitTsc` 0. A PS4 title that reads a status before it registers buffers gets the larger PS5 layout. The PS4 function accepts only linear A8R8G8B8_SRGB (0x80000000) and A8B8G8R8_SRGB (0x80002200) buffers without options; tiled PS4 buffers throw, as their layout differs from the PS5 tiling. Linear PS4 buffers may be 4 KiB aligned: the OpenOrbis graphics sample registers its second 1920x1080 buffer 8,294,400 bytes after the first. The PS4 alignment rule is not known

name: libSceVideoOut.L34
text: [sceVideoOutSubmitEopFlip](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/Buffer.cpp) reserves a flip and returns an opaque DWORD token; presentation is driven by a matching graphics-queue `RELEASE_MEM` with `INT_SEL` 2 and that token in `INT_CTXID`. This five-argument ABI and packet use are inferred from PPSA21564's bundled AGC driver, whose original packet-emission routine is checked in an isolated host ABI probe. The console token encoding, output width beyond the observed DWORD, error policy and reservation capacity are unverified. Host tokens occupy `0x04000000..0x07ffffff`, never repeat within a process, and exhaustion throws. Closing cancels unsubmitted reservations; only live reservations match; consumed or cancelled context IDs execute as ordinary label writes without targeting a reopened port. Async-queue EOP flips throw. Buffer registration, flip modes, queue capacity and vsync presentation follow the existing host VideoOut model, not measured console behavior.

name: libSceVideoOut.L25
text: [sceVideoOutSubmitFlip](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/VideoOutDriver.cpp) (libSceVideoOut, libSceAgcDriver) - in the [AGC driver](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/Driver/Queues/Submission.cpp), a CPU flip waits for the graphics-queue submissions ahead of it when the calling thread has submitted graphics-queue work itself: a title that submits a frame and flips it without waiting relies on that order, since emulated GPU work finishes later than the console's. A flip from a thread that has never submitted graphics-queue work is presented without waiting for queued submissions, unless a command-buffer or EOP flip ahead of it has not been reached. Such a thread can only know its frame is finished by waiting for it, as the PS5 RADV WSI's flip thread waits on the frame's fence. Whether the console ever orders a CPU flip behind the graphics queue is not measured; `APS5_CPU_FLIP_IN_ORDER=1` orders every CPU flip

text: [Mouse capture and delta scaling](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/MouseInput.cpp) (libSceVideoOut) - the console's mouse reports relative motion only, so a host cursor can never coincide with the title's cursor; while a title has a mouse open and the window is focused the host cursor is hidden and captured (SDL relative mode, released on focus loss or while the pad's mouse-to-stick toggle is on). Motion deltas are scaled from the presented image's size in window units to the title's display resolution with sub-pixel carry; the console's deltas are counts, so a title that applies its own sensitivity moves its cursor that much faster than the host pointer would have. The scale takes SDL's relative motion in logical window units, the units of `SDL_GetWindowSize`; under Windows DPI scaling SDL may report it in physical pixels, which is unverified (no Windows run yet), and a drawable larger than the window does not change the scale.

name: libSceVideoOut.L37
text: [Windows game controllers](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideoOut/src/VideoOutDriver.cpp) (libSceVideoOut) - SDL's DirectInput joystick backend is disabled at default hint priority before `SDL_InitSubSystem`, because its device enumeration blocks forever on some vendor HID devices (#1042). XInput and HIDAPI controllers are detected; controllers reachable only through DirectInput are not. Setting `SDL_DIRECTINPUT_ENABLED=1` restores them on hosts without such a device. SDL's Windows.Gaming.Input backend stays on by default. Setting `APS5_NO_WGI` turns it off at default hint priority, for hosts where it faults at `Windows.Gaming.Input.dll+0x10a84` a few seconds into every run: seen on Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (19045) with the Nefarius and Oculus virtual gamepad emulation buses installed and no physical controller connected. With it off, devices and features reachable only through Windows.Gaming.Input are lost: racing wheels, arcade sticks, flight sticks, HID pads without an HIDAPI driver, and Xbox One and Series trigger rumble.

name: libSceVideodec2.L11
text: [sceVideodec2CreateDecoder](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideodec2/Export.cpp) (libSceVideodec2) decodes HEVC (codec type 974921) and VP9 (2382845) through FFmpeg, besides H.264. The tags come from SharpProspero's `Videodec2CodecType` and EVO-PLAYER-PS5's `sce_videodec2.h`, which records them from hardware runs. HEVC input is converted from length-prefixed NAL units to Annex B as for H.264, and VP9 frames are passed through. Output is NV12 for 8-bit pictures. A 10-bit picture is written as 16-bit little-endian words with the sample in the low 10 bits, Y rows then interleaved UV rows at `framePitchInBytes` times the picture height, with `framePitch` in samples and `framePitchInBytes` in bytes (twice the width, aligned to 256), and `QueryDecoderMemoryInfo` sizes a frame of an HEVC or VP9 profile 2 configuration with two bytes per sample. Evidence is from [EVO-PLAYER-PS5](https://github.com/sainsaji/EVO-PLAYER-PS5/tree/9715f6ee9bf9b53461d6fdf9a2e11b4c48357783), which decodes and presents 1080p HEVC Main10 on hardware through this path (`docs/evo-pro/on-demand-decoder-handoff.md`): it takes a picture as 10-bit when `pitch_bytes >= pitch * 2`, puts UV at `pitch_bytes` times the height and samples with a low-bit factor (`projects/evoplayer/media/src/evo_vdec_native.c`, `ro_harvest`), and its hardware logs give 6128 KB and 24496 KB frame buffers for 1920x1088 and 3840x2176 Main10 decoders after rounding to 16 KiB. The 1080p size is what this formula gives; at 3840x2176 it gives 16 KiB less, so the console's size there has another term that is not known. Unverified: `frameFormat` (still 0; no consumer found reads it), VP9 profile 2 output (no hardware evidence), and the layout of 12-bit pictures and of decoded formats other than yuv420p10le, which throw. `sceVideodec2GetPictureInfo` and `sceVideodec2GetAvcPictureInfo` throw for HEVC and VP9 pictures, which use other layouts (`SceVideodec2HevcPictureInfo`, `SceVideodec2Vp9PictureInfo`), and `sceVideodec2GetHevcPictureInfo` is not exported; `sceVideodec2GetVp9PictureInfo` has its own VP9 layout

name: libSceVideodec2.L15
text: [sceVideodec2Decode](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideodec2/Export.cpp) (libSceVideodec2) and `sceVideodec2Flush` output the coded picture, with the chroma plane after its luma rows, as the console does for 1080p H.264 and HEVC streams coded at 1920x1088. An HEVC or VP9 picture whose size is not a multiple of 16, such as HEVC coded at 1920x1080, is output at that size; whether the console pads it is unverified. `sceVideodec2GetPictureInfo` reports no frame cropping

text: [sceVideodec2GetVp9PictureInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceVideodec2/Export.cpp) uses the 88-byte layout and two-pointer signature from [SharpProspero Videodec2.cs](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Video/Videodec2.cs). Frame metadata follows the [VP9 specification](https://storage.googleapis.com/downloads.webmproject.org/docs/vp9/vp9-bitstream-specification-v0.7-20170222-draft.pdf), sections 5.26 and 6.2: profile, key/intra-only flags, bit depth, color space/range, coded/render dimensions and superframe count are retained per emitted buffer. Level is 0 because the elementary stream does not signal a level; the console value is unverified. Null pointers, undersized structures and querying another codec throw; console error codes and support for other structure sizes are unknown. Pictures deeper than 10 bits are rejected. Superframes are submitted as individual coded frames to keep each output associated with its input metadata.

name: libSceVideodec2.L14

TEKKEN DARK RESURRECTION (PPSA31371), which runs in Sony's PSP emulator, decodes after a flush without a reset (#7118), so the console accepts the call. Pictures the flush decoded but has not returned yet are returned before the new ones. What the console returns for them, and for a stream that continues across the flush without a new IDR picture, is not measured.

name: libSceZlib.L5
text: [libSceZlib](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceZlib/Export.cpp) completes RFC1950 decompression during submission and supports one outstanding request, null-timeout waits and one result retrieval. Timed waits, multiple outstanding requests, repeated retrieval and finalization with an unread result throw. The 64-bit initialization length and 64 KiB output limit with 2 KiB destination alignment follow [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Compression/Zlib.cs); the PS4 initialization length is 32 bits. shadPS4 also requires the output length to be a multiple of 2 KiB and returns `0x81120016` for invalid arguments; this implementation accepts any length up to 64 KiB (SharpProspero documents only the pointer alignment) and throws on invalid arguments. Scratch memory is not used, and its firmware size/alignment requirements are unknown. The initialization errors follow SharpProspero; malformed/checksum/truncated streams report `0x811200FF` and insufficient output `0x8112001C` as in [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/zlib/zlib.cpp). PS5 error precedence, scheduling, completion selection, result consumption and cancellation are unverified. The payload SDK's FreeBSD kernel `z_stream` and host errno are not this library's ABI.

name: libc.L71
text: [Guest path names](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/General.cpp) (libc) are checked against FreeBSD 11.4's `NAME_MAX` (255 bytes per component) and `MAXPATHLEN` (1024 bytes with the terminating NUL) before they are resolved, and a longer name fails with `ENAMETOOLONG`, as `namei` does. The host's own limit still applies below that: on Windows a path whose host form exceeds `MAX_PATH` fails with `ENOENT`. A backslash counts as a path separator for the component length, because the guest path resolver turns it into `/` before the host call, while FreeBSD treats it as an ordinary name character, so a 301-byte name that contains one is accepted here. `sceNgs2ParseWaveformFile` resolves its path without a try block, so a long component ends in an uncaught `filesystem_error` there where a missing file ended in a `runtime_error` (both end the title). A path through a regular file (`file/x`, `file/`) is not always `ENOTDIR` on the calls that resolve it. None of this was measured on a console.

name: libc.L31
text: [Dinkumware atomics](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/DinkumwareAtomics.cpp) (libc) - every operation is sequentially consistent whatever memory order it is given, which is never weaker than the console. Matching the `libc.prx` bundled with PPSA08427 (that binary run side by side on every order from 0 to 7), `_Atomic_load_8` returns 0 for a release, acq_rel or invalid order and the 8-byte exchange and fetch operations return 0 without touching memory for an order above `memory_order_seq_cst`; the generic `_Atomic_copy`, `_Atomic_exchange` and `_Atomic_compare_exchange_*` lock the byte flag passed first, as the console does

name: libc.L17

The console returns 4 for other internal pthread errors while this implementation throws.

name: libc.L34
text: [Dinkumware mutexes and conditions](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/Threads.cpp) (libc) use pointer-to-handle arguments, matching the console aerolib signatures reported in [#3079](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/3079). The title's `_Mtx_lock` maps `0` to `_Thrd_success` (0), `0x8002000b` to `_Thrd_busy` (3), and other failures to `_Thrd_error` (4); its internal mutex init recognizes recursive flag `0x100`, while every other type uses default attributes. The observed relock failure for a plain mutex suggests those defaults are error-checking, but that has not been confirmed on hardware. The title's `_Mtx_unlock` and `_Cnd_wait` return success regardless of their internal result. The host implementation treats invalid ownership preconditions as no-ops, and throws for invalid handles, host wait errors and destroying a locked mutex as debug guards; those cases are not confirmed against the console.

text: [_WStoul](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/Strings.cpp), [_Iswctype](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/RuneLocale.cpp), [swscanf_s and swscanf](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/ScanningWide.cpp) (libc) - `_WStoul` is `wcstoul` and throws for a base other than 0 or 2 to 36. `_Iswctype` takes the class numbers of Dinkumware's [xwcc.h](https://github.com/superna9999/ti-cgt6x/blob/cgt6x_7_3_4/include/xwcc.h) (1 `alnum` to 11 `xdigit`, 12 `blank`) and throws for any other value, including the FreeBSD masks `wctype` returns; the numbering is not confirmed on the console's `libc.prx`. `swscanf_s` follows C11 7.29.2.2 and K.3.9.1.5, but reads the size argument as `unsigned int` like `sscanf_s` where K.3.9.1.5 specifies `rsize_t`; the console's width is unverified. A runtime-constraint violation (null buffer, format or receiving pointer) only returns `EOF`, and a too small array gets a null first element as in `sscanf_s`. A literal mismatch is a matching failure and a field that is only a prefix, such as `0x` or `1e`, does not convert, as C11 requires; FreeBSD's `vfwscanf` reports an input failure for the first and converts the second. Integers out of range are truncated from `strtoll`/`strtoull`. `%p` follows FreeBSD 11's [vfwscanf.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/4ab2e064d7950be84256d671a7ae93f87cc6aa36/lib/libc/stdio/vfwscanf.c#L610-L615): a hexadecimal integer with an optional `0x`, converted as unsigned and stored as a pointer; a length modifier on it throws, where FreeBSD ignores it. It throws for `%S`, `%C`, unknown length modifiers, scanset ranges, `%n` with suppression or width, and narrow `%s`, `%c` or `%[` input that the C-locale `wcrtomb` cannot convert. `swscanf` runs the same scanner without the size arguments of `%s`, `%c` and `%[`, as FreeBSD's [swscanf.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/lib/libc/stdio/swscanf.c) passes its arguments to `vswscanf`, so everything above except the sizes applies to it; it also keeps the null buffer, format and receiving pointer checks returning `EOF`, where C leaves those undefined. Neither variant is confirmed on a PS5 title

text: [_Thrd_sleep](../../../core/libs/prx/libc/src/Threads.cpp) (libc, NID `jfRI3snge3o`) follows the Dinkumware threads library shipped with [Visual C++ 2013](https://github.com/adityaramesh/concurrency_runtime/tree/master/VS2013_SP2/crt/src/thr) (`xtime.c`) and C11 Annex K, without console verification. It reads a 16-byte xtime (64-bit seconds and nanoseconds) on the guest `CLOCK_REALTIME`, normalizes the nanoseconds and sleeps through `nanosleep` on POSIX, retrying on `EINTR`, or high-resolution waitable timers on Windows; a null xtime or one whose normalization overflows throws. Guest thread cancellation is not integrated with this wait. The console's `_Thrd_sleep` (disassembled from a title's `libc.prx`) also takes an optional `xtime*` of remaining time and returns `int`; here the sleep is never cut short, so it returns 0 and leaves the remaining time untouched.
