The console's strings are not measured

name: libkernel.L28
text: [sceKernelConvertUtcToLocaltime, sceKernelConvertLocaltimeToUtc](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Time/Time.cpp) (libkernel) convert with the host time zone at the given instant, as libc `localtime` does, instead of the console's time zone setting. `west_sec` holds the standard-time offset in seconds east of UTC, despite its name, and `dst_sec` the daylight saving seconds in effect. This follows PPSA99203 ([PS5SX2](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2/blob/b4cf55e87c34e8a2a1cd9302df4373e5a94d28f4/ps5/frontend/fe_ps5.cpp#L54-L63)), whose author saw a console write 7200 and 3600 into the 16-byte block; which zone that console was set to is not recorded, so whether `west_sec` includes daylight saving is not settled. [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/23c41333/src/core/libraries/kernel/time.cpp) also stores seconds east. PPSA99203 declares the last argument of `sceKernelConvertUtcToLocaltime` as `uint64_t*`; 32 bits are written. On Windows the standard offset and the daylight saving amount are the C runtime's current `_get_timezone` and `_get_dstbias` for every instant, as libc `localtime_s` uses them, so instants under a zone's earlier rules get today's offsets; a `TZ` variable does not set `_dstbias`, which keeps the value an earlier `_tzset` read from the system (0 when the system zone has no daylight saving), and summer time then adds nothing. In a repeated or skipped local hour, `sceKernelConvertLocaltimeToUtc` takes the offset in effect one standard offset earlier. Its last argument receives the zone's daylight saving amount whether or not it is in effect, found by sampling the host zone over the year around the result, while `dst_sec` is the amount in effect: the libc `mktime` that PPSA99109 bundles (text 0x70ebb-0x70ee5) subtracts that amount when `tm_isdst` is set outside summer time. That `mktime` passes `tm_isdst` as the second argument, which is ignored, so it does not choose the offset in a repeated hour. `sceKernelGettimezone` and the `gettimeofday` time zone still report no offset and no daylight saving. A host time the C runtime cannot convert throws

name: libkernel.L123
text: [EVFILT_VNODE, sceKernelAddFileEvent and sceKernelDeleteFileEvent](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/FileEvent.cpp) (libkernel) watch the host file or directory behind the descriptor and turn host changes into FreeBSD 11 vnode hints, which [`filt_vfsvnode`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/34bd34750187bae02a0086402c78c031c59dd8b3/sys/kern/vfs_subr.c#L5032) adds whole when they share a bit with the requested `fflags`: a write that grows a file is `NOTE_WRITE | NOTE_EXTEND`, another write `NOTE_WRITE`, a shrinking truncate or an attribute change `NOTE_ATTRIB`, a higher link count `NOTE_LINK`, a lower one or a pending delete `NOTE_DELETE`, a new path `NOTE_RENAME`; in a directory, an entry created, removed or renamed is `NOTE_WRITE`, with `NOTE_LINK` for a subdirectory, and on Linux an entry moved from or to another directory adds `NOTE_EXTEND`; inotify queues the two halves of a rename one after the other, so a watcher woken by the first can read it alone, and a half read without the other is classified only after a `getdents64` on the watched directory, which takes the directory lock that `rename` holds until both halves are queued ([`do_renameat2`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/fs/namei.c#L4975) around `vfs_rename` and its `fsnotify_move`, [`iterate_dir`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/fs/readdir.c#L103)), an ordering taken from the kernel source, not from inotify(7), which promises none; a directory registered with `NOTE_EXTEND` on Windows is accepted, as `vfs_kqfilter` does not check it, but never receives it, because the directory handle cannot tell a move between directories from a removal plus an addition. FreeBSD's hints depend on the filesystem and the console's filesystems are not known: a growing `ftruncate` reports `NOTE_WRITE | NOTE_EXTEND` where `vop_setattr_post` reports `NOTE_ATTRIB`, and on Windows `utimes` on a file reports `NOTE_WRITE`. The three Windows notifications are told apart in the error, which names the `parent`, `entries` or `subdirectories` watch, the path it was given and `GetLastError`, but a `FindFirstChangeNotification` that fails still throws rather than returning an error to the guest: the EVFILT_VNODE attach path is [`vfs_kqfilter`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/34bd34750187bae02a0086402c78c031c59dd8b3/sys/kern/vfs_subr.c#L4936), which returns `EINVAL`, `ENOMEM` or 0 after `fget` has turned a descriptor that is not open into `EBADF`, and consults no directory permission, so no FreeBSD errno stands for a host that refuses to notify, and what the console does on such a host is not measured. Only the `parent` watch can fail this way in practice: `entries` and `subdirectories` need the `FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY` that opening the watched directory already took. The parent handle produces no hint of its own, as `RunHostWatch` only calls `FindNextChangeNotification` on it, so a later change may leave the watch on its 50 ms poll instead of throwing; that is not done here. Windows uses `FindFirstChangeNotification` on the parent directory (and on a watched directory itself) and compares `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` snapshots at least every 50 ms, because a write through an open handle is reported only when the handle is flushed or closed, so file hints can arrive 50 ms late, and a file deleted while watched, which the POSIX delete of Windows 10 1903 moves into `$Extend\$Deleted` until its last handle closes, reports `NOTE_DELETE` without `NOTE_RENAME` and keeps its handle without a parent directory watch, as that directory cannot be watched; Linux uses inotify on the file and is not run. `NOTE_REVOKE`, `NOTE_OPEN`, `NOTE_CLOSE`, `NOTE_CLOSE_WRITE`, `NOTE_READ`, unknown bits and descriptors other than files, directories, pipes and sockets throw. `sceKernelAddFileEvent(eq, fd, watch, udata)` and `sceKernelDeleteFileEvent(eq, fd)` take the [OpenOrbis](https://github.com/OpenOrbis/OpenOrbis-PS4-Toolchain/blob/0a1aaf9d/include/orbis/libkernel.h#L35) and [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelEqueue.cs#L164) signatures; `watch` is taken as the `fflags` and the event is added with `EV_CLEAR`, neither confirmed on a title (feat(libkernel): implement kevent EV_DISABLE, EV_DISPATCH and EV_FORCEONESHOT) (fix(libkernel): follow kqueue_register for EV_FORCEONESHOT and modify flags)

name: libkernel.L225
text: [pthread_atfork](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/Posix/Atfork.cpp) (libkernel) appends the three handlers to a process-wide list and returns 0, or `ENOMEM` when the entry cannot be allocated, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`_pthread_atfork`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libthr/thread/thr_fork.c#L78-L100) does; null handlers are accepted. The handlers never run: `fork` throws and `vfork` is absent, so no child process is created. Handlers of a module that is unloaded stay in the list, where FreeBSD's `__pthread_cxa_finalize` removes them. PPSA97358 has a source-level call from the constructor `rcu_init` ([rcu.c](https://github.com/ZiZc3/XPSemu/blob/8eec07b4e31f66dce8e0b05c1ca1281af303e933/util/rcu.c#L488-L495)), but current-main runtime reachability is unverified; XPSemu currently stops first at the unresolved `mlockall` import (#4386)

name: libkernel.L219
text: [_fstatfs](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) fills the FreeBSD 11 `struct statfs` of the PS5 payload SDK with the host volume that holds the file: block size, transfer size, total, free and available blocks, maximum name length and the read-only, `nosuid` and `noexec` flags (on Windows only read-only, and `f_files` and `f_ffree` are 0, as NTFS has no fixed number of files). The filesystem type number and name, mount paths, owner, filesystem id and I/O counters are left 0 or empty, since they would describe a host mount, not a console one. Sockets and pipes return `EINVAL`, as FreeBSD's `getvnode` does; a Windows descriptor that is neither a file nor a pipe throws. Stremio Plus (PPSA74126) reads the free space before a download and only logs the other fields

name: libkernel.L213
text: [ioctl, _ioctl](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) handle only `FIONBIO` and `FIONREAD` on a socket, and any other request there fails with `ENOTTY`. On the other descriptors they follow FreeBSD's [`kern_ioctl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/sys_generic.c#L758), [`vn_ioctl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/vfs_vnops.c#L1488) and [`pipe_ioctl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/sys_pipe.c#L1346): `FIONBIO` sets `O_NONBLOCK` as `fcntl` does, `FIOCLEX` and `FIONCLEX` set and clear the close-on-exec flag `F_GETFD` reports, and `FIONREAD` reports the size past the offset of a file, the queued bytes of a pipe's read end, 0 on its write end and `ENOTTY` on the random device, while it throws on a directory or another character device. Every termios request (group `t`, `TIOCGWINSZ` included) fails with `ENOTTY`, since those descriptors are taken as not a terminal, as in `tcgetattr`, and any other well-formed request throws. An input request with length 0 is not rejected as malformed: [`sys_ioctl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/sys_generic.c#L703-L718) rejects it only in a kernel built without `COMPAT_FREEBSD4`, `COMPAT_FREEBSD5` and `COMPAT_43`, and which of these the PS5 kernel has is unknown. Stremio Plus (PPSA74126) imports `_ioctl` for its statically linked `tc*` functions, which send `TIOCGETA`, `TIOCSETA`, `TIOCSPGRP` and the other termios requests

name: libkernel.L164
text: [Thread cancellation](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/src/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD libthr (states and types 0/1 and 0/2, `PTHREAD_CANCELED` 1, the `_pthread_cleanup_info` node layout), not measured on the console. A request is acted on only in `scePthreadTestcancel`, the condition variable, `sem` and `scePthreadSem` waits, `scePthreadJoin` and the sleeps, and their POSIX names; file and socket calls are not cancellation points. An enabled cancellation request wakes POSIX `sleep` and exits the thread. `usleep`, `sceKernelUsleep`, `nanosleep`, `_nanosleep`, `sceKernelNanosleep` and `sceKernelSleep` check cancellation only before and after the host sleep, so an enabled request during those waits is delivered when the sleep ends. The asynchronous type acts like the deferred one, except at the two set calls.

name: libkernel.L205
text: [sigtimedwait](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Signals.cpp) (libkernel) waits on a process-wide pending set instead of throwing: a signal raised while blocked stays pending and is taken by `sigwait`, `sigwaitinfo` or `sigtimedwait`, delivered to the handler when `_sigprocmask` unblocks it, or delivered by `pause`. The set covers all 128 signals and the lowest number that is pending and in the set is selected (FreeBSD specifies the lowest number only among real-time signals). Selection, `EAGAIN` on timeout, `EINVAL` for a `tv_nsec` outside 0 to 1000000000 while nothing is pending and `NULL` timeout blocking indefinitely follow FreeBSD's [sigtimedwait(2)](https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=sigtimedwait). `sigwait` returns 0 with the number in its output, as POSIX specifies, and `sigwaitinfo` and `sigtimedwait` return the number, as FreeBSD does. The guest `siginfo_t` follows FreeBSD 11's `sys/sys/siginfo.h`: 80 bytes, `si_signo` at 0, `si_code` at 8, `si_pid` at 12, `si_uid` at 16, `si_addr` at 24, `si_value` at 32 and `si_band` at 40; only `si_signo`, `si_code` (`SI_USER`) and `si_pid` (the guest pid) are written, `si_uid` stays 0 because no uid is modelled, and the console's layout is not verified. PPSA85300 imports `sigtimedwait` and fails to load without it; its only call site is VLC's `vlc_writev` ([filesystem.c](https://github.com/videolan/vlc/blob/6de05adcbaf2e8b85fe86aad4169393098628119/src/posix/filesystem.c#L243-L278)), which polls with a zero timeout to drain a `SIGPIPE` only after `writev` fails with `EPIPE`. The waits are not cancellation points and an unblocked caught signal does not interrupt them with `EINTR`, where FreeBSD's `sigwaitinfo` and `sigtimedwait` may return it. `SIGPIPE` has no host equivalent and is never raised by a host write here (see `read, write and vector I/O`), so VLC's drain finds nothing

name: libkernel.L158
text: [pthread_sigmask](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Signals.cpp) (libkernel) shares the process-wide mask of `sigprocmask` and `_sigprocmask`, which keeps only the first 32 signals; FreeBSD keeps a mask per thread

name: libkernel.L162
text: [sigpending](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Signals.cpp) (libkernel) reports the intersection of the process-wide pending set of `sigtimedwait` and the blocked mask of `_sigprocmask`, as FreeBSD's `sys_sigpending` intersects the pending list with `td_sigmask`, and returns -1 with `EFAULT` for a null set. Because `_sigprocmask` keeps only the first 32 signals, signals 33 to 128 are never blocked and never appear in the set, and setting `SIG_IGN` (or `SIG_DFL` on a signal whose default action is to ignore) does not clear a signal that was already marked pending. PPSA99420 imports it

name: libkernel.L160
text: [sceKernelRaiseException](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Exception.cpp) on Windows runs the handler wherever the target thread was interrupted. It waits only while the thread is inside winpthreads or restoring a context through `NtContinue`, and throws if that lasts 1 s, so a handler that calls into other host code the thread was interrupted in, such as the C runtime's heap or a lock of the emulator, can deadlock on it or reenter it. A thread that holds the address-wait lock of `sceKernelSyncOnAddressWait`, `sceKernelSyncOnAddressWake` and `_umtx_op`, or the park queue lock of the guest mutexes, gets the raise as an APC instead, which runs once it has released the lock or while it waits; the other locks of the emulator are not deferred this way

name: libkernel.L57
text: [_umtx_op](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/SyncOnAddress/src/SyncOnAddress.cpp) (libkernel) - the mutex, condition variable, read-write lock, legacy lock and `SEM2` operations throw, and so does a misaligned object. Implemented as FreeBSD 11's [kern_umtx.c](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/stable/11/sys/kern/kern_umtx.c): `UMTX_OP_WAIT`, `UMTX_OP_WAKE`, `UMTX_OP_WAIT_UINT`, `UMTX_OP_WAIT_UINT_PRIVATE`, `UMTX_OP_WAKE_PRIVATE`, `UMTX_OP_NWAKE_PRIVATE`, `UMTX_OP_SEM_WAIT` and `UMTX_OP_SEM_WAKE` (the last two built under `COMPAT_FREEBSD9`/`10`). Operations 0 and 1 fail with `EOPNOTSUPP`, as measured on a PS5 (firmware 12.70). The `SEM2` operations, 23 and 24, were measured on the console and returned `0` for a count of 0 where FreeBSD would time out, so they stay unimplemented.

name: libkernel.L184
text: [socketpair](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) - the pair is the host's `AF_UNIX` pair on Linux and, on Windows, a loopback TCP connection for `SOCK_STREAM` or two connected UDP sockets for `SOCK_DGRAM`; `SOCK_SEQPACKET` throws on Windows. A datagram sent to a full receiver gets `ENOBUFS` on the console, waits or gets `EAGAIN` on Linux and is dropped on Windows, and on Windows a datagram `recv` after the peer closed reports `ECONNRESET` instead of the console's `ENOTCONN`, and a stream `send` after the peer closed reports `ECONNABORTED` instead of the console's `EPIPE`. `read` and `write` on a pair end go to the host like on every guest socket. `getpeername` on a pair end succeeds after the peer closed, where the console returns `ENOTCONN`, and `connect`, `bind` and `sendto` with an address on a pair end report an address-family error instead of the console's `EISCONN`. On Windows `poll` on a stream end reports `POLLHUP` without `POLLIN` after the peer's `shutdown(SHUT_WR)` or `close`, where the console reports `POLLIN`, with `POLLHUP` only after `close`

name: libkernel.L189
text: [bind, connect, sendto](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) check a socket address length as FreeBSD 11.4's [`getsockaddr`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/uipc_syscalls.c) and the `sa_len` test of `tcp_usr_connect` and `in_pcbconnect` do: below 2 or an `AF_INET` address below 16 or an `AF_INET6` address below 28 bytes fails with `EINVAL`, above 255 with `ENAMETOOLONG`. An address longer than `sockaddr_in` or `sockaddr_in6` is still accepted where FreeBSD answers `EINVAL`, and an address of another family still fails with `EAFNOSUPPORT`, as the console's behaviour for these is not known. None of this was measured on a console.

name: libkernel.L229
text: [chflags](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD 11.4's [`kern_chflagsat`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/vfs_syscalls.c#L2366-L2383) and UFS's [`ufs_setattr`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/ufs/ufs/ufs_vnops.c#L509-L556) for a root caller: the path lookup reports `EFAULT`, `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR`, a flag outside the 17 UFS stores (`VNOVAL` included) `EOPNOTSUPP`, and `SF_SNAPSHOT` `EPERM`. Neither host keeps BSD file flags, so every file is taken to have none (`stat` reports `st_flags` 0): flags 0 succeed without touching the file, and any other flag throws, naming the flags. `UF_READONLY`, `UF_HIDDEN`, `UF_SYSTEM` and `UF_ARCHIVE` are FreeBSD's names for the Windows attributes but are not mapped to them: UFS stores them without enforcing them, `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY` already carries the owner write bit of `chmod` on Windows, and Linux has no equivalent a process can set without `CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE`. The console's filesystem types, `EROFS` on read-only mounts and the change-time update are not modelled

name: libkernel.L230
text: [fchflags](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) has the gaps of `chflags`: a valid non-zero flag throws, and the console's filesystem types, `EROFS` and the change-time update are not modelled. Character devices, the random device, other host descriptors and files read from app0.zar throw, since their console filesystems and the privilege check for devices are not modelled. On Windows, anonymous shared memory objects are temporary files that are not told apart from regular files, so they are treated as files instead of reporting `EINVAL` as FreeBSD 11.4's [`getvnode`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/vfs_syscalls.c#L3850-L3877) does.

name: libkernel.L227
text: [clock_settime](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Time/Time.cpp) (libkernel) validates like FreeBSD 11.4's [`kern_clock_settime`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_time.c#L396-L412) for a root caller: `EFAULT` for a null time, `EINVAL` for any clock but `CLOCK_REALTIME`, a negative second count or a nanosecond count outside 0 to 999999999. A valid `CLOCK_REALTIME` request throws, naming the requested time, since the host clock is never set and no guest clock offset is kept. FreeBSD checks `PRIV_CLOCK_SETTIME` first, which a jailed process fails with `EPERM`; whether a title holds it on the console is unverified. PS5MC (PPSA99420) imports it; no call site is known

name: libkernel.L122
text: [kqueue and kevent](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/Kqueue.cpp) (libkernel) follow FreeBSD 11's [`kern_event.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/34bd34750187bae02a0086402c78c031c59dd8b3/sys/kern/kern_event.c) (`kqueue_kevent`, `kqueue_register`, `kqueue_scan`, the timer and user filters) over the event queue; nothing is measured on a console. The descriptor is a host null device registered as the kqueue: `close` and `sceKernelClose` close the queue and `dup`/`dup2` of it throw, but `read`, `write` and `fstat` act on the null device instead of failing with `EOPNOTSUPP` or reporting `S_IFIFO`. Read and write events are supported on guest sockets only, plus `EVFILT_READ` on the read end and `EVFILT_WRITE` on the write end of a pipe (see the kevent on a pipe entry) and the timer, user and [vnode](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/FileEvent.cpp) filters and a read event on the host stream on descriptor 0, which never triggers, as `select` never reports descriptor 0 readable; PPSA34015 registers descriptor 0 for reading in a new kqueue at start-up and does not check the result; other filters, `EV_CLEAR` on a socket or a pipe off Linux (see the kevent EV_CLEAR entry), `EVFILT_READ` on another kqueue, a `NOTE_NSECONDS` period above one second with a fraction (11.0 converts the fraction with the microsecond macro) and any change to an existing timer (11.0 keeps the armed expiry and applies the new period after it, 11.4's `filt_timertouch` restarts it) throw. `EV_DISABLE`, `EV_DISPATCH` and `EV_FORCEONESHOT` follow kern_event.c: a disabled knote stays registered, stops polling or firing and is not reported, a trigger raised while it is disabled is kept and reported after `EV_ENABLE`, where `knote` would drop it, `EV_DISPATCH` reports once and then disables the knote, and `EV_FORCEONESHOT` is ignored on a new knote while on an existing one it sets `EV_ONESHOT` and fires the knote; a negative `nevents` fails with `EINVAL`. A new user event keeps its `fflags` unmasked and is not triggered by `NOTE_TRIGGER`, because `filt_userattach` reads the already cleared `kn_fflags`. The timer limit `kq_calloutmax` (`ENOMEM`) is not enforced, and closing a kqueue wakes a thread waiting on it in `kevent` with `EBADF`, where `kqueue_drain` makes the close wait for that thread. A level-triggered event is reported once per call and moved behind the other events, as in `kqueue_scan`; the `sceKernel*Equeue` calls keep their own collection loop. `NOTE_LOWAT` on a socket sets the low-water mark as FreeBSD 11's [`filt_soread` and `filt_sowrite`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/uipc_socket.c) do, and a later change of the knote replaces it as `kqueue_register` replaces `kn_sdata`: a read event fires once the buffered bytes reach the mark, or at end of file or on a listening socket. A read mark above 1 is taken on stream sockets only: on a datagram socket Linux's `FIONREAD` reports the next datagram where FreeBSD's `sbavail` counts every queued byte, so it throws. A write event fires once the send buffer's free space reaches the mark, as `filt_sowrite` does with `sbspace`; the host reports that space as `SO_SNDBUF` less `SIOCOUTQ` on Linux and as `SO_SNDBUF` alone elsewhere, so off Linux it does not shrink while data is queued. Marks below 1, which make FreeBSD's read filter always fire, throw

name: libkernel.L113
text: [close, sceKernelClose](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/HostStreams.cpp) (libkernel) - descriptors 0 to 2 that are open when libkernel loads belong to the host process: closing one fails with `EBADF` and leaves it open. The console's result is unknown. PPSA21703 calls `sceKernelClose(0)` repeatedly; closing the host stream let the host C runtime give descriptor 0 to the next file opened, which the next call then closed

name: libkernel.L142
text: [close](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) and [setsockopt](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) reach a [libSceNet](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceNet/Export.cpp) socket through hooks libSceNet registers, as `select` polls them; the other libkernel socket calls do not. libSceNet numbers its sockets from 32 in its own table, so a CRT file descriptor and a socket can share a number; `close` then closes the socket. On the console both are one kernel descriptor space

name: libkernel.L196
text: [Socket error numbers](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/include/SocketError.hpp) (libkernel) - a host socket error becomes the FreeBSD 11 `errno.h` number of the same name; the numbers are not checked on the console. Winsock `WSAESHUTDOWN` becomes `EPIPE`, as a send after `shutdown` does on FreeBSD, and a host error with no FreeBSD socket counterpart becomes `EIO`. A nonblocking `connect` in progress reports `EINPROGRESS` on Linux but `EAGAIN` on Windows (`WSAEWOULDBLOCK`), where FreeBSD reports `EINPROGRESS`. On Windows a refused nonblocking `connect` is never reported (`SO_ERROR` is unsupported), so a repeated one keeps reporting `EALREADY` where FreeBSD reports `ECONNREFUSED`. A receive after `shutdown(SHUT_RD)` reports `EPIPE` on Windows where FreeBSD returns 0

name: libkernel.L166
text: [cpuset_getaffinity](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/Posix/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) - the calling thread, another live guest thread selected by its guest TID, or the calling process is handled; other levels (ROOT/CPUSET) and other scopes (CPUSET/JAIL) throw as unmodelled, invalid levels or scopes return `EINVAL` and unknown thread or process IDs return `ESRCH`, following [FreeBSD 11.4](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/sys/kern/kern_cpuset.c#L426-L437) guest-TID selection, not measured on PS5. For the process the mask is the union of the affinities of the live guest threads, as [FreeBSD 11.4](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/sys/kern/kern_cpuset.c#L1150-L1156) ORs the mask of every thread in the process; threads the guest did not create through libkernel are not included, and the console result is unverified

name: libkernel.L167
text: [pthread_setaffinity_np](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/Posix/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) - follows [FreeBSD 11.4](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libthr/thread/thr_affinity.c#L41-L62) libthr over `kern_cpuset_setaffinity` for the calling thread and any live guest thread: a size other than the 32-byte `cpuset_t` returns `ERANGE`, an unknown or finished thread `ESRCH`. Bits outside `sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask` are dropped and a mask with none of those bits returns `EDEADLK`, as `cpuset_setaffinity` does; the affinity is recorded on the guest thread and not applied to the host thread, and the console result is unverified

name: libkernel.L165
text: [cpuset_setaffinity](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/Posix/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) - the calling thread, another live guest thread selected by its guest TID, or the calling process is handled; other levels (ROOT/CPUSET) and other scopes (CPUSET/JAIL) throw as unmodelled, invalid levels or scopes return `EINVAL` and unknown thread or process IDs return `ESRCH`, following [FreeBSD 11.4](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/d106002967eff712894ab8b5337bbbff106ce5e0/sys/kern/kern_cpuset.c#L1281-L1286) thread selection. Bits outside `sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask` are dropped, and a mask with none of those bits fails with `EDEADLK`, as FreeBSD does when the new set has no CPU in common with the parent set. Guest-TID lookup and the update hold the thread registry lock so a join cannot release the target during access. Affinity is recorded for guest CPU reporting and child inheritance, not applied to host scheduling; PS5 behaviour has not been measured

name: libkernel.L45
text: [sceKernelGetModuleInfoForUnwind](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/Module.cpp) (libkernel) - on Windows the `.ehmeta` tables and the image file name are cached per allocation base and dropped after a loader free (`dlclose`, `sceKernelStopUnloadModule`, the thread atexit release) when the module is no longer loaded. A table changed in place, or an image freed by anything other than the loader, is not noticed. An address inside an image of the Windows loader's module list whose tables are cached is resolved with `RtlPcToFileHeader` and no `VirtualQuery`; other addresses, and images without tables, still use `VirtualQuery`. The `.eh_frame` walk that finds its end is done once per image instead of once per call

name: libkernel.L234
text: [app0.zar files](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/ArchivedFile.cpp) (libkernel) - `sceKernelOpen`, `open`, `sceKernelStat` and `sceKernelCheckReachability` resolve a path missing from `app0/` in `app0.zar`. An archived file is a read-only host null device whose reads, positioned and vectored reads, AIO reads, seeks, `fstat` and `FIONREAD` are served from the archive, with the position shared by `dup`, `dup2` and `F_DUPFD`; writes fail with `EBADF` as on a read-only descriptor, opening one for writing or truncation fails with `EROFS` and `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` with `EEXIST`. `fstat` and `sceKernelStat` report mode `0444` (`0555` for a directory), the node index as inode and the archive file's device and times. Opening an archived directory or a directory present both on disk and in the archive throws, as `getdents` would miss entries. On an archived descriptor `mmap`, `flock`, record locks, `fstatfs`, `ftruncate`, `fsync`, `fdatasync`, `getdirentries`, `fchmod` and `futimes` throw instead of acting on the null device; `mmap` is `noexcept`, so its refusal terminates the process. `lstat` and the other path calls on archived files are not implemented

name: libkernel.L211
text: [fcntl](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/DescriptorControl.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD 11.4's [`kern_fcntl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L479-L799) and [`kern_dup`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L812) on file, directory, pipe and character device descriptors; a socket keeps the libSceNet path (`F_DUPFD`, `F_DUP2FD`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `F_DUP2FD_CLOEXEC`, `F_GETFL`, `F_SETFL` with `O_NONBLOCK`, `F_GETFD` and `F_SETFD`, `EINVAL` for every other command, see the next entry). On Linux and macOS a host socket that is not a guest socket, such as a standard descriptor a service manager connected to its journal, takes the flag handling of a pipe end and `FIONREAD` asks the host for its queued bytes (for a datagram socket Linux counts only the next datagram, where FreeBSD's [`soo_ioctl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/sys_socket.c#L202-L205) counts every buffered byte); its record locks and read-ahead hints fail with `EBADF`, as FreeBSD fails them on a descriptor without a vnode, and `O_ASYNC` on it throws. The close-on-exec flag and the status flags live in a guest table, the status flags shared by `dup`, `dup2` and `F_DUPFD` as in an open file description; a descriptor the table has not seen, such as 0 to 2, starts from the host's flags, since the console's are not known. `F_GETFL` takes the access mode from the host (the granted access of the handle on Windows), so pipe ends report `O_RDONLY` and `O_WRONLY` where FreeBSD's bidirectional pipes report `O_RDWR`. `F_DUPFD` and `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC` return the lowest free host descriptor at or above the start, so the bound is the host table (`EMFILE` on Windows, `EINVAL` past `RLIMIT_NOFILE` on Linux), not the console's unknown `RLIMIT_NOFILE` and `kern.maxfilesperproc`. `O_NONBLOCK` switches a host pipe (`PIPE_NOWAIT` on Windows, where an empty read and a full write then report `EAGAIN`) and is only recorded on files, directories and the random device, as their reads never block; on a Windows console or other character device it throws. Changing `O_APPEND` on a Windows file, changing `O_FSYNC` on a file, `O_ASYNC` on a pipe or character device (`SIGIO` is not delivered), `F_GETOWN`, `F_SETOWN` and `F_SETLK_REMOTE` throw; `O_DIRECT`, `F_RDAHEAD` and `F_READAHEAD` are recorded as the hints they are. Record locks (`F_GETLK`, `F_SETLK`, `F_SETLKW` and their forms without `l_sysid`) use the host's POSIX locks on Linux and macOS. `F_GETLK` with `F_UNLCK` asks the host with `F_RDLCK`: as in [`lf_blocks`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_lockf.c#L866) only another owner's overlapping write lock conflicts with either request. On Windows they follow [`kern_fcntl`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L607-L752) and [`lf_advlockasync`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_lockf.c#L433-L487) for the one guest process, which owns every lock: `EOVERFLOW` for an `SEEK_CUR` start past `OFF_MAX`, then `EBADF` for `F_RDLCK` without read access or `F_WRLCK` without write access and `EINVAL` for another type, then `EINVAL` and `EOVERFLOW` for the range; as [`lf_blocks`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_lockf.c#L866) never lets locks of one owner conflict, whichever descriptor or thread asks, `F_SETLK` and `F_SETLKW` then succeed without waiting and `F_GETLK` reports `F_UNLCK`, so no lock list is kept and merging, splitting and the release on close have nothing to change. Nothing is held on the host, since Windows byte-range locks are mandatory and would fail the guest's own reads and writes through other descriptors, so other host processes neither see these locks nor are seen; a lock from the end of a directory throws. The return values and error codes are unverified on a console

name: libkernel.L168
text: [dup and dup2](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) throw for the combinations they do not model: `dup2` of a guest socket onto descriptors 0 to 2, whose host streams libc writes without the socket table, and on Windows duplicating a directory descriptor. Guest sockets share one socket object between the duplicates; the numbers come from the host descriptor table like those of files. The errno values for descriptor exhaustion are not verified against the console. On Windows a guest `dup2` onto descriptor 1 or 2 keeps host logging on an `_fdopen` of a duplicate, and the guest `FILE` stays on the descriptor that was replaced; opening that duplicate throws (#7791)

name: libkernel.L212
text: [fcntl on a guest socket](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) answers `F_DUPFD`, `F_DUP2FD`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `F_DUP2FD_CLOEXEC`, `F_GETFD`, `F_SETFD`, `F_GETFL` and `F_SETFL` and fails every other command with `EINVAL`; FreeBSD 11.4's `kern_fcntl` also handles `F_GETOWN` and `F_SETOWN` on a socket. `FD_CLOEXEC` is only recorded (there is no `exec`): `dup`, `dup2`, `F_DUPFD`, `F_DUP2FD` onto another descriptor and an accepted socket start without it, `F_DUP2FD` onto the same descriptor keeps it, and `SOCK_CLOEXEC`, `F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC`, `F_DUP2FD_CLOEXEC` and `F_SETFD` set it. None of this was measured on a console.

name: libkernel.L170
text: [execv](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) throws: replacing the process image is not supported, the same as `execvp`. PPSA97358 imports it and fails to load without it.

name: libkernel.L171
text: [execve](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) throws like `execvp`: replacing the process image is not supported. The console behavior for invalid arguments and executable path lookups is not modeled.

name: libkernel.L182
text: [execvp](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) throws: replacing the process image is not supported. PPSA85300 imports it and fails to load without it; its `fork` and `vfork` fail with `ENOSYS` ([libc_missing.c](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC/blob/f3253020a64368153233ede29183014c0b6c8979/ps5/compat/libc_missing.c#L290-L292)), so the child process that would call it is never created.

name: libkernel.L210
text: [sceKernelFcntl](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Open.cpp) (libkernel) runs the POSIX `fcntl` below and returns its guest errno as `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_*`, the form the other `sceKernel` file exports use. The return values and error codes are unverified on a console

name: libkernel.L195
text: [kevent on a pipe](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/Kqueue.cpp) (libkernel) - host pipes are one-way, where FreeBSD's [`kern_pipe`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/sys_pipe.c#L422) opens both ends for reading and writing, so `EVFILT_READ` on the write end and `EVFILT_WRITE` on the read end throw; on macOS `EVFILT_WRITE` on a pipe throws, as the host has no call for a pipe's capacity. `EVFILT_WRITE` reports the free space of the host buffer, not of FreeBSD's 16 KiB one, and on Linux fires when the host says the pipe is writable rather than at `PIPE_BUF` (512) free bytes. Windows pipes cannot be waited on, so a kqueue waiting on one checks it every 1 ms. Otherwise [`filt_piperead`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/sys_pipe.c#L1787-L1828) and `filt_pipewrite` are followed: `EV_EOF` once the other end closes, `EPIPE` for a write event added after the read end closed, and `NOTE_LOWAT` ignored. On Windows `fcntl` cannot make a pipe write end non-blocking, so the full-pipe and drain case of `EVFILT_WRITE` is tested on Linux only and the `NtQueryInformationFile` write quota is checked there only for the free space, `EV_EOF` and `EPIPE`.

name: libkernel.L137
text: [/dev/random and /dev/urandom](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/RandomDevice.cpp) (libkernel) opened for reading return a descriptor backed by the host null device whose reads are filled with host OS entropy (`getentropy`, `rand_s` on Windows); both paths behave the same, never block, and positioned reads ignore the offset (FreeBSD `random(4)`). Only the exact paths are recognised, `fstat`, `lseek` and `mmap` see the null device, and opening them for writing throws

name: libkernel.L128
text: [Windows file identity](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/NativeStat.cpp) (libkernel) - `stat` and `fstat` report the volume serial number as `st_dev` and the 64-bit file index folded into the guest's 32-bit `st_ino` (never 0), so two different files can in principle share an `st_ino`; the fold is not taken from a reference. `st_nlink` is clamped to 65535, the width of the guest field. The call keeps the `_wstat64` values when `GetFileInformationByHandle` fails

name: libkernel.L214
text: [Regular file mappings](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) - on Linux `mmap` maps a regular file's descriptor shared or private like a shared memory object, with the same access checks; SQLite's WAL index (`-shm`) in Dusklight PPSA99305 needs it. FreeBSD 11 `mmap(2)` and shadPS4's `MemoryManager::MapFile` map regular files; the console's behaviour is not measured. Other descriptors (pipes, sockets, directories, devices) still fail with `EOPNOTSUPP`. On Windows a shared mapping is a view of a file section (`CreateFileMappingW` on the descriptor's handle, read-write when the descriptor is, otherwise read-only), so writes through the descriptor and the mapping see each other. This also maps anonymous `shm_open` objects and JIT shared memory descriptors, which are temporary files on Windows. A shared mapping may end inside the 16 KiB page that holds the end of the file, as POSIX [`mmap`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/mmap.html) allows (llama.cpp in PS5LM Plus PPSA99581 maps a whole model file this way): the section keeps the file's size, so the file never grows, the view ends with the 4 KiB host page that holds the end of the file, which Windows fills with zeros past it, and the rest of the guest page is private zero pages. As POSIX requires, the bytes past the end read zero and are never written to the file; bytes written to those private pages are seen only through that mapping, not through other mappings of the file, and a file that grows later does not show its new bytes there. A shared mapping that reaches a whole page past the end of the file fails with `EOPNOTSUPP`, where POSIX maps it and delivers `SIGBUS` on access, as do `PROT_EXEC` and a write-only descriptor. A read-write alias (`GuestArenaMapAlias`) of a mapped page that holds the end of the file throws. `mprotect` above the view's protection (writing through a read-only descriptor, or adding `PROT_EXEC`) fails with `EACCES` before anything changes; FreeBSD allows `PROT_EXEC` on a readable descriptor. Shrinking the file with `ftruncate` fails with `EINVAL` while any shared mapping of it exists, even one that does not cover the removed part, because the section keeps the file's size at `mmap`; FreeBSD truncates. A read-write alias of a view (`GuestArenaMapAlias`, used when the GPU imports guest memory) of a read-only file section fails, as the alias is mapped `PAGE_READWRITE`. Views of the same file made by separate `mmap` calls are separate sections, so write tracking does not treat them as aliases of each other. A private mapping on Windows is a copy of the file read at `mmap`, which POSIX allows (later changes to the file need not show); pages wholly past the end of the file fail with `EOPNOTSUPP` instead of faulting on access, and a write-only descriptor fails with `EOPNOTSUPP`.

name: libkernel.L135
text: [ftruncate, truncate, sceKernelFtruncate](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) extend a file on Windows with `SetFileInformationByHandle` (`FileEndOfFileInfo`), which reserves the clusters but writes no zero bytes, and report `EFBIG` for a length the volume cannot hold (`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` on a disk file; seen with a length of `INT64_MAX`, the size from which NTFS refuses it was not measured) and `ENOSPC` when the free space is smaller. FreeBSD 11.4 makes the extension a hole on a file system that has them ([`ffs_truncate`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/ufs/ffs/ffs_inode.c) writes only the last block), so a length above the free space succeeds there. A write behind the end of the file still makes NTFS write zero bytes over the gap, as the file is not sparse. None of this was measured on a console.

name: libkernel.L126
text: [Windows file timestamps](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/include/WindowsFileTime.hpp) use the host filesystem's timestamp range and resolution. `utimes`, `futimes`, and `lutimes` reject timestamps outside nonnegative signed 64-bit Windows file-time ticks with `EINVAL`, including exactly 1601-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, whose zero value means "leave unchanged" to `SetFileTime`. Directory timestamp updates resolve the current path of the opened handle. Filesystems with coarser timestamp resolution cannot retain every guest microsecond

name: libkernel.L134
text: [Windows directory descriptors](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/DirectoryDescriptor.cpp) (libkernel) take one snapshot of the directory, on the first `getdents`, `getdirentries` or non-zero `lseek` (`SEEK_SET` or `SEEK_CUR`), and keep it until it is discarded; `lseek` to offset 0 only discards the snapshot, and the next read lists the directory again, so every rewind costs O(entries) on the next read. `lseek` takes the offset as an entry index and `SEEK_CUR` with offset 0 only reports the index. `SEEK_END` throws because FreeBSD defines it relative to the directory size, which is not modelled. A negative result returns `EINVAL` and a `SEEK_CUR` offset that overflows returns `EOVERFLOW`, as FreeBSD `vn_seek` reports them. Names whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds the one-byte `d_namlen` limit are not representable in this guest directory-record layout: `getdents` returns `ENAMETOOLONG` without consuming the entry. Repeated calls therefore report the same error and entries after that name cannot be reached through this descriptor; FreeBSD's `getdents` behavior for host filenames that exceed its `MAXNAMLEN` is not verified. `getdirentries` still reports 0 through `basep` instead of the position of the block it read, so only 0 and values returned by `lseek` are valid offsets; FreeBSD offsets are filesystem cookies. Descriptors retain the opened directory's native handle across renames. Enumeration reloads and `*at` operations resolve its current path, so a concurrent rename between resolution and the operation is not atomic. Enumeration of a removed directory and network-share path queries have not been verified

name: libkernel.L180
text: [getrlimit](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - `RLIMIT_CPU`, `RLIMIT_FSIZE`, `RLIMIT_CORE`, `RLIMIT_SBSIZE`, `RLIMIT_VMEM`/`AS`, `RLIMIT_NPTS`, `RLIMIT_SWAP`, `RLIMIT_KQUEUES` and `RLIMIT_UMTXP` report infinity as in FreeBSD's process-0 defaults, and `RLIMIT_DATA` mirrors the host limit; a payload process on a PS5 (firmware 12.70) reads 0x800000000 for both limits. `RLIMIT_NOFILE` reports, as both soft and hard limit, the number of descriptors after which AnyPS5 itself fails with `EMFILE`: on Windows the C runtime's 8192 low-level descriptors, which guest files, pipes and sockets all take, and as many stdio streams, which libkernel raises from 512 at load with [`_setmaxstdio`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/setmaxstdio), on Linux the host's `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, whose soft limit libkernel raises to the hard limit at load, and on macOS the smaller of the host's hard limit and `kern.maxfilesperproc`, which libkernel sets as both limits at load, since macOS fails with `EMFILE` at `kern.maxfilesperproc` whatever the soft limit. A payload process on a PS5 (firmware 12.70) reads 13952 for both limits, while `getdtablesize` returns 12555 and the process can open descriptors up to 12554. XPSemu (PPSA97358) reads `RLIMIT_NOFILE` in QEMU's `os_setup_limits` and raises the soft limit to the hard one when they differ. `RLIMIT_STACK` (0x200000), `RLIMIT_RSS` and `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` (infinity) and `RLIMIT_NPROC` (1604) report the soft and hard limits a payload process reads on a PS5 (firmware 12.70). Guest locking still follows the host: `mlock` and `sceKernelMlock` fail at the host's hard `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` on Linux, and on Windows when the process working set cannot grow, although `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` reports infinity. There the main thread's stack is 0x200000 as well (`pthread_attr_get_np`); here the main thread runs on the host thread's stack, whose size can differ. Whether a title process reads the same limits is unverified.

name: libkernel.L112
text: [getdtablesize](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - returns the smaller of the `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit of `getrlimit` and the host's `getdtablesize()`, capped at `INT_MAX`: FreeBSD returns the smaller of the `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit and `maxfilesperproc` ([`sys_getdtablesize`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L338-L355)), and the host call supplies that bound on macOS, where the soft limit alone is not one (`setrlimit` accepts soft limits above `maxfilesperproc`, `RLIM_INFINITY` included); `maxfilesperproc` is not measured on the console. The guest limit is the host's soft limit, raised to the hard limit when libkernel loads only on Linux: `core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/OpenFileLimit.cpp` is `__linux__`-only, so on macOS the guest gets whatever soft limit the host process inherited. VLC (PPSA85300) imports it for a `closefrom` loop in the child of its spawn helper ([libc_stubs.c](https://github.com/ZiZc3/VLC/blob/d46be6a68f4244466b041c2dc1b640915ac1a983/ps5/compat/libc_stubs.c#L66-L72)), which never runs because its `fork` fails with `ENOSYS`

name: libkernel.L29
text: [getuid, geteuid, getgid, getegid and issetugid](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) report the root identity (0) and a process that never changed credentials (`issetugid` 0), as a jailbroken process has; the host user and group are not exposed to the guest. The values a title sees on a console are unverified

name: libkernel.L82
text: [seteuid, setegid, setuid, setgid, setreuid, setregid, setgroups, getgroups](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - the guest process is assumed to run as root, with real, effective and saved user and group ids 0. As in FreeBSD's `sys_seteuid`, `sys_setegid`, `sys_setuid`, `sys_setgid`, `sys_setreuid` and `sys_setregid`, id 0 (or -1 for an unchanged `setreuid`/`setregid` id) is then accepted without a privilege check and changes no credential, so 0 is returned; any other id would change an id, which is not modelled, and throws. `setgroups` keeps the supplementary group list as `kern_setgroups` does (`NGROUPS_MAX` 1023, an empty list leaves the effective group as the only entry, a first entry other than 0 would change the effective group and throws) and `getgroups` reports it. The ids and privileges a title has on a console are unverified

name: libkernel.L17
text: [getlogin_r](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Login.cpp) (libkernel) returns the host effective account name: `GetUserNameW` as UTF-8 on Windows and `getpwuid_r(geteuid())` on POSIX. A valid account returns a name even without a login session; host `getlogin_r`, `USER` and `LOGNAME` are not consulted. The console's login name and behaviour without a session are unknown. Account lookup or encoding failures, a missing or empty account name, and POSIX account records exceeding the 16 KiB lookup buffer throw; there is no replacement name or retry. A short guest buffer returns `ERANGE` without modifying it, and a null output returns `EFAULT`.

name: libkernel.L231
text: [getpriority](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD 11.4's [`sys_getpriority`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_resource.c#L93-L165) for the only guest process, which is taken to run at nice 0: `PRIO_PROCESS` and `PRIO_PGRP` with 0 or its own pid (the guest is taken to lead its own process group, see `kill`) and `PRIO_USER` with 0 or its user id 0 return 0, any other id fails with `ESRCH` and any other `which` with `EINVAL`. As in FreeBSD's libc, where `getpriority` is the bare system call, errno is left unchanged on success. The nice value of a title process on the console is unverified, and the host nice of the process or of the threads `APS5_THREAD_PRIORITY=high` raises is not reported. `setpriority` accepts the same target ids (any other id fails with `ESRCH`, any other `which` with `EINVAL`), clamps the value to FreeBSD's `PRIO_MIN`-`PRIO_MAX` (-20 to 20) and stores it as the guest process's nice value, which `getpriority` returns; the host scheduling class is not changed, and whether a title process may lower the value without privilege is unverified

name: libkernel.L181
text: [setrlimit](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) validates the resource and input in FreeBSD order, maps negative limits to infinity, and lowers a soft limit above the hard limit. A request other than `RLIMIT_NPROC` succeeds when its normalized values match `getrlimit`, or, for `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, when `rlim_max` does not exceed the current hard limit and `rlim_cur` does not exceed `rlim_max`, storing the updated limits for subsequent `getrlimit` queries; `RLIMIT_NPROC` always throws; descriptor allocation enforcement of the lowered soft limit is not implemented, and changing other limits throws because guest limit state is not stored. In a payload process on a PS5 (firmware 12.70), `setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE)` lowers a requested 13952 to 12555, as the hard and as the soft limit; here a request within the current hard limit is stored as given and one above it throws; setting `RLIMIT_STACK`, `RLIMIT_RSS` and `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK` to their current values succeeds and changes nothing, as here; setting `RLIMIT_NPROC` to its current 1604 also succeeds but leaves 1443, as FreeBSD 11 would if the console's `maxproc` were 1604: process 0's limit starts at `maxproc` ([`init_main.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/init_main.c#L550-L551)), `maxprocperuid` starts at nine tenths of it ([`subr_param.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/subr_param.c#L258)), and `setrlimit` lowers an `RLIMIT_NPROC` limit above `maxprocperuid` to it ([`kern_resource.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/kern_resource.c#L714-L718)); 1604 × 9 / 10 gives 1443. Neither value is measured: `kern.maxproc` fails with `ENOENT` in the payload process. Here that call throws, because the limit is not stored. Java 25 LAN / DNS (PPSA99869) sets `rlim_cur = MIN(0x100000, rlim_max)` during VM initialization

name: libkernel.L20
text: [sysconf](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/SystemConfiguration.cpp) (libkernel) - `_SC_CLK_TCK` returns 128, FreeBSD's `CLK_TCK` as its [`sysconf`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/sysconf.c#L100-L101) returns it ([`time.h`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/include/time.h#L48-L54)); the console's value is not checked, and no `times` reports ticks at that rate. CPython's `posix` module stops its import with "cannot read ticks_per_second" when the value is below 1, as the Python in PS5MC (PPSA99420) does. `_SC_ARG_MAX` returns 262144 (FreeBSD's `NCARGS`), `_SC_OPEN_MAX` returns the `RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft limit via `getrlimit` ([`sysconf.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/sysconf.c#L106-L115)), and `_SC_IOV_MAX` returns 1024 (FreeBSD's `UIO_MAXIOV`). Names other than `_SC_ARG_MAX`, `_SC_CLK_TCK`, `_SC_OPEN_MAX`, `_SC_PAGESIZE`, `_SC_IOV_MAX`, `_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF`, `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` and `_SC_PHYS_PAGES` fail with `EINVAL`

name: libkernel.L207

name: libkernel.L218
text: [inet_ntop, inet_pton](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/AddressConversion.cpp) (libkernel) - an `AF_INET6` result of `inet_ntop` is followed by zero bytes up to `size`. In a payload process on a PS5 (firmware 12.70), the text forms, the order of the checks and this padding were measured through both exports. The padding was sampled at sizes from 3 to 65536, above 64 only at 65, 128, 256, 1024, 4096 and 65536; the sizes that were not sampled, sizes above 65536 and a title process are assumed to behave the same

name: libkernel.L140
text: [sceKernelAddReadEvent and sceKernelAddWriteEvent](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/Equeue.cpp) (libkernel): a read event on a listening socket, here and in `kevent`, reports the number of completed connections waiting to be accepted in `data`, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`filt_solisten`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/uipc_socket.c#L3384-L3392) reports `so_qlen`: on Linux a TCP listener's accept queue from `TCP_INFO` (`tcpi_unacked`, which Linux fills with the accept backlog for a listening socket), and elsewhere, or for a listener that is not TCP, 1 while a connection is waiting, as no host call reports that count. A write event reports the free space of the socket's send buffer in `data`, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`filt_sowrite`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/uipc_socket.c#L3358-L3382) reports `sbspace`: on Linux the host's `SO_SNDBUF` less the bytes `SIOCOUTQ` counts as queued, which include the host's per-packet overhead, so the space shrinks by somewhat more than the bytes sent. Windows has no query for that space and macOS is not wired up, so both report the whole `SO_SNDBUF`, which does not shrink as data is queued. Only guest sockets are supported; other descriptors and a low watermark above 1 throw

name: libkernel.L222
text: [sceKernelGetEventError](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/EventAccessors.cpp) (libkernel) returns the event's `data` as an `int` when `EV_ERROR` (0x4000) is set in `flags` and 0 otherwise, as [KytyPS5](https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5/blob/947627d10d4ef4b68ba3c0189aab6c368e70a8d2/src/kernel/eventQueue.cpp#L663) does and as FreeBSD 11's [kevent](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.0.0/sys/kern/kern_event.c#L1005) reports a failed change (`flags = EV_ERROR`, errno in `data`). [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/kernel/ps4_queue.pas#L643) instead returns `fflags` plus `0x80020000` when `fflags` is nonzero. Whether the console reads `data` or `fflags` and returns the raw errno or an SCE error code is unverified. No event delivered by the equeue here carries `EV_ERROR`, so the call returns 0 for every event `sceKernelWaitEqueue` reports

name: libkernel.L141
text: [sceKernelAddReadEvent on pipes](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/Equeue.cpp) (libkernel) is the one exception to the sockets-only rule above: it also takes the read end of a pipe, as `kevent` does through FreeBSD's `filt_piperead`, and ignores the size argument there. name: libkernel.L209
text: [kill, killpg](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Signals.cpp) (libkernel) follow FreeBSD's `kern_kill` and `killpg1` for the only guest process: `EINVAL` for signals outside 0 to 128 and for negative `killpg` process groups, signal 0 only checks that the target exists, and its own pid, 0 and minus its own pid (the guest is taken to lead its own process group) signal it through `raise`, so they share `raise`'s limits above. Any other pid, and -1, which skips the caller, report `ESRCH`, so `EPERM` is never reported

name: libkernel.L208
text: [sigaction](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Signals.cpp) (libkernel) records the handler, flags and mask of every signal from 1 to 128 and reports them back, following FreeBSD's `sigaction` (`EINVAL` for other signals, and for a handler on `SIGKILL` or `SIGSTOP`); `signal` records its handler with `SA_RESTART`, as FreeBSD's libc does. Only handlers without `SA_SIGINFO` on the signals `signal` already delivers (`SIGINT`, `SIGILL`, `SIGABRT`, `SIGFPE`, `SIGSEGV`, `SIGTERM`) run, the same way `signal` handlers do; their mask and flags are not applied. `SA_SIGINFO` handlers are recorded but never called, since that needs FreeBSD's `siginfo_t` and `ucontext_t`, and neither are the handlers of other signals (`SIGBUS`, `SIGHUP`, ...), whether they are set by `sigaction` or by `signal`, which records them too (every number from 1 to 128, with `SA_RESTART` and an empty mask replacing what `sigaction` stored; `SIGKILL` and `SIGSTOP` accept only the default handler in both calls, as in FreeBSD's `kern_sigaction`). `raise` and `kill` accept every number from 1 to 128 now: a blocked one stays pending on the set of `sigtimedwait`, an unblocked one whose handler is registered runs it on the calling thread, and an unblocked one that has no host equivalent and no handler still fails with `EINVAL`, where FreeBSD runs its default action. `raise` of an `SA_SIGINFO` handler still throws instead of terminating

name: libkernel.L201
text: [madvise](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) accepts `MADV_PROTECT` (10) as a no-op hint without modifying process protection. FreeBSD 11's `kern_madvise` (`sys/vm/vm_mmap.c`) handles it before the address check, ignores the address and length, and calls `kern_procctl(..., PROC_SPROTECT, PPROT_SET)`, which requires `PRIV_VM_MADV_PROTECT` and fails with `EPERM` without it. Returning 0 unconditionally assumes the calling process is privileged. Console behaviour is unverified

name: libkernel.L202
text: [mincore](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD 11's `sys_mincore` (`sys/vm/vm_mmap.c`), not measured on the console: the address is rounded down to the page, length 0 returns 0, a null vector over a mapped range returns `EFAULT`, an overflowing range or any unmapped page in the range (as reported by `sceKernelVirtualQuery`) returns `ENOMEM`. For valid ranges, a page reports `MINCORE_INCORE` (0x1) when `sceKernelVirtualQuery` reports it committed and 0 when it is only reserved; actual residency, referenced and modified bits are not modelled. Length 0 returns 0 when the start page is mapped and `ENOMEM` otherwise, and the range and mapping checks come before the null vector `EFAULT`, as in `kern_mincore` Java 25 LAN / DNS (PPSA99869) imports it

name: libkernel.L203
text: [mlockall, munlockall](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) - `mlockall` returns `EINVAL` for zero or unknown flags. Valid `MCL_CURRENT` throws because it would lock host stacks, heaps, modules and driver mappings along with guest memory; `MCL_FUTURE` throws because later mappings are not tracked for locking. FreeBSD 11.4's `sys_munlockall` (`sys/vm/vm_mmap.c`:1133-1165) checks `priv_check(td, PRIV_VM_MUNLOCK)` first (returning `EPERM` without it) and unwires the user map (`vm_map_unwire` over `vm_map_min`...`vm_map_max` with `VM_MAP_WIRE_HOLESOK`). Returning 0 unconditionally assumes the calling process is privileged. `munlockall` unlocks memory locked by `mlock` (`VirtualUnlock` on Windows, tolerating `ERROR_NOT_LOCKED` for pages never locked, and `munlockall` on Linux). On main, XPSemu (PPSA97358) fails to load at these imports (mlockall #4386, munlockall); their calls in QEMU `os-posix.c` execute only when `-overcommit mem-lock=on` is enabled. The call has not been observed in a run with this implementation.

name: libkernel.L200
text: [msync](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) follows FreeBSD 11's `kern_msync` and `vm_map_sync`, not measured on the console: the address is rounded down to the page, a range that wraps is `EINVAL`, as is `MS_ASYNC` with `MS_INVALIDATE`, and a range whose start or any page is not mapped (as `sceKernelVirtualQuery` reports it, reservations included) is `ENOMEM`; a page unmapped from inside a larger mapping still counts as mapped there, since `sceKernelVirtualQuery` keeps reporting the whole mapping. The guest has no file mappings, so a successful call writes nothing back. `MS_INVALIDATE` on a mapped range throws: FreeBSD returns `EBUSY` when the range holds `mlock`ed pages, and locked pages are not tracked

name: libkernel.L121
text: [JIT shared memory](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Jit.cpp) (libkernel) - `sceKernelJitCreateSharedMemory`, `sceKernelJitCreateAliasOfSharedMemory` and `sceKernelJitMapSharedMemory` take the signatures of [Orbital](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital)'s `tools/ida/db_types.json` (name, length, maximum protection, descriptor out; descriptor, maximum protection, descriptor out; descriptor, protection, address in and out), which ps4sdk, ps5-jar-loader and the call sites in RetroArch PPSA99169, XPSemu PPSA97358 and VLC PPSA85300 match; SharpProspero declares the alias as returning the descriptor. The object is a host anonymous file shared by its descriptors (a `memfd` on Linux, a delete-on-close temporary file mapped as an executable section on Windows), the alias is a duplicate descriptor, and every map maps the whole object, so writes through one view show through the others; a non-null address is a hint, as in `mmap` without `MAP_FIXED`. Not measured on the console: a length that is zero or not a multiple of 16 KiB and protection bits other than CPU read, write and execute are `EINVAL`; an alias or a map asking for more than the descriptor's maximum protection (write and execute counting as read) is `EACCES`, as FreeBSD 11's `vm_map_protect` treats a protection past `max_protection`; a descriptor that is not a JIT object is `EBADF`. The name is ignored, the objects do not count against the flexible memory budget, `mprotect` of a view is not limited to the maximum protection, and `mmap` of the descriptors maps the object as a [regular file](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp), so its views and the JIT views see each other's writes. On Linux the `memfd` is created without `MFD_EXEC`, which Linux 6.3 added and older kernels reject with `EINVAL`, and relies on the protection of the mapping: the flag only sets the file's execute permission bits, and the direct memory `memfd` is mapped executable the same way; a host with `vm.memfd_noexec` set to 2 refuses the creation and the call throws

name: libkernel.L174
text: [kern.proc.vmmap](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/SystemConfiguration.cpp) (libkernel) - `sysctl` {`CTL_KERN`, `KERN_PROC`, `KERN_PROC_VMMAP`, pid} returns packed FreeBSD 11 `kinfo_vmentry` records (144 bytes each, an empty path) for the used ranges of the guest address-space arena, in address order, as [`kinfo_getvmmap`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/releng/11.0/lib/libutil/kinfo_getvmmap.c) reads them. A range is one record: the type is always `KVME_TYPE_DEFAULT`, the protection is `sceKernelVirtualQuery`'s for the range's first page (0 where it reports none), and offset, object, resident page counts, flags and path are 0. Only the calling process's pid is accepted (`ESRCH` otherwise, -1 included, as FreeBSD's `pget` gives); a write returns `EPERM` and a short buffer `ENOMEM`. Ranges outside the arena, which guest code cannot map, are not reported. The walk takes the arena lock once per range, not for the whole walk as FreeBSD holds the map lock, so an `mmap` or `munmap` on another thread can change the list between two records. Whether a PS5 application may read its own map, and what types and paths the console reports, is unverified

name: libkernel.L139
text: [Shared memory](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/SharedMemory.cpp) (libkernel) on Linux implements anonymous and named objects, bounded descriptor writes and seeks, and `shm_unlink` with effective read/write permission checks from FreeBSD 11. Named paths up to 1023 bytes use `/anyps5-shm-` plus SHA-1; collisions are not detected, and the namespace is shared across processes in the host mount namespace. Named creation applies the guest umask without changing the host mask. Linux procfs and `/dev/shm` are required. Operations use an advisory directory lock; external host operations bypass it, unrelated objects serialize, and descriptor operations require two spare host descriptors and compare device/inode with the initial descriptor identity on both the pinned-object and ordinary-file fallback paths. [Guest mappings](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) support shared and private mappings of these descriptors through the allocation tracker and pin a duplicate descriptor during validation and mapping; mapping requires one spare host descriptor; file-backed mappings use the write-watch scan fallback because aliases and descriptor writes bypass per-mapping tracking. On Windows, anonymous objects are delete-on-close temporary files and `mmap` maps them as [regular files](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp); named objects remain unsupported. Invalid non-null name pointers, console behaviour and title compatibility remain unverified.

name: libkernel.L74
text: [Fixed anonymous mmap](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/PosixMemory.cpp) (libkernel) - `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANON | MAP_FIXED` replaces the requested range through the existing guest mapping machinery and zeroes the new memory. `MAP_EXCL` is checked under the allocation-registry mutation lock, including virtual reservations, and returns `ENOMEM` without changing an occupied range; without `MAP_FIXED` it is `EINVAL`. Lengths are rounded to 16 KiB and fixed addresses must be aligned. The complete rounded range must lie inside the guest arena or, for POSIX fixed anonymous `mmap` on Windows, one current or registered native thread stack; other mapping APIs do not opt into stack replacement. Native stack replacement keeps the reservation, decommits and recommits fresh pages, and rejects foreign allocations, ranges spanning reservations and host `PAGE_GUARD` pages before mutation. Current-stack ranges must end at least 64 KiB below the active host frame; callers replacing another thread's stack must coordinate with that thread. If recommitting fails, the call returns `ENOMEM` with the range still reserved; thread cleanup attempts to recommit it before restoring write access. This follows FreeBSD 11.4 [argument validation and rounding](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/vm/vm_mmap.c#L226-L299), [fixed replacement](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/vm/vm_map.c#L1455-L1464), and [collision errno](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/vm/vm_mmap.c#L1604-L1613). The console behaviour has not been measured. AnyPS5 starts the guest arena at 0x200000000, so the fixed path rejects the low 0x400000 address requested by PICO-8 PPSA99808. The console address-space layout is unmeasured; executable placement outside the host arena is tracked in #5217. Static catalog disassembly finds `0x1012` in PPSA98001/PPSA99808 and `0x5012` in PPSA99808; these titles were not run.

name: libkernel.L152
text: [scePthreadAttrGet, pthread_attr_get_np and sceKernelIsStack](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/src/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) report the stack of a host thread the library did not create, on Windows, from one allocation granule (64 KiB) above the bottom of its reservation when everything above that is committed read-write, as in a relinked executable's main thread and its default-size host threads (0x200000 committed of 0x210000 reserved), so the guest can protect the lowest reported pages, as HotSpot does for its stack guard pages in Java 25 LAN / DNS (PPSA99869). Any other such thread, and every such thread on Linux, gets its whole host stack: on Windows `mprotect` commits its reserved lower pages before protecting them and drops the guard flag of Windows' guard pages, and on Linux it cannot change the unmapped lower pages

name: libkernel.L119
text: [sceKernelMprotect, sceKernelMtypeprotect](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/DirectMemory.cpp) (libkernel) over a range with a gap that is not registered in the allocation tracker protect the registered parts and skip the gap, and return 0, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`vm_map_protect`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/vm/vm_map.c) does (it has no check for holes); a range whose start is unmapped (also when later pages are mapped) returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EINVAL` (`mprotect`: `EINVAL`) because an existing test pins that for an unmapped start; FreeBSD answers 0 there too (`vm_map_protect` takes the next entry), so this errno is not taken from the source and was not changed. `sceKernelMprotect` threw for a gap before, which ended the title. Every part is checked for a GPU or image pin before the first one is protected; the parts are then protected one after the other, so a host protection failure in a later part leaves the earlier parts changed (FreeBSD's `vm_map_protect` cannot fail in its second pass). The behaviour on the console is not known. None of this was measured on a console.

name: libkernel.L120
text: [sceKernelMprotect protection bits](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) - bits outside `0x3F7` are dropped instead of refused, as a PS5 (firmware 13.60) drops them: Onimusha: Way of the Sword (PPSA27836 01.000.001) maps direct memory with `0xf2` and then protects it with `0xfffffff2`, which the console reports as `0xf3` and then `0x3f3`. In a payload process the console also drops the CPU execute bit (`0x4`) of flexible, direct and JIT memory, and POSIX `mprotect` with write and execute reports write only (`0x2`). A title process may keep execute, so it is kept here. The map calls and `sceKernelMtypeprotect` refuse undefined bits on the console with `EINVAL` (`0x80020016`), and the direct map calls refuse execute; here both throw for undefined bits, and the direct map calls map execute

name: libkernel.L228
text: [Short sleeps ended by GPU and flip completions](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Time/SleepWake.cpp) (libkernel) - a `sceKernelUsleep`, `usleep`, `nanosleep` or `sceKernelNanosleep` of 1 ms or less returns before the requested time, which FreeBSD and the console do not do: it ends once the AGC driver reports a completed GPU batch or batch completion action, or VideoOut completes a flip, so a title that polls a GPU label or the flip status between sleeps does not sleep the rest. A title that paces frames with such a sleep can wake up to 1 ms early. A thread returns early at most 8 times in a run of sleeps; the run restarts when the thread submits AGC work or did not sleep the requested time since its last sleep, so a loop that counts sleeps to time out still sleeps all but 8 in full. `APS5_NO_SLEEP_WAKE=1` keeps every sleep in full

name: libkernel.L183
text: [nmount](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Stdio.cpp) (libkernel) throws: mounting file systems is not supported. Prospero Themes (PPSA90210) imports it and fails to load without it; it opens its theme library without calling it, and its strings (`/dev/ssd0.system_ex`, `/system_ex`, `exfatfs`, `fstype`, `fspath`, `from`, `ignoreacl`) point to remounting the console's `/system_ex` partition to write theme files there.

name: libkernel.L129
text: [lstat of a Windows symbolic link](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/NativeStat.cpp) (libkernel) reports a link whose target is relative, as `symlink` creates them, with the link's own times, `st_dev` and `st_ino`, mode `S_IFLNK | 0777` and the length of the target `readlink` returns as `st_size`. FreeBSD gives a new link `0777` less the creating process's umask, which the host does not keep, so the permission bits are not the console's. A link with an absolute target is reported the same way, using its print name, or its substitute name when the print name is empty, without a `\??\` or `\\?\` prefix. A directory junction is reported the same way when the name left after that prefix is a drive path (`X:\...`): the print name when that name is a drive path, otherwise the substitute name. A mounted volume, whose substitute name is `\??\Volume{GUID}\`, and any other reparse point throw, as for `readlink`. `open` with `O_NOFOLLOW` returns `EMLINK` for that junction and does not open the target

name: libkernel.L16
text: [physhm_open, physhm_unlink](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Unimplemented.cpp) (libkernel, NIDs `n371J5cP+uo` and `AUqJNkobQ1c`) - declared as throwing stubs: the PS5 physical shared memory API is not documented, and [shadPS4's module generator](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/moduleGenerator/blob/main/libraries/kernel.cpp) also declares both with no arguments and returns `ORBIS_OK`, so the signature, the handle a success would return and the console's behaviour are unmeasured. The no-argument `int` signature follows shadPS4. Forever Launcher (PPSA99030) imports both and stops at load on `physhm_open`, and the relinker resolves no call site for either in that title, so no handle is fabricated and both throw

name: libkernel.L193
text: [poll](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) waits on guest sockets and pipes, through `WSAPoll` on Windows and `poll` on Linux; the `pollfd` layout and flag values are FreeBSD's. A libSceNet socket joins the same host wait through the native socket libSceNet lends to libkernel. `WSAPoll` rejects `POLLPRI`, so on Windows a socket's `POLLPRI` is asked as `POLLRDBAND` and `POLLIN` as `POLLRDNORM`; Winsock reports urgent data until it is read with `MSG_OOB`, where FreeBSD 11.4's `sopoll_generic` stops once the normal stream passes the mark. Guest `send` and `recv` refuse `MSG_OOB` with `EOPNOTSUPP`, so urgent data can only come from an outside peer and Windows keeps reporting `POLLPRI` after the stream passes the mark. A pipe follows FreeBSD's `pipe_poll`: the read end is readable when data is buffered, either end reports `POLLHUP` once the other end is closed, with the requested `POLLIN` and `POLLRDNORM` bits and without `POLLOUT`, which `pollscan` clears, and the write end is writable when `PIPE_BUF` (512) bytes are free on Windows, or when the host kernel says so on Linux. `POLLOUT` on a read end throws: FreeBSD opens both ends for reading and writing and reports it writable, and host pipes are one-way. Windows pipes cannot be waited on, so while a pipe is polled `poll` checks it with `NtQueryInformationFile` and waits on the sockets in slices of 1 ms. A regular file, a directory or a file read from app0.zar is always ready for `POLLIN`, `POLLRDNORM` and `POLLOUT` and never for `POLLPRI`, `POLLRDBAND` or `POLLWRBAND`, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`vop_stdpoll`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/vfs_default.c#L563-L574) and `vop_nopoll` answer every event `poll` accepts; which of the two the console's filesystems use is not known, and they agree on these events. `/dev/random` and `/dev/urandom` follow FreeBSD 11.4's [`randomdev_poll`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/dev/random/randomdev.c#L274-L285) for a seeded device: a request with `POLLIN` or `POLLRDNORM` gets only those bits back, and any other request gets every requested bit. Open descriptors 0 to 2 follow the console model `select` uses: descriptor 0 never reports an event and descriptors 1 and 2 report `POLLOUT`, whatever the host attaches to them. A closed descriptor reports `POLLNVAL`, and an open descriptor that is neither a guest socket, a libSceNet socket, a pipe, a file, a directory, the random device nor descriptor 0 to 2 (other devices, a kqueue) throws, as do event bits other than `POLLIN`, `POLLPRI`, `POLLOUT`, `POLLRDNORM`, `POLLRDBAND` and `POLLWRBAND` (the `POLLERR`, `POLLHUP` and `POLLNVAL` bits are ignored in `events`), an infinite timeout with no socket or pipe to wait on. A closed socket descriptor reports `POLLNVAL`; the console's limit on the descriptor count is unknown and not checked

name: libkernel.L78
text: [select](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Socket.cpp) (libkernel) - descriptor 0 is never reported readable and descriptors 1 and 2 are always writable, as for a console title with no input; reads from descriptor 0 still go to the host stdin. `/dev/random` and `/dev/urandom` follow `randomdev_poll` for a seeded device under [`selscan`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/sys_generic.c#L1178-L1236), which asks once with the flags of every set the descriptor is in: in the read set they are readable and reported in no other set, and otherwise they are reported in the write and exception sets they were asked in. Guest sockets and libSceNet sockets are polled. A kqueue is readable while one of its events is triggered and is never writable or in the exception set, as FreeBSD 11.4's [`kqueue_poll`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/kern_event.c#L1900-L1924) answers, on every host.
