name: libkernel.L86
text: [sceCoredumpGetThreadContextInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Coredump.cpp) (libkernel, NID `ShChva57wIM`) takes `(void* threadContextInfo, size_t threadContextInfoSize)` as in the [Orbital type database](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/cc408367da6a6ebbf5ac1ac559fefeadc73b2831/tools/ida/db_types.json); the 144-byte block of 18 64-bit registers follows [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelSystem.cs#L120-L141). It answers as `sceCoredumpGetStopInfoCpu`: the handler is never invoked here, so an aligned 144-byte request returns `NOT_IN_COREDUMP_HANDLER` without reading or writing the block, and null, unaligned or wrapping buffers and other sizes throw, as the console validation order is unverified. Planet Coaster (PPSA01736) imports it

name: libkernel.L85
text: [sceCoredumpGetStopInfoCpu](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Coredump.cpp) (libkernel) takes `(void* info, size_t size)` as in the [Orbital type database](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/cc408367da6a6ebbf5ac1ac559fefeadc73b2831/tools/ida/db_types.json); the 16-byte, 8-byte-aligned block follows [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelSystem.cs), which places coredump reads inside the handler. The handler is never invoked here, so a well-formed request returns `NOT_IN_COREDUMP_HANDLER` without reading or writing the block. Its value `0x81180003` follows [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1aacbc8db8253be685bf7ab4d9daae/src/core/libraries/kernel/coredump/coredump_error.h) and the NHL 27 (PPSA34063) call site reported in [#4275](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/discussions/4275), not a PS5 measurement. The console validation order is unverified: null, unaligned or wrapping buffers and sizes other than 16 throw instead of guessing an argument error. Information from an active coredump handler remains unsupported

name: libkernel.L42
text: [sceCoredumpGetStopInfoGpu_Agc](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Coredump.cpp) (libkernel, NID `Jrs7UUkGOFo`) - `(void* info, size_t size)` follows the same `libkernel.sprx` at 0x137E0: a null `info` returns `0x81180000`; syscall 601 (command 21) failing with `EPERM` returns `NOT_IN_COREDUMP_HANDLER`; otherwise two `libSceAgcDriver` imports (NIDs `+NIAY3DWpOw` and `LgctzJSGy7s`, names unknown) decide between `0x81180005` and, for a `size` of 8, storing the second one's 64-bit result and returning 0, with any other size returning `0x81180000`. The handler is never invoked here, so a non-null `info` returns `NOT_IN_COREDUMP_HANDLER` without writing, assuming `EPERM` outside the handler as above; the AGC branch is not reached

name: libkernel.L40
text: [sceCoredumpWriteUserString](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Coredump.cpp) (libkernel, NID `32KQRUK13kI`) - `(uint32_t, const char* text, int)` follows the console's `libkernel.sprx` (SDK 4.5x build of `J03950001`) at 0x13050: a null `text` returns `0x81180000`; otherwise the three arguments go to syscall 601 (command 10), whose `EPERM` becomes `SCE_COREDUMP_ERROR_NOT_IN_COREDUMP_HANDLER` (0x81180003), `EINVAL` `0x81180000`, and a success returns the value the kernel wrote back. Measured on a PS5 (firmware 13.60) from a homebrew payload with no core dump handler: the call succeeds with 0, the kernel rejects a first argument above 15 or a third outside 0 to 256 with `0x81180000`, and a 2047-character text is accepted. Those checks are reproduced and anything else returns 0; nothing is recorded, as there is no dump, and what the two numbers mean is unknown. PPSA16064 imports it

name: libkernel.L90
text: [sceKernelAddTimerEvent](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/Equeue.cpp) (libkernel) - `usec` is taken as the period in microseconds; re-adding an existing timer keeps its pending expiration count and restarts the period from the time of the call, where FreeBSD 12+ `filt_timertouch` clears pending expirations on `EV_ADD`; `usec == 0` fires on every wait. None of this is confirmed on a PS5 title

name: libkernel.L91
text: [sceKernelWaitEqueue](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/Equeue.cpp) (libkernel) - a level-triggered user event (`sceKernelAddUserEvent`) is reported at most once per call, as in FreeBSD `kqueue_scan` (`sys/kern/kern_event.c`), which re-queues a reported knote without `EV_CLEAR` or `EV_DISPATCH` behind the scan marker, and kevent(2), where several triggers do not produce several kevents. Not measured on a console. Events are scanned in list order and the list is not rotated, so when `num` is smaller than the number of ready level events the later ones can starve, where FreeBSD moves a reported level knote to the tail. Several completions of one AMPR or VideoOut event within one call are returned as separate entries, where FreeBSD would aggregate them; the Orbis behaviour is unconfirmed

name: libkernel.L145
text: [sceKernelAioSetParam](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Aio/src/Aio.cpp) (libkernel) writes the five values into the 20-byte scheduling struct the first argument points to, following the declarations in [Orbital](https://github.com/AlexAltea/orbital/blob/cc408367da6a6ebbf5ac1ac559fefeadc73b2831/tools/ida/db_types.json), [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/5dfdb4b0b166e83dc9ae275001afb695f12c7174/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelAio.cs) and [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu/blob/cfa85df379f6eeeb165d7badf9b648e266fe77b7/ps5/include/sce/_fs.h). Whether the console checks the values is unknown, so a null struct, a scheduling window or delayed count limit outside 0..128, a split flag other than 0 or 1 and a split size or chunk size above 0x1000000 (SharpProspero's maximums) throw. The scheduling settings are not used: `sceKernelAioInitializeImpl` ignores the struct and requests run synchronously on submit

name: libkernel.L144
text: [sceKernelAioSubmitReadCommands, sceKernelAioSubmitWriteCommands and their Multiple variants](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Aio/src/Aio.cpp) (libkernel) on Windows transfer through the same positioned path as `sceKernelPread`/`sceKernelPwrite` and restore the descriptor's file pointer afterwards; positioned transfers, plain transfers and seeks of one descriptor are serialized per descriptor (shared across duplicated descriptors), so a concurrent transfer observes a stable file pointer

name: libkernel.L53
text: [sceKernelAvailableDirectMemorySize](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) - how the console handles invalid arguments is not measured. A negative `search_start`, a `search_end` at or below `search_start` and an alignment that overflows when rounded up to 16 KiB return `EAGAIN` (`0x80020023`); bounds that are not multiples of 16 KiB are rounded inward, the alignment is raised to a multiple of 16 KiB and need not be a power of two, and a `search_end` past the pool is cut to it. fpPS4's HLE wrapper on its trunk branch refuses all of these with `EINVAL` ([ps4_map_mm.pas](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/kernel/ps4_map_mm.pas#L558-L570))

name: libkernel.L10
text: [sceKernelInternalMemoryGetAvailableSize](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) reports 0 bytes and returns 0: what the console's internal memory pool holds and how large it is are unknown. The `int (size_t*)` signature is from [xUtilty](https://github.com/Backporter/xUtilty/blob/328a856af1ef/source/SystemWrapper.cpp#L85) (PS4). PPSA99203 calls it once beside `sceKernelAvailableFlexibleMemorySize` while starting its GS renderer and never reads the result ([GS.cpp](https://github.com/Swordpdf/PS5SX2/blob/b4cf55e87c34/pcsx2/GS/GS.cpp#L233-L247))

name: libkernel.L52
text: [sceKernelAvailableFlexibleMemorySize](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) - the segments of the title's executable and of its `.guest.prx` modules count against the configured flexible-memory budget (448 MiB by default) while loaded, for this size and for flexible maps. A title may declare a larger budget through `kernel.flexibleMemorySize` in `param.json`; this does not reduce the 13.5 GiB direct-memory size. Rejection of zero or a value not aligned to 16 KiB has not been measured on a console. This segment-accounting model follows [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/3a9f57265d28975658f1ca941daa5c879c7a74bd/src/core/module.cpp#L165), which maps every segment of a module outside its system module directory as flexible memory on the PS4. [Counted](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) are the segments the title's ELF gives permissions, each rounded to 16 KiB pages; not counted are segments without permissions, the relinker's own blocks (on Linux both are the read/write/execute `PT_LOAD`s, plus the header block at file offset 0; on Windows everything outside the `.elf` sections) and the host system libraries. The Linux image carries no marker for the relinker's blocks, so they are told apart by those flags and that offset only: a title segment that is writable and executable, or starts at file offset 0, is not counted. A module whose segments exceed what is left still loads, and the available size then reads 0; shadPS4 fails the segment map instead ([memory.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/3a9f57265d28975658f1ca941daa5c879c7a74bd/src/core/memory.cpp#L519-L524) returns `EINVAL`, [module.cpp](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/3a9f57265d28975658f1ca941daa5c879c7a74bd/src/core/module.cpp#L168-L169) asserts). Which segments the PS5 charges, its rounding, whether system modules use the title's budget and when an unload releases the charge are not measured. PPSA15508 subtracts the reported size and a 10 MiB module allowance from its own 448 MiB budget at start-up and stops when the result exceeds its 146 MiB code and data limit ([#2883](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/2883))

name: libkernel.L72
text: [sceKernelMtypeprotect](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/DirectMemory.cpp) (libkernel) - sets the memory type of the direct mappings in the page-rounded range and of the direct memory behind them, as shadPS4 and prosper do (KytyPS5 ignores the type); the type is not validated, flexible pages in the range only get the protection, and a later map of the retyped direct memory reports the type it was allocated with. `sceKernelBatchMap2` operation 4 takes the same path with the entry type

name: libkernel.L9
text: [sceKernelEnableDmemAliasing](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) returns 0 and changes nothing: direct memory can always be mapped more than once here, as `DoMapDirect` in [DirectMemory.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/DirectMemory.cpp) only checks that the physical pages are allocated, so there is no aliasing to turn on. [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1aacbc8db8253be685bf7ab4d9daae/src/core/libraries/kernel/memory.cpp#L39-L43) (PS4) sets a flag there that lifts the `EBUSY` its [`sceKernelMapDirectMemory2`](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1aacbc8db8253be685bf7ab4d9daae/src/core/libraries/kernel/memory.cpp#L299-L301), and [`sceKernelMapDirectMemory` for SDK 2.50 and later](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1aacbc8db8253be685bf7ab4d9daae/src/core/libraries/kernel/memory.cpp#L237-L242), return for direct memory that is [already mapped](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1aacbc8db8253be685bf7ab4d9daae/src/core/memory.cpp#L548-L553); that check is not applied here. The no-argument `int` signature follows shadPS4 and ProsperoEden (PPSA99008), which calls it before mapping the same direct memory again. Whether the PS5 refuses such a mapping without the call is unverified

name: libkernel.L15
text: [sceKernelError](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Error.cpp) follows [shadPS4's kernel implementation](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/23c41333822fe8eca4c609b43119180af63ae4ac/src/core/libraries/kernel/kernel.cpp): zero returns zero; other guest POSIX error values receive the `0x80020000` bias without modifying errno. Arithmetic is defined modulo 32 bits to avoid signed overflow for inputs outside the errno domain. Console behavior for those inputs and PS5 equivalence have not been measured.

name: libkernel.L27
text: [sceKernelGetAllowedSdkVersionOnSystem](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/SoftwareVersion.cpp) (libkernel) reports the system software version with the 12 patch bits set, `0x01000fff`, as [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/98fd0689/src/core/libraries/kernel/kernel.cpp) does on the PS4 and as [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/main/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelSystem.cs) describes it, which Prospero Explorer (PPSA99109) reads it through; a null pointer returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EINVAL`. The console's value and its errors are unverified

name: libkernel.L30
text: [sceKernelGetAppInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - only `app_id` and the title ID (offset 0x10, up to 9 characters plus a terminator) are written; callers declare the structure with different sizes, so the rest is left alone. `app_id` is 1, the running title's id in libSceSystemService, which is a guess, not something measured. The error codes follow shadPS4: `EPERM` for another process, and 0 without writing anything for a null pointer.

name: libkernel.L69
text: [sceKernelGetCurrentCpu](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - guest affinities are not applied to host threads, so the host CPU index is mapped into the calling thread's affinity clipped to `sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask` (the available mask when they do not overlap): host CPU n reports the (n modulo the CPU count)-th CPU of that mask, so a thread pinned to one CPU reports that CPU, as a FreeBSD `cpuset` guarantees on the console. Which CPU the console reports for a thread allowed on several is not known; shadPS4 returns 0

name: libkernel.L68
text: [sceKernelGetAvailableCpumask](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/src/Thread.cpp) (libkernel) - returns the default thread affinity, 0x1FFF (CPUs 0 to 12), as KytyPS5 does. Titles pin threads within it (PPSA02664 passes 0x1FFB, Hades II PPSA36082 0x3 and 0x3F); whether CPU 13 is available to a title is not confirmed

name: libkernel.L8
text: [sceKernelGetMainSocId and sceKernelGetCpumode](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) both return 0, and [sceKernelGetCpuFrequency](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Time/Time.cpp) returns the host TSC frequency measured for `sceKernelGetTscFrequency`, not the console CPU clock. The PS5's SoC id and CPU mode are unknown; shadPS4's PS4 values are [0x710f10/0x740f30 and 0, 2 or 5 from the param.sfo CPU-mode flags](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/e0a466753a1a/src/core/libraries/kernel/process.cpp). PPSA99203 only logs them (`[console] main SoC id: result=%#x out=%#x`, `CPU: %llu Hz, cpumode %d`), passing a pointer that `sceKernelGetMainSocId` leaves untouched

name: libkernel.L109
text: [sceKernelGetCpuTemperature, sceKernelGetSocSensorTemperature](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/ThermalSensors.cpp) (libkernel) - read the host's thermal sensors: on Linux from `/sys/class/hwmon` and `/sys/class/thermal`, on Windows from the ACPI thermal zones (`MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature` over WMI) and the storage temperature property of the first physical drive. Sensor 0 is the CPU/package value, 1 the first other value and 2 an NVMe value; a host that exposes none reports every sensor as unsupported (`EINVAL`). The console's SoC channel count and meanings are hardware-dependent and differ from the host's, the host sensors are not the console's, the ACPI reading is unavailable on many machines, and the storage temperature property is numbered 52 on Windows 10 2004 and later and 22 before it, so the mapping, the values and the unsupported-input error are unverified; the storage channel was checked against the drive's own SMART composite temperature on one NVMe host (`StorageDeviceTemperatureProperty`, 36 °C on a WD_BLACK SN7100). `sceKernelGetCpuTemperature` reports sensor 0. PPSA99058 and PPSA99420 call both

name: libkernel.L146
text: [sceKernelGetFsSandboxRandomWord](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Sandbox.cpp) (libkernel) returns a fixed directory name, `gkbHtXc3Wq`. On the console the name is the process's randomized path (syscall 602, `randomized_path`), and the sandbox exposes system files under it, such as `common/lib` and `common/cert`. Nothing is mounted under the name here, so `/gkbHtXc3Wq/common/...` resolves under the guest root like any other path and does not exist, except `/gkbHtXc3Wq/common/cert/CA_LIST.cer`, which [SandboxCertificates.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/SandboxCertificates.cpp) serves from the host trust store

name: libkernel.L43
text: [sceKernelInternalMemoryGetModuleSegmentInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - the `(InternalSegmentInfo* result)` signature, the 16-byte `{address, size}` result and the choice of the main program's first segment follow [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/kernel/ps4_libkernel.pas#L343-L355) only, which fills it through its `sceKernelGetLibkernelTextLocation` from the first segment of `eboot.bin`; whether the console reports that segment, the text of libkernel itself or the calling module's is unknown. The segment is the first one `sceKernelGetModuleInfo` reports for the main program, and 0 is returned. A null result throws. 44 audited titles that bundle their own `libc.prx` import it; no call has been observed

name: libkernel.L50
text: [sceKernelGetLibkernelTextLocation](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - the `(void** address, std::size_t* size)` signature and the choice of the main program's first segment follow [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/kernel/ps4_libkernel.pas#L338-L348); whether the console reports that segment, the text of libkernel itself or the calling module's is unverified. The segment is the first one `sceKernelGetModuleInfo` reports for the main program, and 0 is returned. A null argument throws.

name: libkernel.L49
text: [sceKernelGetModuleList2 and sceKernelGetModuleInfo2](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - the title-module variants follow [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/main/src/core/libraries/kernel/process.cpp): `sceKernelGetModuleList2` lists what `sceKernelGetModuleList` lists without system libraries, and `sceKernelGetModuleInfo2` answers `EPERM` for a system library after the `EFAULT`, `EINVAL` and `ESRCH` checks of `sceKernelGetModuleInfo`. A system library here is a loaded `.prx` image that is not a relinked title module (`.guest.prx`); the main program and the title's own modules are listed. Not verified on the console. PPSA34063 imports both and fails to load without them

name: libkernel.L48
text: [sceKernelGetModuleInfo](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - the 0x160-byte layout (`st_size`, `name[256]`, 4 segments, `segment_count`, `fingerprint[20]`) follows [fpPS4](https://github.com/red-prig/fpPS4/blob/04cefd43e6fddd1ab033e7980cd356d14c964905/sys/sys_types.pas#L319-L337) and [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/module.h#L15-L31). Only that `st_size` is accepted, as in shadPS4; other sizes return `EINVAL`, a null pointer `EFAULT` and a handle `sceKernelGetModuleList` does not list `ESRCH`. Name and segments are the ones `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` reports, on Windows from the same PE sections, so `prot` uses the read/write/execute bits 1/2/4, while fpPS4 and shadPS4 store the ELF `p_flags`. The fingerprint is left zero, as the host image does not carry it

name: libkernel.L44
text: [sceKernelGetModuleInfoForUnwind](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/Module.cpp) (libkernel) - on Linux the tables come from `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr`, whose `eh_frame_size` includes the zero terminator, as measured on firmware 13.60 (reported in [#2419](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/issues/2419), not reproduced here); on Windows it is assumed to stop before the terminator. LLVM libunwind's `CFI_Parser::findFDE` stops at the terminator or the length, whichever comes first, so it finds the same FDEs either way. Only the main executable and `.guest.prx` images report tables; other host images report none, as on Windows

name: libkernel.L47
text: [sceKernelGetModuleList](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - lists the main program and every loaded `.prx` image in load order; host runtime libraries are left out. The handles are the ids `sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr` reports, not the console's. The `(int32_t* handles, size_t count, size_t* actual)` signature and returning `ENOMEM` without writing `actual` after filling the first `count` handles when more images are loaded follow [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4/blob/0fe263a4760dfbfa973366890061749b4af0de97/src/core/libraries/kernel/process.cpp#L244-L264); whether the console writes any handles in that case is unknown

name: libkernel.L46
text: [sceKernelGetModuleInfoFromAddr](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Module/src/ModuleInfo.cpp) (libkernel) - the 0x1A8-byte info layout follows the [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4) reimplementation; a title's `libc.prx` reads only `id` (PPSA14632). The meaning of `flags` is unknown; only 2 is accepted. The input `st_size` is ignored, because PPSA21703's `libc.prx` passes an uninitialized 0x1A8-byte buffer; the full size is written back. The id is the `sceKernelLoadStartModule` handle of an image opened through the loader and otherwise a stable id from the same range. The name is the host file name without `.guest.prx`. An image with more than 4 load segments (the converted executable has 7) reports its first 4. `tls_offset` is 0 and `ref_count` is 1, as the host loader exposes neither. On Windows the module is the PE image holding the address: a relinked image reports its `.elf` sections as segments and the eh_frame_hdr recorded in `.ehmeta`, any other image its first 4 sections with memory access and the `.ehfram` section without an eh_frame_hdr; the TLS fields and `init_proc_addr`/`fini_proc_addr` are 0

name: libkernel.L84
text: [sceKernelGetOperationMode](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) - the signature `(int* mode, int* submode)` comes from PPSA12544, which logs both values after the call and ignores the result. A homebrew payload on a PS5 (firmware 13.60) reads mode 2 and submode 0, nothing else is written, and the result register holds no status, so the function is taken to return nothing. Whether a title process reads the same values is unverified. Null outputs throw

name: libkernel.L226
text: [sceKernelGetPageTableStats](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/Export.cpp) (libkernel) reports 8192 entries on each side and counts them as a PS5 (firmware 13.60) counted them for a payload process: one cpu entry for each 2 MiB granule that holds a committed mapping, whatever its protection (none included), and one gpu entry for each 1 GiB region that holds a GPU-accessible mapping, plus one for each 2 MiB granule of such a mapping that is not a whole granule of direct memory at a 2 MiB-aligned physical address. A granule or region shared by several mappings counts once, and reservations do not count. On the console the first GPU mapping of a process also takes three gpu entries and one cpu entry that stay after it is unmapped, which is not modelled, and only the ranges whose protection is recorded here are counted. A null pointer returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EFAULT`, where the console faults. Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy (PPSA30601) calls it at start-up (#4067)

name: libkernel.L26
text: [sceKernelGetProsperoSystemSwVersion](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/SoftwareVersion.cpp) (libkernel) reports system software version `0x01000000` ("01.000.000"); the console's firmware version is not modeled. The 0x28-byte block (a 64-bit size at 0, the version string at 8 and the packed version at 0x24) follows [SharpProspero](https://github.com/SvenGDK/SharpProspero/blob/main/src/SharpProspero/Interop/Kernel/KernelSystem.cs), which Prospero Multi Tools (PPSA99110) and Prospero Explorer (PPSA99109) are built with and which sets the size to 40, and the same fields in [etaHEN](https://github.com/etaHEN/etaHEN/blob/main/Source%20Code/daemon/include/ipc.hpp) and [shsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/shsrv/blob/master/sh.c). A size other than 0x28 returns `SCE_KERNEL_ERROR_EINVAL` without writing; whether the console checks the size is unverified, since etaHEN and shsrv declare a 0x30-byte block and do not set it

name: libkernel.L5
text: [sceKernelGetSocPowerConsumption](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/ThermalSensors.cpp) (libkernel) - returns `EINVAL` and writes nothing, as `sceKernelGetSocSensorTemperature` does when the host has no sensor: the host's package power is not read (Linux RAPL `energy_uj` is readable by root only, and Windows has no general source). text: [Protecting a host thread's stack](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/DirectMemory.cpp) (libkernel) - on Windows `sceKernelIsStack` reports a host thread's whole stack reservation, which Windows commits on demand from the top down behind a guard page. A protect over that range changes only the pages above the guard; the guard page and the reserved pages below it are left as they are, so the stack still grows and an overflow still raises a stack overflow. A protect that starts at the bottom of the reservation and stops short of the guard page, as HotSpot makes its stack guard zones, is committed and protected. Windows moves the guard page down by committing the pages below it as read/write guard pages, whether they were reserved or committed, so those pages come in read/write as the stack grows to within one guard region of them (three pages on GitHub's runners). A protection other than read/write on them, `PROT_NONE` included, does not hold once the stack is that close, where on the console every page of the reported range takes the protection. Holding it would mean removing the thread's guard page and keeping the stack limit in its TEB by hand. On Linux the reported range of the main thread is mostly unmapped; the unmapped pages from the bottom of a protect up to the top of the stack are mapped read/write in place, then the protect is applied, so the stack never has to grow down to the protected pages, which Linux refuses within its stack guard gap (1 MiB by default) above a readable mapping. The pages below a protect stay unmapped and out of the stack's reach, where on the console the stack goes on below them

A payload process on a PS5 (firmware 12.70) gets -1 with `ENOENT` for it, for a read, a size query and a null length; what a title process gets was not measured. mimalloc reads it in [`unix_detect_overcommit`](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc/blob/31d034d94cdb8e22f7d7ed55967f581a2d6e831d/src/prim/unix/prim.c#L129-L153) and takes 0 as no overcommit, as PS5MC (PPSA99420) does at start-up

name: libkernel.L132
text: [system](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/Process.cpp) (libkernel) runs no command. It follows FreeBSD 11's `lib/libc/stdlib/system.c` for a sandbox without `/bin/sh`: a null command returns 1 unconditionally, as that version does, and any command returns the wait status of a child that could not exec the shell and called `_exit(127)` (`0x7f00`). Whether the console's application sandbox has no shell, and whether `vfork` succeeds there (FreeBSD returns -1 when it fails), is unverified

name: libkernel.L125
text: [tcsendbreak, tcdrain, tcflush, tcflow, tcgetpgrp, tcsetpgrp](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/Terminal.cpp) (libkernel) follow FreeBSD 11.4's [`termios.c`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/lib/libc/gen/termios.c): `tcflush` answers `EINVAL` for a queue other than `TCIFLUSH`, `TCOFLUSH` or `TCIOFLUSH` and `tcflow` for an action outside `TCOOFF`..`TCION` before the descriptor is looked at, and every other call fails as its terminal ioctl does on a descriptor that is not a terminal, with the errors `tcgetattr` gives, so `tcsendbreak` never reaches its 0.4 s pause. FreeBSD's `pipe_ioctl` answers `TIOCGPGRP` and `TIOCSPGRP` on a pipe or FIFO with the descriptor's SIGIO owner, which is not modelled, so `tcgetpgrp` and `tcsetpgrp` throw on a host pipe or FIFO above descriptor 2; descriptors 0 to 2 are taken as non-terminals that are not pipes, whatever the host attaches to them, so a pipe the guest creates on a freed descriptor 0 to 2 gets `ENOTTY` there. The PS5 `libkernel` is assumed to use this FreeBSD code, and `tcdrain` is not a cancellation point here

name: libkernel.L131
text: On Linux, [direct memory](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/DirectMemory/DirectMemory.cpp) lives in one sparse memfd at file offset = physical address, so the [GPU imports](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/GuestBufferMemory.cpp) can share one udmabuf buffer object per 64 MiB of it. Released direct memory is not punched out of the file, because a live import of its chunk pins the pages and the GPU would keep reading the old ones: its pages stay committed (the process keeps the high-water mark of the direct memory it used) and are zeroed when the range is allocated again.

text: [The sandbox CA list](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/File/src/SandboxCertificates.cpp) (libkernel), `/<sandbox word>/common/cert/CA_LIST.cer`, is a PEM bundle of the host's trust anchors, written once per process to `cert_cache/CA_LIST.cer` in the run directory with the owner write bit cleared: on Windows the current user's `ROOT` store, filtered through Disallowed and the combined EKU extension/property for TLS server authentication (Windows fetches missing roots on demand, so a root that was never fetched is absent), elsewhere `SSL_CERT_FILE` or the first of `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, `/etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem` and `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` that exists. On macOS, `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` is a static snapshot and does not reflect roots added to or distrusted in the Keychain. Existing guest files, explicit aliases and blocked mounts take precedence over the provider. The PEM snapshot does not carry Windows CTL restrictions beyond EKU, native revocation policy or later trust-store changes. Without any certificate the path does not exist. The console file's format is unverified: only that bundled OpenSSL accepts a PEM bundle there is shown (ProsperoRadio PPSA99001 and SwanStation PPSA98510, #5001). The other entries of the console's `common/cert` directory, the directory itself (it does not exist here) and the error a write open gets (`EACCES` from the host here) are unverified

text: [Host CPU check](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/System/src/HostCpu.cpp) (libkernel) - when libkernel loads on a Linux or Windows x86-64 host, it logs which of the PS5 CPU's user-mode extensions CPUID reports and throws, naming the host CPU, if any extension is missing that LLVM selects from plain C/C++ for the PS5's Zen 2 (`-march=znver2`, [feature list](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-19.1.7/llvm/lib/Target/X86/X86.td#L1459-L1513)): SSE to SSE4.2, SSSE3, POPCNT, LZCNT, BMI1, BMI2, MOVBE, CMPXCHG16B, LAHF/SAHF, AVX, AVX2, FMA, F16C, and the operating system's AVX state in XCR0 (#3719). SSE4A, CLZERO and SHA, which `--to-intel` converts, and AES, PCLMULQDQ, RDRAND, RDSEED, ADX, CLFLUSHOPT, CLWB, RDPID, XSAVEOPT, XSAVEC and PREFETCHW, which compilers emit only for intrinsics or explicit prefetches, are logged but not required: a title that executes one of them on a host without it still stops with an illegal instruction. macOS hosts are not checked: some Rosetta versions execute extensions without reporting them through CPUID, but support differs by host. ANDN and RDRAND fault on an M1 with macOS 15.3.1; see the [Rosetta conversion limits](relinker.md)

name: libkernel.L192
text: [fstat on a guest socket](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) fills the fields FreeBSD 11's soo_stat and pru_sense_null fill and zeroes the rest: S_IFSOCK, the read bits while the receive side is open or data is queued, the write bits while the send side is open, st_size and st_blksize. Only this process's shutdown closes a side here; a peer's shutdown, close or reset does not clear the bits as FreeBSD's socantrcvmore and socantsendmore do. st_size is the host's FIONREAD, which for a Linux datagram socket is the size of the next datagram where FreeBSD counts every queued byte, and st_blksize is the host's SO_SNDBUF, which Linux reports as twice the size that was set. A socketpair end reports st_dev and st_ino 0, where FreeBSD's uipc_sense reports NODEV and a per-socket number

name: libkernel.L194
text: [kevent EV_CLEAR on a socket or a pipe](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Equeue/src/EdgeWatch.cpp) (libkernel) - FreeBSD 11 activates an `EV_CLEAR` knote when `kqueue_register` finds it ready, which every `EV_ADD` or `EV_ENABLE` of an enabled knote does again, and on each `KNOTE` the socket or pipe raises (`sorwakeup`, `sowwakeup`, `pipeselwakeup`); [`kqueue_scan`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/release/11.4.0/sys/kern/kern_event.c) checks the filter again before reporting, drops a knote that is no longer ready and deactivates a reported one until the next activation. On Linux each such knote registers the host socket or pipe with its own epoll instance in edge-triggered mode (`EPOLLIN | EPOLLRDHUP` for `EVFILT_READ`, `EPOLLOUT` for `EVFILT_WRITE`), and a wakeup of the host descriptor with that mask stands for a `KNOTE`: the knote is then checked with the same readiness test as a level-triggered one, `NOTE_LOWAT` mark included, and a wait blocks on the epoll descriptor instead of the socket, so a socket that stays readable does not wake it. The host's wakeups are not FreeBSD's: FreeBSD raises `sowwakeup` whenever send buffer space is freed, while Linux TCP wakes `EPOLLOUT` waiters only once the socket is writable again after a write found it full (`SOCK_NOSPACE`, [`tcp_check_space`](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v6.8/net/ipv4/tcp_input.c#L5639)), so a TCP writer that never fills its buffer sees fewer `EVFILT_WRITE` events than on FreeBSD; a host stack may also coalesce data wakeups, so the number of times a busy socket fires can differ. Windows and macOS throw, as the host there has no edge-triggered wait over these descriptors that is wired up; `EV_CLEAR` on the timer, user and vnode filters does not use this and works everywhere.

name: libkernel.L198
text: [connect to AF_UNSPEC](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Socket/src/Udp.cpp) (libkernel) dissolves a datagram association as FreeBSD 11.4's `udp_disconnect()` does, which resets the local address to the wildcard address and keeps the port. On Linux a socket bound to an explicit port keeps its local address as well (`127.0.0.1:<port>` stays `127.0.0.1:<port>`), because a bound socket cannot be bound again; one bound to port 0 is bound again to the wildcard address with the port it had

AnyPS5 represents the 32-bit type word as low 16-bit type and high 16-bit recording flags. Command encoding is AnyPS5 internal: opcode 29 and three 32-bit words encode the high offset byte, length minus one and low offset word. The 12-byte size reduces HFW's 1 MiB buffer pressure; it is not a claim about console opcode encoding. name: libkernel.L34
text: [AMPR counter access](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Apr/src/Apr.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - signatures and checks of `WaitOnCounter_04_00`, `WriteCounter_04_00`, `ConstructNop` and `ConstructMarker` taken from the [ampr_emu](https://github.com/drakmor/ampr_emu) reimplementation, which hands counter commands to the console and does not show their effect. The counters are taken as 32 bits each: the 8-byte access of counter n spans n (low) and n + 1 (high), the 2- and 1-byte accesses select a half or a byte of the counter by its offset, waits compare at the access width (signed and wrapped compares included), the AND mask applies to both sides and the atomic writes wrap within the access. The `ConstructNop` type is not recorded

name: libkernel.L37
text: [AMM remap, multimap and protection changes](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Apr/src/Apr.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - signatures and the protection and mask checks taken from ampr_emu; the effects are inferred from the names, not confirmed on a title. A remap moves every page of a fully mapped range to the new address with the given protection and leaves the old range reserved; a multimap maps the same pages at a second address, anywhere in the AMM ranges, and a pool page goes back to the pool once its last mapping is unmapped; a multimap onto its own source range throws. A protection change sets the masked bits on every page of a fully mapped range; the memory type is recorded and ignored. A command on a range that is not fully mapped throws

name: libkernel.L38
text: [AMM PRT ranges](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Apr/src/Apr.cpp) (libSceAmpr) - signatures, checks and their order taken from ampr_emu, where `MapAsPrt` is a map with the PRT flag and protection 0 and `AllocatePaForPrt` a memory type and protection change with mask 1019, both checking the buffer memory after its size; the effects are inferred from the names, not confirmed on a title. Unbacked PRT pages are zero-filled pages with GPU read access, so CPU reads see zeros instead of faulting and GPU writes fault instead of being dropped. `AllocatePaForPrt` backs each unbacked page with a pool page and sets the type and protection of backed ones; `RemapIntoPrt` moves a fully mapped range into a PRT range, its opcode argument (1011 when 0, as in ampr_emu) is recorded and ignored; `UnmapToPrt` returns the pages to the pool and zero-fills them again. A plain map, unmap or remap over a PRT range ends it; `AllocatePaForPrt`, `RemapIntoPrt` or `UnmapToPrt` outside a PRT range throws

text: [scePthreadCondWait / scePthreadCondTimedwait](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel/Pthread/src/Cond.cpp) (libkernel) - before waiting, FreeBSD libthr's [`cond_wait_common`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/main/lib/libthr/thread/thr_cond.c#L1992-L2029) checks ownership through [`_mutex_owned`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/main/lib/libthr/thread/thr_mutex.c#L1166-L1178): an unowned mutex returns `EPERM`, while its destroyed marker returns `EINVAL`. An untouched adaptive static initializer (slot value 1) therefore returns `EPERM`; the test covers this, an uninitialized slot, a mutex owned by another thread, and the destroyed marker for both timed and untimed sce and POSIX waits. A recursive mutex locked several times is released completely for the wait and relocked to the same depth afterwards, as FreeBSD libthr does (`_mutex_cv_unlock`, `_mutex_cv_lock`). These FreeBSD-derived behaviors remain unverified on console hardware. Cancellation follows the [POSIX condition wait contract](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/pthread_cond_clockwait.html): the original mutex and recursive depth are restored before cleanup, and a canceled waiter forwards a wake to the remaining waiters. The host condition state is retained across mutex reacquisition so the guest can destroy and free its condition after notification; cancellation ordering and signal replacement are not measured on a console

name: libkernel_sys.L17
text: [renameat](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) (libkernel_sys) passes `AT_FDCWD` (-100) and absolute paths to `rename`. Any other relative path is joined to its descriptor's host directory, found the same way as for `fchdir`, so guest path aliases and case-insensitive name matching do not apply to relative descriptors, and a `..` component is not kept inside the guest root. It returns `EBADF` for a descriptor that is not open and `ENOTDIR` for one that is not a directory. Console behaviour is unverified

name: libkernel_sys.L10
text: [fchmodat](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) (libkernel_sys) passes `AT_FDCWD` (-100) and absolute paths to `chmod`; any other relative path is joined to the descriptor's host directory the same way as for `openat`, so guest path aliases and case-insensitive name matching do not apply to it and a `..` component is not kept inside the guest root. A flag other than `0` or `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW` (0x200) returns `EINVAL`; the mode is masked to `07777`. With `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW` a symbolic link returns success silently on Windows and Linux, since the host cannot change a link's own mode, while a regular file is changed either way. The mode maps to the host file mode, which on Windows is only the CRT's read-only bit. PPSA99621 calls it through `std::filesystem::permissions`. Console behaviour is unverified

name: libkernel_sys.L20
text: [fchown](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) (libkernel_sys) - ownership is not modelled: the guest's own owner and group (0) and the unchanged value (-1) are accepted, a descriptor that is not open fails with `EBADF`, and any other owner or group throws, naming it. The check reads the descriptor with `fstat`, ignoring the CRT's invalid-parameter handler on Windows as `DescriptorControl` does. The console's ownership rules are unverified. Morrowind (`mshivam019/morrowind-ps5`) imports it

name: libkernel_sys.L18
text: [fork](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) (libkernel_sys) throws: creating a child process is not supported. PPSA19111 imports it and fails to load without it. Its engine calls `fork` in `Posix_Daemonize`, only with `-daemonize`, and in `Platform_ShellExecute` before `execvp("xdg-open")`, which the main menu's Previews button reaches, so pressing Previews ends in this throw. [setsid](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) fails with `EPERM`, as FreeBSD's does for a process group leader, since the guest is taken to lead its own process group (see `kill`). text: [chroot](../../../core/libs/prx/libkernel_sys/Export.cpp) (libkernel_sys) follows FreeBSD 11.4's [`sys_chroot`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/vfs_syscalls.c#L776-L807) and [`pwd_chroot`](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/blob/8c639945a44588f6cfdddfb057bb5aad88735da0/sys/kern/kern_descrip.c#L3059-L3085) for a root caller: `EFAULT` for a null path, `ENOENT` for an empty or missing one, `ENAMETOOLONG` for a path of 1024 bytes or more or a component over 255, and `ENOTDIR` for a path that is not a directory or passes through a file. A directory that is the guest root (`/`, `/..`, or `.` after `fchdir` to a descriptor of `/`) succeeds and changes nothing, as the root stays the same directory; the guest is taken never to have changed its root, so open directory descriptors do not make it fail with `EPERM` (`kern.chroot_allow_open_directories` 1). Any other directory throws, naming the path: the guest path resolver has a fixed root and mount aliases (`/app0`, `/savedata0`) that do not move with it. On the console a title starts in a sandbox root, where `pwd_chroot` refuses with `EPERM` while a directory is open; whether that holds for titles, and whether a title holds `PRIV_VFS_CHROOT`, are unverified. Porpoise (PPSA99764) weak-imports it and calls it only as `fchdir` to its saved descriptor of `/` then `chroot(".")`, to put its sandbox root back after a jailbreak daemon replaced it ([`put_root_back`](https://github.com/elripalda/Porpoise-Dolphin-Emulator-for-PS5/blob/2ed1ab5a06995aa198f7bccd4da0f90c3fc29d39/src/porpoise_jailbreak.cpp#L303-L331))

name: relinker.L20

name: relinker.L22
text: In the same executables and modules, the bytes between unwind functions are 16-byte slots of function tails and padding, and a tail can begin inside an instruction. The [instruction scanner](../../../core/relinker/codegen/src/InstructionScanner.cpp) of the syscall and call-site scans therefore resumes at the next byte when bytes outside every unwind function do not decode, and ends a decoding outside them at the start of the next unwind function. Code without an unwind entry that does not decode from its first byte is skipped by these scans instead of failing the relink; inside an unwind function a decode failure still fails it.

name: relinker.L23
text: Read-only data can also sit between the unwind functions of such images. There, a `syscall`, `sysenter` or `int 0x80` pattern fails the [syscall scan](../../../core/relinker/relinker/src/analysis/SyscallScanner.cpp) only when a constant syscall number is set before it; the others, and every `sysret`, are skipped and counted in one message. The number is looked for in the decoded instructions and, whatever alignment the decoding took, in the bytes before the pattern: a `mov eax, imm32`, `mov rax, imm32`, `mov rax, imm64` or `xor eax, eax`, optionally followed by `mov al, imm8` or `mov ax, imm16`, then by any number of register moves or zeroings that leave `rax` alone. A real syscall without an unwind entry whose number is set otherwise is not refused and runs on the host: from memory or another register (`mov eax, ecx`), by `push`/`pop` or arithmetic (`or eax, imm32`), or with any other instruction between the load and the pattern.

name: relinker.L24
text: In the [code analysis](../../../core/relinker/relinker/src/analysis/CodeInstructionCollector.cpp) of the Windows and macOS outputs for such images, a relocation or `lea` target outside every unwind function is followed as code only when its linear decoding, up to the first jump, return or trap, the next unwind function or 256 instructions, holds an `fs:[disp32]` access, or when it is 16-byte aligned, starts less than 256 bytes after an unwind function and ends in a jump, return or trap. Every other such target is taken as data and counted in one message, and the Windows TLS rewrite fails instead of overwriting one. A TLS access of another form, such as `mov rax, fs:[rax]`, or a `gs` instruction in code reached only through such a target is therefore not rewritten or trapped. Other fs and gs instructions do not tell code from data there: string bytes decode as these prefixes, and in two measured titles about 2,500 of about 5,500 such targets decode to one before their first jump.

name: relinker.L25

name: relinker.L29
text: `--to-rosetta` lowers what Rosetta lacks on top of `--to-intel` ([matcher](../../../core/relinker/codegen/src/x86/Amd64OnlyInstructionMatcher.cpp)). AVX2, FMA, BMI1/2, F16C and MOVBE were observed to execute on an M5 Max without being reported through CPUID; this is not a guarantee for other Rosetta hosts. ANDN and RDRAND fault on an M1 running macOS 15.3.1 and execute on an M1 running macOS 26.6.2, so on the M1 the difference follows the macOS version; on that host BEXTR, BLSI, BLSMSK, BLSR, TZCNT, LZCNT, POPCNT, BZHI, MULX, PDEP, PEXT, RORX, SARX, SHLX, SHRX, MOVBE, FMA, AVX2 and F16C execute as well, its CPUID leaf 1 reports none of MOVBE, FMA, AVX or F16C, and RDSEED, RDPID, CLWB, ADCX and ADOX raise SIGILL. They also execute on an M5 running macOS 26.4, where the rest of BMI1 and BMI2, LZCNT, PREFETCHW, CLFLUSHOPT, AVX, AVX2, FMA, F16C and MOVBE execute as well although CPUID leaf 7 reads zero and leaves 1 and 0x80000001 report none of them, and where RDSEED, CLWB, RDPID, ADCX and ADOX raise an illegal instruction. ANDN is lowered, but RDRAND and other BMI instructions still depend on the host. RDSEED becomes RDRAND and CLWB a NOP. RDPID returns processor 0, and RDTSCP runs unchanged with ECX set to 0 after it, because Rosetta's TSC_AUX is the constant 0xAAAAAAAB (also measured on an M5, macOS 27.0.1). An RDPID or RDTSCP site with no movable instruction after it for the jump is kept; a kept RDTSCP reports 0xAAAAAAAB. ADCX/ADOX fault under Rosetta and are not converted: compilers do not emit them, and code that checks CPUID sees no ADX. The conversions are covered by the converter tests. ANDN lowering is also executed by an x86-64 test build under Rosetta on the M1; the other conversions were originally checked on an M5 Max, outside this repository's CI.

name: relinker.L30
text: `--to-intel` replaces the approximate legacy SSE and VEX.128 register forms of RSQRTPS/RCPPS and VRSQRTPS/VRCPPS with [correctly rounded](../../../core/relinker/codegen/src/x86/ReciprocalLowering.cpp) 1/sqrt(x) and 1/x, not with the AMD approximation: its tables are not public. Intel's approximation of 1/sqrt(1.0) is 0x3F7FF000, and two Newton-Raphson steps on it settle on 0.99999994 instead of 1.0; a renormalised identity quaternion then turns into a NaN axis in PPSA21564, which the console does not show. Refined results now reach the exact value; unrefined ones can still differ from the console in the low bits. Each site costs an out-of-line stub (two jumps, a spill below the red zone, SQRTPS/DIVPS). Legacy SSE forms preserve the destination's upper YMM bits; VEX forms clear them. The 256-bit, scalar and memory forms keep the native instruction, as does a site shorter than 5 bytes with no movable instruction after it for the jump (5 sites in PPSA21564, counted before a following RIP-relative instruction could move into the stub; not recounted).

name: relinker.L33
text: [ANDN lowering](../../../core/relinker/codegen/src/x86/AndnLowering.cpp) uses scalar NOT and AND for 32- and 64-bit register and memory operands under `--to-rosetta`, following the ANDN entry in [Intel SDM volume 2A](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/812383/253666-sdm-vol-2a.pdf). SF and ZF follow the result, CF and OF clear, and AF and PF are undefined. The scratch register is saved below the 128-byte red zone. A 64-bit stack-relative displacement that exceeds signed disp32 after reserving the spill frame throws; other BMI instructions are not lowered. The M1 test covers register overlap, RSP operands, memory addressing, RIP relocation, flags and red-zone preservation; precise fault delivery inside a spill sequence has not been verified.

name: relinker.L5
text: [Executable guest imports](../../../core/relinker/relinker/src/guest/GuestModuleBuilder.cpp) - on Linux and macOS, a relocated executable import resolved to one guest provider requires that module and its dependencies at startup, even when it was discovered through `--module-dir` without a DT_NEEDED entry. Unreferenced symbols and no-op relocations do not require an otherwise deferred module. Console module-start ordering is unmeasured.

name: relinker.L7
text: Windows [file identity checks](../../../core/relinker/io/src/FileIdentity.cpp) (input and output collisions, the input skipped during guest module discovery, executables converted twice) compare the volume serial number and the 64-bit file index from `GetFileInformationByHandle`. ReFS file IDs are 128-bit, so two distinct files on ReFS can in principle compare equal: a collision or a repeated executable is reported, or a module is skipped; `FILE_ID_INFO` is not used.

name: relinker.L8
text: [Runtime-loaded modules](../../../core/relinker/relinker/src/guest/GuestModuleBuilder.cpp) (`--module-dir`) that another module needs are initialized at startup with no start arguments, before the module that needs them is loaded; the console is assumed to start them when that module is loaded.

name: relinker.L9
text: The executable file that [relinker](../../../core/relinker/elfpatcher/src/windows/WindowsPeWriter.cpp) generates opens a console when launched, unless it is relinked with `--windows-gui`, which selects the GUI subsystem. A GUI build started from Explorer has no standard output or error handle; the [entry stub](../../../core/relinker/elfpatcher/src/windows/WindowsEntryStubBuilder.cpp) gives each missing one `anyps5.log` beside the executable, replacing the previous run's file (#3282). Errors about the executable path or about waiting for the previous LoadExec process are written before the log is opened and are lost when the standard error handle is missing. If the log cannot be created, output to the missing handles is lost.

name: shader.L66
text: [Image atomics](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) on 32_SINT and 32_FLOAT surfaces act on the raw dword through an R32_UINT storage view. On gfx1100 (RDNA3, [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md), wave32 and wave64), all 13 integer image atomics, `swap` to `dec`, return the old dword and store the raw-dword result identically on 32_UINT, 32_SINT and 32_FLOAT T#s, over 121 old/data pairs per op, among them 0x80000000, 0xffffffff, 1.0, -1.0 and NaN: `add` adds the bits and `umin` is unsigned on every format. A 16_UINT control differs, so the format is read. gfx1031 (RDNA2) gives the same rows, and its `fmin`, `fmax` and `fcmpswap`, which gfx1100 lacks, also match on the three formats ([measured by thuanquang](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/pull/7939#issuecomment-6275099482)). The console's gfx1013 is unmeasured. Other formats throw.

name: shader.L110
text: [f16 unary, frexp and conversion denormals](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/FloatInstructions.cpp) follow the `FLOAT_MODE` f16 denormal field: `v_ceil_f16`, `v_floor_f16`, `v_fract_f16`, `v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16`, `v_sqrt_f16`, `v_log_f16`, `v_exp_f16`, `v_sin_f16`, `v_frexp_mant_f16`, `v_frexp_exp_i16_f16`, `v_cvt_norm_i16_f16`, `v_cvt_norm_u16_f16` and `v_cvt_f32_f16` flush a denormal half input to its signed zero when bit 0 is clear (0 and 2), and the f16-result ones flush a denormal half result to its signed zero when bit 1 is clear (0 and 1), after the host rounds it to half. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with denorm16 0..3 over every non-NaN f16 input (63,490 rows per mode and instruction): the only mismatches are the 1-ULP driver differences of `v_exp_f16` (2 inputs) and `v_sin_f16` (14), which are the same with denormals kept. NaN inputs are not compared. `v_ldexp_f16` shares the input rule. `v_cvt_pknorm_i16_f16` and `v_cvt_pknorm_u16_f16` flush both half inputs by the same bit, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1030) over every f16 input (each half also negated in the other source) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with denorm16 0..3 and at f16 rounding 1..3: every row matches. Shaders without a known float mode keep the previous lowering.

name: shader.L11
text: [VCC-backed MIMG samplers](../../../core/shader/recompiler/RdnaDecoder/src/RdnaImageOpDecoder.cpp): the s104/s105/vcc_lo/vcc_hi tuple follows LLVM's [SGPR register classes](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/d8219b47422f7322db252ad29ca8ea87993fb433/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SIRegisterInfo.td#L452) and [gfx10 sampler operand](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/d8219b47422f7322db252ad29ca8ea87993fb433/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/MIMGInstructions.td#L1379), using the existing VCC word reads. Recompiled wave32/wave64 reads are checked by [bilinear and white-border cases](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/ImageSampleVccSampler.cpp); raw RDNA execution of this tuple on gfx1013 or gfx1036 is unmeasured.

name: shader.L113
text: [f32 denormals](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/OperandAccess.cpp) follow the shader's `FLOAT_MODE` f32 denormal field (bits 5:4) when it flushes them (0, and shaders without a known float mode, as in the 0xc0 most titles use), measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) over 1444 rows per instruction at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1. `v_add/sub/subrev/mul/mul_legacy/mullit/fma/fmac/fmamk/fmaak/min/max/min3/max3/med3/fract/floor/ceil/frexp_mant/sin/cos_f32` flush their f32 inputs and their result to a zero of the same sign (`v_mullit_f32` measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 6907 rows per mode at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, so a positive denormal src2 counts as zero); the f32 compares, `v_cvt_i32/u32/rpi_i32/flr_i32_f32`, `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32`, `v_cvt_f64_f32`, `v_cvt_f16_f32`, `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32`, `v_cvt_pknorm_i16/u16_f32` and `v_cvt_pk_u8_f32` flush their f32 inputs. `v_div_scale_f32` flushes all three inputs to signed zeros, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 2744 operand triples per mode at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f32 denormals flushed and kept; its scale-down behaviour and host denormal preservation remain incomplete. `v_div_fixup_f32` flushes its src1 and src2 and keeps a denormal src0 and result, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 6859 rows per mode at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1. Tininess is detected after rounding, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) for `v_mul_f32` and `v_mullit_f32` at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1: a product is flushed when its value rounded to 24 bits with an unbounded exponent is below 2^-126, so `0x3f7ffffe * 0x00800001` (2^-126 * (1 - 2^-46)) gives `0x00800000` and `0x3f7fffff * 0x00800000` (2^-126 * (1 - 2^-24)) gives zero. The check rounds in the f32 round mode of `FLOAT_MODE` (bits 1:0), measured in all four modes, while the products themselves are still rounded to nearest even. This applies to `v_mul_f32`, `v_mul_legacy_f32`, `v_mullit_f32`, and to `v_fma_f32`, `v_fmac_f32`, `v_fmamk_f32`, `v_fmaak_f32` and `v_fma_mix_f32` when the addend is zero; with a nonzero addend the fused result is kept, so an exact result just below 2^-126 that rounds to it is not flushed. In the three directed modes the check is computed exactly from the significands. To nearest even (0, the mode of shaders without a known float mode) one factor is multiplied by 2^64, which is exact below 2^64, and the product with the other factor is compared with 2^-62. That multiply is a plain `OpFMul` like the product, and no f32 rounding mode is requested in the SPIR-V, so the check relies on the driver rounding f32 to nearest even by default, as the products do, and a product that rounds up to 2^-126 is the emitted product. `v_fma_mix_f32` follows this rule with mixed f16/f32 sources too, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) with f16 in either multiplicand slot, low and high half selection, and an f32 or f16 zero addend: f32 `0x00801002` times f16 `0x3bff` gives `0x00800000` to nearest at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, while the neighbours `0x00801001` and `0x00801003` give zero and `0x00800001`. The tiny-product boundary was also measured for both signs in all four f32 round modes at IEEE=0; Its f16 sources are flushed to a zero of their sign when bit 0 of the f16/f64 denormal field is clear (0 and 2), whatever the f32 field, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1031, Radeon RX 6700 XT, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002 through HIP) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f32 denormal modes 0 and 3 and f16 denormal modes 0 to 3, over 2744 triples of 14 halves with all three sources f16 and 1960 rows with an f32 multiplicand. `v_fma_mixlo_f16` and `v_fma_mixhi_f16` flush their f32 sources too and keep a product below 2^-126, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036). `v_mad_legacy_f32` and `v_mac_legacy_f32` flush their inputs, their product and their result in every mode, see its entry; their product is still checked for tininess on its exact value, so one below 2^-126 gives zero even when it rounds to 2^-126, as the console's separately rounded encoding is not measured at this boundary. Denormal modes 1 and 2 throw for the other instructions. Not covered, and not measurable on RDNA2 (no such opcodes) or not measured: `v_mac_f32`, `v_mad_f32`, `v_madak_f32` and `v_madmk_f32` (rounded separately), `v_dot2_f32_f16` and `v_div_fmas_f32` (on hardware `v_div_fmas_f32` flushes only its result), f32 interpolation and `ds_add_f32` keep the previous lowering; `ds_min/max/cmpst_f32` flush both operands by the field, see the LDS float atomics entry. With f32 denormals kept (3) the results depend on the driver's default denormal behaviour, as no `DenormPreserve` execution mode is requested; `v_ldexp_f32` and the f32 compares are the exceptions. `v_cmp_X_f32` and `v_cmpx_X_f32` compare the operands as sign-magnitude integers with the NaN cases handled apart, so a denormal is not read as zero, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 256 operand pairs per opcode at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f32 denormals kept and flushed. `v_ldexp_f32` preserves subnormal inputs and rounds a subnormal result in the f32 round mode of `FLOAT_MODE`, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 2163 rows in each of the four round modes at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1. An overflow rounds like any other result (infinity, or the largest finite value when the mode rounds that sign toward zero). With f32 denormals flushed it flushes a subnormal input and result, measured over the same rows in each round mode at IEEE=0 only. A device whose driver splits `Fma` into a multiply and an add flushes a product below 2^-126 before adding a non-zero addend in `v_fma_f32` and `v_fmac_f32`: `0x1fffffff * 0x1fffffff + 0x00800000` gives `0x00800000` instead of the fused `0x00ffffff` on RADV RENOIR (Mesa 26.2.4), whose compiled shader has `v_mad_f32` and no `v_fma_f32`. [F32DenormalFlush](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/F32DenormalFlush.cpp) accepts that sum on such a device.

name: shader.L147
text: [Unaligned 32-bit buffer atomics](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvRuntimeBuffer.cpp) (shader recompiler) act on the dword that holds their address, as section 8.1.7 of the [RDNA2 ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) describes for alignment mode DWORD ("the two LSBs of the byte-address are ignored, thus forcing Dword alignment"). The mode comes from `SH_MEM_CONFIG.alignment_mode`, and the console's mode is unknown. MXGP 26 (PPSA30839) sets bits with `buffer_atomic_or` at odd byte offsets, so the console is not in a strict mode, where section 3.11 reports a memory violation for a misaligned atomic. In mode UNALIGNED, which Linux KFD sets, a misaligned atomic stops the dispatch (measured on gfx1031 and gfx1036), so the console is not in that mode either. A 64-bit buffer atomic off an 8-byte boundary still records an unaligned BDA fault: mode DWORD would align it only to 4 bytes, which a host 64-bit atomic cannot address. When the V# base itself is off a DWORD boundary and the containing dword lies before the first aligned dword the buffer view binds to, that atomic is out of bounds and returns 0 without writing. Covered by [BufferAtomicUnaligned.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/BufferAtomicUnaligned.cpp).

name: shader.L15
text: [Packed pixel ancillary word](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ConstantFolder.cpp) (shader recompiler) - the sample index at bits 8-11 and the render target index at bits 16-28 follow #295. The sample index is the SampleId builtin in a pixel shader the guest iterates per sample (`PS_ITER_SAMPLE` on a multisampled draw), an equality inferred, not measured. In any other pixel shader it is 0, the iterated sample number of a pixel the hardware does not iterate (also inferred), so reading it does not make the host shade per sample. The render target index is the Layer builtin when the draw exports it (a layered draw, `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` bit 18; the pipeline specialization constant `LayerExported`) and 0 otherwise, the first layer Vulkan renders when no pre-rasterization stage writes Layer. Reading the unwritten Layer builtin instead makes AMD's Windows driver drop the fragment's writes (#4800); with the constant at 0 the load is folded away. Mesa reads both fields from those bits, with the layer 14 bits wide only from GFX12 on ([ac_nir_lower_intrinsics_to_args.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/bffd91947efc1932da99aca69fc540d6d4201b0c/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_intrinsics_to_args.c#L342-L368)). A value passed through a select, move or phi whose every read is an extract inside one of those fields is rebuilt from the two fields alone. Any other read the masked-select pass cannot drop gets the whole word: the primitive class at bits 0-1 (0 point, 1 line, 2 triangle, 3 rectangle), which the draw sets as a pipeline specialization constant ([RasterPrimitiveOf](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Graphics/src/State.cpp)) in the shaders that read it, plus the sample field, with every other bit zero. That layout comes from the RDNA 3 and 3.5 ISA guides (prim type 1:0, VRS rates 3:2 and 5:4, eye id 7, sample 11:8, render target index 28:16). The GCN register guides give the same prim type and sample fields and put the render target index at 26:16, so the two sources agree for layers below 2048. AMD's LLPC reads the primitive class from bits 1:0 with the same encoding ([LowerGlCompatibility.cpp](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/llpc/blob/40cb8d95ad8d6f7f1652e3fd47d39667594cce08/llpc/lowering/LowerGlCompatibility.cpp#L830-L836)) and without a GFX-level check ([getPrimType](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/llpc/blob/40cb8d95ad8d6f7f1652e3fd47d39667594cce08/lgc/lowering/LowerInOut.cpp#L5307-L5315)). Nobody has checked it on gfx1013. In the whole word only bits 0-1 and 8-11 have a source. Bits 2-7, 12-15 and 29-31 are assumed zero, not measured: the VRS rates (2-5) and the eye id (7) because the driver supports neither variable-rate shading nor multiview, so a title that enables either would read other bits on the console, and bits 6, 12-15 and 29-31 because no source gives them a meaning. The sample field reads SampleId only in iterated shaders. The whole word has the same 0 at bits 16-28. A change that makes draws export a layer must restore the Layer read in both places

name: shader.L153
text: [`ds_ordered_count`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/MemoryInstructions/SharedMemoryInstructions.cpp) (GDS only) reads its operand fields as LLVM encodes them for `llvm.amdgcn.ds.ordered.add` ([SIISelLowering.cpp](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-19.1.0/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SIISelLowering.cpp#L8844-L8894)): `offset0` is the counter's byte offset (index times 4) and the whole GDS address, `offset1` bit 0 wave release, bit 1 wave done, bits 2-3 the shader type, bit 4 swap instead of add and bits 6-7 the dword count less one. `M0` holds the ordered wave ID, not a GDS address as for `ds_append` (radeonsi passes `TG_SIZE` bits 6-17 as the intrinsic's pointer in [si_compute_prim_discard.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-20.3.0/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_compute_prim_discard.c) and `gs_tg_info` bits 0-11 in [gfx10_shader_ngg.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-21.3.0/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/gfx10_shader_ngg.c), with "The GDS address is always 0 with ordered append"); it only orders the waves, which is not modeled, so it is ignored. Each wave adds the value of its first active lane to the counter with one device-scope atomic and every active lane gets the counter's previous value (the `ORDERED_APPEND_ENBL` dispatch modifier is accepted for it). The hardware also serializes the waves of a dispatch in launch order, which is not modeled: the waves add in any order, so counters a title reads back as ordered offsets give the same totals but may hand out ranges in another order. Which lane's value is added is not documented; the first active lane is assumed and not measured on hardware. A swap (`offset1` bit 4) stores the first active lane's value in place of the counter with one device-scope atomic exchange and returns the counter's previous value to every active lane; with the waves unordered, which wave's value the counter keeps and which previous value each wave gets need not follow the launch order the hardware gives. Counts of more than one dword and LDS forms throw. Covered by [GdsAppendConsume.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/GdsAppendConsume.cpp).

name: shader.L172
text: [Spanned wave64 compute](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvSubgroup.cpp) (shader recompiler) - `APS5_SPANNED_WAVE=1`, off by default, runs a single-wave wave64 compute program at one lane per invocation on a 32-lane host subgroup and exchanges ballots, shuffles and reductions between the two host subgroups through workgroup memory and barriers. The driver turns it on only where compute subgroups can be pinned at 32 full lanes (`subgroupSizeControl` and `computeFullSubgroups`), passes it as `SpirvTarget::spannedWaves` (part of the cache key and the serialized request), and creates the pipelines of spanned programs with `REQUIRE_FULL_SUBGROUPS`, since the lane number `SubgroupId * 32 + SubgroupLocalInvocationId` needs two full subgroups. Those barriers are correct only where every invocation of the workgroup reaches them, which holds for the guest's wave-uniform control flow. The emulated 64-bit LDS atomics ([LockedLdsUpdate](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp)) run only on the lanes the exec mask keeps, so their lock loop ballots within its own host subgroup, as its elect already does. Any other cross-lane exchange emitted inside per-lane control flow would hang a spanned wave in the same way, and the emitter does not reject one: there is no uniformity check. The only check so far is manual: disassemble the module (`spirv-dis`), list the selection and loop constructs that enclose each `OpControlBarrier`, and read the condition of each enclosing selection. In Ghost of Yōtei's program 0x80003af600 (PPSA26344), 108 of 111 barriers sat only in loops on wave-uniform conditions and 3 inside per-invocation conditionals, all in the lock loop. Other programs and titles have not been scanned. An earlier, cheaper ballot (one barrier instead of three) also lost the device for a reason that is not understood, which may be another barrier placement problem. Measured on an RTX 4090 (Windows): an offline replay of that program and two Yōtei runs that previously lost the device (NVIDIA TDR) now run past it, and [LdsMaskWaterfall.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/LdsMaskWaterfall.cpp) runs both modes and covers a half-inactive wave. Stray (PPSA02101) on Intel ANV and a Demon's Souls (PPSA01342) request replay showed no fault, before this fix

name: shader.L173
text: [Guest memory load guards](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (shader recompiler) - a guest load whose lane is inactive or whose address is out of bounds is still performed and its result replaced by 0 with `OpSelect`, instead of a selection per guard, when the load can be pointed at a location nothing writes: scratch reads its own element 0; storage buffers (direct buffers, GDS) read element 0xfffffffe, which `robustBufferAccess2` turns into a zero load with no memory access, so the extra read cannot race with a write the guarded program would not have raced with ([Vulkan memory model](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/appendices/memorymodel.html#data-race)). Without `robustBufferAccess2` ([VulkanDevice.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/VulkanDevice.cpp) enables it when the device has it) those loads keep their selections; LDS loads, stores, atomics, formatted and physical-address (BDA) accesses always do. LDS keeps the branch because NVIDIA's compiler predicates a branched LDS load at no cost, while the select form costs about 2.5 instructions per dword and splits a `ds_read_b128` into four loads (RTX 4060 measurements by @karanvora2599 in #4048); Intel's static counts favour the select only for wide reads, and run time was not measured on either. The aligned high word of a misaligned-capable buffer read re-reads the low word's own element. A selection guard costs four blocks per lane half and the host compiler's time grows with the block count: PPSA11142's merged PSP vertex program (3176 ISA words, wave64) emitted 16,983 blocks and 1,710 conditional branches, 5,907 and 868 with the selects. `agc_guarded_memory_loads` traces the emitted loads in both device modes. AMD's proprietary driver does not get `robustBufferAccess2` ([RobustBufferAccess.hpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/include/RobustBufferAccess.hpp)), so its loads keep their selections. On an RX 6700 XT with driver 32.0.21045.5002, enabling the feature broke `agc_driver_layered_volume_draw` and `agc_driver_layered_volume_vertex`: the vertex draw left the volume untouched even with the selections kept. `agc_driver_subvector_loop` failed too, with the selected loads: the driver compiled the begin instruction's `exec_lo == 0` as a test of the whole 64-bit mask, so the high half of a wave64 skipped its loop. The begin instruction now tests for an empty mask as `(exec_lo | exec_hi) == 0` rather than `exec_lo == 0 && exec_hi == 0`, and that driver compiles it correctly. The cause of the layered-volume failures was not found.

name: shader.L20
text: [s_subvector_loop_begin and s_subvector_loop_end](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/ControlFlowInstructions.cpp) (core/shader/recompiler) - follow AMD's RDNA 2 instruction set reference and a gfx1036 (wave64) measurement, pinned in [SubvectorLoop.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/SubvectorLoop.cpp); `S0` in the end instruction's `elif(S0 == 0)` is read as its SGPR operand. A wave32 shader and a destination other than an SGPR throw because neither is measured. Measured on PC RDNA2 (Radeon 610M), not on a PS5. The [specialization pass](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvSpecialization.cpp) keeps a constant-condition branch whose untaken target is a loop header, since folding it removes the loop's back edge, which SPIR-V requires exactly once per loop header (SPIRV-Tools rejects the module and the NVIDIA driver 615.78.08 crashes compiling it); a loop whose back-edge block becomes unreachable in another way is not handled

name: shader.L24
text: [32_AR color exports](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (shader recompiler) - with `SPI_SHADER_COL_FORMAT` 3 the red value is export channel 0 and the alpha is export channel 1, the GFX10 layout of Mesa's [`emit_ps_color_export`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/3e32b0e1f132231b7a972c1b0b5b06c7e16cf8b9/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_ps_late.c#L400-L411), ACO and radeonsi in Mesa 22.0 ([aco_instruction_selection.cpp](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/a82920af6efa4a7a66919885c6477fbd8fdc7b9d/src/amd/compiler/aco_instruction_selection.cpp#L11087-L11096), [si_shader_llvm_ps.c](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/a82920af6efa4a7a66919885c6477fbd8fdc7b9d/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_shader_llvm_ps.c#L323-L333)) and AMD's [LLPC](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/llpc/blob/40cb8d95ad8d6f7f1652e3fd47d39667594cce08/lgc/lowering/FragmentColorExport.cpp#L157-L168); before GFX10 the alpha was channel 3. Channels 2 and 3, which none of these compilers enables, are ignored; green and blue are 0 and the alpha of an export without channel 1 is 1.0, the defaults of the other formats, which no source gives. Not measured on hardware, neither on gfx1013 nor on a PC RDNA 2 GPU; pinned in [Pixel32ArExport.cpp](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/tests/execution/Pixel32ArExport.cpp)

name: shader.L67
text: [`s_memtime`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) on RADV with a GFX10.3 to GFX11.7 GPU (RDNA 2, RDNA 3, RDNA 3.5) reads the Vulkan device clock instead of the subgroup clock, which [ACO](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/amd/compiler/instruction_selection/aco_select_nir_intrinsics.cpp) reads from the 20-bit `SHADER_CYCLES` register there and which wraps every 2^20 cycles. The device clock is a monotonic 64-bit counter, but it counts the 100 MHz reference clock (the same one as `s_memrealtime`), not shader cycles, so `s_memtime` deltas are about 20 times smaller than on hardware. The families are matched by the name RADV reports ([`NarrowSubgroupClock`](../../../core/libs/prx/libSceAgcDriver/Execution/src/SubgroupClock.cpp)); a family added to Mesa later reads the subgroup clock until it is listed.
