name: shader.L123
text: [Image loads](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceTracker.cpp) (shader recompiler) - an image_load reads a sampled binding, also of an image the shader stores to, so in a primitive-ordered pixel shader it misses an earlier overlapping primitive's image_store in the same draw.

name: shader.L124
text: [Tessellation rings](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/TessellationLowering.cpp) of local, hull and domain programs become Vulkan tessellation interfaces and are never written to guest memory; a title that reads the off-chip or factor ring back sees no data.

name: shader.L125
text: [Hull input control points](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (shader recompiler) - a hull LDS read at a control-point index computed from data reads `gl_in` at that index clamped to the patch's last input control point, and a domain off-chip read at a computed index reads `gl_in` clamped to the patch's last output control point. On the console an index past the patch reads the LDS slot or off-chip record of a neighbouring patch or of no patch; the host has no such memory, and Vulkan leaves an out-of-range `gl_in` index undefined. The lowering refuses a computed offset that is not a whole number of control points, but the index itself is only known when the program runs.

name: shader.L126
text: [Inner tessellation factors](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) of integer, fractional-even or fractional-odd triangle patches that are NaN tessellate as 1 (fractional-even then raises them to 2, as Vulkan does), as in the D3D11 reference tessellator; the console is not measured.

name: shader.L127
text: [Hull programs](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/InstructionTranslator.cpp) start from the hull launch registers (user data, ring bases, v0, v1); on the console they start with what the local program leaves, and that it leaves them unchanged is not checked.

name: shader.L128
text: [Quad tessellation factors](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/TessellationLowering.cpp) are taken as outer[0..3] then inner[0..1], 24 bytes per patch, as [Mesa stores them](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/blob/b3588f78dd7fd46fbadc7ecd487e5f14d4213e4b/src/amd/common/nir/ac_nir_lower_tess_io_to_mem.c); unmeasured on the console.

name: shader.L129
text: [VGT_HOS_MIN/MAX_TESS_LEVEL](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) clamp positive tessellation factors (inner ones to at least 1); outer factors that are zero, negative or NaN still cull the patch and such inner factors become max(HOS_MIN, 1). The console's clamp and cull order is not measured.

name: shader.L130
text: [Patch constants](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/TessellationLowering.cpp) that hull programs write and domain programs read are placed by their off-chip address modulo the record stride, as the two compile apart; a domain read of a field the hull never writes, or of only a neighbouring patch's record, is not detected.

name: shader.L131
text: [Integer partitioning](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (`VGT_TF_PARAM.PARTITIONING` 0) is drawn with Vulkan's equal spacing, which [radeonsi programs as `PART_INTEGER`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-24.0.0/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state_shaders.cpp#L539-540), with factors bounded at 64 instead of fractional-odd's 63; how the console rounds a clamped factor up to a whole number of segments is not measured. Power-of-two (1) partitioning throws.

name: shader.L132
text: [Fractional-even partitioning](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (`VGT_TF_PARAM.PARTITIONING` 3) is drawn with Vulkan's fractional-even spacing, which [radeonsi programs as `PART_FRAC_EVEN`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-24.0.0/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/si_state_shaders.cpp#L536-537), with factors bounded at 64. Vulkan raises every factor that is not culled to at least 2 after `VGT_HOS_MIN/MAX_TESS_LEVEL`, so a `VGT_HOS_MAX_TESS_LEVEL` below 2 still tessellates at 2; the D3D11 range for this mode is also [2, 64], but the console's order of the HOS clamp and that minimum is not measured.

name: shader.L133
text: The [relative patch index](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/TessellationLowering.cpp) that hull and domain programs use as data is (PrimitiveID mod PRIM_GRP_SIZE) mod NUM_PATCHES, with the draw-relative instance times the patches per instance added when GE_CNTL.BREAK_WAVE_AT_EOI is clear and the instances share hull threadgroups; a domain that uses it in such a draw, and a hull without shaderDrawParameters, throw. Unmeasured on hardware; PPSA26344 programs 64 primitives for 63 patches.

name: shader.L134
text: The [output modifier](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/OperandAccess.cpp) (`mul:2`, `mul:4`, `div:2`) follows the shader's float mode as measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035): the hardware applies it only with IEEE mode off and output denormals of the result's precision flushed (bit 1 of the `FLOAT_MODE` denormal field clear), and ignores it otherwise. On f32 results it is applied as the hardware does with f32 denormals flushed; a shader without a known float mode is translated with IEEE mode off and f32 denormals flushed, the mode titles use. On f16 and f64 results it is ignored, and it throws in the modes where the hardware applies it. `v_cubeid_f32`, `v_cubesc_f32`, `v_cubetc_f32` and `v_cubema_f32`, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) with `DX10_CLAMP`=1, apply it whenever IEEE mode is off, in all four f32 denormal modes (`v_mul_f32_e64` in the same measurement follows the rule above), with the same bit-level result as the f32 path, and ignore it with IEEE mode on; clamp is applied after it. Only round to nearest even is modelled: in the other round modes (measured with IEEE mode off) gfx1036 rounds an overflow as the mode says (to the largest finite value when rounding toward zero), in `v_cubema_f32`'s own result and in the `mul:2` and `mul:4` scaling, where the translation gives infinity, and when rounding toward negative infinity a zero `v_cubema_f32` result with a NaN input is -0, where the translation gives +0.

name: shader.L135
text: The [clamp modifier](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/OperandAccess.cpp) follows `DX10_CLAMP`, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) for f32, f16, packed f16 and f64 results at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1: with `DX10_CLAMP`=1 (and in shaders without a known float mode) a NaN result clamps to +0, including the quieted NaN that `v_pk_min_f16` and `v_pk_max_f16` return for a signaling NaN operand with IEEE=1 (measured on RDNA2 gfx1036 at both `IEEE_MODE` and both `DX10_CLAMP` settings); with `DX10_CLAMP`=0 a NaN result is written unchanged and every other value clamps to [0, 1] as before. f64 results follow the same rule on hardware, but a clamped f64 result with `DX10_CLAMP`=0 throws until it has an execution test. With `DX10_CLAMP`=0 the NaN's bits are those the translation already produces for the instruction without clamp, so where those are left to the driver (f32 and scalar f16 arithmetic) the payload is the driver's, not the hardware's input propagation. `v_dot2_f32_f16` and the integer clamps are unchanged.

name: shader.L136
text: [FP16_OVFL](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/OperandAccess.cpp) follows the shader's float mode as measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with f16 denormals kept and flushed: with `FP16_OVFL`=1 an f16 result that rounds to ±infinity is written as ±0x7bff unless a source operand is infinite, so `v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16` and `v_log_f16` of ±0 and `v_exp_f16` of 16 or more are clamped while an infinite input passes through, and `v_div_fixup_f16` keeps the infinity it writes for a zero denominator or an infinite numerator and clamps any other infinite quotient, a NaN one included. `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` rounds toward zero and never overflows. The sources are checked as the f32 values the translation computes with; the rule is applied to `v_fma_mix*_f16` with f32 sources and to `v_interp_p2_f16` without a measurement of infinite f32 sources or parameters. Round modes other than nearest even are not modelled, so the overflow threshold is the nearest-even one (65520).

name: shader.L137
text: [Directed f16 rounding](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/SubwordPacking.cpp) for `v_cvt_f16_f32`, `v_cvt_f16_i16`, `v_cvt_f16_u16` and `v_ldexp_f16` follows `FLOAT_MODE` bits 3:2 in every f16 denormal mode, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036 with f16 denormals preserved, gfx1030 in all sixteen combinations of f16 rounding and denormal mode). When bit 7 flushes f16 results, `v_cvt_f16_f32`, `v_cvt_f16_i16` and `v_cvt_f16_u16` write a zero of the result's sign for a value that, rounded in that mode with an unbounded exponent, is below 2^-14, so a value just below 2^-14 that rounds up to it stays 0x0400; `v_ldexp_f16` keeps its rule above. The `clamp` modifier is applied before the rounding. On gfx1030 every row matches: 8,996 f32 inputs around the half denormal, normal and overflow boundaries with and without `clamp`, every 16-bit integer, and 2,470 `v_ldexp_f16` operands.

name: shader.L138
text: [v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32 and v_pack_b32_f16 denormals](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/ConvertInstructions.cpp) follow the `FLOAT_MODE` f16 denormal field: `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` flushes each denormal half result to its signed zero when bit 1 is clear (0 and 1), and `v_pack_b32_f16` flushes each denormal half input to its signed zero when bit 0 is clear (0 and 2). Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1031, Radeon RX 6700 XT, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002 through HIP) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with denorm16 0..3 and f32 denormals kept, over 256 pairs of 16 f32 values around the f16 denormal range for `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` and 256 pairs of 16 halves (zeros, denormals, minimum normals, ±1, the largest finite value, infinities and quiet and signaling NaNs) for `v_pack_b32_f16`. Shaders without a known float mode keep the previous lowering. The PS5's gfx1013 is not measured.

name: shader.L139
text: [Comparison sampling of a color texture](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvImageEmitter.cpp) (`image_sample_c`/`image_sample_c_lz` on a texture that is not R32 float or R16 unorm) is emulated in the shader, since Vulkan compares only depth formats: the red channel is fetched, compared and, for bilinear filtering, blended (compare, then filter). Only 2D, 2D array and cube views, float/unorm/snorm formats, wrap, clamp-to-edge and clamp-to-border addressing (border red 0 for the black borders, 1 for opaque white) and point or bilinear filtering at one level are implemented, with texel offsets added to the texel indices; LOD biases and clamps are accepted, as they cannot select another level of a single-level sample. Half-border addressing, the border color table, gradients, gathers, other dimensions, anisotropy (except on the 8-bit formats below) and mip filtering throw. Under bilinear filtering, taps past a clamp-to-border edge compare the border value and blend with the texel taps, so results near the edge depend on the filter weights. AMD documentation does not say how a color format's reference is handled: it is clamped to [0, 1] for unorm and [-1, 1] for snorm, as Vulkan does for unorm depth, and not clamped for float. 8-bit sRGB and UNORM (`Format8Srgb`, `Format8_8Srgb`, `Format8_8_8_8Srgb`, `Format8UNorm`, `Format8_8UNorm`, `Format8_8_8_8UNorm`) return 0 for every compare function, measured with `image_sample_c_lz` on gfx1035 over references -0.5..1.5 and texel codes 0..255. A bilinear cube of those 8-bit formats without `DISABLE_CUBE_WRAP`, and an anisotropic S# on them, return 0 for the same reason; float, snorm and the other unorm bilinear cubes without that bit still throw. Bilinear weights are full float, not the hardware's fixed-point subtexel weights

name: shader.L14
text: [MUBUF/MTBUF descriptors ending in VCC](../../../core/shader/recompiler/RdnaDecoder/src/RdnaMemoryOpDecoder.cpp): the four dword descriptor at s104 is s104, s105, vcc_lo and vcc_hi, as LLVM's [VCCTuple/SReg_128](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/d8219b47422f7322db252ad29ca8ea87993fb433/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SIRegisterInfo.td#L422) and [buffer resource operands](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/d8219b47422f7322db252ad29ca8ea87993fb433/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/BUFInstructions.td) describe. Existing translation maps scalar codes106/107 to the raw VCC words. Recompiled loads/stores, both words, bounds, formats and wave32/wave64 execute on NVIDIA and AMD Vulkan; raw gfx10/gfx1013 hardware is not measured. Higher descriptor bases remain refused; the normal SGPR bound is unchanged.

name: shader.L140
text: [Negative color-texture comparison wrap indices](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvImageEmitter.cpp) (libSceAgcDriver) use explicit `OpSRem` normalization to implement modulo; the negative-offset point-wrap regression fails with direct `OpSMod` and passes with normalization on Mesa 22.3.6 llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.6), but negative-index wrap has not been measured on PS5 hardware.

name: shader.L141
text: [Converted unorm images](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvImageEmitter.cpp) (10_11_11_UNORM, read and written through an R32_UINT view) are sampled in the shader, the way color comparisons are emulated: `image_sample` of a 2D or 2D array view fetches the one or four texels at LOD 0, decodes them and blends them, for point or bilinear filtering with equal minification and magnification filters and wrap or clamp-to-edge addressing. A shader gets these sample modes only once a converted descriptor reaches one of its sampled images: that capture throws `ConvertedSampleRequired`, the driver records the program and prepares it again with `GuestContext::convertedSamples`, so such a shader is prepared twice per run and its first capture is repeated. The record lives with the registered program and is not kept across runs. Bilinear weights are rounded to the hardware's 8-bit grid (`roundEven(fraction * 256) / 256`, ties to even), as measured with `image_sample_lz` on RDNA2 (gfx1035) for 10_11_11 UNORM texels by adriadam10 in #5958; point sampling, decoding, swizzles and wrap and clamp-to-edge addressing matched the same measurement. A sample that is not `_lz` needs an image with one mip level; gathers, LOD queries, clamp-to-border and mirrored addressing, other filters, min/max reduction, unnormalized coordinates, images selected at run time, 16-bit data and a DST_SEL of the missing W channel throw.

name: shader.L142
text: [Converted unorm image loads](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvImageEmitter.cpp) divide by 2^n - 1 with the buffer format path's `OpFDiv`, which Vulkan allows to be up to 2.5 ULP off, so some drivers are not bit-exact.

name: shader.L143
text: [64-bit LDS atomics](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (`ds_*_u64`, `ds_*_b64`, `ds_*_f64`) read and write the two dwords under a workgroup lock stored after the guest LDS, as LDS is a 32-bit array without 64-bit atomics. On RDNA2 (gfx1036) the LDS serialises a 32-bit atomic on a slot's high dword and a 64-bit atomic on that slot: 128 lanes of `ds_add_u32` and 128 lanes of `ds_add_u64` on one slot sum exactly. Only that pair was measured. Every 32-bit LDS atomic of a program that contains a 64-bit LDS atomic therefore takes the same lock, including a 32-bit `flat_atomic_*` whose address lands in the LDS aperture (a 64-bit one takes it already); the flat forms were not measured against a 64-bit atomic either (the other 32-bit LDS atomics, `ds_min/max`, `ds_cmpst`, the float forms, `ds_inc/dec`, `ds_mskor` and `ds_wrxchg`, are extrapolated from `ds_add_u32` and were not measured against a 64-bit atomic); a program without a 64-bit LDS atomic keeps its native 32-bit atomics. `ds_condxchg32_rtn_b64` is two `ds_mskor` halves, each under the lock but not atomic as a pair, so a 64-bit atomic between the two halves is not excluded. Sub-dword writes (`ds_write_b8`, `ds_write_b16` and their `_d16_hi` forms) and plain `ds_read_*`, `ds_write_*`, `ds_append_u32` and `ds_consume_u32` are not taken under the lock, so a plain access racing a 64-bit atomic on the same dwords can see or overwrite one half of it; whether the hardware orders them was not measured. The lock serialises the workgroup's LDS atomics of such a program; the throughput cost was not measured. `VK_KHR_workgroup_memory_explicit_layout` with `shaderSharedInt64Atomics` would make both widths native and is not used. A 64-bit atomic at an address that is 4-byte but not 8-byte aligned faults the wave on gfx1036, as on gfx1035. When the LDS lives in device memory (compute LDS beyond the device's shared-memory limit) and the device has `shaderBufferInt64Atomics`, no lock is used: a 64-bit atomic is a compare-exchange loop on a 64-bit view of the storage buffer and a 32-bit atomic is a native buffer atomic, a misaligned 64-bit atomic records the `Unaligned` shader fault with the LDS byte address instead of updating, so a mixed-width pair on one slot relies on the device ordering both widths on one buffer address; only `ds_add_u32` against `ds_add_u64` was measured, on gfx1036 (AMD Windows driver 32.0.21042.62) and an RTX 4070 SUPER. The lock is not used there because AMD's Windows driver compiles an acquire or release on a storage buffer, at workgroup scope or wider, to `s_barrier`, and those barriers inside the lock's divergent loop pair with the program's own `s_barrier`s. The fence after each LDS atomic compiles to `s_barrier` on that driver as well, so a wave that skips an LDS atomic that other waves of its workgroup execute misses a barrier they reach; its effect was not measured. On that path a 64-bit atomic at an address that is 4-byte but not 8-byte aligned is skipped and returns 0.

name: shader.L144
text: [LDS float atomics](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (`ds_min/max/cmpst_f32`, `ds_min/max/cmpst_f64` and their `_rtn` forms) follow the hardware measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) over 14 x 14 operand sets (zeros, ones, infinities, denormals, quiet and signalling NaNs of both signs and with payloads) in IEEE 0 and 1 with every value 0-3 of the type's denormal field: both operands are flushed to a signed zero when bit 0 of the field is clear (0 and 2; 1 and 3 keep them; the f32 field for the f32 forms, the f16/f64 field for the f64 forms; a shader without a known float mode flushes f32 and keeps f64), then a signalling-NaN data operand is stored quieted, else a signalling-NaN old value is stored quieted, else a quiet-NaN old value is replaced by the data, else a quiet-NaN data operand loses, else the ordered compare with -0 below +0 decides, and the flushed value is what is written, also when the old value wins. `cmpst` compares the flushed bits (both zeros equal, NaN never equal) and leaves memory unchanged when they differ. The returned value is always the old value as it was in memory. `IEEE_MODE` has no effect. The same bit rule serves the buffer float atomics (`AtomicFloatBits`). Not measured: a denormal or signalling-NaN `data1` of `cmpst` (stored as given). `ds_add_f32` and `ds_add_rtn_f32` follow RDNA1 (gfx1010, RX 5700 XT), measured with the [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) template run through the Windows driver's comgr and HIP runtime over 1574 operand pairs (signed zeros, denormals, the smallest normals, infinities, quiet and signalling NaNs with payloads, the largest normals, random pairs near the denormal range and pairs that nearly cancel) in all 16 combinations of the f32 denormal field and the f32 round mode, and at IEEE 1 and DX10 clamp 0: both operands are flushed to a signed zero when bit 0 of the field is clear and the result when bit 1 is clear, the sum is rounded to nearest even whatever the round mode, a NaN data operand is stored quieted, else a NaN old value is stored quieted, `+inf + -inf` stores 0xffc00000, and `IEEE_MODE` and `DX10_CLAMP` have no effect. The sum is the host's `OpFAdd` between those flushes, so where the field keeps f32 denormals the result also depends on the host preserving them, which the module does not request. thuanquang measured the same rule on RDNA2 (gfx1031, RX 6700 XT) in #5492, with the same operand classes and 18 modes in wave32 and wave64; the PS5's gfx1013 is not measured.

name: shader.L145
text: [LDS in pixel, vertex-path and fetch programs](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAnalysis.cpp) (shader recompiler) - is an array private to each host invocation, in `Function` storage, as only compute and mesh programs get workgroup memory; on the console one LDS region is shared by the wave (RDNA 2 ISA sections 3.6.6 and 10.4), so a lane does not see another lane's LDS writes. Sub-dword writes (`ds_write_b8`, `ds_write_b16` and their `_d16_hi` forms), the 32-bit LDS atomics, `ds_append` and `ds_consume` load, update and store the invocation's own dword without an atomic, as Vulkan allows atomics only on `Uniform`, `Workgroup`, `Image`, `StorageBuffer`, `PhysicalStorageBuffer` and `TaskPayloadWorkgroupEXT` pointers (VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-04686). `ds_append` and `ds_consume` update only the first active lane's copy and return its old value to every lane, so a second append after the first active lane changes, or a read of the counter by another lane, differs from the hardware. Not measured on hardware.

name: shader.L146
text: [V# bases off a DWORD boundary](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (shader recompiler) - raw accesses use the exact bytes and `s_buffer_load` reads `(base & ~3) + (offset & ~3)`, as measured on gfx1035 (Linux, alignment mode UNALIGNED; the console's mode is unknown). Formatted accesses off their element's alignment throw. Atomics use the byte address `base + offset`, base's low two bits included: measured on RDNA2 (gfx1031, Radeon RX 6700 XT, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002 through HIP) with `buffer_atomic_add`, `buffer_atomic_swap` and `buffer_atomic_cmpswap` and bases 0 to 3 bytes past a DWORD boundary with offsets 0 to 7, an address on a DWORD boundary updates that DWORD and returns its old value, and any other address stops the dispatch, which the recompiler reports as an unaligned access fault.

name: shader.L148
text: [32-bit bitfield masks](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/IntegerInstructions.cpp) (`S_BFM_B32`, `V_BFM_B32`) use the truncating 32-bit shift specified by the [RDNA 1.0 ISA](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf), sections 12.1 (opcode 36) and 12.12 (opcode 867). Width and offset use their low five bits. This matches gfx1035 (Linux) for every width/offset pair, with and without upper operand bits set, and both leave SCC unchanged; not measured on the console.

name: shader.L149
text: [Vector buffer offsets that are not a multiple of 4](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (shader recompiler) - dword accesses count whole dwords from the V# base, where the hardware reads the exact bytes at base + offset.

name: shader.L150
text: [Raw `buffer_load_dwordx2`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) is one 64-bit access on the hardware (with or without glc), so it never sees half of a `buffer_atomic_swap_x2`. Only a glc load that is 8-byte aligned and in bounds, in a program that has the 64-bit storage view (it uses 64-bit buffer atomics), is read with one 64-bit atomic load; every other dwordx2 load is two dword loads and can tear against a concurrent 64-bit write: loads without glc, and loads in a program without 64-bit buffer atomics while another shader writes the pair with `swap_x2`.

name: shader.L151
text: [Buffer loads without GLC or DLC](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAnalysis.cpp) (shader recompiler) are not coherent in a program that has GLC or DLC buffer accesses and no `buffer_gl0_inv`, `buffer_gl1_inv`, `s_gl1_inv` or `s_dcache_inv`: only its GLC and DLC loads, stores and atomics use the `Coherent` buffer view, so a plain load can return a value cached before another work-group's write. This follows the [LLVM AMDGPU memory model for GFX10](https://llvm.org/docs/AMDGPUUsage.html#memory-model-gfx10-gfx11), in which a load-acquire is a GLC DLC load followed by `buffer_gl1_inv` and `buffer_gl0_inv`; it is not measured on the console or on RDNA hardware.

name: shader.L152
text: [DS src2 operations](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/MemoryInstructions/SharedMemoryInstructions.cpp) (`ds_*_src2_*`, GFX10.1 only) read `DS[B]`, with `B = A + 4 * sext(offset1[6:0]:offset0)`, and then update `DS[A]` with the matching 32-bit atomic, so the read of `B` is not atomic with the update of `A`. The form that takes the offset from the address (`offset1[7]` set), the 64-bit forms and GDS throw: whether the LDS address keeps `A[31:17]` in that form, and whether the 64-bit forms scale the offset by 4 or 8, is not documented. `ds_min_src2_f32`, `ds_max_src2_f32` and `ds_add_src2_f32` throw: on RDNA2 (gfx1035, the oracle's hardware, which has no src2 opcodes) `ds_min_f32`, `ds_max_f32` and `ds_add_f32` ignore `IEEE_MODE` but depend on whether f32 denormals are flushed (28, 28 and 12 of 196 special rows differ), and that is not modelled for LDS float atomics yet (#981).

name: shader.L154
text: [s_swappc_b64](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/ControlFlowInstructions.cpp) writes the link pair with the same model as `s_getpc_b64`: the guest return address `pc + 4` as a byte offset over `GetShaderBase`. Any other use of the link pair (arithmetic, hash, store) throws, apart from the overwrites, SOPC compares and shared links that [static scalar calls](../../../core/shader/recompiler/ControlFlow/src/GraphBuilder.cpp) allow; constant-offset folding over the link is not modeled. The special encoding `s_swappc_b64` with SDST 125 still decodes as `s_setpc_b64`, which matches the hardware: measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) in wave32 and wave64, it branches to the source pair and leaves a marker SGPR pair untouched, and with an SGPR destination the link is `PC + 4`.

[`IndexedWindowSlots`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvModuleSetup.cpp) bounds each relative index through the IR (bit-field extracts, masks, shifts, adds, selects, phis, `ReadFirstLane` and the window stores that reach a load); the storage is an array of the slots below the largest bound that is under half the window, and one function variable per slot after it. A constant index uses the array element or the slot's variable; a relative access whose index has no such bound, or lands past the array at run time, indexes the array below its size and otherwise branches through an `OpSwitch` over the slot variables, so the bound only decides speed. When no index has a bound under half the window, the whole window is the array, as with `APS5_NO_WINDOW_NARROWING=1` (a recompiler switch in the shader cache key). Measured on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (driver 615.78.08, Linux) with a compute program whose 167-register window an ALU loop reads and writes in full and whose relative accesses take `m0 = s8 & 3`: a 2048-group dispatch took 70.2 ms in wave32 and 123.3 ms in wave64 with the whole window in the array (as before narrowing) and 1.9-2.1 ms and 7.8 ms narrowed; with a second relative access whose index has no bound and lands past the array at run time (index 50 or 166), 113 ms and 5.8-6.0 ms in wave32. In the PPSA08427 (Killing Floor 3) hub it made no measurable difference to presents or to the GPU time of the eight most expensive programs. Whether the host compiler keeps the array and the slot variables in registers or spills them to scratch is not measured. A register in the window the program never wrote reads 0, as an unwritten SSA register does; the console's value is undefined. M0 is unsigned: an index at or past the window reads `v0` and drops its write, and `v_swaprel_b32` writes neither side when either is out of range, as measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035, `agc_driver_relative_indexing`). The window ends at the last register the program names rather than at the shader's VGPR allocation, which the recompiler does not receive, so a relative write past the named registers but inside the allocation is dropped where the hardware keeps it for a later relative read. Killzone: Liberation's PSP vertex program (PPSA11142, 3176 ISA words, 104 relative accesses over 154 registers) went from 649,515 to 392,333 SPIR-V words with this. A fold after masked-select elimination lowers fields whose consumers become visible only after redundant copies are removed. A whole-word use that the masked-select pass keeps gets the composed word described under the packed pixel ancillary word. Both representations include implicit entry inputs in the inferred register limit and retain unsigned M0, inactive-write and DPP update rules; wave32/wave64 native Vulkan readbacks cover relative reads, writes, split-offset swaps, inactive writes, DPP masks and out-of-range accesses, but console comparison and the performance cost of selecting over this span are unverified.

name: shader.L41
text: An [image table](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceTracker.cpp) whose key is neither a V#-relative scalar read nor a value the SRT walker evaluates (for example a shifted or masked runtime-offset V# read, a per-lane value made uniform by `v_readfirstlane`, or a loop-carried phi) binds every record of the snapshot domain instead of the selected ones. A key the walker evaluates selects its one record instead, unless the shader may write the memory the key is read from at run time (the same buffer, or any memory when the read or a write goes through a pointer or a GPU-only descriptor); then the column binds the whole domain too. A write to the key's memory through another V# over the same bytes is not detected. A shader whose selected records would pass 64 images or 64 sampled image/sampler pairs binds, for the heaps with the most such reads, the union of their keys in one table instead.

Every register is zero when the mip level is past the last level, `x + N - 1` is outside the level's width (unaligned x, unsigned), or y is outside its height. Data only comes back when the N texels fit in one dword: R8 and R16 (DMASK 0x3) or RG8 (0xf) for BY2, and R8 (0xf) for BY4. With 32-bit texels (R32, RG32, RG16, RGBA8) the hardware returns zeros. text: [2D accesses through a cube T#](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) (#4139) read the T#'s `BASE_ARRAY` face as a cube access with face coordinate 0 does, measured on RDNA1 (gfx1010, RX 5700 XT) with the [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) template run through the Windows driver's comgr and HIP runtime on 8x8 and 32x32 32_FLOAT cubes (`DEPTH` 5 and 11, `BASE_ARRAY` 0 and 6): `image_sample_lz`, plain `image_sample` (one level, and six levels in 2x2 compute quads) and `image_sample_l` (the third address VGPR is the LOD, integer and fractional) with DIM 2D equal DIM CUBE with face 0 on every row, with point and bilinear filters, wrap, clamp and mirror addressing and `DISABLE_CUBE_WRAP` 0 and 1, and the VGPR after the two coordinates is not read; `image_load` with DIM 2D reads texel (x, y) of the `BASE_ARRAY` face. text: The bundled [SPIRV-Tools build](../../../core/shader/recompiler/PatchSpirvTools.cmake) replaces the redundancy-elimination source with a build-directory copy. This extends the processed-map release fix in [SPIRV-Tools #6962](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Tools/pull/6962). Remove the patch when the pinned dependency has equivalent copy-free traversal; #6962 alone still copies maps for sibling branches. name: shader.L72
text: [8_SRGB and 8_8_SRGB loads](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvImageEmitter.cpp) on a device that cannot sample R8_SRGB or R8G8_SRGB return the sRGB EOTF rounded to nearest even at bf16 precision, as adriadam10 measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) in #866; the PS5's gfx1013 is not measured. This is the path on a device that cannot blit R8 or RG8 to RGBA8, and with `APS5_SRGB_SHADER_DECODE=1`; otherwise a load of a sampled texture reads the RGBA8 sRGB copy and gets the device's own decode.

name: shader.L74
text: [Bindless image table](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) entries of 8_SRGB and 8_8_SRGB textures read zeros, like converted formats, on a device that cannot sample R8_SRGB or R8G8_SRGB.

name: shader.L75
text: [Shader MODE register access](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/RoundingMode.cpp) starts from the rounding fields of `GuestContext::floatMode` and follows immediate rounding writes (`s_round_mode`, `s_setreg_imm32_b32` on MODE bits 0-3) through the control flow graph; `s_getreg_b32` of those bits returns the tracked value. Only `v_cvt_f32_i32`, `v_cvt_f32_u32`, `v_ldexp_f32`, the f16 conversions and `v_ldexp_f16` (with f16 denormals kept) and the instructions that already read `FLOAT_MODE` follow a rounding mode set at run time; any other float instruction that runs while a directed rounding mode differs from the initial one throws at that instruction. Rounding bits written from an SGPR (`s_setreg_b32`) or that differ between the paths reaching an instruction throw where they are read or used. A shader without `FLOAT_MODE` metadata throws on any rounding change. Non-rounding register reads still throw; `s_setreg_b32` writes to other hardware registers are still ignored. Tests follow the public RDNA2/LLVM contract, not console measurements.

name: shader.L77
text: Repeated `s_load`s of one [flat SRT](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/SrtWalker/SrtDescriptorEvaluation.cpp) dword through a null or unmapped pointer report one of their pcs, and an `s_load` whose inaccessible dwords are all unused, or only address repeated loads, reports no fault of its own.

name: shader.L78
text: A value read through a null or unmapped pointer still throws at record time if a [uniform fill or table base](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/SrtWalker/SrtDescriptorEvaluation.cpp) needs it, or if the pointer comes from user data and is not null, even if the console skips the read.

name: shader.L79
text: A [V# or flat SRT word](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/SrtWalker/SrtEvaluator.cpp) read through a null pointer taken from user data is zero and counts as a [poisoned SRT read](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp), so a dispatch that reads it is not cached. The console faults if the program executes the read; PPSA28416 branches around it with `s_cbranch_execz`. The fault is not modeled.

name: shader.L80
text: A [V#, T# or S#](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/SrtWalker/SrtDescriptorEvaluation.cpp) loaded through a null or unmapped pointer read from memory is zero when the work is recorded, and the capture throws if no flat SRT slot records that read.

name: shader.L81
text: [2D accesses through a 1D T#](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) read the texel the 1D addressing selects and ignore the second coordinate, as simonbbby measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) in #2237 for `image_sample_lz` and mip-less `image_load` with point filtering and wrap, clamp and border addressing; `image_sample_l` was measured the same way on gfx1036 against `image_sample_l` with DIM 1D through the same T#, for u inside, on and past the edges, v of 0, 0.5, 1, -0.25 and 3, LOD -1 to 6 on a 5-level R32_FLOAT texture, point, linear and linear-mip filtering, wrap, clamp and border addressing and HEIGHT or DEPTH 3: all 4725 rows matched. The PS5's gfx1013 is not measured. A plain `image_sample` (implicit LOD) through such a pair takes its LOD from the derivatives of the first coordinate alone, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1036) with the [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) on the quads of a compute kernel (wave32 and wave64, IEEE off, DX10 clamp on, denormals preserved, round to nearest even): on a 16-texel, 5-mip 32_UINT T# with point filters it picks the same mip and texel as DIM 1D for first-coordinate steps of 0, 1, 2, 4 and 8 texels per lane along x or along y, whatever the second coordinate does (normalised steps up to 16 per lane), while the same rows on a 16x16 2D T# move the mip with the second coordinate. Outside the pixel stage a plain `image_sample` is emitted with LOD 0 for every image type, so this pair reads mip 0 there, where the kernel measurement shows the quad's derivatives being used. `image_sample_c_lz` and plain `image_sample_c` through such a pair compare against the texel the DIM 1D comparison with the same reference and first coordinate reads, measured on RDNA1 (gfx1010, RX 5700 XT) with the [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) template run through the Windows driver's comgr and HIP runtime (wave32 and wave64, IEEE off, DX10 clamp on, denormals preserved, round to nearest even): 8-texel 32_FLOAT and 16_UNORM T#s, also with HEIGHT 3, point and bilinear filters, wrap, clamp and opaque-white border addressing, less and gequal functions, second coordinates 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, -0.25 and 3; on a 64-texel, 7-mip 32_FLOAT T# `image_sample_c` picks its LOD from the first coordinate's steps alone (1, 4 and 16 texels per lane give mips 0, 2 and 4; second-coordinate steps up to 64 texels leave it unchanged). Only comparisons the runtime does natively (32_FLOAT, 16_UNORM) reach the 1D view; comparisons the runtime emulates for other color formats still throw through such a pair. 2D-array `image_sample_l` and `image_sample_lz` through a 1D T# read as DIM 1D too, ignoring v and the slice: measured on gfx1036 with the hardware oracle (template assembled by the AMD Windows driver's `amd_comgr_2.dll` and launched through its `amdhip64_6.dll`) against the same sample with DIM 1D on a 16-texel 8_8_8_8 UNORM T# with 1 or 5 levels, HEIGHT or DEPTH 3, for u inside, on and past the edges, v of 0, 0.5, 1, -0.25 and 3, slices 0, 1, 2.7, -1 and 5, LOD -1 to 6, and the five filter and address cases above: all 48000 rows matched. A 2D-array `image_load` through a 1D T# is not the same: on gfx1036 it returns the DIM 1D texel only at slice 0, and zeros at slices 1, 2, 5 and -1 even with DEPTH 3, so it, the plain `image_sample` and the other 2D-array accesses still throw. Other 2D accesses through a 1D T# (storage, depth, packed, BY loads, mips other than explicit LOD, explicit LOD with comparison, bias, offsets, derivatives) still throw.

name: shader.L82
text: [3D image accesses bound to a 1D T#](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) follow a [hardware oracle](../HW_ORACLE.md) measurement on RDNA1 (RX 5700 XT, gfx1010; wave32 and wave64, IEEE off, DX10 clamp on, denormals preserved, round to nearest even), not the PS5's gfx1013, on 8x1 R8G8B8A8_UNORM linear 1D T#s with HEIGHT and DEPTH 0 or 3 and point filters. `image_sample_lz` reads the texel u selects for v and r in {0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, -0.25, 3}, with wrap, clamp and border addressing, and v and r never produce the border; u wraps, clamps and borders as with DIM 1D. Mip-less `image_load` reads the x texel for any y in {0, 1, 2, 3, -1} when z is 0, returns zero for z in {1, 2, 3, -1}, whatever DEPTH says, and returns zero for x past the width. A plain `image_sample` (implicit LOD) on the quads of a compute kernel takes its texel and LOD from u alone: on a 64-texel, 7-mip 1D T# steps of 1, 4 and 16 texels per lane pick mips 0, 2 and 4, as DIM 1D `image_sample_l` does, and steps in v or r alone stay at mip 0. Outside the pixel stage a plain `image_sample` is emitted with LOD 0, as for 2D accesses through a 1D T#. Every other 3D access of such an image (`image_load` with mips, storage, explicit LOD, bias, derivatives, offsets, comparison, gathers, queries) keeps throwing. SONIC SUPERSTARS (PPSA06888) samples a 1x1 1D T# this way with plain `image_sample` and `image_load`.

name: shader.L83
text: [Emulated comparison of a 2D-array access through a 2D T#](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/ResourceMaterializer.cpp) samples the 2D image and ignores the slice, as the native modes of a 2D-array access through a 2D T# already do. This follows the T# type deciding the addressing; it is not measured on hardware for comparison samples

name: shader.L84
text: [Flat aperture bases](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (core/shader/recompiler) - the layout follows the gfx9+ one in the AMD KFD driver's `kfd_flat_memory.c` (`MAKE_LDS_APP_BASE_V9`, `MAKE_LDS_APP_LIMIT`): each aperture is a 4 GB window whose base is the high dword, so a flat address is routed by its whole high dword, as measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035: `src_shared_base` 0x00010000_00000000, `src_shared_limit` 0x00010000_ffffffff). The PS5's base values, high dwords 0x80000000 (shared, `SharedApertureHigh`) and 0x70000000 (private, `PrivateApertureHigh`), are inferred from GTA V's traversal addresses, not measured on a console or read from SH_MEM_BASES. The scalar aperture sources read the same two values

name: shader.L85
text: [Flat accesses outside the aperture routing](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvMemory/SpirvMemoryInstructions.cpp) (core/shader/recompiler) - only compute stages route flat accesses, so graphics-stage flat accesses to the shared or private aperture still go to BDA. In compute, a 64-bit flat atomic whose address is in the shared aperture takes the workgroup lock (`ldsLock`) for its two-dword update, and every such atomic requests that lock, so a shader with one pays for it even on global addresses (the path is exercised by `agc_driver_global_atomics_float`). Inferred, not measured on LDS or scratch: an aperture access that is not inside one dword is done byte by byte, an unaligned aperture atomic records the BDA unaligned fault, and LDS or scratch accesses past their end are dropped or read zero.

name: shader.L86
text: On a host subgroup narrower than 32 lanes, [`threadBit`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/ExecMask.cpp) reads an EXEC written as a value (`s_mov_b32`/`s_mov_b64`) at bit (subgroup invocation id) of EXEC_LO, so lanes at or above the subgroup size read a lower lane's bit.

name: shader.L87
text: [EXEC read as a value](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/TranslationContext/ExecMask.cpp) (`s_mov_b64 sN, exec`, the `s_*_saveexec` copy, ALU sources) is limited to host lanes. Pixel reads retain helper bits in quads with an active fragment, preserving whole-quad masks across copies. Quad expansion follows the [RDNA 2 ISA, section 12.3, S_WQM_B32/B64, page 111](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=119); save/restore followed by implicit-LOD sampling is checked on an RX 6700 XT, not on a console. The console also holds lanes the host lacks, e.g. 32-63 of a wave64 on 32 host lanes.

name: shader.L88
text: [`v_readlane_b32`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAlu/SpirvAluEmitterMath.cpp) and fetch-inactive `v_permlane16_b32`/`v_permlanex16_b32` read undefined data from a lane that the host subgroup does not hold or whose host invocation is inactive; the console reads the lane's VGPR.

name: shader.L89
text: Without fetch-inactive, [`v_permlane16_b32` and `v_permlanex16_b32`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAlu/SpirvAluEmitterMath.cpp) take a source lane that the host subgroup does not hold as inactive and keep the old value (0 with bound_ctrl); the console reads that lane's VGPR.

name: shader.L90
text: On a host subgroup narrower than the wave, [`v_readlane_b32`](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAlu/SpirvAluEmitterMath.cpp) of a constant lane outside it builds only as lane 63 of a half-wave scan (DPP row_shr 1/2/4/8, `v_permlanex16_b32`, EXEC -1) or, in a program whose entry EXEC is every lane (vertex, local and tessellation stages), as 0 when the value is 0 in lanes 32-63; other such reads throw. A value is 0 there when it is built from 0 through selects under a lane index (lane id or `v_mbcnt` of -1) below at most 32, `v_cmp_ne_u32` against 0, OR, DPP and permlanes; the counts in `s3` give such a bound on a 32-lane host. On a 32-lane host a half-wave scan may also run under `s_mov_b64 exec, -1`, use bound_ctrl:1 steps for an OR, add or unsigned max, and take keys that are 0 in lanes 32-63; its lane 31 is then the subgroup reduction of the host's invocations (a shuffle of the scan on a device without subgroup arithmetic): idle invocations add the identity, where the console would add the keys of the lanes `s3` claims.

name: shader.L91
text: [NGG mesh entry](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/InstructionTranslator.cpp) uses the guest wave size (32 or 64) for wave indices, per-wave vertex and primitive counts, and the workgroup wave count in `s3`. The four-bit wave fields follow Mesa's [get_wave_id_in_tg, get_tgsize and get_thread_id_in_tg](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromiumos/third_party/mesa/+/refs/heads/stabilize-13982.70.B-chromeos-amd/src/gallium/drivers/radeonsi/gfx10_shader_ngg.c); partial waves and groups exceeding 15 waves throw. Indexed and non-indexed wave32 mesh rendering with 32, 64 and 128 threads was checked by pixel readback on Windows with an NVIDIA RTX 4070 Laptop GPU. The guest register values have not been compared with console hardware.

name: shader.L92
text: [Mesh shader grid size](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (shader recompiler) - every mesh shader loads `NumWorkgroups.x` and declares no vertices when it is 0, which no dispatch produces. The read is a workaround for RADV (Mesa 26.2.4, seen on an RX 9070 XT, GFX12): binding a mesh pipeline whose shader reads neither `NumWorkgroups` nor `DrawIndex` keeps the user SGPR count and draw-id flag of the vertex pipeline bound before it in the same command buffer (`radv_bind_pre_rast_shader` updates them only when the shader has the `AC_UD_VS_BASE_VERTEX_START_INSTANCE` slot), so `radv_emit_userdata_mesh` opens a 3-register `SET_SH_REG` and writes one value, the CP takes the following `DISPATCH_MESH_DIRECT` as register data and the GPU hangs (gfx ring timeout, MODE1 reset). Kena: Bridge of Spirits (PPSA01802) hits it on its layered volume draws. Reading `NumWorkgroups` gives every mesh shader the grid-size slot, so the count and the values match; drop the read once a fixed Mesa is the minimum

name: shader.L93
text: [Mesh layer output](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvModuleEmitter.cpp) (shader recompiler) - a mesh shader writes each primitive's layer through a one-member `Block` struct array whose member is decorated `BuiltIn Layer` and `PerPrimitiveEXT`, as glslang declares `gl_Layer` inside `gl_MeshPerPrimitiveEXT`, not through a standalone `PerPrimitiveEXT` `Layer` array. Both forms pass `spirv-val`, but AMD's Windows driver (32.0.21045.5002, RX 6700 XT) crashes in `amdvlk64.dll` creating a pipeline whose mesh shader writes the standalone form, whether the layer is signed or unsigned and whatever the target, while the block form draws, also with a pixel shader that reads the layer.

name: shader.L94
text: [Shader recompilation](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Recompiler.cpp) currently occurs right before it was transferred to Vulkan with caching, but should be moved to the [relinker](../../../core/relinker/main.cpp) stage. For this purpose, [shader/recompiler](../../../core/shader/recompiler) was written completely independently from [libs/prx](../../../core/libs/prx).

name: shader.L95
text: [v_interp_p1ll_f16, v_interp_p1lv_f16 and v_interp_p2_f16](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/AttributeInstructions.cpp) read the 16-bit halves of each vertex's parameter through `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`, as fixed-function interpolation cannot split a 32-bit attribute. Without the extension the pixel shader takes the [barycentric emulation](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/BarycentricGeometryShader.cpp), whose generated geometry stage passes each vertex's parameter to it as a flat input, so the halves arrive bit for bit; a device without geometry shaders takes the tessellation stages of the same emulation instead, which no 16-bit interpolation test has run through yet. P10 and P20 are the vertex differences rounded to f16 to nearest even, which is not confirmed on hardware. v_interp_p1ll_f16 and v_interp_p1lv_f16 round the exact `P10 * I + P0` once to f32 and v_interp_p2_f16 rounds the exact `P20 * J + S2` once to f16, as measured on RDNA2 (#697); the exact sums are computed in f64 or, on a device without the Float64 capability, in 64-bit integers: the exact product is added with a sticky bit and rounded once. They follow the shader's float mode, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) in all eight combinations of `IEEE_MODE` and kept/flushed f32 and f16 denormals over 768 special and 1,024 random rows. With IEEE=1 a NaN operand is returned quieted; with IEEE=0 it is returned unquieted, except that v_interp_p2_f16's f16 result is always quiet. Flushed f32 denormals flush I/J, v_interp_p2_f16's f32 S2 and the f32 result; flushed f16 denormals flush P0, P10/P20, v_interp_p1lv_f16's f16 S2 and the f16 result. Denormal modes 1 and 2 (flush only inputs or only outputs) and rounding other than to nearest even are not measured and throw. An unknown mode follows IEEE=0 with denormals kept. Lavapipe has no barycentrics, so the draw test is skipped in CI; `agc_driver_interpolation_modes` checks the integer arithmetic on every device, and the f64 arithmetic on devices with Float64. It checks both against the hardware rows in every mode, and against a CPU reference on random rows in every mode and f16 rounding.

name: shader.L96
text: Without `VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric`, a pixel shader whose I/J VGPRs [only feed `v_interp_p1_f32`/`v_interp_p2_f32` of their own pair](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Optimization/src/HostInterpolationChecker.cpp) reads the attribute Vulkan interpolated. Any other read of them or of a raw vertex parameter takes the weights and the three vertex values from a [generated geometry stage](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/BarycentricGeometryShader.cpp), which needs `geometryShader` and a vertex shader before it. On a device with `tessellationShader` but no `geometryShader` (MoltenVK), a triangle list without primitive restart takes them from [generated tessellation stages](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/BarycentricGeometryShader.cpp) instead: each triangle is one three-point patch at tessellation level 1, the evaluation stage writes the corner `gl_TessCoord` points at as the weights, and the vertex clip distances are forwarded: the control stage reads them as the separate `ClipDistance` array the vertex shader writes, so the vertex-to-control interfaces match, and passes them on inside its per-vertex block, which the evaluation stage reads and writes. MoltenVK 1.4.2 (SPIRV-Cross) cannot translate a separate `ClipDistance` array in a tessellation evaluation stage (`no member named 'gl_ClipDistance' in 'main0_out'`), so the two generated stages keep it in their blocks. A flat parameter takes the first vertex's value there, as the geometry stage's strip gives it; the last provoking vertex throws. The patch keeps the triangle's facing with `VertexOrderCw`, checked with face culling on MoltenVK 1.4.2 (Apple M2) only. Tessellation, mesh and rect-list pipelines, primitives other than triangles, triangle strips and fans without `geometryShader`, more than 32 fragment input locations and interfaces beyond the device's geometry or tessellation limits throw.

name: shader.L97
text: [v_fma_f64 and v_div_fmas_f64](../../../core/shader/recompiler/SpirvBackend/src/SpirvAlu/SpirvAluEmitterFloat64.cpp) with a subnormal operand or result round once, as IEEE 754 fusedMultiplyAdd does with f64 denormals kept, measured on RDNA2 (gfx1035) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1, `v_div_fmas_f64` with VCC clear and set. The f16/f64 denormal field of `FLOAT_MODE` (bits 7:6) is not read: when it flushes, the hardware flushes the operands and the result of `v_fma_f64` (tininess before rounding) and only the result of `v_div_fmas_f64`, while these keep them. Shaders with f64 instructions declare `DenormPreserve` for 64-bit floats only when `shaderDenormPreserveFloat64` is true and Vulkan reports `denormBehaviorIndependence` as `ALL`; other independence modes are not handled by the current backend because they require coupled execution modes. See [VkShaderFloatControlsIndependence](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkShaderFloatControlsIndependence.html). Elsewhere (including lavapipe), the driver may flush f64 subnormals, and `agc_driver_f64_fma_subnormals` is skipped.

name: shader.L98
text: [v_floor_f64, v_ceil_f64, v_fract_f64, v_frexp_mant_f64 and v_frexp_exp_i32_f64](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/Float64Instructions.cpp) follow the `FLOAT_MODE` f16/f64 denormal field: a denormal input is flushed to a zero of its sign when bit 0 is clear (0 and 2), and `v_fract_f64` flushes a denormal result, the fraction of a positive denormal input, to +0 when bit 1 is clear (0 and 1). `v_trunc_f64` and `v_rndne_f64` give the same results either way and are unchanged. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1031, Radeon RX 6700 XT, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002 through HIP) at IEEE=0 and IEEE=1 with denorm16 0..3 over 23 f64 values (zeros, denormals, minimum normals, ±0.5, ±1, values next to 1, the largest finite value, infinities and quiet and signaling NaNs) and 16 of them with neg and abs modifiers. Shaders without a known float mode keep the previous lowering. The PS5's gfx1013 is not measured.

name: shader.L99
text: [v_add_f64 and v_mul_f64 denormals](../../../core/shader/recompiler/Translation/src/Float64Instructions.cpp) follow the `FLOAT_MODE` f16/f64 denormal field; the PS5's gfx1013 is not measured. Inputs flush to a zero of their sign when bit 0 is clear (0 and 2). When bit 1 is clear (0 and 1), a sum below 2^-1022, or a product whose exact value rounded to 53 significant bits with an unbounded exponent is below 2^-1022, flushes to a zero of its sign, so `0x2000000000000001 * 0x1ffffffffffffffe` (exactly 2^-1022 - 2^-1126) rounds to 2^-1022 and is kept. Measured on RDNA2 (gfx1031, RX 6700 XT, AMD Windows driver 32.0.21045.5002, HIP) at IEEE=0 and 1, denorm16 0..3, over 576 pairs of 24 f64 values (zeros, denormals, minimum normals, values next to 1 and to 2^-1022, products just below 2^-1022, the largest finite value, infinities), with neg, abs and clamp. `v_fma_f64`, `v_div_fmas_f64` and shaders without a known float mode keep the previous lowering.

name: ulobjmgr.L5
text: [ulobjmgr](../../../core/libs/prx/ulobjmgr/Export.cpp) registers no object: `_sceUlobjmgrRegisterObject` always hands out id 0 and `_sceUlobjmgrUnregisterObject` releases nothing, as shadPS4 does

name: ulobjmgr.L9
text: [_sceUlobjmgrRegisterObject](../../../core/libs/prx/ulobjmgr/Export.cpp) (ulobjmgr) - parameters taken from shadPS4 (PS4): a nonzero 64-bit object, a nonzero 32-bit kind and a 32-bit id output; the meaning of the first two and the PS5 signature are unverified. The id bound of `_sceUlobjmgrUnregisterObject` (below 0x4000) and the raw `EINVAL` (22) return also come from shadPS4
